articles.abstract_zh: 光学晶格中原子的运动压缩态受到捕获势非谐性的影响。不相等的振动能量间隔会导致所占用的动态相干性之间的相移，从而导致波包的畸变和挤压的减少。我们通过数值证明，向一维晶格添加弱的二阶或三阶空间谐波会减慢挤压的初始衰减。压缩态是通过晶格深度的一两次突然变化来准备的。对于每个谐波和每个准备方案，我们选择谐波幅度，使演化状态最接近其在谐波陷阱中的演化，平均超过 1 ms。然后，我们将挤压与具有相同初始挤压和陷波频率的正弦晶格中的挤压进行比较。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 光学晶格中原子的运动压缩态受到捕获势非谐性的影响。不相等的振动能量间隔会导致所占用的动态相干性之间的相移，从而导致波包的畸变和挤压的减少。我们通过数值证明，向一维晶格添加弱的二阶或三阶空间谐波会减慢挤压的初始衰减。压缩态是通过晶格深度的一两次突然变化来准备的。对于每个谐波和每个准备方案，我们选择谐波幅度，使演化状态最接近其在谐波陷阱中的演化，平均超过 1 ms。然后，我们将挤压与具有相同初始挤压和陷波频率的正弦晶格中的挤压进行比较。在研究的所有四种情况中，连续的挤压最大值最初在成形晶格中衰减得更慢。之所以会出现这种改进，是因为最佳谐波几乎使压缩波包占据的区域上的两个主要振动能级间距相等，而单独取消势能的四次项是无法实现的。由于添加的谐波的幅度是静态的，并且可以使用现有的傅里叶合成技术产生，因此晶格整形提供了一种简单的方法来保持运动挤压，而无需额外的时间相关控制。

articles.title: Structure-preserving finite element method for the 2D MHD-α turbulence system
articles.title_zh: 二维MHD-α湍流系统的保结构有限元法
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a structure-preserving finite element method for the two-dimensional MHD-α turbulence model, which filters the transport velocity at a length α while retaining the ideal invariants of the original MHD equations, with the energy replaced by an α-dependent energy. The scheme preserves mass conservation and the magnetic Gauss law pointwise and satisfies discrete dissipation laws for the energy, the cross helicity and the mean square magnetic potential, which reduce to exact conservation in the ideal limit. The discrete systems are solved by an augmented Lagrangian preconditioner with monolithic geometric multigrid, observed to be robust with respect to the filter width α and the Reynolds numbers, and to the mesh size for small time steps. The scheme converges at the optimal rates and agrees with a Fourier pseudo-spectral direct simulation of the original MHD equations at the large scales. In under-resolved flows, the unfiltered scheme has no numerical dissipation and accumulates energy at the grid scale. Filtering relieves this accumulation and a larger α gives a more compact spectrum. Long-time simulations reproduce selective decay, including relaxation toward the Arnold-type bound and the inverse cascade of the mean square potential.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们提出了一种用于二维 MHD-α 湍流模型的结构保持有限元方法，该方法在长度 α 处过滤传输速度，同时保留原始 MHD 方程的理想不变量，其中能量由 α 相关能量代替。该方案逐点保持质量守恒和磁高斯定律，满足能量、交叉螺旋度和均方磁势的离散耗散定律，从而在理想极限下简化为精确守恒。离散系统通过具有整体几何多重网格的增强拉格朗日预处理器求解，观察到对于滤波器宽度 α 和雷诺数以及小时间步长的网格尺寸具有鲁棒性。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们提出了一种用于二维 MHD-α 湍流模型的结构保持有限元方法，该方法在长度 α 处过滤传输速度，同时保留原始 MHD 方程的理想不变量，其中能量由 α 相关能量代替。该方案逐点保持质量守恒和磁高斯定律，满足能量、交叉螺旋度和均方磁势的离散耗散定律，从而在理想极限下简化为精确守恒。离散系统通过具有整体几何多重网格的增强拉格朗日预处理器求解，观察到对于滤波器宽度 α 和雷诺数以及小时间步长的网格尺寸具有鲁棒性。该方案以最佳速率收敛，并与大尺度下原始 MHD 方程的傅里叶伪谱直接模拟一致。在未解析的流动中，未过滤的方案没有数值耗散，并且在网格尺度上累积能量。滤波可以缓解这种积累，较大的 α 可以提供更紧凑的频谱。长时间模拟再现了选择性衰减，包括向阿诺德型界限的弛豫和均方势的逆级联。

articles.title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
articles.title_zh: 更少的参数，更长的运行时间：混合量子物理神经网络的挂钟成本
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural networks (QCPINNs) are often described as efficient because they have fewer trainable parameters than classical PINNs, parameter count does not measure wall-clock cost. To examine this gap on a one-dimensional seawater temperature diffusion benchmark, with the quantum circuits simulated on a CPU, we time the four cumulative stages a PINN needs (the forward pass, the first- and second-order input gradients, and the PDE-loss parameter gradient) for a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations that differ in qubit count and circuit depth, and size-matched classical controls that share the hybrids' classical layers. We find that the hybrids are 14-56x slower than the classical PINN for the forward pass and 10-97x slower for the PDE-loss parameter gradient, and even against the size-matched controls, they remain 9-85x slower. Further, over the tested ranges, runtime increased approximately exponentially with qubit count, approximately linearly with circuit depth, and sub-linearly with batch size, while for the circuit-only forward pass, a second simulator backend was 10-165x slower under the same calling pattern. Although the hybrids have 38-44% fewer parameters than the classical PINN, this reduction comes from their smaller classical layers, as the quantum circuit accounts for at most 2.5% of each hybrid's parameters. Yet parameter count failed to predict runtime even among the classical networks, since the size-matched controls, despite having fewer parameters than the classical PINN, run slower than it. Our conclusion is that fewer parameters did not mean lower cost: every hybrid took at least ten times longer than the classical PINN at every stage, and the gap grew quickly with the number of qubits.
articles.abstract_zh: 虽然混合量子经典物理学神经网络 (QCPINN) 通常被描述为高效的，因为它们比经典 PINN 具有更少的可训练参数，但参数计数并不能衡量挂钟成本。为了检查一维海水温度扩散基准上的这一差距，使用在 CPU 上模拟的量子电路，我们对经典 PINN 所需的 4 个累积阶段（正向传递、一阶和二阶输入梯度以及 PDE 损失参数梯度）、四种量子位计数和电路深度不同的混合配置以及共享混合经典层的尺寸匹配经典控制进行了计时。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 虽然混合量子经典物理学神经网络 (QCPINN) 通常被描述为高效的，因为它们比经典 PINN 具有更少的可训练参数，但参数计数并不能衡量挂钟成本。为了检查一维海水温度扩散基准上的这一差距，使用在 CPU 上模拟的量子电路，我们对经典 PINN 所需的 4 个累积阶段（正向传递、一阶和二阶输入梯度以及 PDE 损失参数梯度）、四种量子位计数和电路深度不同的混合配置以及共享混合经典层的尺寸匹配经典控制进行了计时。我们发现，混合模型的前向传播比经典 PINN 慢 14-56 倍，PDE 损失参数梯度慢 10-97 倍，即使与大小匹配的控件相比，它们仍然慢 9-85 倍。此外，在测试范围内，运行时间随量子位计数呈指数增长，与电路深度呈近似线性增长，与批量大小呈次线性增长，而对于仅电路前向传递，第二个模拟器后端在相同调用模式下慢了 10-165 倍。尽管混合体的参数比经典 PINN 少 38-44%，但这种减少来自于其较小的经典层，因为量子电路最多占每个混合体参数的 2.5%。然而，即使在经典网络中，参数计数也无法预测运行时间，因为尺寸匹配的控件尽管参数比经典 PINN 少，但运行速度却比经典网络慢。我们的结论是，更少的参数并不意味着更低的成本：每个混合体在每个阶段所花费的时间都比经典 PINN 长至少十倍，而且差距随着量子比特数量的增加而迅速扩大。

articles.title: Lossless propagation of gain-compensated graphene plasmons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.21274v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graphene plasmons offer strong electromagnetic confinement and electrical tunability, but dissipation in the graphene sheet limits their propagation. Here, we investigate how optical gain in the surrounding dielectrics can compensate these losses in single- and double-layer graphene. Starting from the full electromagnetic boundary conditions and a finite-temperature graphene conductivity, we derive the compensation condition for a single sheet and the separate optical and acoustic dispersion relations for two coupled sheets. We show that the required gain depends both on material loss and on where the gain is placed. When gain is present throughout the dielectric environment, the two double-layer modes have nearly identical compensation thresholds. When it is confined to the spacer or the outer claddings, their thresholds separate because the modes overlap differently with each region. Full-wave finite-element simulations reproduce the predicted branches and field symmetries and show a strong suppression of attenuation together with a substantial increase in propagation length. The analysis also identifies the range over which a local conductivity provides a controlled description. These results show how the spatial distribution of gain can be used to control the compensation thresholds of the optical and acoustic graphene plasmons.

articles.title: Relaxed magnetohydrodynamics with cross-field flow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.03545v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The phase-space Lagrangian model of Dewar et al. (Phys. Plasmas 27, 062507, 2020) provides a framework for incorporating cross-field flow into relaxed equilibria while retaining ideal magnetohydrodynamics force balance. Here, we characterize the steady-state solution space and identify a solvability condition that couples the prescribed constrained flow to the geometry through the metric tensor. Using this condition, we construct equilibria in slab, cylindrical, and toroidal geometries. In toroidal geometry, the cross-field flow strongly correlates with magnetic-island structure: varying the rotation frequency modifies the dominant Fourier harmonic of the radial component of the magnetic field and can drive a transition from a primary (m = 1) island to secondary (m = 2) islands. In slab and cylindrical geometries, flow parameters weakly affect island width but strongly modify equilibrium profiles.

articles.title: Rotational energy levels in the ground vibrational state of methane with kHz-level accuracy from comb-referenced double-resonance and Lamb-dip spectroscopies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.13060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Methane is a key spherical-top molecule, yet restrictive selection rules for one-photon transitions have prevented determination of its ground state (GS) energies with state-of-the-art kHz-level accuracy. We report the GS rotational energy level differences with kHz-level accuracy from two frequency-comb-referenced Doppler-free methods: optical-optical double-resonance spectroscopy in the Λ-type configuration, and Lamb-dip spectroscopy of allowed and forbidden transitions. A Hamiltonian fit to the data yields GS term values with rotational numbers up to itJ = 12 with kHz level accuracy.

articles.title: Demonstration of H-mode Error Field Identification in a Single Discharge via Island Healing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.30452v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-disruptive compass scan error field identification via island healing is demonstrated on KSTAR in a single H-mode discharge. This method can allow for up to a 75% reduction in the operational time necessary for a complete compass scan by reducing the required discharges from four to one. Previous experiments on DIII-D, JET, and MAST-U have demonstrated the technique in Ohmic and L-mode but required multiple discharges and high fidelity real time n = 1 magnetic diagnostics located close to the plasma, which are unlikely to be viable for future devices. The results presented here were made possible by implementing a new set of triggering algorithms relevant to fusion pilot plant operation into the KSTAR plasma control system, along with KSTAR's strong RMPs and long pulse lengths. This represents a significant step towards the disruption-free error field identification method being demonstrated for deployment on future disruption-averse tokamaks, including ITER and fusion pilot plants. Steps needed to close remaining gaps to viability are addressed.

articles.title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem in the SU(8) dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator acting on its phase space. Using a complete basis of real 8× 8 matrices constructed from five-dimensional gamma matrices and the mathfraksu(2) generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we decompose the conserved quantities of the harmonic oscillator into representations of SO(5) × SU(2) and identify the SU(2)-singlet sector. We show that the corresponding conserved quantities generate an SO(6) subgroup of the SU(8) dynamical symmetry. We then perform the Hurwitz transformation and symplectic reduction with respect to SU(2), obtaining the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian. We explicitly show that the SO(6) moment map reduces to the angular momentum and the suitably normalized Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem on a fixed negative-energy surface. This establishes the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector in the dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator.

articles.title: Plasma transport by carrier electrons: delocalization length for heat-flux
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The kinetic understanding of the three magnetized heat-flux components is unified in the linear regime with a full electron-electron collision operator and a converged harmonic expansion of the electron distribution (up to f₆). The delocalization length λ_d=λₑᵢ Z/sqrtZ+4.45 is an improved heat-flux non-locality metric accounting for the localizing effect of electron-electron collisions on the electron population carrying heat-flux. Magnetization also localizes the carrier electrons; the delocalization Hall parameter ψ_d=13.4 χ Z/(Z+4.45) shows that this occurs at a faster rate than magnetization of thermal conductivity (ψκ= 9.94χ(Z+0.17)/(Z+5.88)). The traditional Knudsen number, which uses the electron-ion mean-free path, does not fairly represent non-locality across ionization and magnetization; Kn_d = 8.28λdbₒₜ/L_T should instead be used. Righi-Leduc suppression is found to be the square of the perpendicular suppression, with no additional length-scale required. This approach lays the groundwork for consistent treatment of kinetic plasma transport, with subsequent papers addressing the kinetically-modified induction equation.

articles.title: Scale-Dependent Statistics of Coherent Magnetic Structures in Early IMAP Observations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze early Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) magnetic field observations (November 2025 to May 2026) to quantify the statistical properties of helical magnetic structures and their relationship with turbulence intermittency. Intermittent structures, such as current sheets, are identified using the Partial Variance of Increments (PVI) method, and the scale-dependent normalized magnetic helicity is computed over scales corresponding to 0.5-3 correlation lengths. Prior studies have typically applied the PVI-helicity method to individual events; here we extend this technique to the ensemble statistics of a multi-month sample spanning many correlation times. To separate coherent helical structures from random turbulent fluctuations, significance thresholds for helicity are determined using phase-randomized surrogate realizations. We find a clear scale dependence in the occurrence, duration, and waiting time of coherent magnetic helicity, reminiscent of the scale-transfer arguments underlying inverse cascade, selective decay, and Taylor relaxation theories. Event duration and waiting-time distributions are well described by power-law and exponential models over different ranges, consistent with previous findings. In addition, PVI and magnetic helicity are anticorrelated, suggesting that high-PVI regions are preferentially associated with the boundaries of flux ropes, while their interiors tend to exhibit lower PVI and stronger magnetic helicity.

articles.title: Time Travel Paradoxes and Entangled Timelines
articles.abstract: arXiv:2303.07635v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in different timelines. However, so far, a concrete mechanism by which parallel timelines can be created has never been satisfactorily formulated in a way that makes the relationships between the timelines clear. In this paper, we propose such a mechanism based on the Everett (many-worlds) interpretation of quantum mechanics. The timelines in our model are variants of the "worlds" of the Everett interpretation that can connect to each other via the time machine. They are created by the entanglement of the time machine with the environment and the resulting decoherence; therefore, we call them "entangled timelines" or E-CTCs. As the entanglement gradually spreads out to additional systems, the timelines spread out as well, providing a local and well-defined mechanism for branching timelines. The E-CTC model is similar to Deutsch's familiar D-CTC model but differs from it mainly by imposing a different consistency condition, based on pure states, which allows the information about the entanglement to be preserved. These differences allow us to create a clearer practical definition of the timelines and avoid some of the surprising consequences of the D-CTC model's non-linear evolution.

articles.title: The Role of Preceding CMEs and SIRs in Enhancing Shock Acceleration of Electrons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.03709v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The role of large-scale pre-existing interplanetary structures, including preceding coronal mass ejections (CMEs) and stream interaction regions (SIRs), in shaping the shock acceleration environment for energetic electrons remains not fully understood. In this study, we investigate nine interplanetary shocks observed by the Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory (STEREO) that are associated with significant MeV electron enhancements, as such enhancements are rarely observed at interplanetary shocks. We combine remote-sensing observations, drag-based modeling, and in-situ measurements to analyze the shock propagation through pre-existing interplanetary structures. Eight of the nine events are associated with a preceding slow or intermediate-speed CME, while six shocks are in-situ observed propagating within preceding ICMEs, indicating that large-scale upstream trapping structures are a common feature of these events. Further analysis identifies three distinct scenarios associated with enhanced electron acceleration: shocks propagating through preceding ICMEs, shock-SIR interactions, and direct injection of flare-accelerated electrons into SIRs. As a representative shock-in-ICME event, the 2012 January 29 low-β, quasi-perpendicular shock (θBₙsim87^circ) is further investigated using observations together with one-dimensional Monte Carlo test-particle simulations of a shock propagating into a large-scale upstream magnetic loop. The simulation suggests that the upstream loop prolongs electron residence near the shock and substantially enhances acceleration efficiency. These results demonstrate that large-scale interplanetary structures can precondition the upstream magnetic environment, providing favorable conditions for prolonged electron residence and efficient shock acceleration.

articles.title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Signal Space, Sampling Operators, and First Recorded Crossing Time
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.11610v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multi-threshold sampling encodes signals through crossing times at prescribed thresholds, offering an alternative to uniform time-domain sampling. Its potential to reduce hardware requirements and power consumption motivates its use in high-speed pulse acquisition, including scintillation detector readout. We model the relation between signal statistics and recorded-crossing statistics by composing measurable stochastic crossing, timing, and selection operators. The threshold noise processes are independent across thresholds. The sampler applies independent timing jitter at each analog crossing before quantization and enforces dead time separately at each threshold in the recording window. We express the joint cumulative distribution function of first recorded crossing times using path infima and suprema when crossings at each threshold share the same timing jitter. Specializing this formula to a single threshold gives the marginal distribution, from which we obtain the conditional standard deviation. We use these formulas to approximate the corresponding exact quantities under independent timing jitter at each crossing and bound each approximation error. In a scintillation example, the shared-jitter formulas and independent-jitter waveform simulations agreed within Monte Carlo sampling uncertainty for the joint and marginal distributions and for the conditional standard deviation. Engineers can use these results to choose thresholds and assess how sampler changes affect timing precision.

articles.title: Geophysics-informed invertible operator network for Bayesian geophysical inversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geophysical inverse problems are inherently ill-posed because of sparse observations and measurement noise. Classical sampling-based Bayesian inference methods, such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), are computationally prohibitive because they require many forward simulations. Data-driven machine-learning methods often struggle to produce physically consistent solutions when training data are limited. To address these issues, we propose a geophysics-informed invertible operator network (GI-ION) that integrates an invertible neural network (INN) within a deep operator-learning framework for efficient Bayesian geophysical inversion. The INN serves as the branch network and transforms the model parameters into branch coefficients that represent the forward solution and a latent variable that captures uncertainty in the inverse problem. By learning the forward operator and enforcing statistical independence between the branch coefficients and the latent variable, GI-ION enables efficient sampling from a learned conditional approximation, even with sparse boundary observations. We validated GI-ION on three representative cases: 1D surface-wave dispersion and travel-time tomography for a 2D synthetic random-field model and a seismic-slice model. Numerical experiments demonstrate robust performance across diverse problem settings and efficient conditional sampling.

articles.title: The Marauder's Map: Bézier Manifolds Reveal Hidden Surfaces for Model Merging and Ensembling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural circuits are famously more robust than deep networks. This is often explained through degeneracy, where structurally distinct configurations support the same function. However, real biological systems exhibit a more flexible form of degeneracy in which specialized circuits continually adapt towards new competencies through localized changes while preserving existing function. Deep learning studies degeneracy through mode connectivity, which connects same-task networks by low-loss curves, sheets, or volumes. However, the field lacks a counterpart to flexible degeneracy, which demands more than ordinary mode connectivity. Defining such an analogue requires asking whether many independently initialized models trained on distinct tasks can be connected by a high-dimensional region of multi-task solutions. We introduce Nimbus, which learns a high-dimensional Bézier manifold connecting N specialists, going beyond the one-dimensional paths and two-dimensional sheets of mode connectivity work. A naive parameterization would scale combinatorially with N, but Nimbus requires learning corrections of only 3 interaction orders, showing that the connecting manifold has surprisingly low complexity yet supports multi-task competencies. The resulting manifold forms a navigable "Marauder's Map" that connects specialist models through a shared geometry of competent solutions. Trained across vision and language domains, Nimbus produces manifolds that are functionally and locally weight-flat: ensembles sampled from them degrade more gracefully than baselines under input and weight perturbations, with the largest gains in NLL loss and calibration error. Nimbus supplies a deep learning interpretation of flexible degeneracy, recasting model connectivity from a low-dimensional path between distant solutions into a high-dimensional volume of nearby ones.

articles.title: Discovering Explicit Magnetic Core-Loss Equations via Symbolic Sparse Identification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact core loss equations are essential tools in magnetic component design, but existing approaches trade accuracy against interpretability. Empirical models such as the Steinmetz Equation (SE) yield compact expressions of limited accuracy, while machine learning methods achieve high accuracy as black-box predictors. This paper bridges the gap with a Symbolic Sparse Identification (SSI) framework, which casts core loss modeling as a data-driven symbolic regression problem and recovers unknown equations directly from measured data, without presuming a functional form. First, a comprehensively expanded library of symbolic candidate terms far richer than the SE is constructed. Second, the governing terms are isolated from this library by sparse regression. Third, the coefficients of the retained terms are refined with an AdamW optimizer to maximize accuracy and form an analytical equation. Experiments on Fair-Rite 78, 79, and 95 yield test mean absolute percentage errors of 1.89%, 1.01%, and 1.56%, respectively, with only 10, 10, and 7 active terms. Comparisons with empirical, numerical, and symbolic models quantify the resulting balance of accuracy and compactness. SSI thus provides an explicit and physically guided approach for high-frequency magnetic characterization and design.

articles.title: Pretraining for Forecasting in Relational Databases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world forecasting increasingly relies on asynchronous transaction logs in relational databases rather than uniformly sampled arrays. While relational deep learning (RDL) models can forecast from these complex histories, they are typically trained separately for each specific target and root entity type. We introduce Query-Conditioned Relational pretraining (QCRP), a self-supervised framework that enables a standard RDL backbone to act as a universal forecaster across a database. QCRP generates diverse forecasting objectives using a structured temporal query grammar and interleaves them through a shared conditional predictor. This produces a robust, frozen encoder reusable for downstream tasks via lightweight predictors or a zero-shot interface. Evaluated on large-scale RelBench databases, QCRP learns frozen representations that support competitive forecasting across tasks and entity types. Furthermore, a single unified QCRP model checkpoint is competitive with isolated, entity-specific specialists. We demonstrate promising results for reusing the learned representations from standard RDL backbones for forecasting tasks in relational databases.

articles.title: Assessing the Physical Interpretability of AlphaEarth Foundation Embeddings Through Multi-Sensor Satellite Time-Series Benchmarking for Agricultural Mapping
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and dynamic maps of agricultural LULC are important for agricultural water resource management, particularly in areas where water scarcity is prevalent, such as Morocco. Here, we evaluate the utility of AlphaEarth Foundation Model (AEF) embeddings for agricultural LULC and irrigation-type mapping in Morocco. AEF embeddings were compared to single-date and time-series remote-sensing features using three machine-learning classifiers: XGBoost, CatBoost, and TabPFN. We also evaluated whether AEF embeddings can: (a) provide an efficient and transferable alternative to conventional direct use of Earth observation products and (b) reconstruct biophysical information. Results showed that multi-temporal feature time series achieved the highest performance, with accuracies of 0.93 for agricultural LULC and 0.87 for irrigation-type mapping when using TabPFN. However, AEF embeddings yielded comparable results, achieving accuracies of 0.91 for agricultural LULC and 0.85 for irrigation-type mapping, while reducing the need for extensive data processing and manual feature engineering typically required for satellite products. Spatial LULC mapping using TabPFN achieved comparable overall accuracies (0.85-0.86) across the three feature configurations, but revealed substantial differences in mapped tree cover, ranging from 14.57% for surface reflectance to 29.79% for AFE. Physical probing revealed that AEF embeddings strongly encode spectral indices (A30-SWIR: rho=0.58-0.67), (A38-NDMI: rho=-0.72), vegetation (A49-NDVI: rho = 0.72-0.73), and SAR structure (A25-VH: rho = 0.71). Future research should focus on enhancing the interpretability of embedding-based approaches by incorporating physical knowledge to develop more transparent and trustworthy AI systems for agricultural applications.

articles.title: Investigating the efficacy of vortex beam speckle patterns for the recognition of atmospheric turbulence and fractional topological charge with a deep learning model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional topological charge (TC) enlarges the usable mode set of orbital angular momentum (OAM) links, but reading it reliably after atmospheric turbulence remains difficult. Interferometric and diffractive methods need an undistorted beam and a careful alignment, while most learned approaches treat integer or coarsely spaced charges and do not include turbulence. Here we ask whether the charge of a scalar vortex beam can be regressed directly from a single speckle image, and at which turbulence strength this stops working. We propagate vortex beams over 1500~m through 150 von Kármán phase screens, scatter them with a fixed random diffuser, and record 256×256, 16-bit speckle images for TC from 0 to 10 in steps of 0.01 and turbulence strengths D/r₀ from 0 to 50; the results reported here use a subset of 20,000 images, and a data set of 10⁶ images is in preparation. A convolutional neural network estimates the TC and, through an auxiliary head, the turbulence category. On charges withheld from training, the mean absolute error is 0.031 without turbulence (with a common intensity scale) and rises to 0.78 at D/r₀=10 and 1.85 at D/r₀=50, against 2.5 for a constant prediction, and the turbulence category is identified correctly in 78% of the images. The results show that, at the present training size, the charge is read accurately only without turbulence, and that the charge and the turbulence oth act on the speckle grain size, which may limit the readout. Experimental validation and the extension to vector vortex beams are left for future work.

articles.title: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less than You Think
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting, the drastic loss of previously acquired capabilities when learning new ones, is a central challenge in language model fine-tuning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is widely believed to be prone to such forgetting. Recent works have attributed this to the off-policy nature of SFT, arguing that on-policy learning is key to continual learning. In this paper, we challenge this premise. We show that while maximizing new-task performance can induce catastrophic forgetting, alternative hyperparameter choices (lower learning rate and batch size) can yield similar gains with little to no forgetting. With hyperparameters selected jointly for gain and retention, vanilla SFT retains prior capabilities far better than previously suggested and can be competitive with Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT), an on-policy approach designed to mitigate forgetting. While SDFT can be more robust to hyperparameter choices, it also requires a retention-aware criterion to identify hyperparameter configurations that avoid catastrophic forgetting. Our results challenge the view that on-policy training is what enables learning with retention and raise broader questions about what drives catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning.

articles.title: ChemoMAE: Self-Supervised Spectral Representation Learning Reveals Chemical Heterogeneity in Historical Wood
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In historical timber buildings, multiple environmental factors act over centuries on wood whose chemical composition varies across anatomical regions, producing complex patterns of degradation. Understanding how timber members degrade is important for the effective conservation and restoration of historical buildings, yet the mechanisms underlying these patterns remain unclear. To investigate these mechanisms, we used self-supervised learning to establish a common basis for comparing specimens from timber members that differ in wood species and service history. We examined transverse sections of 49 wood specimens from several historical buildings in Japan using near-infrared hyperspectral imaging. ChemoMAE, a self-supervised Transformer, learns pixelwise spectral representations through masked denoising that exploits multicollinearity among spectral variables. Clustering these representations yields spatial maps without predefined chemical-state categories. Because anatomy and degradation can produce spatially continuous regions, we formulated Local Label Agreement (LLA) to quantify agreement among labels assigned to neighboring pixels. Using spectra alone, ChemoMAE yielded higher mean LLA than baseline methods on validation specimens. We then trained ChemoMAE anew and fitted cluster centers across all specimens. Spatial structures consistent with wood anatomy and the expected effects of surface exposure emerged in the resulting maps. By cross-referencing regional spectra and spatial distributions across specimens in light of wood anatomy, service histories, and prior studies, we proposed models of internal and surface degradation as mechanistic hypotheses. This exploratory AI for Science framework gives researchers a basis for linking latent patterns learned through self-supervision with domain knowledge when investigating how material states form.

articles.title: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to bound approximation errors for deep neural networks, we split the problem into two steps: First the selection of optimal infinite width limits for each layer and second an optimal discretization of all layers to obtain finite sized networks. We show that in expectation, the latter problem is equivalently characterized by a layer wise generalization of Barron norms. Moreover, we provide an analysis of the optimization landscape and show that local minima are characterized by an equidistribution principle akin to similar ideas in adaptive spline and finite element approximation.

articles.title: The Symmetry Budget: How Much Group Structure Should a Network Architecture Assume?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A network architecture is, in large part, a symmetry assumption: convolution ties weights across translations, attention ties them across permutations, and a fully connected layer ties nothing. When the data are only approximately symmetric, tying trades approximation error against estimation error, and the right amount of tying is a property of the dataset, not of the architecture alone. We study this trade-off in an exactly solvable model: linear maps on signals over the cyclic group Z_d, with architectures indexed by the subgroup lattice of Z_d, so that a single integer k mid d interpolates between an unconstrained layer (k=1, d² parameters) and a fully equivariant one (k=d, d parameters). We derive the finite-sample excess risk in closed form, show that for a generic symmetry defect the leading-order risk is affine in 1/k, and prove that intermediate architectures are then never strictly optimal: the lattice collapses to an all-or-nothing choice with phase boundary n^star = σ² d(d-1)/ε². Structured defects break this collapse and restore interior optima, and we give a closed-form defect profile for a graded defect. Measurements agree with the theory on 60/60 cells of a (ε,n) phase diagram and 48/48 cells of a second phase diagram at d=16, recover the predicted exponent as -1.92 against -2, and exhibit the predicted k^star: 12 → 4 → 1 ladder under graded defects; a two-layer nonlinear control reproduces the crossover. We also characterize when the affine collapse survives for non-abelian groups.

articles.title: A Realistic End-to-End Runtime Crossover Estimation for Quantum-Enhanced Training of Large-Scale Machine Learning Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is one promising application domain for Quantum Computing (QC) speedups, but asymptotic complexity considerations often mask the actual engineering costs of actual end-to-end workflows. For the use case of training a linearized Neural Network with a Quantum Linear Solver, a provably favorable quantum scaling has been suggested. We present realistic resource estimates for this problem, accounting for data access, computation, and readout. Our analysis examines three increasingly complex benchmarking scenarios, under distinct sparsity-scaling assumptions, thereby enabling progressively more realistic resource estimates. We identify crossover regimes relative to classical methods and find that crossover points emerge only for very large problem sizes, long computation times, and highly restrictive output requirements. This work provides a blueprint for evaluating quantum-enhanced ML algorithms under realistic hardware constraints and help identifying the bottlenecks that must be overcome to approach industrial quantum utility.

articles.title: FokasNets: Completing missing boundary data in Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operators via the Global Relation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce FokasNets, a framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and operators (PINOs) with the Global Relation (GR) formulation of the Fokas method (also referred to as the Unified Transform), for mixed boundary problems. The general framework considers lifted representations of the neural network models, where the Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed by construction and the neural network learns the interior correction. The Global Relation is used as an additional solve during training that provides the missing boundary conditions to the lifted neural network, making training more efficient and accurate in the interior and on the boundary. We develop the construction of FokasNets for elliptic and evolution PDEs (Fokas-PINNs), and the corresponding PDE solution operator problems (Fokas Operator Networks - FONets), using the Global Relation formulations for these PDE classes. Furthermore, we develop the necessary theoretical framework for FokasNets, including error and stability analysis and show that FokasNets are universal approximators. We provide comprehensive numerical experiments, using examples with manufactured solutions and literature benchmarks. Compared to standard PINNs and Physics-Informed DeepONets and their lifted versions, FokasNets achieve significant improvements in solution accuracy in the interior and boundaries, both for single PDEs and particularly for solution operators, where the improvement reaches multiple orders of magnitude and fixed threshold errors are reached faster during training.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Learning for Multiplayer Differential Games
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computing per-player feedback strategies in N-player adversarial differential games is challenging as the associated coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman system is high-dimensional and generally lacks classical solutions. We address this by approximating viscosity solutions using physics-informed neural networks within a policy iteration scheme with a vanishing-viscosity annealing schedule. Theoretically, we establish an explicit ε-Nash guarantee by bounding per-player regret via computable residuals and prove our method reaches this stopping criterion in finite time. For two-player zero-sum games, we further establish a computable bound on the approximation error of the value function. Numerical experiments on pursuit-evasion scenarios illustrate the tightness of these computed bounds and the framework's scalability to high-dimensional environments.

articles.title: Nepali Currency Denomination Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and MobileNetV2: An Experimental Comparison
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated currency denomination recognition is a computer vision task with applications in cash handling, financial technology, and assistive systems. This study classifies seven Nepali currency denominations (Rs. 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, and 1,000) using three configurations: a conventional convolutional neural network (CNN), MobileNetV2 with transfer learning, and MobileNetV2 with hyperparameter tuning. A compiled dataset of 16,249 images was used, comprising 10,500 training, 3,500 validation, and 2,249 independent test images. Images were resized to 128 x 128 pixels, normalized, and augmented to vary orientation, scale, illumination, and appearance. Models were evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and precision-recall and ROC analysis. The hyperparameter-tuned MobileNetV2 achieved the highest validation accuracy (95%), with precision, recall, and F1-score of 0.93, 0.91, and 0.92, but reached only 84% accuracy on the held-out test set. MobileNetV2 with transfer learning but no additional tuning achieved 89% test accuracy, and the conventional CNN achieved 85%. Transfer learning therefore provided a competitive approach under the evaluated conditions, while higher validation accuracy from tuning did not yield higher test accuracy. To demonstrate practical deployment, a Flask-based web prototype using TensorFlow Lite was developed, supporting image upload and live webcam recognition with both visual and voice output. The study shows the feasibility of combining lightweight deep learning with a voice-assisted web interface for Nepali currency recognition, and highlights the need for more diverse datasets, greater robustness under uncontrolled imaging conditions, and broader real-world evaluation.

articles.title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.

articles.title: Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34905v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs. We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last m observations to the nearest regime mean. For two regimes with conditionally independent, stochastically ordered observations, a switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly 1/2. Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most bar P(m)+bar s(m-1)/2, where bar P(m) is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and bar s the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly 1/2, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor pₘᵢₙm⁻¹. For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of σ²/Δ², depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is bar slog(1/bar s)/(2I)(1+o(1)), with I the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most 2log2approx1.39, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with ±1 steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.

articles.title: BayesFlow 2: Multi-Backend Amortized Bayesian Inference in Python
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.07098v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modern Bayesian inference involves a mixture of computational methods for estimating, validating, and drawing conclusions from probabilistic models as part of principled workflows. An overarching motif of many Bayesian methods is that they are relatively slow, which often becomes prohibitive when fitting complex models to large data sets. Amortized Bayesian inference (ABI) offers a path to solving the computational challenges of Bayes. ABI trains neural networks on model simulations, rewarding users with rapid inference of any model-implied quantity, such as point estimates, likelihoods, or full posterior distributions. In this work, we present the Python library BayesFlow, Version 2, for general-purpose ABI. Along with direct posterior, likelihood, and ratio estimation, the software includes support for multiple popular deep learning backends, a rich collection of generative networks for sampling and density estimation, complete customization and high-level interfaces, as well as new capabilities for hyperparameter optimization, design optimization, and multilevel modeling. Using a case study on dynamical system parameter estimation, combined with comparisons to similar software, we show that our streamlined, user-friendly workflow has strong potential to support broad adoption.

articles.title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning Under a Generative Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.02826v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning is a subfield of machine learning that studies how an agent interacts with an environment in order to extract as large a reward as possible. A standard approach to study such interaction is through Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) and the task of choosing an optimal policy---a function that tells the agent which action to take. In this work, we study two types of time-dependent MDP---finite-horizon and infinite-horizon discounted---and propose new quantum algorithms for computing approximate optimal policies. Our quantum algorithms are based on a new combination of standard value iteration and quantum subroutines like quantum mean estimation and quantum maximum finding, overall enhanced with techniques from sample-optimal classical algorithms. Our resulting query complexities improve upon previous works, thus approaching already established quantum lower bounds.

articles.title: Controllable CAD Generation and Interactive Editing of Fluid Rotors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-aided design (CAD) provides the geometric foundation for rotors in fluid rotating machinery. However, creating models for different rotors requires different modeling processes, making it difficult to control geometry through design intent and reuse existing models. We introduce VaneCraft, an agent-driven framework for rotor generation, inverse recovery, and editing through a unified analytical representation. The agent interprets design requests and invokes geometric modeling operations. The representation defines geometric controls through meridional geometry and independent boundary angle laws. An anisotropic partial differential equation (PDE) maps these controls to the blade surfaces. Geometric parameter correction (GPC) uses a joint geometric encoder and a parameter decoder to refine controls initialized from rotor category and dimensions. Inverse recovery maps existing CAD to the same geometric controls for reconstruction and continued editing. Experiments demonstrate that VaneCraft supports anisotropy control and parameter editing and outperforms representative baselines in rotor CAD generation tasks. Project page is available on hrefhttps://github.com/shenchen333/vanecraftGitHub.

articles.title: SlicePlanner: Logic-Guided Agentic AI for Online QoS-Aware Network Slicing in Open RAN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive network slicing in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) demands reconfiguration decisions that respond to live traffic conditions while remaining safe with respect to Service Level Agreement (SLA) constraints, a combination that purely data-driven controllers cannot reliably guarantee without continuous retraining. We present SlicePlanner, a logic-guided closed-loop framework that treats each RAN reconfiguration as a controlled hypothesis: proposed from live and historical KeyPerformance Indicator (KPI) evidence, filtered through explicit SLA constraints and mined RAN control rules, and committed only when post-action measurements confirm improvement. SlicePlanner comprises two cooperating agents: SliceSense, which monitors live KPIs, retrieves context-conditioned evidence, and ranks candidate RAN actions through a surrogate-guided admissibility filter; and SliceGuard, which validates post-action KPI responses, rolls back harmful configurations, and refreshes rules under distribution drift. Validated over the air using OpenAirInterface, FlexRIC, and commercial Sierra Wireless 5G devices, SlicePlanner reduces SLA latency violations by up to 86% over static slicing and 50% over Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based slicing, while maintaining comparable cell throughput and auditable decisions without online retraining.

articles.title: Poisoning Self-Evolving Security Policies in LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-evolving defenses improve LLM-agent security by learning reusable policies from observed attacks. However, we demonstrate that this learning process itself can become an attack surface. Using SED (Self-Evolving Defense) in the AgentDojo benchmark, we construct a single prompt-injection episode that causes the defense to learn an over-broad policy and subsequently refuse legitimate requests. Across 10 Nemotron runs, every poisoned run over-refuses at least one legitimate task, while unrelated-task performance remains unchanged and the original prompt-injection defense remains effective. The attack also transfers to gpt-oss-120b; however, its poisoning mechanism depends on a successful initial prompt injection and therefore fails to activate when the target agent resists the underlying injection. In contrast, integrity-oriented attacks targeting SED's judge, policy synthesis, retrieval, and organization mechanisms fail in our evaluated settings, identifying over-refusal as the primary exploitable failure mode observed in our experiments. We further identify self-poisoning from false-positive harm judgments without an attacker. Finally, contrastive policy synthesis and an automatic broadness-check gate substantially reduce, but do not eliminate over-refusal, without compromising security in our evaluated settings.

articles.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by operating in exponentially large Hilbert spaces, can efficiently represent such distributions and provide favorable inductive biases for learning, offering a promising pathway to overcome these limitations. However, their practical deployment in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era is severely hindered by gradient coupling, barren plateaus, data-loading bottlenecks, and high inference latency. To bridge classical AI and QML, we propose QPAT (QCBM-Prior-Assisted Training), a universal framework that employs a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) as a learnable generative prior to provide a task-aligned structured inductive bias during classical model training. The framework can be seamlessly integrated into any classical backbone, including LSTMs, CNNs, and Transformers. We introduce a decoupled fitness-based scoring mechanism and a stochastic "Drop-Prior" mechanism to implicitly distill quantum structural knowledge into the classical weights during training. Evaluated extensively on six benchmarks spanning time-series forecasting, computer vision, and natural language processing, our framework consistently outperforms purely classical backbones in both predictive performance and stability across random seeds; ablation studies further show that these gains are not reproduced by unstructured random priors or a classically learned generative prior. Remarkably, our approach enables completely classical inference, bypassing quantum latency while preserving quantum-enhanced accuracy, paving a highly practical path for QML deployment.

articles.title: Latent-in-the-Middle: On the Security of Cross-Model Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models increasingly collaborate in heterogeneous multi-agent systems, latent communication has emerged as an efficient alternative to exchanging natural-language messages. By sharing internal representations, agents can avoid repeatedly processing the same context, reducing communication overhead and prefill computation. One such mechanism is cross-model Key-Value (KV) cache transfer, which uses a learned mapper to translate a source model's KV cache into one a target model can use. However, this handoff means the target model consumes context it did not encode itself, thus calling into question whether its safety alignment still holds. In this work, we investigate the security implications of latent handoffs by introducing Chasm, a framework characterizing cross-model handoff attacks across three new attack surfaces: the source model, mapper, and handoff mechanism itself. Our experiments reveal that latent handoffs substantially undermine safety alignment and prompt-injection defenses. Notably, a target model that follows only 0.4% of benchmark prompt injections natively, follows up to 44.2% when transferred through a mapper from a source model. On the other hand, for jailbreak attacks, transfer alone raises attack success by up to 24.6 pp within a model family and zero-shot attacks by up to 69.2 pp, whereas white-box optimization through the mapper boosts the attack success rate to 92.5%, against 37.5% for ordinary GCG on the same target. To address these vulnerabilities, we propose a lightweight target-side cache guard that corrects transferred caches to restore the target model's refusal, considerably mitigating these attacks.

articles.title: When Skills Fail to Compose: Compatibility and Retention in Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Skill acquisition alone does not establish a reusable skill library: task proficiency does not specify a compositional interface. Motivated by agents that acquire and refine skills, we study independently learned soft-prompt skills on frozen language models, with skill identities and execution order supplied. Across four digit-task bases and three record-editing models, mean composition accuracy in one call is at most 7.6%, compared with 88.2% to 100% over two calls that add computation and an explicit intermediate output. Neutral-insertion training improves robustness but leaves substantial interference, which block length and per-token norm alone cannot explain on two of four digit bases. Blocks of the same operation need not be interchangeable: after training next to frozen learned partners, a post hoc test on two Qwen bases shows that replacing those partners with independently learned blocks of the same operations lowers median composition accuracy from 98.0% and 95.3% to 12.7% and 0.5%, although every replacement scores at least 90% alone. Repair can improve a composition while impairing the original skill, and rehearsal improves retention while transfer remains limited on Qwen2.5-0.5B. Internal interventions constrain explanations without identifying a shared failure mechanism. These findings motivate evaluating compatibility, retention and transfer alongside acquisition when building skill libraries for self-evolving agents. Code is available at https://github.com/YanLin-Quinne/SkillCompatibility.

articles.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues λ_X,λ_Y,λ_Z, the advantage is governed by λ_X²+λ_Y²+λ_Z². We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a Rényi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model predicts. A three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one with all processor and readout errors included, and under dephasing its memory performs better than Bell sampling in any memory frame on a perfect processor.

articles.title: Unsupervised Learning of Neural Implicit Functions from Point Clouds via Graph Filtering
articles.abstract: This paper presents an unsupervised method for directly learning neural implicit functions from 3D point clouds, aiming to tackle the core challenge of lacking ground-truth implicit values for supervisory training. Current approaches typically rely on global geometric constraints to learn implicit functions; however, this strategy often causes the optimization process to fall into local minima, resulting in over-smoothing artifacts, loss of fine geometric details, and blurring of sharp features. Although hand-crafted filters can be applied to point clouds to capture high-frequency details---thereby mitigating over-smoothing of geometric structures and avoiding the generation of coarse surfaces---their performance is highly dependent on manual parameter tuning, which severely restricts their generalization ability across diverse 3D shapes. To address these limitations, we propose a dynamic graph filter that integrates the adaptability of graph neural networks with the geometric characteristics of hand-crafted bilateral filters, enabling the learning of high-quality neural implicit functions from 3D point clouds. Our approach dynamically evolves graph features during the training process, automatically capturing high-frequency geometric details without the need for manual parameter adjustment. Ultimately, high-quality surface reconstruction can be achieved from the learned neural implicit function, even in the complete absence of ground-truth supervision. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that our proposed method effectively preserves complex geometric details and sharp features, achieving superior surface reconstruction quality compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

articles.title: Heat-transport networks reveal life-cycle organization and a warm–cold asymmetry of marine temperature extremes
articles.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) and cold spells (MCSs) are usually described as space–time objects, their internal heat pathways unresolved. Here we represent all 672 large offshore MHW and MCS objects of the East/Japan Sea in 1993–2022 as daily weighted directed networks whose nodes are the 0–50 m grid cells of an event and whose edges are anomaly heat fluxes across cell faces, closed by atmospheric and subsurface reservoirs. The mean net convergence of the network tracks the mean anomaly tendency of the members (median correlation 0.73). The inflow fraction from outside follows the perimeter-to-area ratio of the growing and shrinking object; per face, the boundary carries less flux than the interior, least near the peak, when recirculation, bottlenecks and hub persistence exceed early-growth values in 55–73% of events. Cold-spell networks recirculate more, carry more flux per boundary face and are less hierarchical than heatwave networks, with no detectable difference in the concentration of transport on dominant links; the recirculation and hierarchy contrasts are modest, robust to the object definition and associated with coherent anticyclonic flow through warm anomalies and rotational cyclonic flow around cold ones. The framework turns the object-based description of extremes into a quantitative account of how heat moves inside them, yields a testable hypothesis for other basins—that the asymmetry follows wherever warm anomalies ride boundary currents and cold anomalies form in cyclonic interiors—and produces daily graphs whose node features and edge weights are natural inputs for graph neural networks, a route to data-driven prediction of ocean extremes.

articles.title: Beauty and charm jet identification with end-to-end training on a superconducting quantum processor
articles.abstract: The identification of heavy-flavor jets, i.e. collimated streams of particles originating from the fragmentation of beauty and charm quarks produced in proton–proton collisions, represents one of the most challenging classification tasks in measurements at Large Hadron Collider experiments. In recent years, advanced machine learning techniques have been successfully employed to address this problem, while quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising alternative approach. However, the high dimensionality of the problem, typically involving hundreds of observables, raises an open question: whether the current generation of quantum computers, characterized by limited qubit count, can effectively tackle such complex tasks.In this work, a variational quantum circuit for the classification of b- and c-jets at the LHCb experiment is implemented on a 5-qubit superconducting quantum computer manufactured by IQM and installed at the Politecnico di Torino. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a quantum algorithm for jet identification using simulated data from an LHC experiment in which all stages of the machine-learning workflow, including training and testing, are performed on real quantum hardware. The results demonstrate that the impact of hardware-induced quantum noise does not significantly degrade the performance. A framework for the evaluation of the training time on the quantum hardware and for the circuit optimization is also proposed.These findings pave the way for future applications on larger quantum devices based on superconducting qubits, featuring a larger number of qubits enabling the encoding of information beyond the reach of classical simulation and providing a step toward investigating whether quantum advantage may eventually be achievable in high-energy physics classification tasks.

articles.title: Structural basis for alpha-actinin inhibition of cofilin binding to actin filaments
articles.abstract: Actin is a conserved cytoskeletal protein essential for morphogenesis, motility, and division. Its versatility arises from filament assembly and regulation by actin binding proteins. Among these, alpha-actinin organizes filaments into bipolar or unipolar networks, whereas cofilin binds preferentially to ADP-actin regions and forms clusters to shorten the half helical pitch (HHP). Here, we investigated the molecular mechanism of how alpha-actinin alters filament and protomer conformations and influences cofilin binding. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, and principal component analysis, we show that alpha-actinin crosslinking stabilizes actin filaments in the canonical helical state, thereby preventing the cofilin-induced helical shortening required for cooperative filament decoration. Stabilization occurs without significant changes in protomer twist and rise and subdomain geometry and maintains a flattened protomer conformation that restricts twisting needed for cofilin binding. Furthermore, myosin II (S1) and cofilin preferentially bind to normal and shortened half-helical structures, respectively. In contrast, the isolated alpha-actinin-1 actin binding domain mutant (ABD-E235K) and wild-type (ABD-WT) induce local transitions from the canonical double-helical filament to the single-helical protofilament, parallel-helical protofilament state (PPS), and nano-ring structures, while only weakly affecting cofilin binding and cluster formation on PPS. Notably, cofilin can bind and form clusters along single protofilaments without inducing helical-pitch shortening. Together, these findings reveal a mechanistically distinct function of full-length alpha-actinin and its isolated ABD and support a stepwise mechanism in which cofilin cooperative binding to canonical double-helical actin filaments requires initial binding to actin regions with shortened HHP, followed by protomer twisting and further helical shortening.

articles.title: Quantum Entanglement Witnesses in Neutron-Proton Scattering and Radiative Capture
articles.abstract: We present a theoretical framework that relates quantum entanglement witnesses to low-energy neutron–proton scattering, to the structure of the deuteron, and to the radiative capture reaction n + p → d + γ. Three modern nucleon–nucleon potentialsare combined with density-matrix techniques and with the electromagnetic transition operators that govern the capture process. The witness operator is constructed on the physical Hilbert space Hd ⊗ Hγ, where the deuteron carries spin one and thephoton carries polarization two. We show that the operator is Hermitian, derive an explicit rescaling that enforces the separability bound analytically, and demonstrate through numerical examples how its sign separates separable from entangled states.The dependence of the witness on the tensor force is quantified through a dimensionless logarithmic measure and compared with the corresponding dependence of the quadrupole moment, the D-state probability, the magnetic moment and the asymptoticD/S ratio. Restricting attention to the two-nucleon sector, we find a negative expectation value of the rescaled witness at low energies, ⟨ W ⟩ = −0.42 ± 0.02 at thermal energy, which signals d–γ entanglement in the final state and, through the coherent electromagnetic transition, points to non-classical correlations generated in the np system within the present model. Calculated capture cross sections are compared with experimental data between 25meV and 10MeV; the Argonne v18 results reproduce the data at the few-percent level, with the best agreement (0.03%) at thermal energy and deviations of 1–3% at higher energies. We also compute the negativityof the dγ density matrix as an independent entanglement measure and find it consistent with the witness result. The limitations of the present two-nucleon treatment are discussed, and the ingredients that would be required before any statement aboutthe astrophysical S-factor can be defended are identified. Every quantitative result is presented either as a theoretical prediction or as an order-of-magnitude estimate, and the sources of model dependence and uncertainty are stated wherever they arise.

articles.title: Protein engineering and yeast surface display of cellulases for improved bioethanol production
articles.abstract: Bioethanol production is important because of its positive impact on the environment. Cellulose is the most abundant raw material available. The enzymatic breakdown of cellulose by the cellulase enzyme leads to the formation of glucose, aiding in the production of bioethanol with commercial potential and lower production costs. Three cellulase enzymes endocellulase, cellobiohydrolase and β-glucosidase, were protein-engineered at variable regions via rational design. The protein-engineered genes were modelled, and molecular docking was performed to assess the binding affinity of the enzymes for the cellulose substrate. Compared with the wild-type enzymes, the engineered enzymes displayed greater stability, with a significant increase in amino acid interactions. Codon optimization, and synthetic gene synthesis, followed by vector preparation and subcloning into yeast for surface display, were carried out. The transformed OC21 yeast cells were analyzed for enzyme activity, and expression studies revealed that the membrane fractions had enzyme activity of endocellulase (28 ± 0.0024 IU/ml), cellobiohydrolase (16 ± 0.04 IU/ml) and β-glucosidase (11 ± 0.09 IU/ml), confirming the surface anchorage of the enzymes. The protein-engineered enzymes resulted in higher hydrolysis efficiencies of 81.9 ± 2.2% and 78.1 ± 1.2% for swollen cellulose and pretreated rice straw, respectively, at the 10-gram level. Separate and simultaneous saccharification studies of swollen cellulose and pretreated rice straw for ethanol production by thermotolerant Saccharomyces cerevisiaeOC21 surface displaying yeast strains at 42°C to asses fermentation efficiency. Separate saccharification and fermentation yielded 93.6 ± 0.58% and 91.4 ± 0.32%, respectively, for swollen cellulose fermentation and pretreated rice straw fermentation. A significant improvement in the production of bioethanol was observed in simultaneous saccharification and fermentation for swollen cellulose and pretreated rice straw, with 95.1 ± 0.45% and 92.3 ± 0.29% ethanol fermentation efficiency, respectively, in fermentation by surface-displaying OC21 yeast. The ethanol was further purified by distillation and molecular sieve absorption to obtain fuel grade ethanol with purity of 99.6 ± 0.2% (v/v). This result demonstrates that engineered cellulase enzymes, surface displayed in yeast strains can be an effective approach for improved bioethanol production.

articles.title: The fats and the furious: An aggressive interaction and season alter circulating medium and long chain fatty acids in a wild songbird
articles.abstract: Aggression is crucial to acquire limited resources, such as food, but has energetic costs. Fatty acids (FAs) can be used to fuel aggression, and seasonal shifts in FA profiles may influence the energetic and physiological costs of aggression. Surprisingly, the effects of an aggressive interaction on FAs remain unknown. Here, we assessed the impact of a 10 min simulated territorial intrusion in the breeding season or non-breeding season on circulating FAs in wild male song sparrows (Melospiza melodia). Plasma FAs were derivatised via acid-catalysed methylation, which hydrolyses complex lipids to yield total FA levels. We examined 52 FAs using gas chromatography coupled with flame ionisation detection and mass spectrometry, and quantified 33 medium and long chain FAs. Season was the primary driver of FA composition, significantly impacting nearly all FAs. Relative to breeding subjects, non-breeding subjects exhibited higher total FA level, elevated omega (ω)-6:ω-3 ratio, and lower FA unsaturation and peroxidisability indices. Crucially, a brief aggressive encounter significantly decreased total FA level and increased vulnerability to lipid peroxidation, and the intensity of aggression correlated positively with the ω-6:ω-3 ratio. Notably, aggressive behaviour and its effect on FAs were similar across seasons. To our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate how aggression influences FA species across seasons in a free-living animal, and it provides one of the most comprehensive circulating FA profiles reported to date for a songbird. Our results highlight FA metabolism as a potentially important pathway underlying the energetic, oxidative, and inflammatory costs of territorial aggression.

articles.title: Learning Protein-Protein Interaction Interfaces from Multimodal Representations
articles.abstract: Background: Protein-protein interactions govern essential cellular processes, making the identification of interface residues critical for protein engineering and molecular design. Although complex deep learning algorithms like AlphaFold3 generate full atom resolution assemblies, they are not optimized for residue-level interface identification. Existing methods face inherent limitations: sequence-based models lack explicit 3D context, while structure-based approaches can overlook evolutionary signals. Results: By combining evolutionary context with 3D geometry, the multimodal protein language model ESM3 offers the ideal foundation for residue-level interface classification. This results in the ESM3-PPISites model, which outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across diverse training and benchmark sets. Generalization is assessed through stringent sequence- and structure-based redundancy filtering to ensure evaluation on previously unseen proteins. Notably, finetuning the open-weight ESM3 architecture meaningfully narrows the performance gap with its proprietary full-scale counterpart. Furthermore, integrating predicted interaction sites as spatial restraints into HADDOCK significantly improves the recovery of near-native binding poses while reducing computational search time by an order of magnitude compared with blind docking. Conclusions: ESM3-PPISites enables accurate interfaces identification without relying on complex structural inputs at inference time, establishing a reliable and computationally efficient strategy for mapping protein-protein interaction sites.

articles.title: Projected expansion of Aedes albopictus habitat suitability in Austria under a changing climate
articles.abstract: Background The Asian tiger mosquito, Aedes albopictus, is an invasive vector of dengue, chikungunya and Zika viruses whose European range is expanding through human-mediated dispersal and increasingly favourable climatic conditions. In Austria, the species was first detected in 2012 and has since been reported from all federal states, with established populations in several urban centres such as Vienna and Graz. Because colonisation remains incomplete and occurrence records are spatially biased, current observations may not represent the full range of environments in which the species could establish. We therefore developed a transparent, ecologically and climatologically informed habitat suitability model for data-limited early-colonisation conditions.Methods The national-scale model integrates three hierarchically weighted domains: summer climatic suitability, overwintering potential and environmental habitat suitability. Historical climate conditions were represented using SPARTACUS data for 1991–2020. Future projections comprised 2036–2065 under representative concentration pathway (RCP) 8.5 and 2071–2100 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, using 16 ensemble members from Austria’s regional climate scenarios (ÖKS15). Environmental indicators were derived from Copernicus land-cover products. Habitat suitability classes were derived from ranked index values at verified citizen-science presence locations and applied consistently across scenarios. Climate-model uncertainty was quantified from the ensemble spread, population exposure was estimated using current and SSP population projection data, and Monte Carlo simulations evaluated sensitivity to expert-derived weights.Results Current suitability is concentrated in low-elevation urban and peri-urban areas with relatively mild winters. Across all future scenarios, suitable conditions expand through eastern lowlands and major valley systems. The proportion of Austria classified as Medium to Very high suitability increases from 1.6% during 1991–2020 to 4.8% under late-century RCP4.5 and 6.1% under late-century RCP8.5. Under the latter scenario, 55.7% of the projected population occupies cells classified as High or Very high suitability, compared with 34.1% under reference conditions. Climate uncertainty is greatest in transition zones, particularly parts of the Alpine foreland, whereas several urban hotspots show increasing agreement among ensemble members by late century. The broad spatial pattern was robust to substantially broadened weighting assumptions: under the strongest perturbation setting, the modal class differed from the reference over 0.65% of the modelled area using recalculated thresholds and 2.07% using fixed thresholds.Conclusions The framework provides a nationally consistent basis for surveillance prioritisation, vector-control planning and climate adaptation. Its outputs represent relative environmental suitability and population exposure rather than occurrence probability or outbreak risk. The approach is particularly suited to early invasion stages, when available occurrence data remain incomplete and influenced by introduction history and reporting effort.

articles.title: Silicic acid-enhanced anodization coupled with one-step self- assembly toward universal superhydrophobic corrosion protection on magnesium alloys
articles.abstract: Magnesium alloys have attracted extensive attention in aerospace, automotive and electronic fields due to their low density, high specific strength and high specific stiffness. However, their poor corrosion resistance has become a critical bottleneck restricting further application. Constructing superhydrophobic surfaces is an effective strategy to isolate corrosive media and impart multifunctional properties to magnesium alloys. Inspired by the superhydrophobic microstructure of lotus leaves, this work fabricated a biomimetic superhydrophobic coating on AZ31, AZ91 and ZK60 magnesium alloys via a facile anodization process combined with binary low-surface-energy substance self-assembly.
