Silicic acid-reinforced sodium silicate solution was used as the anodization electrolyte to construct a rough oxide layer with abundant reactive sites, and stearic acid (SA) and dodecyltrimethoxysilane (DTMS) were adopted for one-step co-modification. The effects of self-assembly time on surface morphology, wettability and corrosion resistance were systematically investigated. The results show that a typical micro-nano hierarchical structure mimicking lotus leaf surface is formed after 2 hours of self-assembly, with flower-like SA aggregates at micron scale and spherical DTMS aggregates at nanoscale. All modified magnesium alloys exhibit static water contact angles higher than 150°, presenting excellent water repellency and self-cleaning performance. Electrochemical tests indicate that the superhydrophobic coating significantly improves the corrosion resistance of magnesium alloys. The S-AZ91 sample possesses the optimal protective effect with a coating resistance of approximately 7135 Ω·cm², and its corrosion current density is reduced by approximately one order of magnitude compared with the bare substrate, which is comparable to many recently reported superhydrophobic coatings, though still inferior to some high-performance multilayer composite systems. This method has the advantages of simple operation, low raw material cost and wide substrate adaptability, showing great potential for industrial application of magnesium alloy surface protection.

articles.title: Impact based Event attribution for the assessment of potential future disasters caused by typhoons
articles.abstract: Assessing future changes in typhoon-related hazards is essential for climate adaptation. We develop an event-based storyline framework that couples high-resolution meteorological simulations with river discharge and storm-surge models to quantify future risks under specified warming levels. Using Typhoon Hagibis (2019) as a case study, we conduct multi-model, multi–initial-condition (MM–MI) ensemble experiments to account for structural model uncertainty and internal variability. Three meteorological models, each run with multiple initial-condition ensemble members, drive three river models and two storm-surge models. The experiments cover the present climate and two warming scenarios (+ 2 K and + 4 K). Across the ensembles, Hagibis intensifies under warming: precipitation and near-surface winds strengthen, and central pressure decreases relative to the present-climate simulations. Consistent with these changes, many river basins in eastern Japan exhibit increased discharge, amplifying flood risk, and the coastal models indicate larger storm surges. For Typhoon Hagibis, we quantify uncertainties in peak discharge and maximum storm-surge level. By sampling structural model differences, the multi-model combination broadens the range of plausible outcomes and better represents the associated uncertainty. Our MM–MI framework therefore provides a more comprehensive assessment of future typhoon-related risks than single-model experiments.

articles.title: Skew scattering induced contribution to orbital Hall response
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.24671v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Our study investigates the orbital Hall (OH) conductivity originating from the disorder induced mechanisms, namely side-jump and skew scattering. On treating the disorder potential within the first-order Born approximation and beyond and employing the quantum kinetic approach, the general scaling law for both mechanisms in terms of disorder potential is provided to signal out the process experimentally. The calculations have been processed for the three-dimensional Weyl semimetals under an oscillating electric field. We reveal that the higher order disorder contributions leading skew scattering process dominates the orbital Hall conductivity over the intrinsic and side-jump processes. In addition, we demonstrate the tunable nature of the extrinsic orbital Hall conductivity with the strength of the disorder potential and the external field. Finally, our findings highlights disorder scattering as a potential route for orbital transport.

articles.title: Growth Optimization and Spectroscopic Assessment of Low-Density Polyethylene Deterioration by Bacillus paranthracis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
articles.abstract: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is persistent in the environment, and microbial degradation offers a potential laboratory-scale approach to reducing its environmental burden. This study assessed how temperature, pH, supplementary carbon and nitrogen sources, and trace elements affect the growth of two LDPE-associated bacterial isolates from municipal dumpsite soil. We identified the isolates by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and whole-genome analysis as Bacillus paranthracis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, respectively; we resolved the taxonomic assignment of the Bacillus isolate using whole-genome data because 16S rRNA provides limited resolution within the Bacillus cereus group. Under the tested conditions, B. paranthracis showed maximum growth at 30 ℃ and pH 7.0, whereas P. aeruginosa showed maximum growth at 35 ℃ and pH 7.0. Glucose, yeast extract, and the combined trace-element treatment FeSO₄, MnSO₄, and ZnSO₄ supported higher growth in the respective screening experiments. In a 90-day LDPE assay, apparent mass loss was 3.59 ± 0.01% for B. paranthracis and 4.85 ± 0.24% for P. aeruginosa. ATR-FTIR revealed treatment-associated changes in oxygen-containing functional groups. Because complete mineralization, carbon dioxide evolution, and polymer molecular-weight reduction were not measured, the results are interpreted as evidence of LDPE deterioration rather than complete biodegradation. Further work should include abiotic controls, carbon mineralization, molecular-weight analysis and statistically designed optimization.

articles.title: IR-SegDiff: Conditional Diffusion for Subsurface Defect Segmentation and Uncertainty Estimation in Infrared Thermography
articles.abstract: Automatic detection of subsurface defects in aerospace structures is critical for structural safety assessment. In infrared thermography, the low thermal contrast of subsurface defects and measurement disturbances complicate defect segmentation and boundary delineation, while a single segmentation result provides limited information about potential prediction errors. To address these challenges, this study proposes IR-SegDiff, a conditional diffusion-based segmentation model for subsurface defect detection in structural materials commonly used in aerospace applications. The model integrates a conditional encoder, a conditional cross-attention fusion module (CCAFM), and a multi-scale feature fusion module (MSFFM) to guide defect reconstruction. During inference, DPM-Solver accelerates the sampling process, while repeated sampling enables ensemble prediction and pixel-wise uncertainty characterization. On a self-constructed dataset comprising carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP), glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP), and resin specimens, the five-sample ensemble achieves an F1-Score of 76.72% and an intersection over union (IoU) of 65.43%, outperforming seven baseline segmentation networks. The 25-step DPM-Solver achieves a 35.57-fold speedup compared with conventional step-by-step denoising. Controlled noise experiments demonstrate that ensemble sampling improves segmentation performance under noisy conditions, while sampling-based uncertainty provides complementary information for false-negative localization. By integrating condition-guided segmentation, efficient inference, and uncertainty characterization, the proposed method provides an approach for defect identification and assisted interpretation in infrared thermography.

articles.title: Chemia: An LLM-Powered Automated Machine Learning Framework for Chemistry and Materials Discovery
articles.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in chemistry and materials science, but wider adoption is limited by programming effort, model and hyperparameter selection difficulty, and limited reproducibility. We present Chemia, an open-source, configuration-driven automated ML framework in which a complete modeling workflow—from data loading, splitting and featurization to model competition, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and result export—is declared in a single YAML file. Chemia combines physicochemical descriptors, topological fingerprints and pretrained chemical foundation model embeddings; accepts single molecules, multicomponent reactions and user-supplied precomputed descriptors; and compares gradient-boosted trees, kernel methods and neural networks under a common protocol. We evaluated Chemia on molecular property regression and classification, reaction yield and selectivity prediction under random and out-of-distribution splits, and electrochemical property prediction for metal–organic framework supercapacitors from externally computed descriptors. In most tasks Chemia reached test performance similar to original studies or benchmark literature without task-specific code, but was less accurate for volumetric capacitance and extrapolation to unseen ligands. We also describe Chemia-Agent, in which an LLM agent operates Chemia only by editing YAML configurations; in a recorded case study, the agent repaired configuration errors and aligned its evaluation protocol with the original study. Chemia is freely available under the MIT license at https://github.com/flyben97/Chemia. Scientific contribution Chemia brings single-molecule property prediction, multicomponent reaction modeling and precomputed-descriptor materials modeling into one declarative, schema-validated YAML workflow that combines descriptor, fingerprint and pretrained-embedding representations with automated model competition, whereas existing chemistry AutoML tools such as Uni-QSAR, QSARtuna, ChemTorch and ProQSAR each cover only part of this scope. Because every modeling decision is an explicit configuration field, Chemia workflows are reproducible and auditable, and the same YAML layer gives LLM agents a constrained action space in which they can configure, diagnose and repair modeling workflows without generating Python code.

articles.title: Does Bayesian Uncertainty Make Network Intrusion Detectors Robust to Adversarial Evasion?
articles.abstract: Bayesian neural networks are often proposed for intrusion detection because their predictive uncertainty is expected to make them harder to fool and to flag manipulated traffic. We test this expectation under an evaluation designed to avoid the pitfalls that have inflated earlier robustness claims: a leakage-aware split of de-duplicated flows, feature-space constraints that keep perturbed flows consistent, adaptive white-box attacks with expectation over transformation, a gradient-free attack, and a targeted evasion threat in which an attacker disguises its own traffic as benign. On CIC-IDS2017 and UNSW-NB15 we compare a static Bayesian neural network, two variants of a hierarchical automatic-relevance-determination prior, Monte Carlo dropout, a deep ensemble and adversarial training. Without adversarial training, every model is evaded on 47–95% of the attack flows it detects, and its worst-case macro-F1 stays below 0.21. Hierarchical priors improve worst-case macro-F1 by about 0.05 over a static Bayesian network on UNSW-NB15, but have no measurable effect on CIC-IDS2017. Uncertainty separates attacked from clean flows with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of up to 0.86 on CIC-IDS2017, yet an attacker aware of the detector still evades it for 38–44% of attack flows, and the signal is close to uninformative on UNSW-NB15. Adversarial training is the only effective defense, but a gradient-free attack reveals 6.0% residual evasion that gradient-based attacks alone report as 0.3%, concentrated in the rarest attack classes. We release the code to support reproducible robustness evaluation of intrusion detectors.

articles.title: Neural, behavioural and neuroendocrine responses to psychosocial stress in healthy women with adverse childhood experiences: an fMRI study
articles.abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with an altered stress response, yet their neural, behavioural and neuroendocrine signatures in adults without psychopathology remain incompletely understood. We assessed responses to acute psychosocial stress in 79 healthy adult women with extreme scores on the Childhood Maltreatment Index (high ACE, n = 39; low ACE, n = 40), who completed a modified Montreal Imaging Stress Task (MIST) during functional magnetic resonance imaging, while subjective distress (SUD) and salivary cortisol were measured at four time points. Whole-brain analysis showed greater stress-related activation in the high-ACE group in the medial prefrontal cortex, bilateral superior frontal and angular gyri, supramarginal gyrus and posterior cingulate. The groups differed in reaction times during the no-stress condition (p = .034), whereas anxiety independently predicted reaction time under stress beyond maltreatment severity (β = 0.28, p = .011). The high-ACE group reported greater baseline distress (SUD1: 3.87 vs. 2.59; p = .008) and elevated cortisol 20 min post-task (p < .01), indicating delayed HPA-axis recovery rather than hyperreactivity. Resilience moderated the maltreatment–cortisol association at peak stress (β = −0.337, p = .040). These findings suggest that early adversity contributes to a latent, multimodal profile of stress vulnerability, detectable without psychopathology.

articles.title: Land Surface Temperature Responses to Land-Cover Change: Machine Learning Insights from Semi-Arid Peshawar, Pakistan
articles.abstract: Multi-epoch assessments of land surface temperature (LST) often associate thermal differences with land-use/land-cover (LULC) change without separating compositional effects from epoch-wide variations in meteorological conditions, sensors, and retrieval processing. This study examines LULC-associated summer (June–August) LST patterns in Peshawar District (≈ 1,259 km²), a semi-arid basin in northwestern Pakistan, for 2001, 2014, and 2024. Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 imagery was processed in Google Earth Engine, and LULC was classified using gradient tree boosting, achieving overall accuracies of 93–97% and kappa coefficients of 0.90–0.96. Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and LightGBM were employed to model LST using five spectral indices and elevation. Between 2001 and 2024, forest cover declined from 308 to 87 km², while built-up land expanded from 287 to 445 km². District-mean composite LST increased by 10.3°C, although comparable increases across land-cover classes, including forest (+ 8.2°C) and water (+ 6.1°C), indicate substantial epoch-wide differences. Compositional decomposition attributed less than 1°C of the district-mean difference to changing class proportions, leaving the remaining variation unresolved. Relative thermal contrasts also changed, with built-up land becoming warmer than agricultural and forest areas, particularly during 2001–2014. The three models showed similar performance under random pixel splitting (r² ≈ 0.78–0.85; RMSE ≈ 1.7–2.1°C). Predictor importance showed partial agreement but requires reassessment because of a Landsat 8 bare soil index calculation error and predictor redundancy. These findings highlight the importance of compositional decomposition and relative class contrasts when interpreting multi-epoch LST patterns.

articles.title: TTT-TP: Regularized Target Propagation for Multi-Layer Test-Time Learners
articles.abstract: Test-Time Training (TTT) layers use an online learner as recurrent state, so the learner's update rule is itself part of the sequence architecture. In TTT-MLP, the output fast layer has an explicit reconstruction target, whereas the lower fast layer has only a backpropagated gradient. We remove this asymmetry. TTT-TP maps the desired output displacement to the minimum-norm hidden displacement that approximately realizes it, through a Tikhonov-regularized inverse of the current upper fast weight, giving every fast layer an explicit local target. It retains the TTT-MLP forward architecture, upper-layer update, learned inner learning rate, parameter count, and recurrent-state size, and adds no feedback network. A transpose control recovers official TTT-MLP outputs and all fast states to numerical precision, isolating the proposed inverse as the change in lower-layer credit. On held-out episodic moving-hinge regression, TTT-TP reduces mean normalized query error from 0.4044 to 0.1899 across three seeds. On Penn Treebank and WikiText-2, compact two-layer language models match TTT-MLP test perplexity within 0.06%; the unfused reference reaches 82.6--88.7% of baseline throughput and uses 2.7% more peak allocated memory. The target interface also turns each layer's online update into an explicit erase--write Delta decomposition, restoring at the intermediate layer the same local form the output layer has always admitted. Unlike regularized target propagation used as a training algorithm, the inverse here is taken of a fast weight that is itself part of the recurrent state, and is recomputed as the sequence is read.

articles.title: Classification of Electromagnetic Side-Channel Activity in 100BASE-TX Ethernet Using a Random Forest Model
articles.abstract: Electromagnetic emissions from Ethernet cables can provide observable information about network activity without requiring direct electrical access to the communication channel. This study investigates the classification of electromagnetic side-channel activity associated with three operating conditions in a 100BASE-TX Ethernet environment: idle network activity, text-file transfer, and image-file transfer. Electromagnetic signals were captured non-invasively using a HackRF One software-defined radio and an H-field probe positioned near a Cat5e Ethernet cable. The captured complex IQ data were processed offline using overlapping windows of 65,536 samples with 50% overlap. Six signal features were extracted: mean magnitude, root mean square (RMS), standard deviation, peak magnitude, spectral centroid, and spectral bandwidth. A labelled dataset containing 857,130 observations was used to train and evaluate a Random Forest classifier. The optimized model achieved 93.25% accuracy using a stratified random train-test split, while five-fold stratified cross-validation produced a mean accuracy of 93.21%. Class-specific ROC-AUC values ranged from 0.9847 to 0.9931. A separate time-ordered evaluation of the baseline model achieved 91.66% accuracy. Feature analysis identified spectral bandwidth and spectral centroid as the two largest contributors to the optimized model's impurity-based feature importance. However, the evaluation results must be interpreted cautiously because the windows overlap and the training and testing subsets originate from the same original recordings. The study demonstrates activity classification within the collected dataset, but does not establish Ethernet frame decoding, payload reconstruction, independent-session generalization, or real-time classification.

articles.title: Influence of surface textures and DLC coatings on the tribological behaviour of additively manufactured Ti6Al4V
articles.abstract: Surface texturing and diamond-like carbon (DLC) coatings may improve the tribological performance of additively manufactured Ti6Al4V, but their combined effects under protein-containing lubrication remain unclear. This study compared directly printed and laser-machined dimples and grooves with an untextured reference, each with and without DLC coating. Reciprocating tests against transparent polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) were conducted in model synovial fluid at 37°C, with three independent specimens per configuration. Simultaneous friction measurements and in situ fluorescence microscopy evaluated friction and the relative fluorescence response of labelled albumin during sliding and static pauses. Most textured surfaces showed recovery or increases in reservoir fluorescence after running-in, with directly printed grooves exhibiting the largest relative increase. DLC-coated specimens showed less visible surface damage but higher mean friction for most configurations. The strongest reservoir fluorescence response did not coincide with the lowest friction. These findings indicate that local fluorescence, visible surface damage and friction reflect distinct aspects of tribological behaviour. Surface optimisation should therefore consider texture geometry and edge morphology alongside coating effects and lubricant redistribution.

articles.title: Simulating Ground Vibrations Induced by Hypothetical Large Scale Slope Collapse Using Unified Geomechanical and Seismic Methods
articles.abstract: This work introduces a fully deterministic, integrated multi-method framework designed to model a site-specific seismic wave propagation originating from a hypothetical future massive non-tectonic slope failure. Aimed to simulate the ground vibrations generated by a potential, abrupt ten-million-ton collapse within an open-pit mine, the framework characterizes the seismic source by coupling ground based interferometric radar monitoring with macroscopic deformation data. These datasets inform a three-dimensional stress-strain failure analysis to define representative seismic source surfaces, which subsequently drive 3D numerical modeling via the Material Point Method (MPM) to calculate the dynamic contact forces resulting from mass displacement. Next, the Spectral Element Method (SEM) is deployed to simulate mechanical wave propagation through a real geologic medium, accounting for all geometric and elastic wave effects except for intrinsic attenuation. This interconnected computational pipeline bridges large deformation geomechanics with high fidelity wave propagation; unlike existing literature that predominantly focuses on earthquake induced landslides via a SEM to MPM approach, this research introduces a novel inverse pathway (MPM to SEM) where the mining induced failure acts as the primary seismic source. By embedding complex 3D topographies, multi-layered geological interfaces, and heterogeneous lithological variations directly into the elastic model, the framework accurately captures site-specific phenomena, such as surface wave amplification, geometric spreading, and structural attenuation, up to a high frequency limit of 15 Hz. Ultimately, the model successfully quantifies localized ground motion variations in terms of peak velocity, peak acceleration, and complex waveforms across the domain, offering a robust tool for future risk assessment in nearby critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Mechanical Response to Tripping Impact and Multiphysics Coupling Analysis of the Drive Components in a High‑speed Electromagnetic Repulsion Mechanical Switch
articles.abstract: During the tripping phase, the integrated sealed electromagneticrepulsiontype fast mechanical switch is subjected to millisecondscale intense impact loads, which induce significant dynamic mechanical responses in transmission components and directly determine the operational reliability of the whole device. To address the limitation that singlephysicsfield simulation cannot fully reproduce the impactinduced mechanical behavior of the operating mechanism, this paper establishes mathematical models for the pulsedischarge circuit, transmission dynamics, and component dynamic response. A Multiphysics coupled simulation model is constructed based on COMSOL Multiphysics. Comparative simulations are carried out with respect to the material and thickness of the repulsion disc, the diameter of the lower tie rod, and the material of the insulated tie rod, to investigate the mechanicalresponse patterns of key transmission components under different structural and material conditions. A prototype is developed according to the parameter trends obtained from simulations, and a dynamicstrain testing platform is built. Strain gauges are mounted on critical stressprone crosssections of the insulated tie rod to capture the fulltimeseries dynamic stress during tripping. The engineering validity of the simulation model is verified by comparing prototype measured data against simulation outputs. The results show that adopting aerospacegrade aluminum 7075T6 for the repulsion disc can effectively suppress component impactinduced deformation. Adjustments to repulsiondisc thickness and lowertierod diameter significantly alter the mechanical response of the transmission system. Prototype tests yield a relative error of 2.9 % between simulated and measured peak stresses of the insulated tie rod, and the average error over the full time domain is below 7 %, which confirms that the presented multiphysics simulation method can effectively predict the impact mechanical behavior of physical prototypes. This work provides simulation guidance and experimental support for the structural design and engineering development of transmission components for fast mechanical switches.

articles.title: How soil anaerobic nitrogen-transformation processes and rates respond to agricultural use and management intensity in the water-level fluctuation zone of Danjiangkou reservoir?
articles.abstract: The water-level fluctuation zone of reservoirs serves as a critical hotspot for nitrogen transformation, yet the driving mechanisms of nitrogen release during initial impoundment under different cropping systems remain poorly understood. The present study investigated the effects of conventional fertilizer (MN), slow-release fertilizer (MP), and nitrification inhibitor (MQ) application on nitrogen release and transformation under varying fluctuation conditions. MP sustained soil NH4+-N release and supplied organic carbon, increasing soil organic carbon by 9.41%. This coupled carbon–nitrogen input was associated with 17.72% higher denitrification potential than conventional fertilization during early flooding. DNRA potential under MP increased by 85.71% at the mid-flooding stage relative to conventional fertilization, but declined by 81.40% relative to control group after 53 days of flooding. In contrast, MQ suppressed nitrification during early flooding, reducing soil NO3−-N by 28.09% and maintaining a high NH4+-N environment that limited denitrification and favored N retention. Hydrological regime further modulated the dominance of various nitrogen pathways. Compared with continuous flooding, drying after short-term flooding enhanced denitrification potential and suppressed DNRA relative to continuous flooding, shifting N fate from DNRA-dominated retention to denitrification-dominated gaseous loss. At the soil–water interface, MP and MQ reduced NH4+-N concentrations in overlying water by 51.06% and 51.60%, respectively. and reduced total dissolved N relative to MN. These findings show that novel fertilizers mitigate aqueous N-release risk by regulating nitrification and the competition between denitrification and DNRA, while flood–drying transitions may enhance gaseous N loss.

articles.title: A Graph Dynamics Optimizer with Lévy Diffusion and Opposition-Based Learning for Parameter Estimation of Triple-Diode Photovoltaic Models
articles.abstract: High-dimensional and multimodal optimization for estimating the parameters of advanced photovoltaic (PV) models is an unreliable task for many metaheuristics. We propose the Graph Dynamics Optimizer with L´evy Diffusion and Opposition Learning (GDO-LDOL) that embeds the population in a dynamic similarity-fitness graph, and replaces single-leader guidance with attraction to centrality-based hubs. Exploration (Laplacian diffusion with Lévy flights) and exploitation (neighbourhood message passing) are annealed over the run, supported by elitism, periodic opposition based learning and diversity restarts. The GDO-LDOL was applied on the 9, 10 and 11-parameter triple-diode (TDM), modified triple-diode (MTDM) and variable voltage-resistance triple-diode (VVR-TDM) models of R.T.C. France cell and compared with seven optimizers (PSO, APO, ARO, DO, SMA, ZOA, DOA) over 30 independent runs. It obtained the lowest minimum RMSE on all three models (7.425×10⁻⁴, 7.405×10⁻⁴ and 7.252×10⁻⁴) and the lowest mean RMSE: 19.3% lower than PSO on TDM, 8.0% lower than ARO on MTDM and 28.4% lower than PSO on VVR-TDM. The standard deviation on VVR-TDM was 2.68·10⁽⁻⁵⁾, and the maximum absolute current error of the best runs was no more than 1.41 mA. The results indicate that the graph-structured population dynamics can estimate the parameters of complex PV models accurately and stably .

articles.title: Potential distribution of Asplenium prolongatum in China and its response to future climate change
articles.abstract: Asplenium prolongatum is commonly found on forest tree trunks and moist rock surfaces. How its potential suitable area in China will respond to future climate change remains unclear. We fitted maximum entropy (MaxEnt) models to 246 occurrence records using three climate variables and two topographic variables. We evaluated the models with nested spatial cross-validation and assessed future changes using three global climate models (GCMs). Mean temperature of the coldest quarter ranked first in both percentage contribution and permutation importance. Current suitable area covers approximately 1.836 million km², mainly in humid mountains from southwestern to southeastern China; 93.4% remains suitable across all 18 future climate combinations. Under SSP5-8.5 for 2071–2100, we averaged the three continuous GCM projections before thresholding. The resulting suitable area was 15.9% larger than at present, and its area-weighted centroid shifted approximately 91 km northward. Gains were concentrated along the northern margin, with local losses in southern lowlands, coastal areas and parts of Taiwan, China. Nested spatial evaluation yielded a weighted area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.900 and a pooled omission rate of 16.7% at the maximum training sensitivity plus specificity threshold. Omission was higher for northern holdouts. The southern mountains contain most of the areas that remain suitable across climates, whereas projections along the range margins warrant field checks.

articles.title: Cu-Doped ZnIn2S4 Nanowires on Ni Foam as Bifunctional Electrocatalysts for Alkaline Water Splitting
articles.abstract: Zinc Indium Sulfide (ZnIn2S4), a promising catalyst composed of earth-abundant elements, has been extensively investigated for visible-light-driven photocatalytic applications. Its use as a standalone electrocatalyst for alkaline water splitting, however, has been comparatively less explored. This study challenges the application of ZnIn2S4 as an efficient electrocatalyst and enhances its performance by Cu doping for overall water splitting. Cu incorporation provides a systematic compositional route to modify its physicochemical and electrochemical properties for bifunctional water splitting. CuxZn1-xIn2S4 nanowires supported on Ni foam (NF) were synthesized via a hydrothermal method as a promising solution for efficient water splitting. The electrocatalyst was systematically characterized using XRD, XPS, FE-SEM, ICP, and EDX techniques and the electrochemical performance was evaluated through cyclic voltammetry (CV), linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), chronoamperometry, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Cu0.8Zn0.2In2S4 catalyst, with a molar ratio of 8:2 of Cu to Zn, demonstrated superior activity among the tested samples, with overpotentials of 95 mV for HER and 270 mV for OER, along with favorable Tafel slopes and a cell voltage of 1.62 V for overall water splitting. These findings highlight Cu0.8Zn0.2In2S4 as a promising candidate for high-performance water-splitting applications.

articles.title: A Conceptual Framework for AI Supported Representational Coordination and Transfer in Calculus
articles.abstract: Calculus learners may carry out routine procedures while struggling to connect symbolic, graphical, numerical, verbal and contextual representations, particularly in unfamiliar problems (García-García et al., 2025). Digital environments can display linked representations, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) adds a conversational interface; neither feature by itself establishes that learners coordinate the mathematical meanings across forms. This Perspective proposes a framework for designing and investigating AI-supported representational coordination in calculus. Rather than treating AI as an answer generator, it considers a bounded role for a conversational system: eliciting a learner’s interpretation, responding to the learner’s stated reasoning, and inviting the learner to test a claim across representations. The paper adapts established work on multiple representations, covariational reasoning and transfer to propose four iterative stages—notice, translate, coordinate and transfer. Its proposed contribution is an analytic chain linking (i) the learner evidence available to the system, (ii) a contingent AI move, (iii) the learner’s subsequent mathematical action and (iv) an observable outcome that can be studied. A net-change task illustrates the framework, but it has not been implemented or evaluated. The paper makes no effectiveness claims; it offers a set of design propositions and testable hypotheses for future research.

articles.title: Impact of Nanoribbon Width on the Performance of Nanoscale Interconnects: A Material-Device-Circuit Co-modelling Approach
articles.abstract: This work reports an in-depth investigation to understand the width dependence of Zig-Zag Silicon Carbide Nanoribbon (ZZ-SiC NR) interconnect performance through DFT, NEGF, and Cadence Virtuoso EDA-based material-device-circuit co-modelling approach. The investigation is performed for three stable ZZ-SiC NR widths, N = 6, 8, and 10, as identified by MD simulations. The cohesive energy investigation revealed an increase in stability with the ribbon width, attributed to the reduced edge-to-bulk ratio and quantum confinement effects. All the ZZ-SiC NRs exhibit metallic behaviour with increasing states density with the ribbon width near Fermi level. The two-probe device analysis revealed that the drive current increases with the ribbon width, which can be attributed to the availability of a large channel area and significant forward transmission pathways. The distributed parasitic elements, including quantum capacitance, increase with the ribbon width, while the kinetic inductance, magnetic inductance, and electrical resistance decrease. The driver-interconnect-load (DIL) circuit simulations reveal increased average power consumption with ribbon width, attributed to higher drive current. However, the delay and the power delay product (PDP) were found to decrease as ribbon width increased. The maximum frequency of operation (MFOO) is also found to increase with ribbon width, attributed to reduced delay. Thus, it is advised to choose a nanoribbon with a higher width possible, for greater interconnect performance. However, if the power dissipation is a major concern of the IC designer rather than delay, PDP, and MFOO, then it is advised to choose the least ribbon widths possible.

articles.title: Modeling of Physics Based UVActivated Acetone Sensor with Machine Learning Analysis
articles.abstract: Acetone in exhaled breath is a recognised marker for diabetes. However, most gallium oxide sensors need to operate at high temperatures to detect acetone. In this study, we developed a simplified computational model of a proposed UVactivated Ni/(Al0.17Ga0.83)2O3/Ga2O3 acetone sensor. The model describes how electrical current flows through the sensor, how UV light lowers the energy barrier, how acetone molecules attach to the sensor surface, how temperature affects the surface properties, and how the sensor response changes over time. We generated 2000 simulated observations to study whether acetone concentration could be predicted from the sensor’s response. Acetone concentrations ranging from 10 to 500 ppm were selected independently. Seven machine-learning methods were tested. The models were trained and tuned using nested five-fold cross validation on 1,600 observations. The remaining 400 observations were kept separate and used only for final testing. The multilayer perceptron (MLP) produced the lowest cross validation RMSE of 50.92 ± 3.94 ppm. On the final test set, it achieved an RMSE of 55.63 ppm, an MAE of 40.87 ppm, and an R2 value of 0.8475. When one wavelength was left out of the training data, the RMSE ranged from 62.71 to 95.53 ppm. When the model was used the concentrations above 400 ppm, the RMSE increased to 99.92 ppm. The results show that the physical sensor model can be combined with machine learning to estimate acetone concentration. However, the study is based only on simulated data. Experiments with a real sensor are therefore needed to confirm the findings.

articles.title: Quantum leap: Computing's next frontier takes shape
articles.abstract: After several dashed predictions, quantum computing is accelerating rapidly with actual use cases and scientific breakthroughs now expected within years, not decades.

articles.title: Theory of Anomalous Diffusion and Superdiffusion in Integrable Spin Chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrable systems can exhibit diffusive or Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) scaling in two-point correlations even when their current full counting statistics (FCS) differ from those usually associated with these universality classes. We explain this separation using a multispecies particle gas that preserves the scattering structure of integrable spin chains. For anisotropy Δ>1, large particles are advected by a mobile bath. The resulting FCS has a Gaussian-mixture form and approaches the M-Wright distribution at late times, with finite-time rounding due to mobile species. At the isotropic point Δ=1, all particles are mobile, and the charge transfer by large particles is discrete. A self-consistent Poisson distribution describes the FCS, with a nearly Gaussian bulk and model-dependent, non-Gaussian tails. By contrast, two-point correlations follow from the statistics of a large tracer particle. For Δ>1, it undergoes Brownian motion, yielding Gaussian spreading. At Δ=1, we provide evidence from fluctuating hydrodynamics for the emergence of the KPZ Prähofer--Spohn scaling function in dynamical correlations and trace it to the finite coupling of the largest particles to a continuum of slower ones, with long-ranged velocity fluctuations. Our framework shows how universal dynamical two-point correlations coexist with distinct model-dependent current statistics.

articles.title: Pairing from anti-Hund's coupling under infinite Hubbard repulsion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron-phonon coupling is a natural source of superconductivity, but in strongly correlated materials the phonon-mediated interaction is often much weaker than the on-site Hubbard repulsion U. Whether, and how, it can still produce pairing when U dominates is a basic open question. We address this question by studying a minimal model with an anti-Hund's coupling J_A: an on-site spin exchange between two orbitals or two valleys, mediated by optical phonons, that favors a local inter-orbital spin singlet. In the limit U=+infty, the two-orbital Hubbard model on the triangular lattice, doped away from the insulator at n=2 electrons per site, reduces to a four-flavor t-J_A model. Density-matrix renormalization group calculations find robust pairing throughout 1le J_A/|t|le10, with the largest pairing gap at J_Asim|t|. The Cooper pairs reside on bonds and do not come from a direct attraction provided by J_A, since infinite U excludes on-site pairs from the Hilbert space. For J_Agg|t|, the normal state is a second Fermi liquid whose small Fermi surface violates the perturbative Luttinger theorem, and a strong-coupling expansion in t/J_A provides a controlled effective theory of superconductivity from this unconventional metal. Our results provide strong evidence for a strongly coupled superconductor beyond BCS theory, driven by the interplay of the kinetic energy, the phonon-mediated anti-Hund's coupling, and the strong Hubbard U. Finally, we discuss possible applications to magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene.

articles.title: Spin-Wave Excitations in La₃Ni₂O₇: A Dynamical Mean-Field Theory and Bethe-Salpeter Equation Study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We perform a dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) + Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) study of collective spin excitations in La₃Ni₂O₇, using a bilayer two-orbital Kanamori-Hubbard model derived from density functional theory. Our DMFT calculations reveal a double spin-stripe ground state. On this basis, we apply the BSE to compute the lattice transverse spin susceptibility, which exhibits a damped spin-wave spectrum with a bandwidth of sim0.1 eV and a wave vector of (π/2, π/2), in good agreement with resonant inelastic x-ray scattering and inelastic neutron scattering data. We inspect the orbital-resolved bare susceptibility that provides insight into the momentum dependence of the spin-wave line shape. Further analysis of the irreducible vertex reveals notable frequency dependence in the dz^₂ orbital. Finally, we investigate the evolution of the spectrum with varying Hund's coupling and electron fillings. Our study bridges the localized and itinerant descriptions of spin excitations in La₃Ni₂O₇.

articles.title: Bosonic Magic Resources at Quantum Criticality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Gaussianity is a resource for bosonic quantum information processing, providing a necessary ingredient for universal quantum computation in continuous-variable systems. Here we quantify non-Gaussianity in the ground state of the one-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard model using quantum relative entropy (QRE), a measure determined solely by one-body correlations. The scaling of the QRE with system size reveals quantum phase transitions involving hidden and conventional order. We connect QRE scaling in the weakly interacting superfluid phase to Luttinger-liquid correlations and identify distinct critical signatures in its extensive and subleading contributions. At the Mott-Haldane transition, subtracting the extensive background reveals a pronounced peak in the subleading contribution, providing a clear signature of the onset of hidden string order. At the Haldane-density-wave transition, the extensive contribution to the QRE instead exhibits scaling consistent with Ising criticality. These results establish non-Gaussianity as a probe of many-body criticality, linking bosonic quantum resources to strongly correlated matter.

articles.title: On the binding and stability of CeO2 molecules on low-index Au surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many multi-phase thin films grown by self-assembly involve co-deposition of both metallic and oxide phases that grow into the same film. Under such conditions, the oxide species may be present in stoichiometric molecular form on the surface of the metallic phase. Quantifying the stability, binding, and diffusion of such molecular oxide states on metallic surfaces is critical for understanding self-assembly. In this work, we investigate the binding and stability of CeO2 molecules on Au surfaces using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. Specifically, we examine how the configuration of the CeO2 molecule, its binding energy and binding free energy, structural stability, effective charge, and projected electronic density of states vary among various binding sites on Au(001), Au(110), and Au(111) surfaces. Molecular CeO2 was found to be more favorable on all Au surfaces than its atomic constituents. It was also found that the bent CeO2 molecule configuration is more stable than the linear counterpart, with the Ce atom on the hollow site and the O atoms on the top sites. In addition, the configurations of the CeO2 molecule on Au surfaces with a binding energy around or weaker than -1 eV were found to have a low probability of existence above room temperature. Furthermore, the charge transfer was found to occur in such a way that the CeO2 molecule becomes polarized on all surfaces, but the polarization is stronger only for the strongly bonded states on Au(001) and Au(110) surfaces. Finally, three different cases of how the CeO2 molecule binds to Au(001), Au(110), and Au(111) were identified: case 1: chemisorption with symmetric bonds, case 2: chemisorption with asymmetric bonds, and case 3: physisorption with symmetric bonds. These three cases of CeO2 binding are present on Au(001) and Au(110), but only cases 2 and 3 occur on Au(111).

articles.title: Dancing dervishes, spinning skirts and whirling waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the patterns seen in the tunic of a whirling dervish or the long skirt of a Kathak dancer, we study the dynamics of a emphsoft heavy circular sheet spinning steadily around its axis. Using experiments, we show that the initially draped sheet can pass through three archetypal states as it rotates: a gravity-dominated draped rotation state, a flat state, and finally a whirling state marked by retrograde rotation of wavy patterns relative to the rotating frame. We map out these various configurations in a three-dimensional phase diagram, analyze the transitions using a minimal model, and derive scaling laws to describe the phase boundaries which we confirm using experiments.

articles.title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O₃₋δ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) offer efficient energy conversion at intermediate temperatures, but their performance is often constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics at the cathode. Triple conducting perovskite materials such as BaCoₓFe_yZr_zY₁₋ₓ₋y₋zO₃₋δ (BCFZY) have shown promise as air electrodes. In this study, we investigated the impact of Y doping on proton conductivity by decoupling the effects on proton diffusivity and proton concentration. Using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we assessed proton tracer diffusivity across three compositions: BaCo₀.₄Fe₀.₄Zr₀.₂O₃₋δ (BCFZ), BaCo₀.₄Fe₀.₄Zr₀.₁Y₀.₁O₃₋δ (BCFZY0.1) and BaCo₀.₄Fe₀.₄Y₀.₂O₃₋δ (BCFY). Thermodynamic defect models incorporating hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation reactions are employed to estimate temperature-dependent proton concentrations. Our results suggest that increasing the Y content from BCFZ to BCFY increases proton diffusivity by 1.7% at 500 ^circC. Under PCFC operating gas conditions, proton concentration and proton conductivity are predicted to increase by 3.8% and 5.3%, respectively, at 500 ^circC. These increases are modest compared with the larger enhancements reported experimentally under reducing conditions, highlighting the importance of gas conditions in evaluating the effects of Y doping. Under low oxygen partial pressure conditions, we predict that the dominant proton transport mechanism shifts from hydroxyl groups (OH_Obullet) to hydride species (H_Obullet). This work provides mechanistic insight into proton transport in BCFZY cathodes and offers design principles for optimizing proton-conducting air electrodes in next-generation PCFCs.

articles.title: Superconductivity from a Cooper surface instability in a nodal Bose metal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In underdoped cuprates, the superconducting gap is largest where low-energy electron spectral weight is already depleted above the transition. How can a weak attraction drive superconductivity when the one-electron density of states vanishes? In a momentum-space (t)--(J) model, the exactly solvable normal state is a nodal Bose metal with four one-electron nodes. Along two contours called Cooper surfaces, adding or removing a spin-singlet pair of electrons with opposite momenta costs no energy. The resulting logarithmic divergence of the pair susceptibility allows an arbitrarily weak pair-transfer attraction to stabilize a correlated nodal (d)-wave superconductor. Spin-resolved coincidence photoemission could test this pairing mechanism by resolving two zero-energy pair-removal ridges above the transition and a third along the underlying Luttinger surface below it.

articles.title: Cascading LO-phonon-mediated resonant energy transfer from excitons to Eu3+ for ultrahigh color purity red luminescence in europium-doped GaN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-efficiency, wavelength-stable red micro-LEDs with ultrahigh color purity remain a critical bottleneck for monolithic III-nitride full-color displays. Europium-doped GaN (GaN:Eu) offers a compelling solution, yet the microscopic energy transfer mechanism from the GaN host to Eu3+ ions has remained unresolved for three decades, impeding rational performance optimization. Here we report polaron-mediated resonant energy transfer in high-crystalline-quality GaN:Eu epilayers grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Eu3+ doping stabilizes a distinct bound exciton (BX3) state at 3.478 eV, which couples strongly with longitudinal optical (LO) phonons via the Frohlich interaction to form cascading polarons with up to seven phonon replicas at a uniform energy spacing of 92.0+/-0.7 meV. The BX3 polaron coupled with 5LO phonons matches precisely the 7F0-->5D3 intra-4f transition energy of Eu3+ at 3.019 eV. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence reveals non-equilibrium phonon emission, evidencing directional resonant energy transfer. After rapid nonradiative relaxation from the 5D3 excited state to the 5D0 metastable state, the hypersensitive 5D0-->7F2 transition yields sharp 622 nm red emission. Time-resolved spectroscopy confirms a single dominant Eu3+ luminescent site with reduced local symmetry, attributed to off-axis EuGa-VN complexes. This work identifies a key energy transfer channel and provides a clear framework for designing high-efficiency GaN:Eu red emitter.

articles.title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of λ-(STF)₂GaCl₄
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-energy electronic structures of λ-(BETS)₂GaCl₄ and λ-(STF)₂GaCl₄ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For λ-(STF)₂GaCl₄, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 Å² for BETS and 37.578 Å² for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of td₁ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.

articles.title: Frustration in system with intercalated and bilayer smectic structure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dimeric mesogens exhibit an unusual variety of mesophases - nematic and smectic, with distinctly different packing schemes. The relation between molecular and mesophase structure was studied for homologue series of non-symmetric bent dimers CBO6.Om, obtained by serial Pd- and Pt-catalyzed cross-coupling chemical reactions. The shorter homologues of the series form smectics with an intercalated structure, and longer homologues form bilayer smectics with broken up-down symmetry of molecular orientation within the layers, for intermediate homologues frustration leads to a nematic gap. The additional structure complexity arises from the tendency of bent dimers to form twisted structures, in which the azimuthal angle of tilted molecules forms both short- and long-pitch helices. Here we confirm, through resonant X-ray diffraction, that longer homologues form a helical four-layer structure of SmCTB-SH phase, along with a more complex one in which, in addition to the basic four-layer unit, an extra helix is superimposed, SmCTB-DH phase. This additional helix has a periodicity that is strongly temperature-dependent; upon cooling, it changes from 100 nm to 40 nm.

articles.title: Nontrivial criticality and weakly first-order transitions in the frustrated spin-1 chain with single-ion anisotropy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frustrated spin chains host exotic phases beyond the Landau paradigm, yet weak first-order transitions and unconventional criticalities remain elusive. Combining large-scale density-matrix renormalization group with bosonization methods, we map the phase diagram of a spin-1 chain with next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) coupling and single-ion anisotropy (SIA). We pinpoint two topological phase transitions: a weakly first-order transition between the Haldane and NNN-Haldane phases with a tiny gap and a continuous transition from the Haldane phase to the large-D phase located via level spectroscopy with Richardson extrapolation. For negative SIA, a spontaneous dimerized phase emerges between the Néel and NNN-Néel phases. Its transition into the Néel phase is a deconfined quantum critical point falling into the eight-vertex universality class, with central charge c = 1 and critical exponents varying continuously along the phase boundary. For positive SIA, we identify two vector-spin-chirality orders---an ordinary chiral phase and a narrow Haldane-chiral phase---with a weakly first-order transition between them, evidenced by a soft jump in the string order parameter. Our results reveal that frustration and anisotropy generate emergent orders and non-Landau criticalities, providing a platform for deconfined and topological phase transitions.

articles.title: Hidden f-wave TIVC and Quantum Phase Transitions in Metallic States of Twisted Bilayer Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the ground state phase diagram of twisted bilayer graphene at magic angle as function of carrier density and the Coulomb interaction. The carrier density is varied between the fillings ν=-2 and ν=-3 and the Coulomb interaction is tuned by changing the gate distance. Our results reveal that the well established Kramers intervalley coherent (KIVC) phase near ν=-2, contains a hidden f-wave time-reversal symmetric intervalley coherent (TIVC) order, whose strength gradually increases within the metallic regime of the intervalley coherent (IVC) phase away from ν=-2. This finding is interesting in the light of a recent experimental work [26], where the signatures of the TIVC phase has been reported in ultra-clean samples. We further show that the system goes through multiple phase transitions as the carrier density is tuned. Near the ν=-2, the IVC phase is the ground state, which gives way to valley polarized phase through a second-order-like phase transition as the carrier density is lowered. Further tuning of density pushes the system into the quantum anomalous Hall phase through gradual development of the sublattice polarization. These phase transitions are accompanied by major reconstructions of the Fermi contours.

articles.title: Fractional Chern Insulator in a Finite-Range One-Band Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A common route for realizing fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) is to engineer bands that mimic the physics of Landau levels, which serve as the single-particle topological background for the emergence of strongly correlated fractional quantum Hall states. Here we show that FCIs can also arise in a one-band model devoid of any single-particle quantum geometry. Through a systematic trivialization of the single-particle quantum geometry in FCI models that go beyond the Landau-level paradigm, we construct a single-band, interaction-only model on the square lattice, with all terms confined to individual plaquettes. At one-third filling, exact diagonalization and density-matrix renormalization-group calculations reveal a three-state low-energy manifold, a Hall conductance of -2e²/(3h), and fractional charge pumping without translation-symmetry breaking. We trace this behavior to nontrivial topology in the repulsive two-particle sector, offering a microscopic perspective on the strongly correlated origin of fractional quantum Hall order.

articles.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manipulating a physical system at the single-quantum level typically requires an anharmonic energy spectrum. Nanomechanical resonators, however, are commonly admitted to be linear objects in the single-phonon regime, thus motivating most efforts to employ external sources of nonlinearity at the cost of added relaxation and decoherence channels. Here, we take a radically different approach by directly exploiting strong intrinsic mechanical nonlinearities. We quantify this nonlinearity using a novel method based on the coupling between bending modes. Using this technique, we establish an upper bound of 34.0 +/- 9.7 phonons for the onset of intrinsically mechanical bistability. In addition, we highlight a new tuning mechanism based on a mechanical polarization angle of an upward-buckled nanotube resonator allowing us to reach an optimal working point. Extrapolating this level of intrinsic nonlinearity to realistically shorter resonators shows that the single-phonon Kerr regime is within reach, allowing for the realization of purely mechanical Schrödinger-cat states and highly coherent mechanical qubits.

articles.title: Electronic topological modes in hexagonal NbSi₂ with a double helix
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral systems can host nontrivial topological states, including characteristic edge modes and Fermi arcs. Here, we investigate the electronic properties of hexagonal NbSi₂ with chiral symmetry using first-principles calculations for both bulk and slab geometries. We find that spin--orbit coupling (SOC) is relatively weak. Notably, the topological edge state originates from structural chirality rather than the SOC. From the Berry curvature analysis, we confirm the existence of Weyl points, some of which carry a Chern number of ± 2. Furthermore, we demonstrate the existence of chiral edge modes with extended Fermi arcs around high-symmetry points. Finally, we investigate the real-space localization using spatially resolved and site-dependent density of states (DOS). We demonstrate that the surface states can be exclusively associated with the chiral Si chains.

articles.title: Spin-Orbit Coupling in Symmetry-Forbidden Reactions: A Selection Rule Tested on the Chalcogen Trimers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A reaction is forbidden by orbital symmetry when an occupied and an empty orbital of different symmetry change places along its path. With spin-orbit coupling orbitals become spinors, and those of two such orbitals can mix only if the orbitals differ by the symmetry of a rotation; the operator component of that symmetry couples ground state and diradical triplet. We test this rule on the ring opening of the chalcogen trimers O3 to Po3, where an in-plane and an out-of-plane orbital cross (C₂ᵥ surfaces; NEVPT2, spin-orbit configuration interaction), by letting the operator components act separately. In Se3 and Te3 the component named by the rule alone lowers the barrier by 2.2 and 5.1 kcal/mol (complete operator: 2.2 and 5.2), the other two by 0.2 and 1.3 kcal/mol; in Po3 they contribute in second order. The triplet crosses the ground state 6.5 to 9.0 kcal/mol below the forbidden saddle. Spin-orbit coupling makes this crossing passable in O3 and S3 and, from Se3 on, merges the two states into one surface whose saddle lies 2.6, 5.5, and 13.1 kcal/mol lower. Molecular rotation obeys the same rule but is 6 to 2.8× 10³ times weaker, which bears on the lifetime predicted for cyclic ozone.

articles.title: A Thermodynamically Consistent Model of a Rechargeable Salt-in-Polyelectrolyte Battery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an isothermal, thermodynamically consistent model of a salt-in-polyelectrolyte battery with intercalation and deintercalation reactions of cations occurring at the electrode-electrolyte interfaces under galvanostatic conditions. For the electrolyte, we consider polyelectrolytes, which are polyanions, with neutralizing cations (i.e., counterions) such as lithium, along with a monovalent salt containing the same cations. Models of batteries containing either a dual-ion-conductor (DIC) electrolyte (i.e., uncharged polymers with added salt) or a single-ion-conductor (SIC) electrolyte (i.e., charged polymers without added salt) emerge as limiting cases of this thermodynamically consistent model. Once the model is presented in its most general context, we make specific choices so that it captures well-known mechanisms. In particular, the governing diffusion equations recover Fick's law of diffusion, and the cation-transfer reaction rate is described by the Butler--Volmer equation. The DIC and SIC limiting cases provide a framework for comparing the corresponding batteries. One-dimensional DIC and SIC charge--discharge simulations at matched current and duration illustrate concentration redistribution, polarization, and electrode utilization. Numerical accuracy checks quantify sensitivity to discretization; distinct initial inventories qualify the comparison.

articles.title: Signatures of multiorbital density waves in the electronic Raman response of bilayer nickelates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent Raman scattering experiments on bilayer nickelates have revealed pronounced spectral features in the spin-density-wave state, whose microscopic origin remains controversial, with interpretations ranging from two-magnon excitations to electronic transitions across SDW-induced gaps. Here, we demonstrate that the multiorbital electronic structure of low-pressure bilayer nickelates naturally generates distinct orbital-selective Raman signatures in different symmetry channels. Using a two-orbital bilayer model incorporating the d₃z^₂₋ᵣ^₂ and dₓ^₂₋y^₂ orbitals in the orthorhombic structure, we analyze the electronic Raman response of the multiorbital spin-spinless double stripe SDW state and show that the B₂g response exhibits a peak at the energy scale (Mz^₂+Mₓ^₂)/2, associated with SDW gap openings in weakly hybridized bands. In contrast, the dominant peak in the B₁g channel emerges at the multiorbital energy scale (Mz^₂²+Mₓ^₂²)¹/², reflecting the strongly hybridized character of the relevant electronic states. These distinct energy scales provide a unified interpretation of several Raman signatures observed in La₃Ni₂O₇ and offer a means of disentangling the orbital contributions to the SDW order parameters. Our results highlight that in contrast to the superconducting state, Raman peak positions in the SDW state cannot generally be identified with a single SDW gap and establish symmetry-resolved electronic Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of multiorbital density-wave order.
authors: Luis G. G. V. Dias da Silva

articles.title: AFM metrology for 3D high aspect ratio semiconductor structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transistors have long been the foundation of the semiconductor industry, with continuous architectural innovations enabling the scaling of integrated circuits while maintaining high performance. Advancements in deposition and lithographic techniques have further expanded design possibilities, while increasing structural complexity demands stricter process control. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) offers a rapid and reliable metrology solution, providing high-resolution measurements and robust statistical analysis of critical parameters. In this work, we present clearly resolved individual profiles of lines and spaces in high aspect ratio (HAR) gate all around FET (GAAFET)-type structures on both the nanosheet (NS) region and in the isolation region between the nanosheets and we present a comprehensive statistical evaluation of their critical dimensions.

articles.title: Frozen Phonons on Dense q-Grids Using Set Covers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phonon dynamics determine a vast number of properties in the solid state, such as the heat capacity, thermal expansion, and thermal conductivity. Phonons are obtained through the dynamical matrix, which, in the frozen phonon approach, is calculated as a finite difference derivative of the analytical Hellmann-Feynman force. This approach unfortunately typically suffers from requiring very large supercells, even for modest q-grids. The non-diagonal supercell method remedies this issue by determining the smallest supercell commensurate with a given q-point, drastically reducing the supercell size, but in turn requiring a new supercell for each q-point on the grid. This introduces redundancy, however, since a single non-diagonal supercell may be commensurate with several q-points. In this work I present a method to determine a minimal set of supercells, such that every q-point on the grid is commensurate with at least one supercell. I present an algorithm to solve the problem and prove that it yields the optimal solution, before summarizing the algorithm using pseudocode. The scaling of the number of supercells with the density of the grid is discussed. Numerical results on a variety of systems show the significant computational advantage of the method, which increases with the density of the grid.

articles.title: Measuring a buried Bi₂Te₃ epitaxial film through a protective Te cap: an exact three-layer terahertz analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Air-sensitive chalcogenide films are routinely protected by a capping layer, which must then be removed, or contacted through, before electronic transport can be measured, destroying the surface the cap was meant to preserve. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy requires neither, but using it quantitatively demands a transmission model in which cap, film and substrate are treated on an equal footing. We formulate the cap/film/substrate problem exactly using a transfer matrix with a time-gated substrate, and show that the intuitive construction in which each thin layer contributes an independent Fabry--Pérot factor fails for two adjacent thin films. In the thin-film limit we obtain a closed-form inversion together with a criterion for the error incurred by ignoring the cap. We apply the framework to Bi₂Te₃ films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs at three thicknesses, each prepared with and without a 25 nm Te cap. A Te-on-GaAs witness shows the cap to be optically indistinguishable from bare substrate, transmitting 1.00(4) of the substrate amplitude between 0.2 and 1.5 THz, which limits the error from neglecting it to 3.6 % for the 90 nm film, although the same estimate reaches 48 % at 25 nm. In this matched set, the capped films form an ordered series, monotonic in thickness in both conductance magnitude and lineshape, whereas the uncapped films do not. The capping layer therefore presents no obstacle to terahertz characterization, and in this set it coincides with a more reproducible film response.

articles.title: Spin Loop Currents and Bulk-Edge Structure in Correlated Topological States of WSe₂/MoTe₂ Bilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by recent experiments, we theoretically investigate AB-stacked WSe₂/MoTe₂ bilayers. Our theory incorporates valence fluctuations, local and extended (longer-range) Hubbard interactions, including non-local interactions between carriers on the MoTe₂ layer. Within the parton mean-field framework, we show that the non-local interaction between MoTe₂ carriers can drive a transition between a topological Kondo semimetal(TKSM) and a topological Kondo insulator(TKI) at the filling fraction ν =2. We attribute this transition to an emergent spin-loop current arising from the interplay between Ising spin-orbit coupling and non-local electron correlations. In addition, we investigate how the emergent spin-loop current affects edge transport and show that the two-point conductance takes a quantized value at certain bias voltages.

articles.title: Brightening spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons through rhombohedral stacking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brightened symmetry-forbidden excitons can provide critical information about the electronic structure and many-body interactions in semiconductors. Recently, interlayer atomic registry has emerged as a new way to control atomically thin layered materials in both ground and excited states. Here we show that the rhombohedral stacking in a 3R-MoS₂ homobilayer can brighten two symmetry-forbidden interlayer excitons: one is a spin-unlike 1s exciton and the other is a parity-odd 2p exciton. The nature of these interlayer excitons is revealed by their gfactors as well as the hybridization patterns observed when they are tuned to resonate with intralayer excitons. Surprisingly, the hybridized 2p exciton exhibits a constructive quantum interference between the acquired transition dipoles, revealing a hidden gauge-invariant phase contrast between the constituent electronic states. Our results establish stacking control as a powerful approach for modulating quantum phases of excitons in 2D semiconductors.

articles.title: Moiré-induced self-trapping in a Bose-Einstein Condensate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effect of moiré modulations on two-dimensional materials flattens their electronic energy bands, which enhances the effects of interactions and has been seen to give rise to several emergent electronic phases. We demonstrate this behavior with a moiré modulation extends to a quasiperiodic hopping model of interacting bosons on the honeycomb lattice. Without interactions, the velocity vanishes at a magic-angle transition, where a sharp onset of the zero-energy density of states and multifractal low-energy states appear. Including interactions, we study its interplay with quasiperiodicity by tuning the scale associated with self-trapping and diffusive wave packet dynamics. Near the magic-angle, we find that substantially weaker interactions lead to self-trapping and diffusive wavepacket dynamics, which we attribute to the vanishing moiré-induced minibandwidth. A new computational approach is presented that combines split-step time evolution with a truncated Chebyshev expansion as an efficient and general purpose approach to solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the absence of translational symmetry. We discuss how our results can be explored in ultracold atom experiments using momentum space lattices or tweezer arrays.

articles.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store verified predictions, with evidence, outcome and error, as episodes and recall them without retraining. MatRecall improved median performance by 62% over a memory-free model, exceeded specialized models on 11 tasks, remained useful after feedback stopped and transferred between related tasks. Verified experience could become a reusable resource for self-improving discovery loops.

articles.title: Chiral Domain-Wall Modes in Topological Adaptive Quantum Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum dynamical systems driven by both unitary evolution and measurements open a new landscape of nonequilibrium phases of matter. The role of topology in enriching this landscape remains less understood than that of entanglement and symmetry. A particularly interesting question concerns protected dynamical modes localized on spacetime domain walls between topologically distinct dynamical phases. These dynamical topological domain-wall modes (DTDMs) are well understood only for 0+1D walls in 1+1D fermionic dynamics. In this work, we study 1+1D topological domain walls in 2+1D charge-conserving free-fermion dynamics, modeled by topological adaptive circuits that steer the two sides of each wall toward a Chern insulator and a trivial insulator through measurements and feedforward corrections. Although the circuits target no particular wall state, each wall hosts 1+1D chiral DTDMs. At long times in each quantum trajectory, they exhibit logarithmic scaling of entanglement and charge variance and algebraically decaying density correlations, surprisingly consistent with the ground state of a 1+1D chiral free-fermion conformal field theory. This contrasts with purely 1+1D charge-conserving free-fermion dynamics, which exhibits only area-law entanglement at finite measurement rates. We also show that the chiral DTDMs exhibit slow purification dynamics. When the system starts from a maximally mixed state, the DTDMs' entropy decays algebraically, accompanied by a vanishing Lyapunov gap, whereas each domain purifies on an O(1) timescale. Finally, we propose a physical picture for the long-time behavior of the DTDMs by treating the adaptive circuit model as a quantum cooling algorithm. Our results show that topological phases of adaptive dynamics can protect chiral modes on spacetime domain walls against repeated wavefunction collapse and Born-rule randomness.

articles.title: Anomalous scaling of coalescence in a Hele-Shaw cell
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33348v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the merging of two drops between two narrowly spaced plates, a so-called Hele-Shaw cell. For this, we solve the Hele-Shaw equations in two dimensions, driven by surface tension, focusing on early times after initial reconnection. Combining numerical simulations with theory, we show that the coalescence dynamics are self-similar at early times, with the size of the contact region between the drops growing as t³/¹³. We find this power law using a matched asymptotic analysis, which reveals a complex geometry consisting of a small bubble that gets entrained between the drops as they come together. These predictions match perfectly to our simulations, and agree with the most recent experimental data.

articles.title: Identifying Renormalization Group Interfaces of Massless WZW Flows widehatmathfraksu(2)ₖ → widehatmathfraksu(2)₁
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A renormalization-group interface encodes how a flow relates operators at short and long distances. We identify this interface up to topological dressing for the conjectured massless widehatmathfraksu(2)ₖ → widehatmathfraksu(2)₁ Wess-Zumino-Witten flows at every odd level k≥ 3. Global SU(2) symmetry requires the interface to preserve a diagonal current algebra at level k+1, built from the currents on its two sides. The Z₂ center symmetry then selects which representation labels the interface. This identification predicts distinct patterns of low-lying interface excitations for flows to the same infrared fixed point. Spin-chain calculations reproduce these patterns for k=3 and 5, providing independent evidence for both conjectured flows.

articles.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubits, while cross junctions provide routing functionality and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin qubit parameters, we evaluate logical error rates as a function of code distance and estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is required to achieve logical error rates below 10⁻¹⁰ per syndrome cycle. We further analyze wiring constraints based on CMOS-compatible multiplexed control schemes and show that, with optimized wiring efficiency, more than 120,000 logical qubits could be integrated on a 100 mm × 100 mm chip. These results provide a practical roadmap toward large-scale FTQC based on silicon spin qubit technology.

articles.title: Transport Layer-Driven Optimization of Color and Efficiency in TADF OLEDs for Large-Area Applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Balancing structural simplicity with high efficiency is crucial for practical applications of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), especially in large-area lighting devices. Optimizing the charge-transport layers in multilayer OLEDs controls the recombination zone within the emissive layer, thereby enhancing the device's performance. Herein, we experimentally and computationally investigate how the thicknesses of the electron and hole transport layers affect the performance of orange-red thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) OLEDs. Using a TADF emitter, 2-[4-(diphenylamino)phenyl]-10,10-dioxide-9H-thioxanthen-9-one (TXO-TPA), at 10 wt% concentration in 4,4-Bis(N-carbazolyl)-1,1-biphenyl (CBP) host, we achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency (ηEQE) of 20.86% and a peak luminance of 32,800 cd m⁻².
