Using a combination of drift-diffusion and optical simulations, we reveal how variations in hole- and electron-transport-layer thicknesses modulate the charge-carrier balance and shift the recombination zone within the emissive layer. This tuning not only optimizes exciton formation but also enables color tuning from green to red without altering the emissive material. Our findings highlight the critical role of transport layer engineering in achieving efficient, color-controlled OLEDs with simplified architectures. Furthermore, we successfully demonstrate a large-area OLED device (~20 cm²), achieving an impressive ηEQE of 17%, underscoring the scalability and practicality of our approach for general lighting applications.

articles.title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the two-dimensional (2D) Gross-Pitaevskii model for a Bose gas, the naive dimensional non-equilibrium wave-turbulence power-law prediction for the direct energy cascade coincides with thermal equilibrium and therefore carries no energy flux. We resolve this degeneracy by deriving a logarithmically corrected spectrum that supports a positive, constant energy flux toward small scales. A systematic asymptotic expansion of the wave-kinetic collision integral determines the logarithmic exponent to be 1/3, while the small-scale dissipation scale sets the upper cutoff in the logarithmic correction. Regularization of a marginal infrared divergence at the forcing scale yields an estimate of the spectral prefactor for asymptotically well-separated forcing and dissipation scales. Simulations of the Gross-Pitaevskii and wave-kinetic equations support the predicted spectral shape. Over finite spectral ranges, the correction produces apparent power laws steeper than the dimensional prediction, offering a possible explanation for the steep spectra observed in 2D Bose gas experiments. Our approach provides a systematic framework for constructing wave turbulent cascade spectra when the power-law prediction is degenerate with thermodynamic equilibrium.

articles.title: Discrete truncated Wigner approximation of the quantum phase transition in the transverse-field Ising model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The discrete truncated Wigner approximation (DTWA) has been a workhorse for large-scale spin dynamics, but whether it captures dynamics across a quantum phase transition has not been tested systematically. In this work, we use the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) to study the quantum phase transition with DTWA from one to three dimensions and with all-to-all connectivity, using slow linear ramps and fast ramps. We find that DTWA cannot capture the dynamics on the one-dimensional chain, and that its behavior is consistent with classical thermalization, in which its classical spins relax toward a thermal state at a finite effective temperature that does not vanish for slow ramps, while a one-dimensional chain cannot order at any finite temperature. For square and cubic lattices, in contrast to the chain, DTWA builds order, and the order sets in close to the quantum critical point found by quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). However, its correlations do not grow with the Kibble-Zurek exponents, so DTWA captures the onset of order but not the universal dynamics of the transition. For all-to-all coupling, DTWA follows the exact growth of the order parameter along the entire ramp. Our results suggest that DTWA becomes more reliable as each spin interacts with more partners, and that beyond one dimension it can indicate where a quantum phase transition lies but cannot capture its critical scaling.

articles.title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. Uphill diffusion allows us to test this model out of equilibrium, and also test a generalized Darken relation for predicting diffusivities. We derive an analytic theory and compare to three-component molecular dynamics simulations and find very good agreement. This provides a novel out-of-equilibrium test of the generalization of our diffusion model to arbitrary multi-component mixtures.

articles.title: Distribution of the ratio of the two smallest eigenphases of the Jacobi unitary ensemble
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N⁻⁴). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the Nₑff⁻¹ term vanishes, leaving an O(Nₑff⁻²) correction.

articles.title: Rényi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute vacuum tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer Rényi index n≥2, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine multi-entropy therefore approaches twice its strictly adjacent value. The CFT predictions agree with lattice calculations for the critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain. We also exhibit a unitary CFT in which the canonical replica construction yields complex Rényi multi-entropy.

articles.title: Transition Path Sampling for Rare Events in Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rare transitions govern the dynamics of many open quantum systems, but their probabilities and rates are difficult to calculate. Transition path sampling (TPS) of quantum systems has so far been limited to Markovian, perturbative descriptions. Here, we formulate TPS for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion, which is exact for Gaussian baths, extending it to non-Markovian and strongly coupled open quantum systems. For normal-to-superradiant tunneling in the unbalanced open Dicke model, we determine probabilities down to 10⁻⁸ and rates beyond the reach of brute force.

articles.title: Quartet currents in a biased three-terminal diffusive Josephson junction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2307.06839v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Biasing a three-terminal Josephson junction (TTJ) with symmetrical voltages 0,V,-V leads to new kinds of DC currents, namely quartet Josephson currents and phase-dependent multiple Andreev reflection (MAR) currents. We study these currents in a system where a normal diffusive metallic node N is connected to three terminals S₀,₁,₂ by barriers of arbitrary transparency. We use the quantum circuit theory to calculate the current in each terminal, including decoherence. In addition to the stationary combination ϕ_Q=ϕ₁+ϕ₂-2ϕ₀ of the terminal phases ϕᵢ, the bias voltage V appears as a new and unusual control variable for a DC Josephson current. A general feature is the sign changes of the current-phase characteristics, manifesting in minima of the quartet ``critical current". Those sign changes can be triggered by the voltage, by the junction transparency or by decoherence. We study the possible separation of quartet currents from MAR currents in different regimes of parameters, including an "funnel" regime with very asymmetric couplings to S₀,₁,₂. In the regime of low transparency and asymetric couplings, we provide an analytic perturbative expression for the currents which shows an excellent agreement with the full numerical results.

articles.title: Predicted high-Tᵣₘ c superconductivity above 130 K in metastable cubic MH₄ compounds at ambient pressure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.04222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hydrides have long been considered promising candidates for achieving room-temperature superconductivity; however, the extremely high pressures typically required for high critical temperatures remain a major challenge in experiment. Here, we use high-throughput first-principles calculations to propose a class of high-Tᵣₘ c ambient-pressure superconductors with MH4 stoichiometry. These hydrogen-based compounds adopt the bcc PtHg4 structure type, in which hydrogen atoms occupy the one-quarter body-diagonal sites of metal lattices, with the metal atoms acting as chemical templates for hydrogen assembly. Through comprehensive first-principles calculations, we identify three promising superconductors, PtH4, AuH4 and PdH4, with superconducting critical temperatures of 84 K, 89 K, and 133 K, respectively, all surpassing the liquid-nitrogen temperature threshold of 77 K. The remarkable superconducting properties originate from strong electron-phonon coupling associated with hydrogen vibrations, which in turn arise from phonon softening in the mid-frequency range. Moreover, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that PtH4 remains kinetic stable at 300 K over 20 ps, with no atomic diffusion observed.

articles.title: Electron Spin Pumping by Thermal Radiation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.06411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This Letter demonstrates that thermal radiation can pump angular momentum into the spins of itinerant electrons across a vacuum gap, without spatial spin transport or net charge flow. In a monolayer transition metal dichalcogenide radiatively coupled to a thermal emitter, Rashba spin-orbit coupling enables spin-selective transitions between helical conduction bands. Two distinct mechanisms are identified: chiral spin pumping mediated by interference between polarization components of thermal radiation from a nonreciprocal emitter, and nonchiral spin pumping arising from Zeeman-induced asymmetry between opposing spin-flip transitions driven by nonchiral thermal fluctuations.

articles.title: 1/f frequency noise in mechanical resonators scales inversely with volume, not with quality factor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.16668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mechanical frequency-shift sensors have never reached the resolution their thermomechanical or quantum limits predict: a 1/f frequency-noise floor keeps them 1-4 orders short of it. Across the published record, the product of the floor's flicker coefficient h₋₁ and the strain-weighted resonator volume, Vε, is size-independent over 13 decades. It is also independent of measured Q; I find that Q-volume covariance underlies reported Q-dependence. It is defect density that imposes the frequency-noise floor: prestress can dilute it, but only in fixed-end devices. Mass resolution follows as |δ m|proptosqrtV.

articles.title: A General Algorithm for Minimal Uncoupled Stress--Strain Calculations of Elastic Constants
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.11733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We have developed a general algorithm for constructing the minimum number of strain configurations required to extract second-order elastic constants from first-principles stress-strain calculations without algebraic coupling between the constants targeted for extraction. The method operates on the sparsity structure of the symmetry-reduced elastic stiffness matrix, represented by an auxiliary binary matrix, and generates admissible strain patterns algorithmically rather than prescribing separate strain sets for individual crystal symmetries. Each independent elastic constant is obtained from a single stress component, while additional stress relations generated by the same deformation provide internal consistency checks. Because the six-dimensional strain space contains only 2⁶-1=63 non-empty strain patterns, the minimality of the resulting sets can be verified exactly for every elastic-symmetry type considered. The construction reproduces established high-efficiency strain sets in cases where they are minimal and yields improved sets for symmetry classes in which previously tabulated schemes require additional configurations. Because the formulation is based on stress-strain derivatives, it can also be readily extended to finite temperatures using consistently sampled ensemble-averaged thermodynamic stresses. Explicit strain sets are derived for all elastic-symmetry types spanning the 230 crystallographic space groups, and their accuracy and computational efficiency are benchmarked against established approaches.

articles.title: In Situ Thermal Preparation by CO2-Laser and Chemical Characterization of Oxide Substrates Across Multiple Crystallographic Orientations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Atomically flat and chemically controlled oxide substrate surfaces are essential for high-quality epitaxial growth of complex materials and heterostructures. Previous studies have demonstrated in situ thermal preparation of selected oxide substrates, primarily focusing on conventional low-index orientations such as SrTiO₃ (100) and LaAlO₃ (100). Here, we extend these methodologies to a broader range of oxide substrates and crystallographic orientations, including challenging polar surfaces. We present a systematic study of the in situ thermal preparation of SrTiO₃ (100), SrTiO₃ (111), GdScO₃ (110), LaAlO₃ (111), (LaAlO₃)₀.₃(Sr₂AlTaO₆)₀.₇ (001), and NdGaO₃ (110) single crystal substrates. The substrates are annealed in a vacuum chamber under a controlled oxygen background environment using a CO₂ laser heating system. The optimized annealing conditions produce atomically flat step-and-terrace structures, long-range surface crystallinity, and effectively clean surfaces across all the investigated substrates. Our results establish a versatile, reproducible, and broadly applicable platform for the in situ preparation of oxide substrates immediately prior to epitaxial growth. These results also provide practical guidelines for interface engineering and surface-sensitive investigations of complex materials.

articles.title: Renormalization for Robust Memory without Synchronization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40651v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Local error correction can preserve classical information against noise, but protection under synchronized updates need not survive when sites evolve at independent random times. Establishing stability is particularly challenging when protection relies on the collective action of competing local rules. Here we develop a spacetime renormalization framework that reveals how independently acting local updates can collectively stabilize memory. We identify sufficient conditions under which the geometry of stable interfaces and suppression of defect propagation produce reliable erosion at large scales. Applying this framework, we prove the stability of the asynchronous R squeezing code and introduce robust processes in two and three dimensions. In these systems, both encoded phases persist under sufficiently weak noise, even when the noise favors one phase. Our results provide a criterion for designing autonomous memories sustained by competing local stochastic dynamics.

articles.title: Reflected entropy and Markov gap in Lifshitz theories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2307.12247v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the reflected entropy in (1+1)--dimensional Lifshitz field theory whose groundstate is described by a quantum mechanical model. Starting from tripartite Lifshitz groundstates, both critical and gapped, we derive explicit formulas for the Rényi reflected entropies reduced to two adjacent or disjoint intervals, directly in the continuum. We show that the reflected entropy in Lifshitz theory does not satisfy monotonicity, in contrast to what is observed for free relativistic fields. We analytically compute the full reflected entanglement spectrum for two disjoint intervals, finding a discrete set of eigenvalues which is that of a thermal density matrix. Furthermore, we investigate the Markov gap, defined as the difference between reflected entropy and mutual information, and find it to be universal and nonvanishing, signaling irreducible tripartite entanglement in Lifshitz groundstates. We also obtain analytical results for the reflected entropies and the Markov gap in 2 + 1 dimensions. Finally, as a byproduct of our results on reflected entropy, we provide exact formulas for two other entanglement-related quantities, namely the computable cross-norm negativity and the operator entanglement entropy.

articles.title: Ultrasensitive, universal single-ion nanodetector
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.00406v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, a carbon nanotube (CNT) based single-ion detector is proposed and its performance is evaluated with atomistic quantum transport models. The sensor can detect any ion type without molecule-specific functionalization and allows for continuous real-time ion monitoring. A single ion temporarily changes the operating principle of the sensor's CNT field-effect transistor into a resonant tunneling diode. The concrete device example of this paper showed a source-drain current increase of 5 orders of magnitude induced by a single ion.

articles.title: Dressed Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: Opening and Closing a Pandora's box
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dressed time-dependent density functional theory (DTDDFT) has been shown to overcome the inability of adiabatic TDDFT to describe excitation energies and oscillator strengths of double-excitation character, however, it is far from being a black-box method. Here, we outline and address several operational issues while benchmarking the approach on a range of molecules. We define a protocol to determine whether an excitation from adiabatic TDDFT needs a double-excitation correction, without requiring a priori knowledge of the state, and which Kohn-Sham states to build the frequency-dependent DTDDFT matrix from. We present an 'undownfolding' that replaces this frequency-dependent matrix by a linear frequency-independent one in a larger space, eliminating ambiguities in the iterative procedure required to diagonalize the former. We compare the performance of DTDDFT for both excitation energies and oscillator strengths, as measured by an approximate metric for their single-excitation character, for different choices of the underlying adiabatic density functional approximation, with and without employing the Tamm-Dancoff approximation, for molecular excitations predicted by wavefunction methods to have either partial or genuine double-excitation character. We propose a correction to DTDDFT to account for missing dynamical correlation that is removed in the truncation procedure inherent in the method, and discuss the possibility of unphysical imaginary frequencies reminiscent of the 'triplet instability' that may arise. We provide benchmark data for butadiene, hexatriene, octatetraene, cyclopentadiene, acrolein, naphthalene, ethylene, borole, and cyclopentadienone. In some cases, DTDDFT predicts frequencies with about as much accuracy as the same underlying adiabatic TDDFT predicts for the constituent and near-lying single excitations.

articles.title: Basin-Scale Nonlinear Dynamics of Thermohaline Ocean Circulation. Part I: Theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth's thermohaline ocean circulation may support multiple equilibria and abrupt transitions. Similar bifurcation structures for different ocean models suggest common underlying dynamics across the model hierarchy. Here we propose a unifying framework from tracer conservation, in which surface fluxes are balanced by dissipative and advective tracer transport. We express this flux balance through a large-scale tracer gradient and a transport efficiency that measures how strongly circulation displaces the tracer field from its no-flow "conductive" state. The flux balance quantifies the transport contributions that sustain each circulation state and give rise to abrupt transitions. In a three-dimensional ocean-basin model, we find nonlinear salinity advection dominates the collapse threshold and linear dissipation dominates the recovery threshold. Temperature has additional dissipation from surface restoring, making thermal fluxes more dissipation-dominated than salinity fluxes. The tracer contrasts and boundary layers that a given circulation generates produce distinct transport regimes, approximately quadratic in circulation strength for weak flow and linear for strong flow. With a simple circulation closure, the flux balance reduces to longstanding box-model bifurcation results for the weak and strong flow regimes. Thus, by expressing thermohaline bifurcations through basin-scale transport, this framework connects box-model insight to the continuous equations. Furthermore, as this framework exposes the transport processes that balance a changing forcing, it provides constraints on a thermohaline ocean state and its trend toward tipping that overturning strength alone does not. In Part II, we develop flux-balance closures to forecast such tipping points.

articles.title: Physics-Based TCAD Modeling of Nanowire Cryotrons with Coupled Superconducting and Thermal Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanowire cryotrons (nTrons) provide gate-controlled superconducting switching, current gain, and high-impedance outputs for cryogenic computing, detector readout, and superconductor-semiconductor interfaces. We develop a physics-based Sentaurus TCAD framework that couples time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau dynamics, separate electron and phonon energy equations, and mixed-mode circuit simulation. Superconducting terminal-current corrections connect the custom solver to the native electrical solution, linking local suppression of superconductivity, heating and cooling, and current redistribution in the external circuit. To our knowledge, this is the first Sentaurus-based mixed-mode TCAD implementation for nTrons. We calibrate the model against experimental switching data at six gate currents using a single parameter set. The model achieves an RMS load-current error below 1 μA outside the switching region and switching-current differences of about 1 μA or less. Simulations show that a center gate gives the highest switching sensitivity, while a drain-side gate gives the largest post-switch resistance. Narrower channels switch at lower currents and exhibit higher resistance. Transient and bidirectional bias sweeps capture electrothermal hysteresis, gate-controlled switching latency, and bias-controlled recovery. Simultaneous activation of three gates lowers the switching threshold from about 104 μA with all gates inactive to about 12 μA, demonstrating cooperative suppression of superconductivity. The framework supports the design of nTron geometries, operating conditions, and multi-input architectures.

articles.title: APEX: Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensemble-based methods provide a practical framework for history matching, prediction, and optimization of subsurface models. In methodological studies, however, performance is rarely assessed from a single run. Comparisons typically span cases, configurations, and random seeds, while each evaluation may require an expensive external simulator. Keeping such studies computationally bounded, auditable, and reproducible therefore requires more than implementing a numerical method: experiments must be validated before execution, computational costs estimated, repeated runs organized consistently, and configurations and outputs made traceable. To address these needs, we developed APEX (Agentic Platform for Ensemble eXploration), an open-source Python platform that provides a common framework for configuring, validating, executing, recording, and comparing ensemble-based experiments. APEX is organized around three concepts: an experiment defines what is executed, a run records a single execution, and a study coordinates and compares multiple experiments or runs. Experiments are specified through validated configurations, which can also be generated by a planner agent. Before execution, APEX estimates the maximum number of forward simulations required. If the estimate exceeds a user-defined threshold, submission is held for approval. Each run records provenance information, while studies repeat problems across variants and paired replicates and compare results using paired statistical analyses. Scientific and computational components, including methods, simulators, metrics, and optimizers, are implemented as plugins. A command line interface, Python client, REST service with a web interface, and tools for language model agents access these capabilities through a common service layer.

articles.title: Statistical analysis of crossing beam speckle fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on the statistical analysis of single beam speckles, this paper develops a statistical description of speckle fields formed by crossing laser beams. A formal definition of individual speckles and their domains allows us to quantify the effective size and abundance of speckles. For two crossing beams, the effective speckle size is derived from the local curvature of the intensity field, and the expected speckle abundance is found asymptotically with the Kac-Rice formula. Monte Carlo simulations of speckle abundance show excellent agreement with the theoretical abundance formula. The two beam speckle analysis is then applied to a symmetric quad beam configuration motivated by polarization smoothing and demonstrates that increasing the separation between beams reduces expected stimulated Brillouin scattering reflectivity from saturated speckles. The statistical model is then extended to an arbitrary number of beams using a coordinate free formulation to obtain the spectral density of laser driven electron density fluctuations.

articles.title: Development of a low-level radio frequency system for remote in situ superconducting radio frequency cavity measurements and calibrations in conduction-cooling systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We developed a low-level radio frequency (LLRF) system for superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavity measurements in a conduction-cooling system. A voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) was used in a phase-locked loop (PLL) to track the frequencies of SRF cavity modes. ttPython-based software developed in-house controlled and monitored the system. By introducing an additional circulator and associated components, we developed an LLRF system enabling fully remote in situ SRF cavity measurements for the first time. This design also enables remote in situ calibrations. Hence, our LLRF system improves safety through fully remote operation and enhances measurement precision through in situ calibrations, with safety always taking priority. These calibrations are important for measurements in conduction-cooling systems because temperature stability and uniformity in these systems are poorer than those in convection-cooling systems using costly liquid helium and can vary over time and with environmental conditions.

articles.title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme II: multi-frequency radiation transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional discrete ordinate methods are widely used for thermal radiative transfer, but their fixed number of angular degrees of freedom (DoFs) incurs unnecessary computational cost near equilibrium. We therefore develop a nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme (NCUGKS) for multi-frequency radiation transport. The scheme preserves the mul tiscale capability of UGKS through interface evolution that couples transport and collision. Radiation intensity is expanded in an orthonormal basis of the discrete angular space. The expansion coefficients serve as angular DoFs, with their number adapted independently to local nonequilibrium in each cell, frequency group, and quadrant. At each time step, the coefficients to be evolved are selected using the exponentially decayed contribution from the previous step and the requirements of interface transport. The selected coefficients are advanced by the finite volume scheme and corrected to match the macroscopic radiation energy before higher-degree coefficients are discarded according to the prescribed relative tail tolerance. Therefore, in the optically thick limit, the resulting representation retains only one angular DoF per quadrant. Numerical tests spanning different optical regimes show close agreement with reference solutions, validating its accuracy. Furthermore, in terms of memory and computational efficiency, the proposed method reduces memory by factors from 21.7 to 154.0 and achieves speedups from 24.87 to 257.9 compared with the original discrete ordinate UGKS. NCUGKS thus provides the ability to accurately simulate multiscale ra diative transfer with reduced memory and computational costs. The proposed approach also offers a framework for adapting angular degrees of freedom in other discrete ordinate methods.

articles.title: Carrier relaxation confines the Bogdanov--Takens degeneracy of an optically injected semiconductor laser
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optically injected semiconductor lasers are forced nonlinear oscillators whose locking boundaries are organized by codimension-two points. We ask which property of the carrier balance permits or forbids a Bogdanov--Takens (BT) point in the standard three-dimensional rate equations. Taking the carrier inversion n as distinguished observable, the rate that enters the spectral conditions is the slope of the gain--loss balance, ξ=partialdot n/partial n=-2Γ/κ, where Γ is the damping of the relaxation oscillation and κ=1+2Bn the normalized stimulated-emission factor. The two BT conditions become affine in ξ and imply the exact sum rule K²=I[1-(1+κ)I] between injection amplitude K and intracavity intensity I. The product of the two relaxation eigenvalues that survive at a saddle-node is bounded below by 1-16Γ², so that no BT point exists for Γ<1/4, whatever B, the linewidth enhancement factor, the injection strength and the detuning; below this barrier every contact between Hopf and saddle-node curves is a fold--Hopf point. For B=0 the barrier is completed to an exact existence criterion. We prove that the unfolding of a BT point by injection strength and detuning is transversal if and only if two explicit curves cross transversally in the plane of locked states; for B=0 this is a simple root of an explicit function, and transversality fails exactly at the existence threshold. Two BT points at Γ=1/2, α=2 are verified to be generic, and the contacts between Hopf and saddle-node curves are classified into fold--Hopf, BT and nilpotent triple-zero points.

articles.title: Remote and Noncontact Acceleration and Suppression of Heat Convection on Object Surfaces using Intensity-Adjusted Acoustic Streaming
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The temperature of objects in an environment is often controlled by accelerating or suppressing heat convection. Conventional methods generally involve insulation for heat retention and forced convection for cooling. However, there is no practical method for remotely and target-selectively controlling heat convection in objects in room environments. In this study, we demonstrated that intensity-adjusted acoustic streaming (ultrasound-driven airflow) can both suppress natural convection and induce forced convection on the surface of a heat source. The direct acceleration and deceleration of air over the object surface were induced by an ultrasonic beam with high temporal and spatial resolution. The experiment showed that it is possible to switch between insulating and cooling by adjusting the ultrasonic output intensity, and that it is essential for heat retention to prevent heat from escaping from the object surface by convection using acoustic streaming. We consider these results to lead to the realization of a situation where virtual heat-retaining blankets or cooling fans that are customized for specific objects in the environment can be ubiquitously attached to them, opening the door to applications such as temperature control of food and beverages and remote control of temperature profiles in manufacturing processes and laboratory settings.

articles.title: Existence of single-resonance parametric bound states in the continuum: System of Schrödinger equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is an eigenmode of a linear wave system with its eigen-frequency embedded in the radiation continuum of scattering states. At the frequency of a BIC, scattering problems with given incident waves from infinity lose uniqueness. Due to their close connection with strong resonance effects, BICs have found many useful applications in classical and quantum wave systems. Existence theories of BICs have been established for some cases involving the so-called symmetry-protected BICs, Friedrich-Wintgen BICs, and Fabry-Perot BICs. The single-resonance parametric BICs (srp-BICs) are another important class of BICs. Such a BIC emerges from a single resonant state through tuning a real parameter. Using a simple system of two one-dimensional Schrödinger equations, we demonstrate the formation of srp-BICs and establish a rigorous existence theory.

articles.title: TyxonQ: A Workflow Layer for Quantum Computing in Chemistry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computational chemistry is often framed around a hybrid quantum solver. In practical applications, however, bottlenecks to adoption also lie in the surrounding multiscale workflow. A molecular problem may combine classical molecular mechanics and dynamics, conventional electronic-structure calculations, and a quantum solver for selected orbitals or embedded fragments. This division of work is particularly relevant when a chemically important electronic subspace is strongly correlated. The size of the electronic Hilbert space and the qubit, noise, and circuit-depth constraints of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices make active-space and embedding choices central to a feasible quantum calculation. The resulting energies and gradients must remain consistent with the surrounding classical simulation. We present TyxonQ, a workflow layer that connects these levels of treatment rather than addressing only the hybrid quantum algorithm. Four integration interfaces link PySCF-compatible energy/force scanners and embedding, solver adapters, simulator and hardware backends, and classical consumers. The implementation combines QM/MM and fragment embedding with conventional CCSD/FCI fragment solvers, variational and sampling-based quantum methods, and adapters for ASE, i-PI, OpenMM, LAMMPS (through i-PI), and MDI. We describe the contracts and audit coverage, and evaluate correctness, switching cost, reproducibility, and artifact portability on small chemistry workflows, distinguishing executed paths from source-level support. The purpose of TyxonQ is to support incremental integration of quantum calculations into existing computational chemistry workflows, including those used in industry, while retaining appropriate classical treatments elsewhere.

articles.title: Dopamine: A Cartesian grid large-eddy-simulation framework for coastal ocean modelling of free-surface waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a Cartesian staggered-grid large-eddy simulation framework for modelling coastal ocean waves using the Dopamine solver. The framework combines a geometric volume-of-fluid method for simulating free-surface wave evolution with one-way-coupled Lagrangian point-particle tracking for heavy and buoyant particles. A ghost-cell immersed-boundary method represents stationary solid boundaries, including the seabed and coastal obstacles, and their interaction with free-surface waves. The framework includes the Vreman and anisotropic minimum-dissipation (AMD) sub-grid-scale models for simulating near-wall turbulence. Comparisons with analytical solutions and established experimental and numerical benchmarks illustrate the framework's ability to reproduce wave dynamics and particle motion. The results provide promising insights into the framework's capabilities for coastal ocean modelling applications focused on investigating small-scale turbulent physics using a low-numerical-dissipation approach. The solver runs on multi-CPU architectures, with two-fluid strong- and weak-scaling efficiencies at 512 ranks relative to 64 ranks of up to 77% and 73%, respectively, and a single-GPGPU build has been verified against the CPU solver.

articles.title: Pseudospin-mediated broadband hypersonic phonon transport beyond localized Berry curvature
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phononic nanostructures offer compact and highly confined control of elastic waves for signal transport, filtering, and quantum transduction. More recently, topological phononic structures have been explored as a route to robust waveguiding around defects and sharp bends, offering a promising basis for scalable and reliable phononic circuitry. However, how robust transport can persist as conventional localized Berry-curvature signatures diminish with increasing structural perturbation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate bend-resilient hypersonic phonon transport beyond the conventional valley Hall framework. Using an engineered propeller phononic crystal operating at 1.9 GHz, we continuously increase the geometric perturbation to gradually weaken the valley topology while enhancing modal pseudospin character. Strikingly, as the Berry curvature progressively delocalizes from valleys, the complete elastic bandgap broadens to a normalized width of 34% and the interface modes become more strongly confined. Two-port electromechanical measurements on a thin-film lithium niobate-on-SOI platform experimentally confirm broadband interface-mode transport with no measurable bend-induced loss, despite the absence of well-localized valley-topology signatures. Our findings establish modal pseudospin engineering as a powerful design principle for robust acoustic guiding beyond conventional topological constraints, paving the way for broadband hypersonic phononic circuitry for classical and quantum information processing.

articles.title: Fourier-Transform Photothermal Spectroscopy with Transient-Lens Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate Fourier-transform photothermal spectroscopy using broadband supercontinuum excitation and transient-lens detection. The output of a Ti:sapphire oscillator is broadened in a photonic crystal fiber to generate the supercontinuum pump, which is converted into a phase-stable pulse pair with a controllable femtosecond delay using a birefringent interferometer. The absorption-induced heating from the pump generates a transient thermal lens in the sample, which is detected as a function of delay by an off-resonant 800 nm photothermal probe beam. Fourier transform of the interferometric photothermal response yields a frequency-domain signal corresponding to the sample absorptance spectrum weighted by the pump spectrum. After division by the measured pump spectrum, the reconstructed photothermal spectrum is compared with a direct frequency-domain linear absorption measurement to evaluate the accuracy of the reconstruction. This method combines Fourier-transform broadband excitation with thermal-lens readout, allowing broadband linear absorption spectra to be obtained from pump-induced refractive-index changes rather than from transmitted excitation intensity. We demonstrate the method on phloxine B.

articles.title: Numerical model for ice formation in soil samples
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ice formation, or in general liquid crystallization, in porous media is important in various engineering contexts ranging from frost heave in soils to structural damage due to salt crystallization. Developing mesoscopic models for this problem is challenging due to the multitude of phenomena involved - fluid flow, phase transitions and complex porous geometries. In this work, we present an efficient numerical implementation addressing this class of problems. We use a phase field model with a non-conserved order parameter for liquid crystallization and solve it in a Lattice-Boltzmann framework. Our modifications to the phase field model enable the direct capture of important thermodynamic phenomena such as the Gibbs-Thomson effect and Soil Freezing Characteristic Curve (SFCC). We demonstrate our model's capabilities in sphere packings as well as in realistic soil geometries. Our model is able to resolve the pore-scale freezing and capture the macroscopic freezing behavior such as the hysteresis observed during freezing and thawing.

articles.title: Unveiling gauge-invariant on-chip phases from light intensity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed digital twins fitted to output powers increasingly program photonic processors, but these powers do not fix the implemented phase, which determines how light from different inputs interferes. Here we show that a twin trained on intensities alone predicts the gauge-invariant phase of programmed transformations, and that this prediction can be used to program the phase. On a 12×12 mesh, with phases measured by interference protocols formed by the mesh itself, intensity-only and phase-aware programs from random starts reach the same intensity fidelity but phase fidelities of 0.690 and 0.996, both as predicted by the twin. The prediction holds for blocks up to 10×10. With coherent inputs, the programmed phase determines the outputs: phase-aware programming reduces the direction-of-arrival error of an on-chip Butler matrix from 29 degrees to 2.0 degrees. Power measurements alone thus yield a phase-calibrated model of the mesh, without phase data in training or optics beyond the chip.

articles.title: A Monolithic Fully Eulerian Lattice Boltzmann Framework for Fluid--Structure Interaction with Neo-Hookean Elastic Solids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a fully Eulerian, monolithic lattice Boltzmann method for fluid--structure interaction with incompressible neo-Hookean solids at unequal densities, and use it to compute the Turek--Hron FSI2 and FSI3 benchmarks on a single Cartesian grid. A pressure-based kinetic scheme advances the mixture momentum, a polynomial MTHINC reconstruction transports the solid volume fraction with closed-form fluxes, and the left Cauchy--Green tensor gives the elastic stress; all updates are explicit and local. Because the density is transported independently of the populations, two corrections are introduced. A lattice-link correction makes uniform translation an exact discrete solution for any density ratio, which is verified to round-off up to ρₛ/ρ_f=1000. A pressure-mode correction, derived from an asymptotic analysis of the scheme, removes the frame-dependent defect that otherwise causes a secular drift of the solid mass. The verification separates the two sources of error: the scheme is second-order accurate towards the diffuse-interface solution at fixed interface thickness, and first-order towards the sharp-interface solution when the thickness scales with the grid, as predicted by an estimate of the interfacial truncation error. The method reproduces a deformable disk in Taylor--Green and lid-driven-cavity flows, and the FSI3 and FSI2 benchmarks at density ratios of one and ten.

articles.title: Site-Resolved Optical Spectroscopy of Thulium in Solid Argon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We utilize the high resolution of the ground state transition {}²F₇/₂ ↔ {}²F₅/₂ in thulium atoms isolated in solid argon to perform excitation-emission spectroscopy. Decomposition of the excitation-emission spectrum reveals 6 absorption-emission profiles, which are attributed to multiple trapping sites in the host matrix. Comparison with vacuum transition energies shows large matrix-induced shifts for srightarrowp transitions, whereas f → d transitions remain close to their free-atom energies. A single site exhibiting strong emission at 560nm is investigated and a three-photon excitation pathway is determined as a possible origin of the high energy 560nm light. Additionally, for long-lived levels belonging to the f¹²d configuration, narrow, crystal-field split absorption lines are identified. Matrix effects are important for establishing the mechanism behind the observed spectra and long f¹²d lifetimes.

articles.title: CLM-JAX v3.2.46: a differentiable, GPU-accelerated land surface model numerically indistinguishable from the Community Land Model 5.0
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The original Fortran implementation of the Community Land Model version 5.0 (CLM5.0) primarily targets CPUs and does not support GPU computation or automatic differentiation. We present CLM-JAX, a land surface model implemented in Python, based on the CLM5.0 BGC-Crop configuration in the Community Earth System Model version 2.1.3 (CESM2.1.3). CLM-JAX retains the original subgrid hierarchy, parameterizations and coupling among energy, water, carbon, nitrogen and crop processes, runs on CPUs and GPUs, and supports gradient backpropagation through multi-step time integration. Using floating-point perturbations of order 10⁻¹⁴ in the initial state, we construct a stringent ensemble baseline of CLM's own differences and evaluate the numerical consistency of CLM-JAX for 32 variables over five years of continuous global simulation during 2019-2023. CLM-JAX errors relative to CLM generally lie below this ensemble baseline. On a single NVIDIA A800 GPU, CLM-JAX requires 0.7692 s per model hour, yielding sustained integration speedups of 4.04 and 2.57 over CLM compiled with gfortran and ifort, respectively, on 64 CPU cores. In the gradient test, the objective function is the first-layer soil temperature at step 100 (50 h), and its gradient with respect to the initial soil temperature field of all model layers is obtained by backpropagation through the 100 time steps. With converged central finite differences as references, 95.79% of the 84,254 nonzero references have relative errors no greater than 1% and 98.22% have matching signs, with median and 90th-percentile relative errors of 5.862×10⁻⁷% and 3.578×10⁻⁴%, respectively. The differentiability of CLM-JAX provides a basis for gradient-based applications, such as end-to-end parameter optimization and four-dimensional variational data assimilation.

articles.title: Tunable Terahertz Bandpass Filter based on the Photonic Emulation of a 2DEG Interferometer through the Geometric Phase of Light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Terahertz frequencies are expected to become a key player in next-generation wireless communications. For this transition to occur seamlessly, tunable bandpass filters for channel selection are essential. However, conventional Fabry-Pérot cavity-based bandpass filters face inherent limitations. Specifically, their tunability is restricted by physical constraints, such as the maximum achievable mirror separation. In this work, drawing inspiration from electronic interferometers, we demonstrate a continuously tunable bandpass filter operating near 0.3 THz by exploiting the geometric phase of light, the Pancharatnam-Berry phase. Our device incorporates intracavity waveplates for polarization control and is described by a mathematical expression analogous to that of the electronic interferometer governed by the Aharonov-Bohm phase, thereby realizing a photonic analogue. Using custom-designed subwavelength waveplates and cavity mirrors, we achieve a finesse of Fapprox17, a quality factor of Qapprox1.5×10³, and a resonance linewidth of Δ fFWHMapprox 200 MHz. Beyond terahertz communication technology, this system is expected to find applications in fields requiring high frequency resolution, such as spectroscopy.

articles.title: Schrödinger's Legacy: The Wave Function and Quantum Reality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article discusses how Schrödinger arrived at the formulation of wave mechanics and his legacy on the philosophy of quantum mechanics, focusing in particular on the metaphysics of the wave function. Schrödinger's interpretation of the wave function as electron charge density is generally dismissed or presented only as a curious historical example in the literature. On a closer look, however, while this interpretation was eventually abandoned in favor of Born's statistical interpretation, Schrödinger's idea survived in modern realist approaches to the wave function, such as the mass-density approach and the multi-field interpretation. It also proved to be of great utility in modern techniques and approximations in quantum chemistry to compute the shape of atoms and molecules. Overall, Schrödinger's interpretation of the wave function and his realist understanding of quantum mechanics paved the way to modern attempts to define a clear ontology of the microscopic world, a tradition that survived the Copenhagen interpretation of Bohr and Heisenberg and that is still present today.

articles.title: Voltage-Enhanced Photorefractive Hysteresis in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Photonic-Crystal Cavities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We observe voltage-enhanced photorefractive hysteresis in thin-film lithium niobate nanocavities, causing the resonance to appear at different wavelengths during increasing- and decreasing-wavelength laser scans. Their separation grows with bias magnitude and optical power, but depends weakly on scan speed over 1-200 nm/s. A quasi-static surface-trap model links voltage-biased carrier transport to asymmetric trapping, whose space-charge field shifts the resonance through the Pockels effect. The model captures this hysteresis across three cavities through switching between stable steady states. Space-charge feedback opposes further carrier separation, limiting the hysteresis gap. The model informs photorefractive mitigation and resonance control in integrated electro-optic devices.

articles.title: A novel quantum lattice Boltzmann methodology for cosmological radiation transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiation transport is an essential process in many physical simulations, including cosmological codes which track stellar and diffuse radiation. Many present codes utilize ray tracing or moment methods, but these grow increasingly difficult and expensive for large simulations. Quantum lattice Boltzmann methods exponentially reduce complexity by propagating radiation over a lattice, allowing for better spatial resolution without needing to introduce adaptive ray tracing or other optimizations. However, existing formulations result in poor angular resolution for radiation point sources. In this work, we propose an angular redistribution methodology which significantly improves the resolution with minimal increase in complexity. We verify the correctness of the method on both classical processors and quantum simulators and outline how the quantum algorithm can be integrated into existing codes. This method is an important step towards fully-quantum radiation hydrodynamics simulation which could exponentially accelerate existing cosmological codes, enabling simulations at scales currently infeasible.

articles.title: Point vortex dynamics influenced by the surface motion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a coupled system of differential equations, which models the dynamics of fluid with a free surface and a point vortex in the body of the fluid. For long surface waves of small amplitude, the effects of the interaction between the waves and the point vortex are modeled within the framework of the Boussinesq regime. It turns out that the solitary waves on the surface are not destroyed by the interaction with the vortex, and, as a matter of fact, the solitary waves remain practically unaffected for a significant range of the vortex strength. As a result, a further simplification of the model is proposed, where the vortex motion under solitons propagating on the surface is determined from a system of decoupled ordinary differential equations.

articles.title: Quantum Noise-Limited Terahertz Interferometry for Distinguishing Ultra-Compact Supermassive Galactic Objects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33488v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The images of the galactic centers, M87^* and Sgr~A^*, obtained by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) provide hitherto unknown revelations on these supermassive objects. The key issue here is the presence or otherwise of an event horizon at these ultra-compact entities. We show here that distinguishing the central images generated by gravitational lensing of a Schwarzschild black hole and a Joshi--Malafarina--Narayan (JMN-1) central naked singularity provides important insights into the nature of these supermassive objects and would help test the cosmic censorship conjecture, central to black hole physics. For optically thin spherical accretion onto Sgr~A^*, their interferometric visibilities become separable, independently of the emission model, on three baseline ranges within 1.4--6.2 Gλ at errors of simeq36,μJy, and at L_star=2.64,Gλ at simeq71,μJy. This is about 28 times below the 2017 Event Horizon Telescope statistical uncertainty. We suggest that the widest detection window demands minutes-long coherent integrations, favoring a near-quantum-limited space interferometer.

articles.title: On-Demand Tailoring of High-Dimensional Orbital Angular Momentum States via a Phase-Only Hologram
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) provides a naturally discrete and unbounded Hilbert space for high-dimensional encoding and has emerged as a powerful degree of freedom for advanced information processing. On-demand tailoring of both the amplitude and phase profiles of high-dimensional OAM states is essential for numerous applications, particularly in quantum information science. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate an efficient method for achieving such on-demand tailoring using a purely phase-only modulation scheme. The measured fidelity remains above 80% even for a 128-dimensional state, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Compared with previous techniques, our method achieves significantly higher generation efficiency, and this advantage becomes more pronounced as the dimensionality increases. Moreover, our approach substantially reduces experimental complexity while maintaining precise control, thereby offering a practical and scalable solution for high-dimensional OAM state engineering in both classical and quantum information processing.

articles.title: When Malus' Law Meets the Wigner-Bell Inequality: Violation by Nonseparable Classical Light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bell-type inequalities are commonly associated with quantum nonlocality, yet their mathematical structure also reflects more general constraints on the joint probability distributions assigned to measurements performed in different contexts. Here we examine this distinction through the Wigner--Bell inequality using a classical optical field with two nonseparable degrees of freedom. Starting from a subsystem response-factorization assumption, we derive a Wigner-type probability bound requiring the pairwise measurement statistics to be compatible with a single nonnegative global joint distribution. For a classically nonseparable optical field, the corresponding joint probabilities are represented directly by normalized joint intensities and obey Malus' law. We show that these Malus-law probabilities violate the Wigner--Bell bound over a finite range of analyzer settings. The violation does not imply spatial nonlocality or a failure of classical electrodynamics. Rather, it demonstrates the incompatibility of context-dependent optical projection statistics with the global probability assignment underlying the Wigner construction. We further derive an extended Wigner-Bell bound for general imperfect correlations and propose an interferometric experiment for reconstructing the required joint probabilities from intensity measurements. These results provide a transparent optical realization of the probabilistic structure behind Bell-type inequalities and help distinguish consequences of Hilbert-space structure, nonseparability, and measurement context from those specifically associated with quantum nonlocality.

articles.title: A bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs based on beam-like Type-II SPDC
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bright sources of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs are increasingly required for the rapid advancement of quantum technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high brightness and high-dimensional spatial entanglement through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs using beam-like Type-II SPDC in a β-barium borate crystal. Compared with a conventional collinear Type-I source, it exhibits a sim1.56-fold enhancement in the detected single-photon count rate and a sim1.45-fold enhancement in the coincidence count rate. Measurements of position correlations and momentum anti-correlations certify at least 62-dimensional spatial entanglement within a 121-dimensional basis. These correlations are further exploited to demonstrate quantum imaging in both the position and momentum domains. These characteristics make the source a practical resource for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies.

articles.title: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: If the phase of a photon-number state is completely undetermined, how can single photons, sent one at a time through a two-slit apparatus, build up interference fringes? These lecture notes answer this question from first principles. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we expand the field in vector modes, quantize it, and introduce the quantity measured by a photodetector. We then show that the word ``phase'' refers to two different things: the phase of a mode, fixed by the optical setup, and the phase of the quantum state that excites the mode. Only the first determines the fringes. All calculations are given in full, and problems with solutions are included.

articles.title: Comprehensive In Situ Characterization of Amorphous Solid Water Films with COSPINU2 set-up: Optical Properties, Density, Morphology, and Restructuring Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34577v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Amorphous solid water (ASW) dominates interstellar ice mantles, but its porosity, density, optical response, and mechanical stability depend sensitively on how the ice is grown. Here, we present the characterization capabilities of COSPINU2, a cryogenic ultra-high-vacuum set-up designed to prepare and diagnose water ice films under controlled background and doser-assisted deposition conditions. The instrument combines a calibrated gas-handling line, near- and mid-infrared Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, HeNe interferometry, broad-beam optical imaging, and quadrupole mass spectrometry. We demonstrate how these complementary diagnostics provide a coherent description of ASW films grown between 10K and 150K. For background-grown ices, a dual-angle interferometric method is used to retrieve refractive indices near 632 nm, while near-infrared interference fringes provide thickness calibration. The results show that lower deposition temperatures and higher growth rates produce films with lower refractive indices and stronger dangling-OH infrared signatures, consistent with the formation of more porous ASW. We also show that pressure-based density estimates are unreliable in the background geometry because cryopumping decouple chamber pressure from the local substrate flux. For doser-grown films, optical interference imaging allows reconstruction of dome-shaped thickness profiles and estimation of effective densities. Finally, sudden restructuring events are observed in thick (above 2 micrometers), low-temperature porous ASW films, evidenced by abrupt changes in interferometric contrast, optical scattering, and dangling-OH features. These results establish COSPINU2 as a versatile platform for quantitative water-ice characterization and provide the physical baseline required for future studies of infrared irradiation and optical constants of interstellar ice analogues.

articles.title: Quartz Crystal Microbalance impedance of discrete adsorbates with lubricated contact
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present theoretical investigation of the shear force exerted on a horizontal plate undergoing fast (MHz range) longitudinal oscillations in presence of a spherical particle suspended in the liquid at close proximity to the plate. This hydrodynamic problem is relevant toward the analysis of frequency response (i.e., complex impedance) of Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) to discrete (particulate) adsorbates. For low areal density of adsorbates, the contributions of individual particles remain additive, rendering the theory applicable towards quantitative interpretation of the experimental measurements. For adsorbates much smaller than the viscous penetration depth, the closed-form analytical expressions for the complex impedance were derived for particles of arbitrary density, assuming a lubricated contact (i.e., non-localized adsorption). The theoretical predictions were shown to be in an excellent agreement with accurate Finite Element numerical computations. The validity of the theoretical approach was confirmed by QCM measurements conducted for polystyrene nanoparticles in a broad range of sizes, from 32 nm to 510 nm, adsorbing onto gold/silica sensor upon varying the oscillation frequency.

articles.title: Beyond the Federer paradox in tennis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03702v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Roger Federer won about 80% of his professional matches with only 54% of the points. Hierarchical scoring amplifies small advantages on points into large advantages on matches, but also allows a player to win with fewer points than the opponent. Using Monte Carlo simulations and exact Markov chain calculations, we show that in tennis, badminton, volleyball and table tennis this amplification is set almost entirely by the number of points per match. We then let a player win ordinary points with probability p1 and crucial points, those closing a game, set or match, with probability p2. In every sport a narrow region of the (p1, p2) plane exists where a player wins most matches with fewer than half of the points, because crucial points carry more influence than their share of points. Of ATP matches played in 1991-2025, 4.7% were won with fewer points, 16% more than independent points predict (5% including the serve), a constant excess. Pressure performance measured in other seasons predicts match outcomes beyond the points won, and Fabio Fognini won 51% of his matches with 49% of the points, in what we call the Fognini paradox.

articles.title: Interaction-Free Polarimetry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2207.13539v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The combination of interaction-free measurement and the quantum Zeno effect has been shown to both increase the signal-to-noise ratio of imaging, and reduce the energy absorbed by the imaged object. So far, however, it has not been used for quantitative polarimetry, the reconstruction of a sample's Mueller matrix. In this paper, we extend this to the polarimetry of diattenuating samples. For polarisation components that the sample strongly absorbs, the protocol identifies the sample with far less absorbed energy than a single-pass measurement, a benefit for delicate samples probed with high-frequency radiation. For weakly absorbing components the repeated passes through the sample absorb more, so the benefit is confined to strongly diattenuating features. A Fisher-information analysis shows that, for a sample with a lossless transmitting axis, the protocol locates the absorbing axis with far fewer absorbed photons than single-pass polarimetry, while it measures partial transmittances no more efficiently per absorbed photon, and that the same sorting of lossy components to one output port responds to retardance and depolarisation.

articles.title: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symbolic regression seeks to discover interpretable governing equations for dynamical systems from data. In systems biology, however, accurately reproducing system trajectories does not necessarily imply recovery of the underlying reaction mechanisms. Existing benchmarks evaluate numerical accuracy, expression complexity, or equation-level similarity, but not agreement between recovered reactions and reference mechanisms in biological systems. We introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems with reaction annotations spanning mass action, Michaelis--Menten, Hill, and complex kinetics. Trajectory fidelity is evaluated across all systems under in-distribution reconstruction and out-of-distribution (OOD) extrapolation, while mechanism recovery is assessed on the subset of 161 systems. We evaluate trajectory fidelity across 11 symbolic-discovery methods and assess mechanism recovery for three reaction-based methods. Joint analysis across systems highlights how severely trajectory-based evaluation overestimates true mechanism recovery. Motivated by these findings, we develop KineSelect, a framework that searches candidate reaction topologies under biologically grounded kinetic laws to select optimal mechanisms that balance trajectory fidelity with structural parsimony. Compared with the strongest baseline, KineSelect improves aggregate OOD extrapolation (R²) by 19.2% and overall reaction F1 score by 14.3%.

articles.title: Adaptive Reliability Reserves for Residential Battery Fleets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a Houston 2024 replay, replacing a fixed 20 percent battery reserve with a county-risk threshold raises observed five-hour backup coverage from 75.0 percent to 86.5 percent and adds USD 10.2 in modeled annualized margin per home (paired 95 percent interval: USD +1.7 to USD +21.7). The paired coverage-gain interval includes zero. This is a conditional simulation result, not measured company reliability. Residential batteries face this tradeoff because market discharge consumes energy also needed for household outages. We release HomeFleet-ERCOT, combining observed prices and county outages with identified simulated homes and causal controller inputs. We compare independent-home optimization with 21 proximal policy optimization (PPO) training runs; ten promise-cost candidates span 31.1 percent-96.3 percent backup coverage. Of these, 10 have lower modeled margin than fixed 20 percent, and 3 also have lower coverage. Chronological, geographic, fleet, and storm tests examine transfer. An alert charging override has a conditional energy-and-power sufficiency guarantee, but only 19.5 percent of 41 county mass-outage episodes provide enough continuous warning for every battery preset. Synthetic tests include short, missed, and false warnings, load uplift, capacity loss, and dropout. A static AC audit retains existing feeder violations; aging comparisons expose model sensitivity. The released benchmark, controllers, and checkpoints provide a reproducible basis for comparing these tradeoffs. This work supports the design of residential battery programs that assess market value and household backup service together.

articles.title: Generalizable Equivariant Diffusion Models for Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: Analytical Foundations and Numerical Scaling Tests
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03530v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gauge-equivariant diffusion models can be used to generate ensembles of field configurations in non-abelian lattice gauge theories. Previously, we demonstrated the feasibility of modeling these theories by combining L-CNN-based diffusion models with the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA). Here we focus on the underlying analytical framework. In particular, we present a rigorous derivation of the reverse-time stochastic differential equation on the group manifold, discuss the gauge invariance of the denoising loss function, and provide extensive numerical benchmarks regarding the scaling behavior with respect to the lattice volume and the inverse coupling β. Full analytical expressions for arbitrarily sized Wilson loops and the topological charge susceptibility during the forward process are given as well.

articles.title: Evaluating Ensemble Methods for Algorithmic Stability Under Data Perturbations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard classification algorithms often exhibit sensitivity near decision boundaries, which can compound instability that already exists from overfitting to a subset of high-influence samples. Ensembling is commonly used to stabilize classifiers, but we show that it can destabilize those that are already stable. The well-established practice of subbagging can yield substantial improvements in stability, as we validate in the cause-of-death classification setting. However, its effect depends on the perturbation level, and for stable classifiers the finite number of bags introduces destabilizing Monte Carlo noise that shrinks only slowly as the number of bags grows. This instability can be mitigated, though, by the recently proposed inflated argmax, which allows for multi-class predictions in ambiguous cases. We further examine the extent to which the Rashomon set, the collection of distinct models that achieve near-optimal predictive performance, can reduce instability by leveraging predictive multiplicity rather than resampling. We find that the Rashomon ensemble can stabilize unstable classifiers, but requires sufficient predictive multiplicity, which is not guaranteed. It is a promising direction, but not currently a general substitute for subbagging. Our results are consistent with an influence equalization interpretation of why these ensemble approaches stabilize unstable classifiers, although their failures on stable classifiers appear to have distinct sources.

articles.title: Debiased Inference via Posterior Corrections for High-Dimensional Regression
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.09257v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: There has been significant progress in Bayesian inference based on sparsity-inducing priors, such as spike-and-slab and horseshoe priors, for high-dimensional regression. The resulting posteriors, however, in general do not possess desirable frequentist properties, and the credible sets thus cannot serve as valid confidence sets even asymptotically. We introduce a novel debiasing approach that corrects the bias for the entire (possibly approximate) Bayesian posterior distribution. We establish new Bernstein-von Mises theorems that guarantee the frequentist validity of the debiased law. We demonstrate the practical performance of our proposal through Monte Carlo simulations and two empirical applications in economics.

articles.title: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well on chemistry knowledge benchmarks, which mainly assess question answering and isolated tasks. Chemical research, however, requires using specialized tools and interpreting their outputs to obtain chemically valid results. To address this gap, we introduce Crucible Bench to evaluate this ability across all four stages of the design-make-test-analyze (DMTA) cycle. The benchmark contains 1,078 tasks in 12 task families curated from 18 published datasets, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, experimental execution, closed-loop optimization, simulation, and analytical characterization. Agents access 75 domain-specific tools through the Model Context Protocol in seven isolated environments. Sandboxed graders verify the resulting synthesis routes, experimental protocols, and other outputs. Laboratory tasks use robotic simulators or previously measured experimental data. We evaluate 14 LLMs as agents and find that the best achieves an overall score of 0.545, with synthesis planning and closed-loop optimization emerging as the hardest domains. Overall performance does not predict optimization performance well: the model ranked twelfth overall achieves the highest score in closed-loop optimization. Error analysis also shows that agents often submit chemically invalid results despite running their tools successfully. Stronger models benefit more from tool access, but reliable use of chemical software remains a challenge that Crucible Bench can track as models improve.

articles.title: ScanAR: Parallel Row-Scan Decoding for Efficient Image Generation in Unified Autoregressive Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unified multimodal autoregressive (AR) models represent text and images in one token sequence and generate all modalities with a shared next-token prediction head. Their image generation, however, decodes an H× W visual grid token by token in raster order, which takes HW sequential steps and dominates inference time. Existing acceleration methods for visual AR generation either change the tokenizer, the prediction head, or the model interface, or keep the model but cannot reach high parallelism without losing quality, so they do not carry over to unified AR models. We propose ScanAR, a row-scan parallel decoding method that only redefines the predecessors of visual tokens. The first visual row is generated from left to right as usual, and each later row is generated in a single parallel step, with every token predicted from the vertically aligned token of the previous row. Nonvisual tokens keep the standard autoregressive rule. ScanAR reduces the visual decoding depth from HW to H+W without changing the backbone, vocabulary, or output head and without adding parameters, and it supports both training from scratch and lightweight post-training. On Emu3.5-Image-34B, ScanAR post-training reaches a GenEval score of 82.36, the best among post-training acceleration methods trained on the same data, and generates 512×512 images 13.8× faster than raster decoding under the same inference setting. On ImageNet, ScanAR trained from scratch has the highest throughput at every model size with FID comparable to raster LlamaGen. On the 34B Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 model, ScanAR preserves the overall quality of embodied scene generation, interleaved image-text generation, and video generation.

articles.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at aim-uofa.github.io/WorldReforge/.

articles.title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.34128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate 3D surface reconstruction from unposed images remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision.
