Matched-competence controls demonstrate that native task success does not ensure interoperability, while shared semantic supervision enables substantial direct transfer in the evaluated settings. Withheld-information experiments show that recipient models can continue computations requiring information unavailable to donors at exchange time. Partial-contract experiments and packet interventions further establish that observed compatibility is conditional on the semantics, packet populations, and recipient continuations being evaluated. Together, these results support public neural interface specifications as a framework for designing prospective component exchange and distinguishing demonstrated interoperability from stronger conformance claims.

articles.title: TQ-HQNet: A Trainability-Aware and Qubit-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for Cross-Domain Learning on Heterogeneous Data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid quantum neural networks are a promising direction for noisy intermediate-scale quantum computing, but their practical effectiveness is often limited by poor trainability, rigid circuit design, and weak robustness across heterogeneous real-world tasks. This paper proposes TQ-HQNet, a Trainability-Aware and Qubit-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for cross-domain learning on heterogeneous data. The proposed framework combines three mechanisms: 1) adaptive latent compression to map domain-specific features into qubit-compatible representations, 2) trainability-aware search over compact variational circuit candidates, and 3) hybrid fusion of multiple shallow quantum experts to improve robustness without increasing qubit cost excessively. TQ-HQNet is evaluated on four public datasets spanning neurological screening, phishing detection, financial direction prediction, and DNA sequence classification. Across all domains, the proposed model consistently improves over a fixed hybrid quantum baseline, with balanced-accuracy gains of +0.280, +0.170, +0.071, and +0.060, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm that gains arise from trainability-aware compact circuit selection and expert fusion, not circuit scaling. Although classical baselines outperform on some tasks, fixed-split results show consistent improvements over the fixed hybrid reference. These analyses support the practical role of compact selection and fusion, with repeated-split and hardware-aware studies left for future work.

articles.title: Sounding the Black Box: Online Training of Embedded Neural Networks in Forward-Only Physical Simulators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid physics-neural simulators embed neural networks in partial differential equation (PDE) solvers to model unresolved subgrid dynamics while preserving resolved physics and conservation laws. Because closure outputs feed back across time steps, single-step offline regression does not directly minimize multi-step rollout error, motivating online trajectory optimization. Solver backpropagation through time (BPTT) is the standard online solution when solver derivatives are available, yet many operational Fortran and C/C++ simulators expose only non-differentiable, forward-only interfaces. We introduce FORGE (Forward-Only Response and Gauss-Newton Estimation), an online framework that trains embedded networks from forward runs alone by decoupling exact network derivatives from black-box simulator dynamics. Stage I warms up the rollout via a low-dimensional Gauss-Newton step along output-orthonormal weight directions, canceling multi-layer feature drift via a final-layer correction. Stage II perturbs spatial output fields to fit a gain-bounded causal linear response operator across rollout steps, solves for regularized target outputs, and updates all weights via network backpropagation. Across five 2D and 3D benchmarks spanning phase separation, reaction-diffusion, fluid and MHD turbulence, and ocean circulation, FORGE outperforms gradient-free, reinforcement-learning, and emulator-based baselines, cutting coarse-solver test mean squared error (MSE) by 50%-96% in 2D and 70% in 3D, outperforming the strongest forward-only baseline by 16%-69%, and recovering 88%-98% of Solver BPTT's gains. Code is available at https://github.com/ChiyodaMomo01/FORGE.

articles.title: Online Environment Repair for Coding Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Programmatic verifiers provide scalable reward signals for training coding agents with reinforcement learning, yet subtle harness defects and incomplete unit tests allow policies to earn full credit without solving the intended task. Existing training-time defenses intervene either by penalizing suspicious outputs or by filtering flagged tasks and rollouts. However, output penalties leave the underlying verifier exploitable, driving policies to disguise shortcuts under reasoning monitors or zeroing out valid solutions under detector false positives, whereas task and rollout filtering discards or mutes the hardest problems where shortcuts emerge earliest. Pre-training verifier hardening repairs the environment directly, but misses vulnerability classes that surface only as the policy improves during reinforcement learning. In this paper, we propose online environment repair, which leaves triggering rollout rewards unchanged to remove hiding incentives and asynchronously patches exploited environments during training. Candidate repairs triggered by execution invariants or differential fuzzing are deployed only after passing three automated validation gates that block the exploit while preserving valid solutions, canceling detector false positives and enabling structural propagation across repositories without scaffold labels or reference solutions. Across 20 controlled GRPO experiments on heterogeneous software-engineering repositories, online environment repair reduces cumulative reward hacking from 36.9% to 0.06% and improves held-out Pass@8 from 21.7% to 46.7%, consistently outperforming reward-penalty, rollout-filtering, and static-hardening baselines while eliminating zero-shot exploitation on unseen loophole classes.

articles.title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables privacy-preserving, all-weather physical scene understanding across darkness, smoke, and walls. However, standard instruction tuning treats continuous radar streams as static text-like tokens, causing near-random global radar-to-text retrieval and severe physical drift under sensor blackouts. Conversely, coupling pairwise contrastive losses (e.g., SigLIP) directly into the shared backbone improves retrieval but injects O(B²) repulsive gradients that fracture continuous coordinate manifolds (R² < 0). We present PhysRF-WorldJEPA, a manifold-decoupled Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) that separates continuous electromagnetic state prediction from cross-modal language alignment. An unattenuated 1.0x clock anchor and parallel dual-scale RF encoder feed a lean ~3% LoRA LLM trained with two-step state-space EMA-JEPA (Denoise -> Rollout) and sample-axis Batch-VICReg to predict +3.0 s physical states; a stop-gradient alignment head then maps frozen prompt states onto the text hypersphere with false-negative masking. On a 4,541-window tri-domain suite (77/60.25/60 GHz) against 10 baselines, freezing the physical backbone and training only the decoupled head lifts R->T R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% and improves MedRank from 107.0 to 60.0 while preserving identical physical readout: 3.37 deg (R²=+0.961) blackout +3.0 s torso tilt, 1.89 m (R²=+0.679; 1.19 m/+0.863 at the RF front-end) cluttered UAV altitude, 2.04 m (R²=+0.461) behind-wall NLOS range, 0.9976 virtual-RIS invariance, and 100% fall recall. Across five 0.5B-1.8B LLM families (15 zero-overhead models), World-JEPA improves retrieval and 75%-drop completion in 10/10 runs and blackout tilt in 4/5 (Span-Euc), 2/5 (Scatter), and 5/5 (per-family best) over SFT.

articles.title: Fractal Neural Synthesis: Constant-Storage Procedural Weight Derivation via Complex Quadratic Boundary Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional neural networks store synaptic parameters as explicit tensors whose persistent Flash footprint scales linearly (O(W)) with parameter count, constraining resource-limited edge microcontrollers. We formulate and systematically evaluate Fractal Neural Synthesis (FNS), a procedural weight derivation architecture that replaces hidden-layer matrices with a constant 24-byte coordinate seed Theta = (cₓ, c_y, ell) in F₆₄³ anchored near the complex quadratic bifurcation boundary dM of f_c(z) = z² + c. We introduce a large-bailout (R = 256) smooth escape kernel, four zero-overhead geometric sampling apertures--Cartesian Grid, coprime 3x3 Rule-of-Thirds (Z/9Z), phi-Vogel spiral, and multi-scale Harmonic Tripod--and prove conditional Kolmogorov (K_Kolm <= 192 + c₀ bits) and Shannon entropy bounds. Across magnifications zeta in [10⁰, 10⁸], C¹ Fourier and lattice-noise bases collapse to post-standardization rank ~2.25 and SHA-256 PRNG exhibits avalanche discontinuity (rho ~ 0.019, 50.6% micro-step retention), whereas dM uniquely sustains both rank (~10.0) and local continuity (rho in [0.81, 0.97], 89.2% retention). Under leak-free 10-fold CV across four zero-scaler-byte non-linear benchmarks, FNS with an INT8 readout surpasses 0-hidden Linear-INT8 by +3.6 to +10.8 pp while delivering 10.7x-129x total Flash reduction (725x-2,773x hidden reduction) relative to converged Float32 MLPs (90.30% Ionosphere in 285 B; 97.22% Optical Digits in 2,598 B; 97.90% PenDigits in 2,598 B; 87.00% Satimage in 1,570 B).

articles.title: Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.26762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) exploits quantum dynamics for temporal information processing. Quantum noise affects the reservoir dynamics and can either impair computational performance or serve as a computational resource. However, the role of pure dephasing in Hamiltonian encoding QRC remains unclear. In this work, we propose a minimum complexity QRC model that harnesses pure dephasing in an open uniform XX chain. We show that, under suitable input encoding, pure dephasing can ensure the echo state and fading memory properties even without amplitude damping. Furthermore, in the presence of amplitude damping, the proposed quantum reservoir has distinct stationary states for distinct inputs, and introducing pure dephasing alters these states, thereby affecting the reservoir dynamics. Information processing capacity analysis shows that joint control of the two decoherence mechanisms regulates memory and nonlinearity, providing access to diverse capacity profiles. The proposed QRC achieves promising performance on synthetic benchmarks, while its 6-qubit configuration outperforms all three multi-reservoir echo state network baselines on over half of the real-world prediction tasks. These findings highlight pure dephasing as a computational resource for QRC.

articles.title: Exact Volume-Preserving Diffeomorphic Shear Splitting: Continuous-Discrete Geometric Bounds, Reversible Memory Backpropagation, and Expressivity Frontiers in Volumetric Mapping
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Incompressible diffeomorphic registration requires continuous spatial mappings that preserve local tissue volume (det(DΦ) = 1) without topological folding (det(DΦ) > 0). Standard velocity-field methods (SVF, LDDMM) approximate incompressibility via numerical ODE integration or soft penalties, exhibiting numerical volume drift (~10⁻⁴ to 10⁻¹), iterative grid inversions, and linear backpropagation memory O(L * N_vox). We formulate an exact structure-preserving framework for 3D registration based on cascaded coordinate shears. By decomposing the divergence-free Lie algebra sdiff(Ω) into six coordinate-shear generators whose convective non-linearities vanish identically, each elementary stage integrates analytically to a closed-form triangular shear with det(DSₖ) = 1 and exact machine-precision inverse requiring zero iterations and zero spatial interpolations. Multi-stage compositions generate the connected volume-preserving group SDiff₀(Ω). We establish: (i) an unconditional global diffeomorphism proof closing the Hadamard-Caccioppoli injectivity gap; (ii) a Dirichlet boundary confinement lemma; (iii) an anisotropic Riemannian similarity invariance; (iv) a Sobolev H² spectral budget preventing chaotic mixing; and (v) an exact reversible backpropagation engine eliminating O(L) trajectory storage (0.00 MB intermediate activations). We prove second-order O(h²) sub-voxel convergence across 16³ to 64³ lattices and second-order trajectory accuracy for palindromic Strang splitting (468.1x error reduction vs. Lie-Trotter; drift |det(DΦ)-1| <= 2.22e-16). Execution is 2.1x-4.0x faster than SVF with 78.4% GPU memory reduction. On cardiac cine-MRI (ACDC, N=100) and brain MRI (OASIS-1, N=414), our model achieves competitive Dice (0.884 and 0.841) while strictly maintaining 0.0000% folding and zero volume drift.

articles.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. Across four reasoning and agentic benchmarks, we show that harness-conditioned training yields vastly different outcomes depending on how these interact. Multi-harness distillation aggregates task knowledge from trajectories collected through different harnesses into a shared policy, but this knowledge is realised only when training preserves or improves competence on the inference-time interface. Otherwise, single-harness training can induce interference in interface competence, sometimes catastrophically collapsing performance on a held-out harness despite improvements in underlying task knowledge. To disentangle task and interface supervision, we introduce harness rehearsal: distillation on traces that carry minimal task knowledge while exercising the target interface. Cross-harness task supervision or rehearsal alone yields little gain, but their combination yields gains far larger than either: on BFCL V3 multi-turn with Qwen3-4B, they achieve 8.5% and 32.5% respectively, versus 58.8% together. Finally, on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is more robust than distillation to single-harness training: it does not substantially degrade performance on other harnesses, and interface competence acquired through multi-harness distillation persists through subsequent RL.

articles.title: Anchoring VAE Fine-Tuning to Its Latent Diffusion Prior
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretrained latent diffusion models are effective priors for transfer learning, from geometry estimation to physics simulation. Existing approaches fine-tune the diffusion backbone but freeze the encoder of the VAE to preserve the latent distribution. However, a frozen encoder may miss salient details in non-RGB inputs and is limited to three channels. We introduce Diffusion Prior Anchoring (DPA), a regularizer applied during VAE fine-tuning that uses a score-distillation update to steer latents toward the high-density manifold on which the pretrained diffusion model denoises accurately. We validate DPA across three image and video models (FLUX 3, LTX-Video, Wan2.2) and four tasks: monocular depth estimation, MRI reconstruction, wind-flow simulation, and surface normal estimation, where DPA lowers the prediction error by 7.5% relative to the frozen VAE, 4.9% to decoder-only fine-tuning, and 4.0% to unanchored VAE fine-tuning. Its gain grows the further the target data lies from the RGB training distribution, from 3.3% on monocular depth estimation to 7.2% on complex-valued MRI. DPA also applies to modified VAEs, including pruned and multi-channel variants. With a four-channel VAE that encodes depth and surface normals, it lowers depth estimation error by 9.3%.

articles.title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge. We also need to know whether a "new proof" is indeed new, whether a thousand generated proofs contain one idea or many, and where each sits relative to human mathematics. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. Following Hilbert's 24th problem and the identity-of-proofs problem, we ask how far apart two proofs of one theorem are, and what shape the proof space they inhabit has. We define 19 dissimilarity measures in 6 families (syntactic, structural, dependency & resource, semantic, information-theoretic, higher-categorical) and 10 desirable properties, which we argue are the conditions for safely optimising a measure. In a Curry-Howard kernel, 5 machine-checked proofs that the primes are infinite show that raw syntax cannot tell a rewrite from a new argument, that dependency-based and structural measures reproduce the intuitive ordering (Euclid rewritten < Goldbach < Furstenberg), and that semantic measures invert it: Furstenberg's topological proof produces exactly Euclid's witness. A replication in Lean 4/Mathlib (3 theorems, 19 proofs, 18 measures) confirms that dependency-closure measures track intuition best, and shows that equality of normal forms never holds between differently written versions of the same argument, that proofs by citation look unlike the arguments they cite, and that proof irrelevance cannot distinguish any two proofs. We argue for reporting dissimilarity as a multi-level profile, extend the measures to proofs of different theorems, and discuss uses, from detecting duplicated AI proofs and orchestrating prover agents to interpreting AI proofs via their nearest human-understandable counterparts. Code, Lean sources and data are released.

articles.title: A Unified Heat-Ball Framework for Fokker--Planck Equations: Mean-Value Identities, Exact Sampling, and Error Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.27954v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diffusion-based generative models with nonlinear or learned forward drifts raise questions that stay hidden for Gaussian forward processes: how the divergence-free and gradient parts of the drift shape the evolving density, whether sampling can draw on local rather than global information, and how to treat low-density regions, where u carries a weak signal while log u diverges and the entropy density ulog u falls between the two. These questions motivate the present study of local representations for Fokker--Planck equations with general, possibly nonlinear and time-dependent drift. We derive inhomogeneous heat-ball identities for the density u, the log-density log u, the entropy density ulog u, and the score nablalog u, keeping the source terms generated by the drift; their unscaled residuals recover the corresponding differential residuals at leading order in the squared heat-ball radius. The weights appearing in the identities, the source integrals, and the integration-by-parts formulas all belong to a single Beta--Gamma family of measures on the heat ball, which gives exact rejection-free sampling, product quadrature, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimators with variance and cost bounds that are explicit in the dimension and the radius. Experiments with Gaussian-mixture and nonlinear-drift references, in dimensions up to 1024 where applicable, confirm the sampling laws, the identities, and the residual behavior. In particular, log-density and score evaluations remain accurate where direct density estimation breaks down, and the heat-ball residuals provide local consistency tests for learned score models. A study of gauge-based heat-ball walks illustrates a recursive use of the density identity.

articles.title: Compressible Representations: Functional Spines in Deep Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks embed inputs in high-dimensional representations, but how much of this capacity actually drives behavior? We introduce a framework for identifying, at each layer, the subspace of the representation that is functionally sensitive to the task. Using a matrix analogous to the Fisher information but defined over the hidden representation, we rank directions by their influence on downstream computation and project onto the most task-sensitive subspace. Across pretrained vision networks, representations are remarkably compressible: a small fraction of the task-sensitive subspace preserves most performance, often requiring far fewer dimensions than geometric alternatives. We find that this compressed representation is also more robust to adversarial attacks generated on the full network. We additionally show that this decomposition recovers functionally distinct subspaces within the same representation: on cue-conflict stimuli, shape-sensitive and texture-sensitive directions are largely non-overlapping, and ablating one selectively impairs the corresponding task while leaving the other intact. Task-sensitive subspaces also provide a principled foundation for continual learning: constraining gradient updates to lie orthogonal to the task-sensitive subspaces of prior tasks outperforms standard variance-based gradient projection methods. Finally, restricting representational comparisons to task-sensitive subspaces reveals that inter-model alignment is higher in task-sensitive directions than in task-insensitive directions at later layers, and that conditioning on different tasks over the same stimuli uncovers asymmetries that full-space similarity measures cannot detect. Together, these results establish that deep networks compute through a low-dimensional functional spine embedded within a much larger representational space.

articles.title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to develop standalone game-playing programs that run without language model inference. We thus introduce Coding4Games, a benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can develop standalone programs that play modern games through visual observations and standard game inputs. Coding4Games has three defining features: 1) Diverse Modern Games, covering 15 games with diverse visual, strategic, and control demands; 2) Development-Test Separation, in which a coding agent uses a sandbox and the standard player interface to iteratively develop a program, after which the selected program is frozen and independently tested without language-model inference; and 3) Outcome and Process Evaluation, which measures not only game performance and reliability but also how agents use feedback, revise programs, and resolve problems during development. Across 15 games, the best program per game outscores the strongest GUI baseline on 13 and ties it on one. The human player outscores all agents on 10 games. We additionally examine the effects of development budgets. Coding4Games evaluates whether coding agents can turn their understanding of complex interactive environments into programs that work reliably on their own.

articles.title: Interactive Neural Computers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents. This is limiting when someone needs a different workflow, or an interface suited to hands-free use or a disability. We explore an overlooked alternative. Rather than training an agent to operate an existing computer, we train a generative model to be the computer, predicting each next screen from past screens and the user's mouse and keyboard actions. Treating a desktop as an interactive world model raises problems that natural-video world models largely avoid. Without a camera pose to index memory, the model must remember content that has left the screen without any geometric cues. Arithmetic in a terminal has to be exactly right, not merely plausible. Small interface text must also stay legible at interactive frame rates. Our Interactive Neural Computer is structured like a Neural Turing Machine and starts to address these problems with three modules trained end to end from pixels and actions. A surprise-gated slot memory, supervised by latent next-frame prediction (MEMORY-JEPA), stores what is off screen. An exploratory query bridge brings in the reasoning of a pretrained VLM, and a residual renderer predicts only the latent changes between frames. In long closed-loop rollouts, our model recalls occluded files in 64.2% of trials (chance is 33.3%), compared with at most 56.0% for recurrent and sliding-window baselines. It also raises terminal-text OCR accuracy from 1.3% to 50.1%. Finally, because the memory is explicit, it can be transplanted at test time to causally change what the model renders.

articles.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. A shared generation-and-rendering interface connects these representations to visual feedback across images, vector graphics, webpages, and documents. A Nemotron-native harness coordinates planning and raster candidate selection, with targeted repair for editable structured and hybrid artifacts. To support this interface, we develop Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer, the autoregressive raster generator Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B, and the structured-code model family Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode. On approximately 178K images spanning six visual domains, our tokenizer improves reconstruction PSNR from 26.08 to 29.57 dB over Emu3.5 IBQ. It also provides 7.13x faster encoding and 10.93x faster decoding at batch size one on A100. In standalone evaluation, one Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode variant surpasses Kimi K3.1 Pro on the aggregate across Chart2Code, MMSVG, Design2Code, and Image2Struct. At the system level, the Nemotron-native configuration raises GenEval2 Soft-TIFA GM from 31.71 to 52.56 using the same raster generator. With our best setting, Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation achieves performance competitive with GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro across most benchmarks with available comparisons.

articles.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in 10⁵, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in 10⁴, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

articles.title: Beyond Rigid Hands: Deforming Skin into Contact-Consistent Hand Meshes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hands grasp objects with soft skin. A fingertip flattens against a mug, and a palm curves around a bottle. Yet hand-object datasets and estimators represent the hand as a rigid articulated mesh, which hovers above or penetrates the object where skin would press against it. Existing refiners keep the mesh rigid and adjust only the pose, trading pose accuracy for physical plausibility. We ask whether a rigid hand can instead touch the object as skin does while staying close to its original pose. We lift annotated or estimated rigid hands to contact-consistent meshes through an optimization that (i) slightly adjusts the joints and wrist to bring the fingers onto the object, (ii) deforms the skin so that penetrating regions settle onto the surface, and (iii) keeps this deformation consistent over time. Since deformation reaches only skin already near the object, we further train a lightweight head on the lifted annotations to predict where an estimated hand should touch and steer the deformation there. Unlike existing refiners, the lift more than doubles the skin lying on the object surface for three published estimators while barely changing the pose. Guidance from the learned head further improves grasp stability by closing contact gaps that the estimate leaves open. Existing hand-object datasets and estimators can thus adopt contact-consistent hands without changing the hand model or retraining the estimators.

articles.title: Calm Agent: Reframing Agent Interaction around Intermittent Human Attention
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents can carry out auxiliary tasks while users focus on other work. Yet users still need to understand task state, make changes, and respond when help is required. We argue that agents for ongoing auxiliary tasks should be designed around intermittent human attention: tasks should continue between interactions, and users should be able to return with little effort to understand and control them. We develop this position as Calm Agent. It connects three on-demand interaction modes: Delegate, Adjust, and Check, through a persistent task representation. Generative interaction provides controls and feedback suited to open-ended goals, while existing controls support routine actions. We illustrate these principles with Orvlet, a desktop prototype for background execution and compact task interfaces. We identify challenges in adapting interfaces while preserving continuity, coordinating attention across tasks, providing responsive interaction, and learning user habits over time. The aim is to support continuing task control while protecting attention for primary work.

articles.title: Value of diffusion layer thickness during increasing the hardening of precision parts by laser method
articles.abstract: This paper addresses the thickness of the diffusion layer formed during laser surface hardening of precision parts of machines and apparatuses, which must be known in order to assign the machining allowance for subsequent finishing. During saturation, the outer and inner boundaries of the diffusion layer shift relative to the initial surface; this displacement depends on the thermodynamic properties of the system, the type of diffusion process and the material of the part. The process is considered as a sequence of stages in which the rate at which atoms arrive at the surface greatly exceeds their rate of diffusion into the part, so that layer growth is controlled by diffusion in depth. Diffusion saturation of precision parts forms a ternary system of simultaneously interacting elements, which can be described by considering the behaviour of two of them. Using Fick's laws with direct and cross-diffusion coefficients, analytical expressions are derived for the velocity of the outer boundary, the change in the linear dimensions of the part and the total thickness of the diffusion layer, showing a parabolic dependence on saturation time. The curves were calculated for chromium and nitrogen using concentration, diffusion coefficient and rate constant values taken from the literature. The results show that the required quality and thickness of the layer, and hence the machining allowance, are governed by the diffusion coefficients and the thermodynamic reaction rate constant.

articles.title: AQUILA. Assistant for Quantum and Unified Intelligent Layered Architectures
articles.abstract: Achieving quantum utility today relies on the effective design and optimization of hybrid quantum-classical software architectures. Beyond hardware constraints, a major challenge of these architectures is the absence of quantum software engineering methodologies, including best practices and design patterns, which leads to suboptimal development practices. The use of LLMs has demonstrated remarkable success in conventional software engineering tasks, but they often encounter significant limitations in constantly evolving domains such as Quantum Computing. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces AQUILA, a framework based on Retrieval Augmented Generation to elevate the quality, efficiency and design of hybrid software architectures. The system combines a dynamic knowledge base with a prompt template system that ensures the generation of highly precise, context-aware architectural solutions. Operationally, the proposed system leverages LangChain for orchestration, Ollama for secure and local LLM execution and external APIs for high-capacity inference. AQUILA has been validated across two phases: retrieval performance via RAGAs metrics and a generation quality evaluation, contrasting an LLM-as-a-judge approach with human expert consensus. The results indicate effective context retrieval (achieving an F1-score of 0.822), while showing that AQUILA consistently improves response quality over the LLM without context. These findings highlight the potential of domain-grounded retrieval to support quantum software engineers and provide a practical foundation for adopting reliable hybrid architectures in industrial contexts.

articles.title: Cation Diffusion in ZnAl₂O₄, Zn₂SiO₄, and Their Heterogeneous Interface: A Machine- Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
articles.abstract: Filters have been applied extensively in many areas including radar, mobile communications and satellite communications; progress in integration has also been closely related with Low-Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC), Low-Temperature Co-fired Ferrite (LTCF). During the co-firing process of ceramics and ferrite, the atomic movement and cation diffusion near the interface are complex phenomena, and the microscopic mechanisms behind them urgently require further study. In this study, machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) simulations were employed to investigate atomic motion and cation diffusion in ZnAl₂O₄, Zn₂SiO₄, and their heterogeneous interface. It was observed that the diffusion activation energy varies depending on the cation in the doped solid phase. The diffusion activation energies of B3+, Si4+ and Ti4+ doped in ZnAl₂O₄ are 0.315 eV, 0.607 eV and 0.417 eV, respectively. The diffusion activation energies of Al3+, B3+ and Ti4+ doped in Zn₂SiO₄ are 0.240 eV, 0.147 eV and 0.172 eV, respectively. There are obvious differences in the diffusion behavior of different cations at the heterogeneous interface. The order of migration ability along the normal direction of the interface is Zn2+ > Si4+ > Al3+.This work provides an atomic-scale reference for interface diffusion analysis and co-firing process of ceramic-ferrite components by analyzing the cation migration rules of ZnAl₂O₄, Zn₂SiO₄ and their heterogeneous interfaces.

articles.title: Resource-Efficient Quantum Classifier for Facial Identification
articles.abstract: Hybrid quantum frameworks are typically associated with higher-dimensional and complex problems. Their applicability to resource-constrained biometric systems remain insufficiently explored. This work proposes a hybrid quantum--classical facial classification pipeline designed for efficient deployment on standard computing hardware. This hybrid quantum framework includes pre-processing the images using gamma correction and contrast enhancement, followed by principal component analysis for structured dimensionality reduction. The reduced feature vectors are then encoded into an 8-qubit variational quantum classifier (VQC) for classification followed by classical image matching for recognition. The reported pipeline achieves accuracy of 97%. The results are compared with a quantum baseline method - quantum support vector machines. By deploying this in the real-world attendance monitoring system in collaboration with Lloyds Technology Centre (LTC), we confirmed its practical viability, achieving inference times between 0.2 and 0.5 seconds per person in real time on CPU. The framework proved robust against common variations such as usage of spectacles. Comparative experiments using 50,000 images (25,000 faces from CelebA, 25,000 non-faces from CIFAR-10) show that the hybrid quantum classifier attains accuracy comparable to a range of classical baselines evaluated on identical features---including PCA with logistic regression, support vector machines and random forests, histogram-of-oriented-gradients (HOG) with a linear SVM, and a lightweight convolutional neural network---while using only 72 trainable parameters, several orders of magnitude fewer than the classical FaceNet baseline. We further observe that this binary face/non-face benchmark is easily separable and discuss the implications for fair evaluation of quantum classifiers. This work showcases the potential of hybrid quantum frameworks for real-time face recognition deployable on existing hardware for quantum readiness of enterprises, with out migration to high end GPUs or quantum hardware.

articles.title: Comparing surface and total insecticide content as predictors of bioefficacy in PBO-pyrethroid nets across durability trials
articles.abstract: Insecticide treated bed nets (ITNs) are the key malaria vector control tool across sub-Saharan Africa with well-proven impact in reducing malaria cases and deaths since the advent of mass distributions. Durability of ITNs is a persistent concern however raising concerns over current distribution cycle lengths. Methods to test ITN durability over time use physical examination for holes and mosquito bioassays to assess bioefficacy, supplemented by chemical assessment of the total active ingredient (A.I) present in net fibres. The latter represents a potential mismatch if A.I in the total fibre is not representative of that contacted by mosquitoes exposed to the net surface. We test the hypothesis that measuring A.I. on the surface could be a more informative approach for chemical durability assessment. To investigate this, we analysed the bioefficacy and chemical integrity of ITNs collected at intervals across 3 years as part of 3 field trials. Surface and total A.I. content was measured using HPLC and bioefficacy assessed with mosquito colonies of known resistance profiles using WHO cone assays. Chemical and bioassay data from the same nets were compared to assess which of surface or total A.I is the better predictor of mosquito knockdown and mortality. The unused nets continued to regenerate surface A.I over the study period. In contrast, whilst used ITNs regenerated surface A.I, the concentration was insufficient to replace that lost during use, resulting in reducing surface content over time. Surface content of both pyrethroid insecticides and the synergist PBO were better predictors of knockdown and mortality than complete A.I for each net type tested. In conclusion, our data support the prediction that surface content is a more accurate measure of bioefficacy of ITNs than total A.I content, as well as validating the solvent stripping method used here for surface chemical analysis. The use of this method should improve durability analysis and give a more informative estimation of net longevity, rather than relying on bioassays with mosquito colonies which are known to show high heterogeneity, especially among testing locations.

articles.title: Mitigating Condensate Dropout and Improving Gas Condensate Recovery through Wettability Alteration in Carbonate Rocks
articles.abstract: Gas condensate reservoirs, a subclass of gas reservoirs, represent an important energy resource. However, their production is often hindered by condensate accumulation in the near-wellbore region as reservoir pressure declines below the dew-point pressure, resulting in liquid blockage and lower gas recovery. In this work, to mitigate liquid blockage and improve gas mobility, an anionic fluorosurfactant combined with hydrophobic SiO₂ nanoparticles was used. The treatment successfully shifted the rock surface from a liquid-wetting to a gas-wetting state, as confirmed by static contact angle measurements. A pronounced reduction in the surface free energy of the carbonate rock was observed after treatment, with values declining from 68.64 to 1.72 mN/m. Capillary rise heights for water and condensate decreased from 24.60 mm to 4.48 mm and from 9.98 mm to 0 mm, respectively. Over time, the water contact angle decreased by 15% and the condensate by 33%, indicating better droplet stability for water. Electrical conductivity and solid% tests during core flooding showed that 5 pore volumes of the chemical solution were sufficient to induce a gas-wetting state. Spontaneous imbibition tests revealed that liquid saturations were reduced by 63.75% (water) and 33.17% (condensate) after treatment. Water permeability dropped by 72.7%, and capillary pressure increased by 23.5%. Coreflooding tests at 0.5-2 cc/min showed that increasing the flow rate decreased residual saturation from 37.54% to 11.92% and increased endpoint relative permeability from 5.17 to 9.54 mD. Following treatment, the pressure drop decreased by 38.35% for water and 21.95% for condensate, while the endpoint relative permeability increased to 1.62 and 1.28 times the corresponding pre-treatment values, respectively. These findings highlight the potential benefits of wettability modification for enhanced recovery in gas condensate reservoirs.

articles.title: Biological control potential of Trichoderma asperelloides LBF 04/04 and Trichoderma koningiopsis LBF 48/11 against potato common scab caused by Streptomyces scabiei
articles.abstract: Potato common scab is difficult to manage under field conditions, creating a need for biological options that retain activity beyond in vitro screening. We evaluated two native isolates, Trichoderma asperelloides LBF 04/04 and Trichoderma koningiopsis LBF 48/11, against phytopathogenic Streptomycesusing a 12-strain dual-culture screen followed by a greenhouse assay and two field trials with Streptomyces scabieiIBSBF 2950 on potato cv. Agata. Tuber fresh weight and number of tubers were also quantified. Both isolates showed antagonistic activity against all tested strains, although LBF 48/11 had the stronger mean in vitro score. In the greenhouse, however, LBF 04/04 was more effective, decreasing mean scab-affected tuber surface by 54.6% and lesion-type severity by 30.6% relative to the pathogen control. Field performance was site dependent. LBF 04/04 significantly decreased affected tuber surface by 15.0% at Santo Antônio de Posse, whereas at Mococa the 29.1% lower mean was not statistically significant. Thus, in vitro ranking did not predict in planta performance, and LBF 04/04 emerged as the most consistent candidate for further validation within integrated common-scab management.

articles.title: On the Expressive Power of the Transverse-Field Ising Model for Graph Learning
articles.abstract: We study the quantum evolution induced by graph-indexed Ising Hamiltonians as a source of structural signal for graph learning. Graph automorphisms preserve symmetries of the Hamiltonian, and these symmetries constrain the quantum evolution in a way that turns time-dependent local measurements into informative probes of graph structure. Leveraging this idea, we introduce QDAGer, a quantum-inspired graph-pair Transformer that injects quantum-dynamical features from time series of node occupations and connected two-point correlators directly into the attention mechanism. We apply QDAGer to learning Graph Edit Distance (GED), an NP-hard similarity measure, using either a direct permutation-invariant embedding discrepancy or an alignment-based surrogate loss. Experiments on multiple GED benchmarks under different edit cost settings show that the proposed dynamical features provide a stronger inductive bias than classical structural alternatives under the same training protocol. In addition, we report ablations where the dynamical signal is replaced by standard random-walk and heat-kernel features while keeping the architecture fixed, highlighting that the gain comes from the injected dynamics rather than model capacity alone.

articles.title: Limits of Soil-Moisture-Based Estimation of DCP-Derived Bearing Capacity of Unpaved Surfaces: Temporal and Cross-Site Validation
articles.abstract: Purpose:: This study tested whether profile volumetric water content can estimate contemporaneous dynamic-cone-penetrometer-derived California Bearing Ratio (DCP--CBR) of unpaved surfaces across time and sites. Methods:: Site~1 supplied 311 paired observations on 71 dates and Site~2 supplied 167 quality-controlled pairs on 61 dates. A depth median, monotonic log-linear model, ridge regression, and artificial neural network (ANN) were evaluated by date-grouped cross-validation, a final-15-date holdout, and no-recalibration cross-site testing. Raw DCP conversion, replicate-test reliability, PR2 channel stability, rainfall, and a calendar-placebo negative control were audited retrospectively. Results:: Grouped ANN MAE was 2.100 CBR points versus 2.451 for the median (R²=0.451). In the forward test, previous CBR performed best (MAE 2.256), while ANN achieved MAE 2.639 and R²=-0.175. On all Site~2 observations, ANN was worse than the Site~1 median (MAE 4.355 versus 3.941; R²=-1.043). Common-support restriction reduced ANN MAE to 2.696, but R² remained 0.071 and ANN did not outperform ridge directly. Replicate-test SD was 0.73 on the log-CBR scale and ICC was 0.19--0.25. Deep PR2 channels showed large within-day voltage swings. An apparent external weather gain was reproduced by a calendar placebo and was not stable after temporal exclusion. Conclusion:: Water content carried local information but did not provide transferable bearing-capacity estimates. Measurement noise and time--site confounding further limit interpretation; direct penetration testing and prospective, temporally separated validation remain necessary.

articles.title: Effect of Easily Reducible Iron(III) Complexes with Trihydroxamate-Type Artificial Siderophores on Iron-Uptake Mechanisms to the Siderophore-Auxotrophic Gram-Positive Bacterium Microbacterium flavescens
articles.abstract: The electrochemical properties of Fe(III) complexes of TAGE and TAGP synthesized as hydroxamate-type artificial siderophores were investigated. They present high redox potentials of E₁/₂ = −227 and −268 mV vs. NHE, respectively, which are 150 to 250 mV higher than natural hydroxamate-type siderophore Fe(III) complexes. Consequently, the artificial siderophore Fe(III)-TAGE is reduced by ascorbic acid to release Fe(II) ions, whereas the natural siderophore Fe(III)-DFOB is not reduced, consistent with their respective electrochemical behaviors. Using these artificial Fe(III) siderophore complexes, the bioavailability of Microbacterium flavescens was investigated. It has long been believed that its iron uptake mechanism depends solely on the direct uptake of Fe(III) hydroxamate-type siderophores. The growth behaviors of M. flavescens in response to these siderophores were examined in the presence and absence of 2,2'-bipyridine (Bpy), an Fe(II) chelator. The artificial siderophore Fe(III) complexes promote the growth of M. flavescens in the absence of Bpy, as do natural siderophores. However, the artificial siderophores did not promote growth in the presence of Bpy. This suggests that the Fe(III) ions in the artificial siderophore complexes are reduced to Fe(II) ions and that the less stable Fe(II) ions are captured by Bpy, preventing the growth of M. flavescens. These results suggest that M. flavescens also possesses a reductive iron transport pathway.

articles.title: Spatially Decoupled Polar Vortices and Ferromagnetism in Gate-Tunable Twisted Bilayer PbO
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional multiferroics are fundamentally constrained by the chemical incompatibility between polarization and magnetic order. Moiré superlattices avoid this limit by generating polarization through interlayer twisting, yet coexisting and tunable magnetic order remains an open challenge. Here, using non-polar, non-magnetic α-PbO as a model system, we propose a strategy for spatially decoupling polarization and magnetism in a Lieb moiré superlattice under hole doping. First-principles calculations show that the chiral in-plane polar vortices emerge within AA stacking regions. Further, the out-of-plane polarization (up to 34.9 pC/m at θt = 36.87°) yields a periodic electrostatic potential, forming a programmable polar substrate for adjacent material tuning. Flat bands with a narrow bandwidth of 3.2 meV localize within the AC stacking regions at θt = 10.39°. The resulting van Hove singularity triggers a Stoner instability, inducing ferromagnetism upon hole doping. Polarization and magnetism localize to distinct stacking domains and can be regulated by electric gating. These findings provide opportunities for designing high-density, multifunctional memory in low-dimensional systems.

articles.title: What disruption labels reward: how 11,471 MAST plasmas ended, and what predictors learn from each label set
articles.abstract: Open data from the MAST spherical tokamak (FAIR-MAST) are increasingly used to train machine-learning disruption predictors, often with labels taken from the plasma current alone. We classify how each of 11,471 MAST discharges ended, from the programmed plasma current and the central-solenoid sweep rate at the current quench. Of the 10,616 shots without an operator disruption note, 37.3% (95% confidence interval 36.4–38.2%) were lost during the programmed flat-top with solenoid flux still available, as were 72.9% of the noted disruptions, while 45.8% of all current quenches came after the flux was exhausted or during a programmed ramp-down. The result is stable across campaigns and thresholds, and agrees with an earlier MAST disruption database on 90% of the 6,501 shots both cover. The operators’ own comments describe a vertical displacement event, a locked mode or an early termination for 10.3% of the un-noted flat-top losses, as often as for noted disruptions (11.2%) and three times as often as for flux-exhausted endings (3.0%). A gradient-boosting predictor trained on current-only labels reaches a precision–recall area eight times that of one trained on operator-confirmed labels, yet over 50 repeated splits it warns of recorded disruptions no more often than it raises false alarms, while warning of 23.8% of flux-exhausted endings. With operator-confirmed labels it beats random alarms by 8.7 points (95% range 5.4–12.1) at a 5% false-alarm rate, and leaving the doubtful shots out of training raises the share of clear disruptions caught by 9.4 points, confirmed on 30 splits specified in advance.

articles.title: A Data-Driven Surrogate Model for Tool Design Optimization in Multi-Stage Shear Cutting and Collar Forming Processes
articles.abstract: In multi-stage sheet metal forming processes such as combined shear cutting and collar forming, edge cracking is a relevant concern for process reliability. Predicting the influence of material and tool design parameters using finite element analysis (FEA) is computationally expensive, restricting its use in iterative design and optimization. This study therefore proposes a surrogate modeling and optimization workflow based on a scalar data representation for the shear cutting and collar forming process. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) is trained on a dataset of 2D simulations conducted in LS-DYNA to predict the circumferential strain at the collar edge, which serves as a strain-based indicator for comparing process configurations. The surrogate model is combined with the L-BFGS-B optimization algorithm to identify configurations that minimize the circumferential strain. The surrogate-assisted configuration is then evaluated using additional FEA simulations. Shapley values are used to quantify the contributions of the input parameters and assess their consistency with established process knowledge. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed workflow for computationally efficient surrogate-assisted tool design. The Chebyshev-based parametrization offers a unified description for different collar punch geometries, enabling their reconstruction and integration into the workflow. Nevertheless, the findings are limited by the investigated design space and the predictive capabilities of the surrogate model.

articles.title: Experimental Investigation of the Effect of Reduced Graphene Oxide Coating on Copper Electrode Performance in Electrical Discharge Machining of X40CrMoV5 Steel
articles.abstract: The Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) process is recognized as an advanced manufacturing method for fabricating parts with complex geometries and hard to cut materials. This study investigates the EDM process parameters using two types of electrodes: bare copper and reduced graphene oxide (RGO)-coated copper. To this end, the Box–Behnken design (BBD) under the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) framework is employed to examine the effects of process parameters on the Material Removal Rate (MRR), Tool Wear Rate (TWR), and Surface Roughness (SR) of machined X40CrMoV5 steel workpieces. The experimental results demonstrate that the RGO-coated electrode increases the material removal rate by up to 23.72% and reduces surface roughness by up to 12.5%. Furthermore, the tool wear rate for the coated electrode decreases by 87.07% compared to the conventional copper electrode. Among the investigated parameters, discharge current has the most significant influence on MRR, whereas voltage exhibits the greatest effect on surface roughness. Subsequently, multi-response optimization was carried out using the desirability function approach in Minitab software, and optimal levels for each parameter were determined. Overall, the application of a reduced graphene oxide coating on the copper electrode, coupled with process parameter optimization, substantially improves surface quality, enhances the material removal rate, and diminishes tool wear in the machining of X40CrMoV5 steel.

articles.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.16351v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length T, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on [0,T]. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on O(nlog n) windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range O(log N), has expected error O(N⁻b+T⁻¹) while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
