articles.title: Anti-adhesive profile and peritoneal integration of a dynamic scaffold-coupled intraperitoneal shield in a porcine hernia model
articles.abstract: Background Visceral adhesion formation remains an unresolved limitation of intraperitoneal prosthetic hernia repair. The S&S Hernia System (S&S) was developed to address this problem by coupling a defect-obliterating dynamic regenerative scaffold to a reticulated intraperitoneal shield, thereby transmitting cyclical abdominal wall motion from the scaffold to the shield. This study evaluated the temporal behavior of visceral adhesions and characterized the shield–peritoneal interface histologically.Methods Twenty S&S devices were implanted laparoscopically into bilateral abdominal-wall defects in 10 female pigs and assessed at 1, 3–4, or 5–8 months. Serial laparoscopy evaluated shield coverage and adhesions. Haematoxylin and eosin and Azan–Mallory-stained specimens were examined for inflammatory infiltrates, foreign-body reaction, fibrotic encapsulation and tissue organization.Results At 1 month, 2 of 20 shields (10%) had thin adhesion bands; neither was detectable at 3 months. No visceral adhesion involved any shield at explantation. Shield surfaces developed smooth, continuous tissue coverage integrated with the parietal peritoneum. Vascularized collagenous tissue extended through the shield, with a continuous flattened surface lining at 4 months. No morphologically detectable device-associated inflammatory cellular infiltrate was identified in examined sections from 1 month onwards; foreign-body giant cells, granulomatous inflammation and dense fibrotic encapsulation were absent.Conclusion The disappearance of the two early-bands and absence of adhesions on all shields at explantation demonstrated an anti-adhesive profile. Structural integration with the parietal peritoneum without a detectable established inflammatory foreign-body response provided biological context. Dynamic scaffold-to-shield motion is a plausible contributing mechanism that warrants controlled testing as a potentially durable anti-adhesive strategy.

articles.title: Adsorption of Rhodamine B onto Natural Zeolite: Mechanistic Insights, Response Surface Optimization, and Comparative Machine Learning Prediction
articles.abstract: Rhodamine B (RhB) was adsorbed onto an unmodified natural zeolite, and the removal was modeled by response surface methodology (RSM) and by machine learning (ML). X-ray diffraction showed that the zeolite phase is mordenite, with quartz as the main accompanying mineral. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy gave a mean Si/Al ratio of 5.58, and the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area was 26.6 m2/g. The adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second-order model (R2 = 0.980), and equilibrium was reached within 90 min. Among the single-factor experiments, solution pH had the strongest influence: removal decreased from 98.0% at pH 2 to 49.0% at pH 6, as RhB changes from its cationic to its zwitterionic form across its pKa of 3.7. The Langmuir isotherm gave the best fit (R2 = 0.991), with a maximum monolayer capacity of 6.60 mg/g at pH 6. A quadratic RSM model fitted to a three-factor, three-level full factorial design (30 runs) described the data well (R2 = 0.967, predicted R2 = 0.911, p < 0.0001). Support vector regression (SVR), random forest, and extreme gradient boosting were trained on the same dataset and evaluated by leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). SVR gave the highest LOOCV R2 (0.925), but nested LOOCV, which removes the optimistic bias of hyperparameter tuning, lowered it to 0.858, below the value of the RSM model. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) gave the same feature ranking for all three ML models, and this ranking matched the analysis of variance. On this small designed-experiment dataset, the quadratic model predicted as well as the best ML model, and ML served mainly as an interpretive check.

articles.title: Selective Iron Extraction and Ti–V Distribution from Magnetite–Ilmenite Iron Sand via Carbothermic Reduction and Magnetic Separation
articles.abstract: Low-grade iron sand contains iron (Fe), titanium (Ti), and vanadium (V), but their selective recovery is challenging because iron oxides are closely associated with silicate and titanate minerals. This study aimed to optimize coal dosage, reduction temperature, and holding time during carbothermic reduction followed by magnetic separation, and to investigate how mineral phase transformations and metallic iron grain growth affect Fe recovery and Ti–V partitioning. Coal dosage was varied from 10 to 30 wt.% relative to ore mass, reduction temperature from 1000 to 1200°C, and holding time from 30 to 120 min. X-ray fluorescence (XRF) was used to analyze elemental composition, X-ray diffraction (XRD) to identify phase transformations, and scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDS) to characterize microstructural evolution and elemental distribution. Under the optimized conditions of 15 wt.% coal, 1200°C, and 60 min, the process produced a magnetic fraction containing 81.31 wt.% Fe, with an Fe recovery of 82.57% and a metallization degree of 87%. Concurrently, the non-magnetic fraction achieved Ti and V recoveries of 83.56% and 85.12%, respectively. The optimized conditions enabled efficient Fe recovery while controlling Ti and V distribution between the magnetic and non-magnetic fractions.

articles.title: Universal Matrix Multiplication on Quantum Computer
articles.abstract: As the most central and computationally intensive component of deep neural networks, the execution efficiency of matrix multiplication directly determines the training and inference performance of models. Harnessing the parallel processing capabilities afforded by quantum superposition and entanglement to reshape matrix multiplication implementations has become a promising entry point for optimising underlying quantum arithmetic logic and improving the operational efficiency of quantum circuits. This paper proposes a universal quantum matrix multiplication (QMM) framework designed to achieve substantial computational acceleration through an optimised quantum arithmetic logic unit. To circumvent the limitations of multi-register and multi-control gates in conventional quantum arithmetic circuits, we encode classical data directly into parameterised ((R_z)) rotation gates using the quantum Fourier transform (QFT), thereby reducing the base gate complexity of the quantum adder to ((O(n))). In addition, by adopting the column-wise multiplication principle from classical arithmetic, we optimize the gate complexity of the quantum multiplier to ((O(n²))). We further extend this approach to a quantum version of the Strassen algorithm, and experimentally quantify the trade-off between reduced multiplication time and increased overhead in addition resources. This work establishes a reliable technical pathway for constructing general-purpose quantum matrix operations, with the potential to unlock substantial computational power for training modern machine learning models.

articles.title: Metal-organic framework derived cobalt oxides modified by N-doped carbon nanotubes as bifunctional electrocatalyst for Zn-air battery
articles.abstract: Because of high power density, specific capacitance and low cost, Zn-air battery has received great attention. For Zn-air battery, oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are involved in discharging and charging processes. But both ORR and OER suffer from sluggish kinetics, which makes the development of efficient ORR and OER electrocatalysts become an urgent task. Herein, with a Co-based Metal-Organic Framework (MOF) as precursor, bifunctional electrocatalyst is synthesized. In this electrocatalyst, CoO and Co3O4 particles dope in N-doped carbon nanotubes (NCNTs) derived from dicyandiamide (DCDA). In alkaline electrolyte, its half-wave potential (E1/2) and limiting current density (Jd) achieve 0.843 V and 5.59 mA·cm− 2. In OER, the overpotential and Tafel slope are 350 mV and 60.2 mV·dec− 1. Based on the promising ORR and OER activities, Zn-air battery is constructed. Its open-circuit voltage and peak power density reach 1.46 V and 128.2 mW·cm− 2. The specific capacity and energy density of Zn-air battery are 850.63 mAh⋅g− 1 and 1020.72 Wh·kg− 1 at 5 mA·cm− 2. The battery also shows perfect rating capacity and promising long-time charge/discharge performance. This work develops an excellent Co-based bifunctional electrocatalyst as cathode material in Zn-air battery.

articles.title: Can the tunnel magnetoresistance properties of ferritin in avian hair cell organelles generate neural signals like those that cause motion sickness in humans?
articles.abstract: Cuticulosomes are iron-rich organelles in the cuticular plate of avian hair cells that contain tens of thousands of ferritin-like granules, frequently arranged in highly ordered linear arrays. More than a decade after their discovery, no explanation has been established for their function. Recent studies have shown that ferritin supports long-range electron transport, exhibits tunnel magnetoresistance of 25 ± 5% at room temperature, and releases Fe 2+ nonlinearly as electrons accumulate in its core, while other studies have shown that intracellular iron can trigger calcium signaling through redox-sensitive ryanodine receptors. Drawing on these findings, this paper proposes the hypothesis that the ordered ferritin arrays of cuticulosomes use the tunnel magnetoresistive properties of ferritin to redistribute electrons under the Lorentz force generated by movement through the geomagnetic field, causing iron release from ferritin particles at the edge of the array and contributing to hair cell calcium signaling. Because the Lorentz force on an electron or polaron is greatest when the velocity vector is orthogonal to the geomagnetic field and absent when the two are parallel, the mechanism predicts significantly more signaling during east– west travel than during north–south travel. Order-of-magnitude estimates indicate that iron release from a single cochlear cuticulosome could reach approximately 49 µM in a 1 pL cytoplasmic volume, exceeding reported thresholds for calcium signaling in astrocytes and neurons. The resulting signals could resemble the hair cell signals that can trigger motion sickness in humans due to mismatch between visual cues, physical/vestibular cues (from the inner ear), and proprioceptive signals (from muscles and joints), and could discourage east–west travel. Ten experiments are proposed to test the hypothesis.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of SAR and Ein in the Human Head Exposed to Mobile Phone Electromagnetic Radiation
articles.abstract: Mobile phones generate electromagnetic fields during operation, exposing the human head to electromagnetic radiation. Traditional numerical methods are complex and computationally expensive, limiting rapid exposure assessment. This study proposes a 3D U-Net incorporating physics-aware spatial encoding and a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for efficient, flexible assessment of head electromagnetic exposure. First, 3D electromagnetic finite element models of the human head and mobile phone were established. By varying their relative spatial positions, initial 3D point cloud data of SAR10g and induced electric field (Ein) were obtained. Different padding strategies (zero, first-row, and circular padding) were then applied, and the head–phone spatial positions were encoded using physics-aware features. Finally, datasets with different physics-aware encoding methods (6 and 8 channels) trained the 3D CBAM U-Net to determine the optimal network configuration. Results show that zero padding combined with 8-channel physics-aware spatial encoding achieved the best performance, with average relative errors of 0.748% for SAR10g and 1.523% for Ein. Each prediction took only 0.57 s, approximately 51 times faster than the finite-element simulation. The proposed method learns the mapping between phone configurations and electromagnetic responses in the human head, reduces assessment time, and provides an efficient, accurate, generalizable approach.

articles.title: Indole-3-acetic acid regulation of fungal–algal consortia for oxytetracycline removal: Physiological responses, extracellular polymeric substances, and biomass clarification
articles.abstract: Microalgal treatment of antibiotic-containing wastewater is often constrained by physiological stress and the difficulty of biomass separation. This study evaluated the effects of exogenous indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) on a Chlorella vulgaris–Aspergillus oryzae coculture treating synthetic swine wastewater containing oxytetracycline (OTC). An algal monoculture, an IAA-free coculture, and cocultures supplemented with different IAA concentrations were compared over 14 days. Fungal cocultivation increased OTC removal from 48.2% to 74.6%. Supplementation with 10-6 M IAA yielded the highest overall performance, with removal efficiencies of 92.5% for OTC, 91.2% for chemical oxygen demand, 88.5% for total nitrogen, and 89.1% for total phosphorus. This treatment also increased biomass concentration to 3.47 g L-1 and chlorophyll a content to 4.26 mg L-1, accompanied by higher superoxide dismutase and catalase activities and a 48.6% reduction in malondialdehyde content relative to the IAA-free coculture. Extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) content reached 132.04 mg g-1 dry weight, representing a 36.7% increase, while the zeta potential of extracted EPS solutions shifted from −17.45 to −11.36 mV. Clarification efficiency reached 88.2% after 30 min and 93.6% after 60 min. These findings demonstrate that appropriate IAA supplementation can improve wastewater treatment and early-stage biomass clarification, accompanied by coordinated physiological and extracellular responses in fungal–algal consortia.

articles.title: Groundwater Potential and Quality in Rapidly Urbanising Region of Chiplun, Ratnagiri District (Maharashtra, India): A Geo-Statistical and Hydro- Chemical Analysis
articles.abstract: Groundwater is a vital freshwater resource, particularly in regions with seasonal variations in surface-water availability. This study evaluates the groundwater potential and quality of Chiplun Town and its adjoining region in Ratnagiri District, Maharashtra, India, using an integrated approach that considers groundwater occurrence, yield, physicochemical characteristics, and the Water Quality Index (WQI). A total of 182 groundwater samples, comprising 91 monsoon and 91 post-monsoon samples collected during 2023, were analysed for turbidity, pH, TDS, alkalinity, chloride, fluoride, nitrate, sulphate, total hardness, and iron. Groundwater depth generally ranged from 30–80 m below ground level, with several areas showing favourable yields exceeding 800 L/min, indicating considerable groundwater potential. Physicochemical parameters generally fell within BIS drinking-water limits, with only moderate seasonal variation. WQI assessment classified 12 monsoon samples as Excellent and 79 as Good, while post-monsoon samples included 15 Excellent, 75 Good, and one Poor. The mean WQI increased slightly from 29.44 to 30.71, indicating a minor seasonal decline while maintaining predominantly good water quality. Overall, the study demonstrates considerable groundwater potential and generally good groundwater quality in the Chiplun region. The findings provide a scientific basis for groundwater monitoring, recharge-zone protection, controlled abstraction, and sustainable water-resource management.

articles.title: Aeromagnetic and gravity interpretation of basement structure, basin configuration and mineral–hydrocarbon prospectivity in the Okigwe–Afikpo area (sheets 312 and 313), Lower Benue Trough, south-eastern Nigeria
articles.abstract: The Okigwe–Afikpo area (NGSA sheets 312 and 313) lies on the south-western flank of the Abakaliki Anticlinorium in the Lower Benue Trough. Earlier geophysical work there relied largely on aeromagnetic data and gave little attention to structure or to mineral and hydrocarbon prospectivity. This study combines high-resolution aeromagnetic data with a Bouguer gravity grid to describe basement structure and basin configuration at reconnaissance scale. Both datasets were processed in Oasis montaj. The magnetic grid was reduced to the equator and enhanced by regional–residual separation, upward and downward continuation, directional and total horizontal derivatives, the tilt derivative, the analytic signal and the second vertical derivative. The gravity grid received comparable treatment. Depths came from Euler deconvolution, radially averaged power spectra and two-dimensional forward models. The reduced-to-equator anomaly ranges from − 21.8 to 188.2 nT and the Bouguer anomaly from 7.8 to 57.6 mGal. Magnetic lineaments trend mainly NE–SW, with a subordinate E–W set, whereas gravity gradients trend mainly NW–SE and N–S. Magnetic Euler solutions lie between about 296 and 3,265 m, spectral analysis gives deeper sources at 1.7–2.0 km and shallower sources above 0.4 km, and gravity Euler solutions reach more than 2,000 m. Two preliminary profile models place the top of the basement at about 0.1–0.2 km beneath a central high and at more than 1.2–2 km towards the profile ends. The results point to a fault-segmented basin that hosts shallow intrusive bodies. Potential-field data cannot establish source-rock quality, thermal maturity or mineralisation, so the zones identified here are targets for seismic, geochemical and drilling follow-up rather than demonstrated prospects.

articles.title: Comparative analysis of Ferulic Acid from Corn Agro-Waste by alkaline hydrolysis
articles.abstract: Corn agro-waste is an affordable source of ferulic acid (FA), a naturally occurring antioxidant. In this study we compared the release of FA from corn residue using alkaline hydrolysis and optimized its recovery from the most effective method using Response Surface Methodology. Alkaline hydrolysis was used to liberate free FA from corn cob, bran, fiber, and seeds, which were then measured using HPLC. Central Composite Design was used to optimize parameters of corn cob hydrolysis such as temperature, time, sodium hydroxide (NaOH) concentration, and solid-to-solvent ratio. Purified FA was characterized by HPLC, FTIR, NMR, and mass spectrometry. Of all the parts analyzed, the corn cob gave the highest FA release. The quadratic model was significant (p = 0.0001, R² = 0.937), with hydrolysis time the key dominant factor. At the optimum conditions (Time: 33.08 h, Temperature: 30°C, NaOH Concentration: 1.62 M, Solid-to-solvent ratio: 1:50), the practical yield was about 2%w/w. Purified FA had 94% HPLC purity. The study demonstrates the potential of corn cob as a sustainable source of ferulic acid. RSM-assisted optimization combined with a simple purification approach offers a promising strategy for recovering value-added phenolic compounds from agricultural waste.

articles.title: Vertical characteristics of storms on different horizontal extent and reflectivity thresholds over the west coast of India in 2024 during the pre-monsoon and monsoon seasons using C-band radar, INSAT-3D, and reanalysis data
articles.abstract: The vertical profile of radar reflectivity (VPRR) approach is applied to investigate storm intensity across different horizontal scales and at different radar reflectivity (Ze) thresholds from pre-monsoon to monsoon months in 2024 over Thumba using C-band radar. It is observed that the vertical structure of the Ze depends on the horizontal scales and Ze thresholds used in the present study. For example, irrespective of storm size (horizontal extent), the Ze is highest near the surface (~ 2–3 km altitude) and then decreases rapidly with altitude. However, at smaller horizontal scales, Ze peaks at higher altitudes and then decreases with altitude. It is observed that pre-monsoon storms are more intense than monsoon storms, and the intensity difference is smaller at smaller horizontal scales. Within a few months, intense storm activity can develop at small scales with convective intensity similar to other months, when intense storm activity develops only at large horizontal scales. Large-scale storms show greater differences below 4 km altitude than smaller-scale storm activity. On a monthly basis, March- and April-based storms are more vertically intense (higher Ze at higher altitudes) and have greater precipitation echo top heights (ETHs), followed by May and June, though with lower frequency. Pre-monsoon months have more intense individual precipitation hotspots (Ze > 35 dBZ) than monsoon months, and occur over land-dominated areas rather than oceanic ones. July-to September have the weakest and shallower storms (fewer Ze and ETHs). The frequency of intense storms decreases rapidly above 4 km altitude in May and June as the horizontal extension increases; e.g., there is a higher chance in IIVP_storm for the vertically extended and the least and medium horizontal extensions. During the monsoon months, IIVP_storm can be vertically extended, with greater horizontal extension than in the pre-monsoon months, above 9 km altitude. The presence of the Western Ghats (WGs) in the study region strongly affects storm precipitation characteristics, with more severe storms observed on the windward side of the WGs. The reanalysis data reveal that severe storms are linked with moderate Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) and thermodynamic indices, especially during the monsoon months. Numerical modeling of these observations will be the next step to examine how dynamics and thermodynamic features are associated with severe storms across different seasons. The present results provide a quantitative assessment of the vertical structure of storms over Thumba from pre-monsoon to monsoon months, using DWR observations from 2024 for the first time.

articles.title: Coexisting positive and negative ionospheric storms and large-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances over China during the October 2024 geomagnetic storm
articles.abstract: This study combines ground-based GNSS observations, satellite measurements, geomagnetic data, and TIE-GCM simulations to investigate the evolution and driving mechanisms of positive and negative ionospheric storms and large-scale traveling ionospheric disturbances (LSTIDs) over China during the 10–11 October 2024 geomagnetic storm. (a) From the late main phase to the early recovery phase, a low-latitude positive storm coexisted with negative disturbances at higher latitudes, accompanied by enhancement and poleward expansion of the equatorial ionization anomaly (EIA) crest. Around 05:00–06:00 UT, the positive disturbance shifted to midlatitudes, while a negative storm developed at low latitudes. The negative storm was concentrated within 15°-35°N and intensified toward lower latitudes. Within 15°-25°N, the maximum VTEC depletion reached approximately 52 TECU, exceeding 60% of the background value, and the negative storm persisted for about 12.5 h; no sustained negative storm developed within 35°-45°N. COSMIC-2 profiles further revealed a transition from early electron density enhancement to deep depletion, accompanied by an increase in the F2 peak height. Mechanism analysis indicates that nighttime eastward disturbance electric fields and penetration electric fields under undershielding conditions enhanced the fountain effect, while equatorward winds lifted the F layer and reduced plasma loss, jointly producing the positive storm. During daytime, westward disturbance electric fields suppressed plasma supply to the EIA and, together with poleward winds, promoted the development of the negative storm. The absence of widespread O/N₂ depletion suggests that thermospheric compositional change was not the dominant driver of the low-latitude negative storm. (b) Five groups of equatorward-propagating LSTIDs were identified, with phase speeds of 397–662 m/s, periods of 50–64 min, and wavelengths of 1380–2383 km. Their occurrence broadly coincided with enhancements in field-aligned currents and auroral electrojet activity, consistent with excitation by atmospheric gravity waves generated through high-latitude energy and momentum input. These results demonstrate the combined electrodynamic and neutral-atmospheric control of storm-time ionospheric responses and provide observational evidence for magnetosphere-ionosphere-thermosphere coupling over China.

articles.title: Fail-Closed Certification of Multi-Stage AI Policies
articles.abstract: Multi-stage AI systems are deployed as policies, not as isolated predictors. Distribution-free risk-control methods can certify a fixed candidate family, but they leave open a practical question: when may several policies share an ordered testing path, and what must be checked before that order is used? We present Admissible Cascade Envelope via Learn-then-Test (ACE-LTT), a fail-closed framework that derives testing structure from policy semantics. Each constrained loss declares the decision set it concerns, comparability is fixed before test outcomes are observed, and only relations supported by the loss and inference contracts enter a testing chain. If a required premise cannot be verified, the procedure returns a typed refusal rather than a weaker certificate. Under the stated sampling assumptions, ACE-LTT controls the probability of any invalid returned certificate at level (δ) and permits lossless fixed-sequence stopping within admissible chains. With the uniform allocation used here, fewer admissible chains cannot shrink the certified set in a successful execution. In a preregistered Monte Carlo study with known truth, 2.3 million admissible-cover comparisons showed no violation of the predicted set inclusion, and none of 90 validity cells met the failure rule. An edge--cloud wildfire case separates certification validity, family informativeness, and deployment preference.

articles.title: Bacterial Cellulose Nanocrystal Networks in Biodegradable Films: Effects of Matrix Chemistry on Barrier Properties and Disintegration
articles.abstract: Incorporating bacterial cellulose nanocrystals (BCNCs) into biopolymer matrices is a strategy for modifying the functional properties of biodegradable films intended for food packaging applications. In this study, biopolymeric nanocomposite films based on gelatin, pectin, and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) were prepared by incorporating BCNCs obtained through the acid hydrolysis of bacterial cellulose by-products from a wound-dressing biorefinery. BCNCs concentrations were selected to fall below, near, and above the respective theoretical percolation thresholds, corresponding to 5%, 10%, and 15% for gelatin; 4%, 9%, and 14% for pectin; and 3.5%, 8.5%, and 13.5% for HPMC. The films were characterized in terms of optical transmittance, water vapor permeability, wettability, water absorption, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermal stability, and disintegration in natural soil and under composting conditions. Incorporation of BCNCs reduced water vapor permeability in the pectin and HPMC matrices, whereas the reduction observed in the gelatin matrix was not statistically significant. The presence of nanocrystals also reduced the films' moisture content and moderately increased the water contact angle, although all surfaces remained hydrophilic. Even at relatively high BCNCs concentrations, the films maintained high transmittance in the visible region—with values between 97% and 100% at 600 nm—while the incorporation of nanocrystals reduced transmittance in specific ultraviolet spectral regions, particularly in the gelatin and pectin films. FTIR analyses indicated the coexistence of characteristic bands from both the matrices and the BCNCs. The films exhibited high thermal stability, and disintegration behavior was strongly dependent on the nature of the matrix and the BCNCs concentration. Gelatin films underwent complete disintegration in soil, whereas pectin films were more resistant; HPMC films showed intermediate behavior. Under composting conditions, disintegration was accelerated for several formulations. The results demonstrate that the formation and organization of the BCNCs network can simultaneously modify barrier properties, water interaction, and structural stability, while matrix chemistry plays a decisive role in the disintegration behavior of the biopolymeric nanocomposites.

articles.title: Quantum ingenuity can sidestep limits of conventional chips—while using commercially accessible components
articles.abstract: For decades, computers have steadily grown faster and more powerful. Avik Dutt, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Maryland, envisions another dramatic leap forward—one propelled by the quantum properties of light.

articles.title: Laser light reveals where electrons accumulate in atomically thin semiconductor stacks
articles.abstract: Stacking semiconductors—the chips that power phones, computers and so much more—enables quicker signal movement with less energy, but how does the process actually work? Turns out shining a literal light on the semiconducting materials can help elucidate how the electrons move in the stack, according to a multi-institutional team in Japan. The approach could help inform the development of more efficient, low-power electronics, the researchers said.

articles.title: Quantum blueprint maps a practical path to testing unusual entanglement
articles.abstract: Adrian Del Maestro knows how to engineer a quantum fingerprint. Rick Mukherjee has a gift for tuning atoms. Their combined expertise has taken a theory sketched out on paper and created a pathway for real experiments. The results, published in the journal Physical Review Letters, move a law-defying "mathematical oddity" ever so slightly up the technology readiness scale

articles.title: Copper aluminum oxide could make light-controlling components for smart glasses 120 times thinner
articles.abstract: Could augmented reality (AR) glasses become as thin and lightweight as everyday eyeglasses? Researchers at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) and their collaborators have identified a material that could reduce the thickness of polarization-control components to approximately 1/120 that of conventional components while maintaining high light transmission. The discovery could pave the way for smaller, lighter AR devices and more compact optical communication equipment.

articles.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.

articles.title: Band-Selective Coupling to Charge Density Wave Fluctuations in Kagome Superconductors AV3Sb5
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) host multiband superconductivity (SC) within an unconventional charge density wave (CDW) parent phase, yet the relationship between the two remains unresolved. Through time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments on CsV3Sb5 and KV3Sb5, we observe coherent band oscillations driven by coupling to a low-energy CDW amplitude mode at 3.1 THz. We find this coupling to be highly band-selective, differing by a factor of over 2 even between bands with dominant V-3d character. We reproduce these results with frozen-phonon density functional theory calculations, offering insight towards the relation between differing Fermi surface characters and our observed band selectivity. Furthermore, we observe differences in coupling channels between KV3Sb5 and CsV3Sb5. These results establish CDW amplitude mode fluctuations as a band-selective low-energy coupling channel that intimately contributes to the interplay between CDW and SC in the AV3Sb5 compounds.

articles.title: Moiré-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP³) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to 5.5^circ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP³ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above 4^circ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moiré bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching 90%. Our results demonstrate that remote moiré bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.

articles.title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, ϵ_c = Aln rₛ + B + C rₛln rₛ + D rₛ + dots, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients A, B and C are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate D, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is -0.0077880(9) Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of -0.010 Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order rₛ², seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient E₁ sum to (3.653 ± 0.010)× 10⁻³ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient E₂ sum to α²(36π² - 208ln 2 - 221)/(192π⁴) approx -1.433× 10⁻⁴ Ha per electron, where α = (4/9π)¹/³. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at rₛ = 0.5 cannot distinguish between the two estimates of D.

articles.title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute conductivity--shear-modulus cross-property bounds in three-dimensional isotropic two-phase composites using the translation method, and obtain the tightest bounds reported to date. To assess attainability, we perform unit-cell topology optimization on thousands of distinct initial structures and compare optimized designs to the isotropic bounds using an effective-medium approximation that models the macroscopic material as an isotropic assembly of randomly oriented grains. The best jointly performing designs are consistently bicontinuous, triply periodic minimal surface-like microstructures; however, a small but notable gap to the translation bound remains.

articles.title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in γ-InSe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in γ-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of 3.8×10⁻⁶~mathrmcm³,s⁻¹. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in γ-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.

articles.title: Absence of σ-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of σ-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that σ-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called σ-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of σ-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of σ-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.

articles.title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS₂ van der Waals Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS₂ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range 4 le pH le 14 under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range (0 le pH le 14). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40%, well above the 10% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68% under a tensile strain of +6%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS₂ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.

articles.title: Magic-layer scenario for predicting non-van der Waals two-dimensional materials: The case of double-layer honeycomb structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A magic number is a specific size of a van der Waals (vdW) cluster that shows pronounced stability compared to adjacent sizes, and therefore magic clusters are preferentially formed in experiments. We apply the ``magic-layer'' concept to identify non-vdW two-dimensional (2D) materials that are difficult to exfoliate from their parent 3D crystals. As a case, we study the stability of thin films in III-V, II-VI, I-VII, and Mn-based compounds using first-principles calculations. By calculating excess energies for various thicknesses, we find significant stabilization reflecting the formation of double-layer honeycomb structures at specific thicknesses. The stability measure based on the magic-layer concept can distinguish the experimentally synthesized systems from the experimentally unrealized systems, which serves as a key descriptor for predicting the realization of non-vdW 2D materials.

articles.title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems. Quantum simulation provides a complementary approach, although circuit depth and noise limit digital implementations and non-Abelian gauge-matter interactions remain difficult to engineer in analog systems. Here we realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and directly observe its hadronic dynamics using site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This realization is enabled by harnessing two hyperfine states and site-occupation configurations of 87Rb atoms to jointly encode both matter and gauge fields. We tailor resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a gauge sector of a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model with independently tunable mass and gauge coupling. Leveraging this control, we track the conversion of an initially mesonic state into baryonic or vacuum-like configurations through slow mass ramps. Near resonance, we observe coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs and characterize the conversion efficiency as a function of mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. Our realization establishes an atomic platform for non-Abelian gauge dynamics, opening a route to microscopic studies of nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly interacting matter.

articles.title: Towards determination of intrinsic spin properties in MAPbI₃ crystals using spin noise spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin noise spectroscopy in back- and forward-scattering geometries is used to study the spin dynamics of charge carriers in a MAPbI₃ (MA = methylammonium) single crystal. The spectra reveal electrons and holes with different degrees of localization. At low temperatures (T approx 4~K), hole spin relaxation is dominated by the hyperfine interaction with nuclear spins. The broadening of the spectra with increasing temperature can be attributed to thermally activated hopping of localized holes. From the thermal activation energies, we estimate hole localization lengths that are consistent with both the hyperfine-induced dephasing rates and the zero-field frequency shifts measured at low temperature. By contrast, the electron spin dynamics cannot be explained by the hyperfine interaction alone: even at the lowest excitation powers, it is affected by the probe light, and we observe a slowing down of spin relaxation with increasing power. Comparison of the back- and forward-scattered spin noise signals indicates that the spatial distribution of carriers is inhomogeneous: electrons are located preferentially near the crystal surface, weakly localized holes (characterized by slower spin relaxation) are found mostly away from the surface, and strongly localized holes are somewhere in between.

articles.title: Topological Narrow Bands in Twisted Rhombohedral Multilayer Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moiré graphene multilayers provide an atomically thin platform for engineering narrow topological bands through stacking, twist, and electrostatic control. Recent experiments on twisted rhombohedral graphene have revealed a high-Chern-number hierarchy determined by the number of rhombohedral layers. A microscopic description of this hierarchy requires connecting the ideal chiral picture to the realistic electronic structure. Here, we show that the two central moiré bands of twisted monolayer-N-layer rhombohedral graphene originate from hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state located at opposite corners of the moiré Brillouin zone. Increasing N progressively narrows these bands, whereas reversing the displacement field transfers their wave-function weight between the twisted interface and the remote surface. In spectrally isolated regimes, this redistribution switches the lower band between Chern numbers C=N and C=-1. A projected surface theory shows how interfacial tunneling is dressed by virtual propagation through the rhombohedral stack, explaining the field-selected Chern hierarchy and the recurring threefold structure of the real-space charge textures. These results establish layer number and displacement field as complementary nanoscale controls of band flatness, spatial polarization, and topology in graphene moiré heterostructures.

articles.title: Relaxation dynamics of the impurity momentum in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a single mobile impurity coupled by a repulsive contact interaction to a gas of free spinless fermions of equal mass in one dimension. Using the determinant overlaps between the interacting eigenstates and free-fermion states, we derive closed determinant formulas for the matrix elements of the impurity momentum operator and of its square between arbitrary Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of a finite system. At infinite coupling we prove a selection rule: both operators have vanishing matrix elements between distinct eigenstates that share the same rapidity, and every eigenstate carries the per-particle share of the total momentum. For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.

articles.title: Odd Viscosity-Driven Phase Separation in Chiral Active Mixtures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Binary mixtures of active particles spinning in opposite directions can spontaneously separate into homochiral domains, yet the mechanism behind this robust demixing remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a two-fluid hydrodynamic theory that generalizes odd viscosity to multicomponent systems. We show that cross parity-violating viscosities, which couple the stress of one chiral species to the strain rate of another, can destabilize the homogeneous mixture, while odd viscosity within each homochiral domain governs the interfacial stability and dynamics. Microscopic measurements of stress and velocity correlations yield viscosity estimates that predict spontaneous demixing followed by domain coarsening. These findings identify odd viscosity as a route to programming phase behavior and domain morphology in chiral active mixtures.

articles.title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the π-conjugated spacers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nature of the π-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.

articles.title: A macroscopic-atom spectral theory of grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys remains challenging because existing spectral approaches require alloy-specific atomistic calculations to resolve segregation-energy distributions and correlations across non-equivalent boundary sites. Here, we develop a transferable macroscopic-atom spectral theory that predicts the joint segregation behavior of multiple species from physically interpretable elemental descriptors. The theory is founded on the finding that local strain and bond deficit account for 91% of the site-to-site co-variation of 40 solutes in a density-functional-theory (DFT) Al polycrystal. Linked to atomic size and surface enthalpy, these coordinates allow prediction of individual segregation spectra and their cross-species correlations, which determine whether species compete for or share grain-boundary sites. A closed-system formulation unifies host-element redistribution and dilute-solute segregation, couples metallic and light-element sublattices, and accounts for bulk compound formation and solute pairing. Calibrated using binary spectra only, the theory predicts unseen-host spectral means with a correlation coefficient of 0.81, outperforms embedded-atom spectra against DFT benchmarks, and ranks site competition across 870 solute pairs with a Spearman coefficient of 0.90. Without fitting to multicomponent observations, it reproduces 11 of 12 equilibrium Fe ternaries and 49 of 55 Mg ternaries. Predictions recorded before simulations of an 82,699-atom polycrystal identify site competition as the baseline behavior and metal-metalloid pair chemistry as a source of deviations requiring atomistic resolution. These results establish a physically grounded route to screening grain-boundary chemistry in multicomponent alloys, including steels and high-entropy alloys.

articles.title: Reversible Self-Assembly of a P-Ir(100)-P Trilayer on Ir(111)
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adsorbate-induced surface reconstructions offer a route to engineer low-dimensional materials with atomic arrangements and electronic properties fundamentally different from those of their parent substrates. Here, we demonstrate how phosphorus adsorption on Ir(111) drives the formation of an incommensurate P-Ir-P trilayer, in which a square Ir(100)-like atomic lattice emerges from the underlying hexagonal crystal. This transformation illustrates how strong adsorbate-substrate interactions can stabilize unconventional atomic coordination within an ultrathin metallic structure. Remarkably, the process is reversible, allowing the system to switch between distinct structural phases through phosphorus deposition and thermal annealing. The resulting trilayer exhibits a two-dimensional, semimetal-like electronic structure dominated by Ir 5d states. Our findings establish adsorbate-driven symmetry transformation as a strategy for engineering atomically thin transition-metal compounds with structural and electronic properties inaccessible through conventional surface growth.

articles.title: Impact of Taylor-Aris dispersion on chemical patterns in confined channel flows
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemical patterns form through non-linear interactions between different species. We study how confined channel flows affect pattern formation using the Brusselator as a paradigmatic activator-inhibitor model. An invariant-manifold method for slender channels reduces the advection-diffusion-reaction equation to one spatial dimension, with species transported at the mean flow velocity and molecular diffusivities replaced by the classical Taylor-Aris dispersion coefficients. We obtain the phase diagram as a function of the Péclet number (i.e., the relative strength of advection to diffusion), the channel slenderness, and the diffusivity ratio of the species. Our analytical results demonstrate that the classical Turing criterion can become inverted at large Péclet numbers and, thus, channel flow can trigger pattern formation even when the molecular diffusivities violate the classical Turing condition, and conversely destroy pre-existing patterns. Both predictions are confirmed by direct numerical simulations, which show advected stripe patterns, whose wavelength can be predicted by our reduced theory, as well as oscillatory dynamics. These findings highlight that hydrodynamic flows can modify chemical mixing and thereby profoundly affect pattern formation in channel geometries.

articles.title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-frac12 fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.

articles.title: Geometry and topology of DNA defects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: DNA defects arise frequently, either as a result of damage, protein binding or the action of molecular enzymes such as an RNA polymerase. Here we combine geometry, atomistic simulations and an analysis of real DNA structures to provide a quantitative characterisation of DNA defects and their dynamics. The composite order parameter describing defects geometrically is a backbone-to-base polar vector, together with a quaternion capturing 3D base orientation in a single strand. There are three types of defects: flips of the polar vector, stacking defects of bases, and composite defects encompassing both. All types of defects feature in realistic structures for DNA and have functional relevance. Additionally, biased molecular dynamics simulations of DNA with an imposed elastic deformation form flip or stacking defects whose abundance and dynamics strongly depend on sequence and type of deformation. Our results provide a link between geometry and biochemistry, and could also be applied, for instance, to identify defects in RNA molecules and nucleosome arrays.

articles.title: Local Thermodynamic Reconstruction of Impurity Entropy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resolving the thermodynamic entropy associated with a local impurity in a spatially extended interacting quantum bath remains a numerical challenge. We develop a Local-Maxwell approach that reconstructs the impurity entropy from local observables in worldline quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. By integrating their temperature responses along the impurity coupling, the method avoids separate estimates of extensive entropies. For nonnegative worldline expansions with bounded local couplings, we establish bath-size independent bounds on all factorial moments of the impurity vertex count. For even vertex counts, the Maxwell estimator variance remains bounded as the coupling approaches zero. The transverse-field Ising benchmark reproduces exact free fermion results, while an interacting XXZ chain demonstrates up to several hundredfold improvement in statistical efficiency over conventional extensive thermodynamic integration. In a three-channel XXZ impurity junction, we reveal entropy recovery upon cooling and a nonmonotonic coupling dependence of the finite-temperature entropy contrast. These results establish local thermodynamic reconstruction as an efficient approach to impurity entropy in interacting quantum baths.

articles.title: Reliability of Language-Model Judges for Quantitative Scientific Question Answering: Evidence from Perovskite Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented language models increasingly relies on automated model judges, yet their reliability on quantitative scientific synthesis remains largely unmeasured. Here, we evaluate automated grading on a quantitative benchmark for perovskite photovoltaics, where all 755 ground-truth answers are deterministically computed from 45,441 experimental device records. We evaluate a frontier judge (Claude Opus 5.5) alongside two local open-weight judges (Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-8B) across 4,530 free-text answers from six retrieval architectures under three regimes: reference-augmented (with the computed key), evidence-augmented (with retrieved passages and query logs), and unassisted (question and answer alone). Equipped with the reference key, Claude Opus reproduces ground truth near-perfectly (Cohen's κ = 0.982 ± 0.003) and preserves exact architectural rankings (τ = 1.00). Withholding the reference causes evaluation fidelity to collapse: frontier agreement drops to κ = 0.557 ± 0.022, and providing retrieved literature passages yields virtually no improvement (κ = 0.576 ± 0.024). Without reference keys, local judges degrade to near-random agreement (κ = 0.087 and 0.112), inverting the leaderboard to rank a hallucinating closed-book baseline first (τ le 0.20). Furthermore, SQL-augmented generations induce severe evaluative blind spots: absent a reference, the frontier judge accepts 46.6% of erroneous SQL answers, overestimating architecture accuracy as 66.4% against its true 52.6%. These findings demonstrate that model-based evaluation in the physical sciences cannot rely on unstructured text inspection; rigorous benchmarking requires reference ground truth precomputed from structured measurement records.

articles.title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.

articles.title: Constructing physical mechanisms with artificial intelligence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mechanisms recur across the sciences: the equation for heat in a solid also describes molecular diffusion or a Brownian particle. A mechanism is rarely written in one equation; its operation, boundaries, parameters and closures are stated at different steps of a derivation, where methods that read text or fit formulas miss it. We built an equation-native system that reads the equations of all 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts, and show that mechanisms can be compiled from them and constructed by deterministic calculation. A constructor detaches, transfers, unfolds, composes and joins their parts across disciplines; where parts do not fit, the failure is an equation for the missing term. Constructions turn a threshold reactor into a memory that a weak signal writes, an oscillator into a switch through two changes that each fail alone, and a rhythm into the regulator of a chemical amount, each with conditions for an experimental test.

articles.title: Emission regimes and characteristic energy scales in reverse-biased 4H-SiC Schottky barriers: unified field-emission formulas and energy-dependent tunneling effective mass
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reverse leakage in 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes is analyzed using a current integral with Fermi-Dirac supply and WKB transmission. The ratio of the interface field to a critical field F_c sets the depth of the thermionic-field-emission (TFE) saddle point. The Airy energy distinguishes the thermionic-tunneling crossover, the validity of the TFE formula, and the TFE/field-emission (FE) boundary, which generalizes to c₁ k_B T approx 1 for arbitrary barrier shapes. Closed-form FE and TFE expressions are given for triangular and quadratic barriers; for the latter, the Padovani-Stratton formulas give 1.4-7.9 times (FE, 10¹⁹ cm⁻³) and 2.5-3.6 times (TFE, low-doped layers, 300-433 K) the WKB current, whereas the present expressions agree within 15% and 2%. Applied to Ti/4H-SiC data (30-160 degC, 50-950 V), an energy-dependent tunneling mass from the complex band structure reduces the residual from 0.17 to 0.11-0.12 dex; it can be implemented in device simulation via the Franz two-band dispersion.

articles.title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32325v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resolving local atomic structures such as defects and interfaces from electron microscopy contrast relies heavily on researcher judgement, leading to low efficiency and subjective standards. Here we present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided and expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that turns one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable capabilities by updating executable operators, parameters and routing rules with versioned inheritance. Given researcher-defined tasks, the system selects analysis paths from image features without expert labels, while testing and inheriting code updates under fixed budgets. Combining physical priors with expert feedback improves atomic point-defect detection over larger models and raises cross-material interface coverage from 5.13% to 72.11% within a 10% area budget. Adapting the framework to micrographs from unseen studies further separates touching nanoparticles by aligning optimization with particle-level measurements. This work moves computational microscopy beyond standalone models and static scripts towards self-evolving platforms that accumulate human scientific expertise

articles.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges c and 26-c. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.

articles.title: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard (JCH) model describes the interaction of light and matter in coupled optical cavities and provides a framework for studying their quantum dynamics. In this work, we design a Trotterized quantum circuit to investigate the real-time dynamics of the JCH model using Bosonic Qiskit and a Matrix Product State (MPS) backend. We simulate single-polariton transport and benchmark site occupations against exact diagonalization results. We then extend the simulations to the two-excitation sector under a hard-core photon constraint, examining excitation transport and symmetry properties. Finally, we study the dependence of bipartite entanglement entropy on the inter-cavity photon-hopping strength. The results illustrate how hybrid qubit-boson circuits, simulated with matrix product states, can be used to study light-matter lattice dynamics. This work provides a numerical benchmark for extending hybrid simulation approaches to more complex interacting and open light-matter systems.

articles.title: Dirac Propagation for Simulating Fermionic Observables under Particle-Number-Conserving Unitaries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating the dynamics of interacting fermions remains a central computational challenge across physics and chemistry. We introduce Dirac propagation, a classical method that simulates local observables in fermionic systems subject to particle-number-conserving unitaries. We show that, in the operator expansion, strings with weights above the total particle number can be discarded without incurring any error in the final expectation value. This exact cutoff bounds the number of retained strings polynomially in the number of modes at fixed particle number, including for interacting dynamics. The formalism combines a compact representation with explicit expressions for interacting gates and exact treatment of number-conserving fermionic Gaussian and Clifford unitaries. This framework offers an approach to simulating fermionic many-body dynamics and classically benchmarking fermionic quantum circuits.

articles.title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by 6r_S, independently of the discretization order, where r_S is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to 2²⁶ points. For Rayleigh-Bénard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.

articles.title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Superfluids, in a spinning-down container with pinning centres, exhibit sudden collective migration of quantized vortices. The onset, progress, and termination of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we show that: 1) the first exodus of vortices occurs when a sector of the vortex array, having a minimum opening angle, is vacated close to the wall; 2) driven by this exodus, the superfluid flow near the boundary continually decreases in strength and arrests the exit; and 3) the resultant depletion region has well-defined dimensions---governed primarily by the critical unpinning velocity, the container size, and the initial rotation rate---that limit the angular momentum transferred to the container. We conclude by discussing the relevance to pulsar glitches.

articles.title: Robust growth of α-tantalum on sapphire at room temperature using atomically thin titanium seed layer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33112v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tantalum (Ta) based superconducting circuits have attracted attention for their low microwave loss. However, reproducible growth of high-quality α-phase Ta films remains challenging because film properties are highly sensitive to growth conditions. We present a robust, room-temperature route for α-Ta growth on sapphire substrates using an ultrathin Ti seed layer, which significantly widens the accessible deposition parameter space. We compare this approach to Ta films grown at high temperature without a seed layer and at room temperature with a Nb seed. We assess films using structural and surface characterization and quantify microwave loss with coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonators measured in the quantum regime. We obtain two-level-system (TLS)-limited quality factors comparable to the state of the art for Ta-on-sapphire CPW resonators with similar geometries. In addition, temperature-dependent measurements reveal that high-temperature-grown films and films subjected to extended buffered-oxide etch treatment exhibit additional temperature activated loss, highlighting the role of growth route and post-processing in microwave performance. Our results establish ultrathin seed-layer engineering as a reliable alternative route to reproducible, low-loss α-Ta films and motivate closer study of the interfacial mechanisms that govern Ta phase formation.

articles.title: Accessing Excitation of Many-body Systems via Single-Mode Approximation within Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2312.08626v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the single-mode Approximation (SMA) into quantum Monte Carlo simulations to provides an efficient and fast method to obtain the dynamical dispersion of quantum many-body systems. Based on stochastic series expansion (SSE) and its projector algorithms, the SMA + SSE method can simply extract the dispersion of the dynamical dispersion in the long wave-length limit and the upper bound of the dispersion elsewhere, without external calculations and high technique barriers. Meanwhile, numerical analytic continuation methods require the fine data of imaginary time correlations and complex programming. Therefore, our method can approach the excitation dispersion of large systems, e.g., we take the two-dimensional Heisenberg model on a 512 × 512 square lattice. We demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method with high precision via additional examples. We also demonstrate that SMA combined with SSE goes beyond spin-wave theory with numerical results. We further illustrate that SMA is able to extract useful information in strongly correlated systems with competing states.

articles.title: Time arrow in open-boundary one-dimensional stochastic dynamics: effects of discrete thermal kicks over temperature interface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.09145v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Does nonequilibrium characteristics exhibit in one-dimensional open-boundary stochastic systems? We introduce a discrete-timestep stochastic model, where the particle dynamics follows a discrete overdamped stochastic equation, and thermal kicks are presented over discrete timesteps. These thermal kicks are derived from a position-dependent temperature profile with a sharp interface. The discrete characteristic and the Itô-type stochastic scheme make our model distinct from the conventional discussions of an overdamped colloidal model. Under the open-boundary condition, one cannot observe any net probability current in the nonequilibrium steady state (NESS). On the other hand, the nonequilibrium nature of this system can be extracted through the asymmetry in forward and backward transition probabilities, as is reported in this work through the simulation and theoretic analysis. In particular, our result shows prominent time irreversibility near the temperature interface. We propose a hidden-gyration scenario that demonstrates the source of irreversibility, while the collapse of gyrations on the one-dimensional coordinate accounts for the absence of probability current.

articles.title: Time irreversibility and entropy production in non-Hermitian Model A field theories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.11450v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a systematic framework to quantify irreversibility in scalar Model A field theories with a generic non-Hermitian term driving the dynamics. Using the stochastic path-integral formalism, we perform a controlled small-noise expansion, allowing the computation of the entropy production rate (EPR) and violations of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). We show that the local EPR is entirely determined by the anti-Hermitian part of the linearised Langevin equation. Around steady states, the non-Hermitian component produces linear corrections to FDT violations and contributes quadratically to the EPR. As an illustration of the applicability of our approach, we analyse a minimal non-Hermitian extension of the Ginzburg-Landau ψ⁴ theory describing a non-reciprocal Ising model at coarse-grained scales, for which we obtain explicit expressions of the local EPR, showing that it localises at interfaces in non-uniform states. Our results provide a general characterisation of TRS breaking in non-Hermitian scalar field theories.

articles.title: AutoXRD: Autonomous Large Language Model Agents and Comprehensive Evaluation for Powder X-Ray Diffraction Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.00070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) is a foundational technique for structural and phase characterization in materials science, yet automating its analysis and evaluating it end-to-end remains challenging. Doing so requires an agent to interpret diffraction patterns, run refinement software, manage strongly coupled parameters in a physically meaningful order, and assess both numerical fit quality and physical validity. We propose AutoXRD, an LLM agent framework that organizes powder XRD analysis into refinement stages, uses diffraction diagnostics to select actions, and checks the resulting fits against crystallographic and physical criteria. We further introduce XRDBench with two complementary tracks. XRDBench-QA contains 100 tasks assessing scientific reasoning and decision-making, whereas XRDBench-E2E contains 34 end-to-end workflows requiring data interpretation, crystallographic software execution, iterative refinement, evidence preservation, and reporting. Across 1,340 runs of ten recent LLMs, models average only 57.8 out of 100, falling from 61.9 on XRDBench-QA to 53.7 on XRDBench-E2E. At the task level, they perform best on refinement-history assessment and result acceptance, but remain substantially weaker on refinement-action selection, phase quantification, indexing, and Rietveld refinement. Among individual models, GPT-5.6 Sol achieves the highest overall score of 81.1, GPT-5.6 Terra scores highest on XRDBench-E2E (81.0), and GPT-5.6 Luna provides the best score-cost trade-off. Moreover, ablations confirm that all six AutoXRD components consistently improve performance. Finally, execution-trace analysis reveals recurring failures in coupled-parameter control, quantitative reasoning, evidence preservation, and workflow termination, motivating stronger scientific constraints, uncertainty quantification, and more efficient planning.

articles.title: Foundations of Many-Body Theory of Quantum Unified Statistics: Green functions and Linear Response Theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.05878v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a comprehensive many-body theory for systems of particles obeying quantum unified statistics, or quons. After exploring the properties of the Fock space of this system, we formulate a systematic S-matrix expansion and a generalized Wick's theorem.
