A consistent Green-function formalism is constructed at both zero and finite temperatures, accompanied by a generalized Wick's theorem appropriate for infinite-statistics operator algebras. Within this framework, we establish diagrammatic rules for interacting quon systems. Employing the random phase approximation, we derive the dielectric function and reveal the emergence of anomalous plasmon modes that have no direct counterpart in conventional Bose or Fermi systems. We further analyze the ground-state energy, energy-loss function, generalized Thomas-Fermi screening wave vectors, and Friedel oscillations, elucidating how infinite statistics qualitatively modifies collective behavior and screening properties.

articles.title: Categorical classification of non-Fermi liquids in 2+1 dimensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25713v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A defining feature of non-Fermi liquids is a lack of the quasiparticle peak on the Fermi surface in the spectral function, which is usually realized by coupling a finite density of fermions with critical collective fluctuations. However, these features of the two- and three-point vertex functions are qualitatively the same across many non-Fermi liquids, which has made it difficult to classify them beyond the definition by negation. We point out that the four-point function in the pairing channel contains rich information that positively differentiates distinct types of non-Fermi liquids. Using the generalized notion of fixed points that captures scale-dependent universal pairing interaction, we provide a non-perturbative classification of 2+1-dimensional non-Fermi liquids. In the large Fermi momentum limit with fixed dimensionless couplings, metals coupled with long-wavelength critical fluctuations are classified into seven superuniversality classes. Each of them exhibits a unique phase diagram in the space of temperature and bare four-fermion coupling. The present work generalizes the earlier perturbative classification to strongly interacting non-Fermi liquids by leveraging kinematic constraints.

articles.title: Enhanced SiV-phonon coupling in dissipation-diluted diamond nanomechanics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.

articles.title: Hierarchical Deep Research for Physically Grounded System-Level Materials Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.18303v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Designing multicomponent materials systems requires evidence on composition, interfaces, processing and deviceoperation that is scattered across the literature. Language-model research agents can collect this evidence, but their reports are seldom tested against physics. Here we show that Deep Tree of Research, a hierarchical multi-agent system built on locally deployable open-weight language models, ranks first among 47 agents in blinded evaluationacross 27 nanomaterials and device topics. Candidates from local agents outperform those from the best commercial systems on nine of ten first-principles simulation metrics across five design tasks. In a sensing case study, the agent nominated a fluorinated silver-nanoparticle/MXene architecture for the short-chain pollutant perfluoropentanoic acid; after an expert replaced the anchor with an amine, fabricated sensors respond selectively and reproduciblyintap water, consistent with interfacial calculations. Hierarchical research agents can therefore turn dispersed literatureinto experimentally testable materials hypotheses under human supervision.

articles.title: Approximate Decoherence, Recoherence and Records in Isolated Quantum Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.19703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the framework of decoherent histories, we study which past events leave detectable records in isolated quantum systems under the realistic assumption that decoherence is approximate and not perfect. Using tools from quantum state discrimination, we establish asymptotically for a large class of (pseudo-)random histories how the strength of decoherence changes the number of reliable records, i.e., we quantitatively answer the question: when can approximate decoherence be approximated by exact decoherence? In addition, we reveal a clear decoherence structure for long histories based on a numerically exact solution of a random matrix model that, as we argue, captures generic aspects of decoherence. In particular, we observe strong recoherences for maverick histories that are statistical outliers with respect to Born's rule. From the perspective of the Many Worlds Interpretation, our results reveal a "branch selection problem" and shed light on the emergence of Born's rule and the theory confirmation problem.

articles.title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures of Compact Extra Dimensions and Their Detectability with Third-Generation Interferometers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate gravitational-wave dynamics in theories of gravity formulated in D=4+N dimensions, with matter localized on a four-dimensional brane or coupled to the effective four-dimensional metric obtained after compactification. We consider four representative geometries, namely toroidal and Calabi--Yau compactifications, and the warped Randall--Sundrum I and II models, which cover the principal discrete and continuous Kaluza--Klein spectra. We derive the modifications of binary dynamics, propagation, quasinormal modes and polarization content, and use them as a feasibility screening for third-generation interferometers, with particular attention to the Einstein Telescope. The screening shows that the direct effects of the heavy Kaluza--Klein towers are strongly suppressed and are expected to be inaccessible to third-generation detectors. Indeed, the effective-field-theory corrections scale as (hbarω/m₁c²)²sim10⁻²³--10⁻²², while the explicit conservative inspiral-phase correction of RS2 remains below the ET measurability threshold over the region allowed by laboratory bounds. Nevertheless, the screening identifies additional phenomenological channels that may remain testable: a tidal-charge deformation of the black-hole background, which shifts the QNM frequencies and damping times; a continuum-inspired phase deformation; and a radion-induced scalar polarization. We treat these channels as phenomenological benchmarks and formulate a Fisher-matrix Monte Carlo forecast based on the Earth-fixed geometry of the candidate sites, comparing the triangular and double-L Einstein Telescope configurations within an idealized common-noise setting.

articles.title: Constraints on Finsler cosmology from observational data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate current constraints and conditional detectability of Finslerian ΛCDM (FΛCDM) cosmology using supernova, cosmic chronometer (CC), and baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data. We adopt PantheonPlus SH0ES, CC and BAO data with a free acoustic scale. Supplementary tests with DES supernovae and PantheonPlus without SH0ES absolute calibra?tion verify result robustness. We compare FΛCDM model against ΛCDM and wCDM and find that FΛCDM improves the fit compared to ΛCDM, but the degree of fit is not superior to that of the wCDM model with the same number of parameters. We find that the background variations introduced by FΛCDM can be absorbed to some extent by ΛCDM through adjusting its own parameters. We then use parametric bootstrap calibration and Monte Carlo power estimation to assess the detection power of residual background deviation that ΛCDM cannot absorb. We find no statistically significant ev?idence for a residual background deviation in the main data configuration. For an injection background fixed at the maximum likelihood estimate, the conditional detection power is relatively low. We examine the sensitivity of the detection power of this signal to the injected background. We find that the detection power of this deviation is significantly dependent on the injection context.

articles.title: Modeling of Chemically Reactive Gas Flows for Multi-Scale Problems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate modeling of chemical reactions plays a key role in the investigation of high-temperature flows. The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method provides highly accurate solutions for such flows. However, its computational cost becomes prohibitive for low Knudsen regimes. Particle-based continuum methods employing the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) or Fokker-Planck approximations have gained increasing attention in recent years, improve computational efficiency in low-Knudsen regimes by modeling relaxation processes rather than binary collisions, while retaining the particle approach that enables straightforward coupling with DSMC. In the last years, different continuum-based models in the open-source particle code PICLas have been extended to simulate gas mixtures with internal energy modes. The present work focuses on modeling of chemically reactive gas mixtures in the Ellipsoidal Statistical BGK model. Model accuracy is assessed for two test cases of a reactive gases confined in a reservoir.

articles.title: Critical ocean physics on the edge of AMOC instability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is expected to weaken under global warming, but whether this signifies a transient response or a tipping transition remains unclear. Distinguishing between these cases requires a physical understanding of the boundary separating ocean states leading to AMOC recovery from those leading to collapse. In a global ocean model with 1deg resolution, we compute an AMOC edge state -- an unstable saddle equilibrium that anchors this instability boundary. The edge state maintains weak overturning sourced by marginal deep water formation in the Nordic Seas. Analyzing the North Atlantic freshwater and heat balances that govern the edge state dynamics, we show that near the edge state, thermal and haline components of the surface buoyancy flux approximately compensate. Surface buoyancy loss (gain) coincides with AMOC recovery (collapse). Our findings support using the regional net surface buoyancy flux as an indicator for the onset of AMOC tipping.

articles.title: Ultra-Wideband Stacked Patch Antenna for D-Band Applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article proposes a wideband stacked dual-patch antenna designed for D-band applications. The antenna is demonstrated with both wireless and dielectric waveguide (DWG) channels. The patch dimensions and spacings are chosen to ensure that the 10~dB return loss (RL) bandwidth covers the entire D-band (110--170~GHz). The antenna is fabricated on a seven-layer organic packaging technology. The patches are fabricated on layers 1 and 3 within a shielding cavity formed by closely spaced vias of < λ/20 pitch. The fabrication technology supports direct chip-level excitation of the antenna using a flip-chip packaging interface, and the design methodology for this feeding approach is outlined in the paper. In the fabricated design, however, a transition to the WR6 metallic waveguide with (<~1~dB) insertion loss (IL) is incorporated for feeding. This facilitates alignment and measurement of the structure using external test equipment. The full antenna and transition are integrated in a back-to-back configuration, achieving a measured 10~dB return loss bandwidth of more than 60~GHz (110--170~GHz) for the wireless link, thereby covering the entire D-band. To the best of our knowledge, this is the widest antenna bandwidth reported in the same frequency range. The measured peak gain is 8.5~dBi (35^circ H-plane 3~dB beamwidth) with a gain variation of 3.5~dBi within the operating bandwidth. For the dielectric waveguide configuration, the measured 10~dB RL bandwidth also exceeds 60~GHz, fully encompassing the D-band. The simulated insertion loss coupling into the dielectric waveguide is 3.5~dB. A 1-meter dielectric waveguide channel fed with the proposed antenna is measured. The overall channel exhibits a total insertion loss of 14.7~dB, of which a simulated 3.5~dB at 140~GHz is attributed to the loss of each side that feeds the DWG.

articles.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm² and 66 kA/cm² for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um² and 3 x 10 um², respectively. The specific contact resistance for base is estimated 1.32 x 10⁻² Ohm.cm². The open-base breakdown voltage is characterized ~63 V for a 300 nm collector without dielectric passivation. This work lays the foundation for future development of N-polar III-Nitride HBTs for next-generation RF applications.

articles.title: Phase matching of high-order harmonics driven by a combined coherent and bright squeezed vacuum field
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) driven by non-classical light provides new insights into light-matter interactions and paves the way to quantum attosecond spectroscopy. Achieving phase matching is vital for generating bright HHG sources, while it has received comparatively limited attention in quantum-light-driven HHG. In this work, we investigate the phase matching of HHG driven by an intense coherent field combined with a weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) field, using a semiclassical ensemble of coherent-field realizations sampled from the Husimi-Q probability distribution. We reveal the physical mechanism behind the distinct pressure dependence of the harmonic yields for odd, even and half-integer sidebands spectral components, as observed in our previous experiment [arXiv:2607.20941]. The simulations and phase-matching model demonstrate that the BSV-induced perturbation of the electron action phase could introduce an additional sub-cycle phase mismatch, such that the amplitude of sub-cycle bursts could be significantly modified by gas pressure after macroscopic propagation, even when the harmonic yield is near the optimum. The resulting amplitude asymmetry of sub-cycle bursts leads to a significant intensity contrast between half-integer sidebands harmonics, manifesting as distinct pressure dependence of their yields. Our findings reveal the phase-matching mechanism in two-color quantum-light-driven HHG, and suggest opportunities for macroscopic control of the non-classical HHG source.

articles.title: Electron versus positron impact ionization of inner shells of heavy atoms: distortion, exchange and relativistic effects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triple differential cross sections are presented for electron and positron impact ionization of the K shells of Cu, Ag, Au and U and the L shells of Ag. Relativistic effects are important throughout. For positrons the recoil maximum is suppressed and the recoil-region spin asymmetry changes sign; for the 2s shell the binary peak changes. In symmetric geometry, where theory reproduces the measured absolute electron cross section, the positron peak lies on the other side of zero recoil. Measurements would test relativistic ionization theory in a regime that electron experiments cannot reach.

articles.title: Streaming instabilities and electron transport in electron transpiration cooling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron transpiration cooling requires emitted electrons to travel through a surrounding plasma, where their relative motion with background electrons can drive streaming instabilities. We investigate these instabilities using particle-in-cell simulations with Monte Carlo collisions in a finite helium plasma. Lower neutral densities show pronounced wave activity, while higher densities give smoother electron distributions. A multifluid model constructed from simulated velocity distributions captures the frequency scale and decay direction in selected cases, but underestimates the separate driving and absorbing responses of electron populations. Distinguishing fast and slow emitted electrons and normalizing the field amplitude by the expanding two-peak length improves the low-wavenumber growth comparison, while discrepancies remain. Spatial growth estimates show that finite propagation distance also limits amplification. Strong late-time current fluctuations can coexist with nearly complete mean anode collection. These findings connect streaming instability to electron transport in the cooling model and show both the usefulness and limitations of a fluid description.

articles.title: Noncontact Chemical and Morphological Profiling in Liquid via Fiber-Based Micro-FTIR
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liquid-phase mid-infrared (MIR) imaging is challenging due to the strong MIR light absorption of most liquid media. Existing liquid-phase MIR microscopy approaches overcame the background absorption using predominantly either ultrathin liquid cells or attenuated total reflection (ATR) setups. However, these designs introduce additional challenges, such as sample confinement, limited probe volume, probe perturbation, and/or lack of quantification capabilities. In this work, a fiber-based Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) microspectroscopy method was developed to overcome the technical barriers of liquid-phase MIR characterization. By integrating a tapered fiber microprobe, a transmission-based optical setup, and a scanning stage, we achieved noncontact chemical and morphological profiling in liquid. The micro-FTIR capabilities were benchmarked by measuring a micropatterned photoresist substrate in water, obtaining quantitative spatial chemical distribution and morphological profiles with ~35 μm lateral resolution and nanometer-scale vertical detection limit. This noncontact, quantitative, liquid-phase micro-FTIR technique is promising for non-perturbative characterization of heterogeneous structures in liquids.

articles.title: Cavitation inception delayed by structured surface roughness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cavitation inception over structured rough surfaces is investigated experimentally in the diverging section of a Venturi. The diverging wall carries laser-etched checkerboards of square cavities with roughness aspect ratios 0.03 ≤ k/d ≤ 0.72, tested at a Reynolds number of 95 160. Inception cavitation numbers were measured together with high-speed shadowgraphs of the near-wall flow, from which upstream-migrating nuclei were tracked and vapor-masked velocity fields were obtained by optical flow. Smooth walls recessed by the etched volume served as a control. The roughness delays inception, most strongly at intermediate k/d, where the inception cavitation number falls from 4.07 on the smooth wall to 3.33-3.46, whereas the recessed walls show no delay. The supply of nuclei is similar on all surfaces, so the delay does not come from a lack of nuclei. Instead, the roughness changes the near-wall flow. For 0.08 ≤ k/d ≤ 0.444, a mean reverse-flow layer forms along the wall beneath a lifted shear layer, and vapor at inception appears further from the throat and away from the wall. At k/d = 0.72 the flow reverses only intermittently and the delay is smaller. On all surfaces except k/d = 0.08, the local cavitation number at inception varies linearly with the near-wall fluctuation energy, consistent with nuclei activated by pressure excursions about 6-8 times the r.m.s. fluctuation. The roughness thus delays inception not by limiting the nuclei, but by weakening the near-wall fluctuations that reach them.

articles.title: Elastic rebound in viscous fluid: an efficient rigid--elastic splitting with an asymptotic gap model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and test a model for an elastic body that falls under gravity onto the bottom of a container filled with a viscous incompressible fluid and rebounds without topological contact. The body is a rigid body plus a small, quasi-static elastic deformation, represented by a fixed compliance operator. In the near-contact patch, the thin fluid film is described by a Reynolds equation with cavitation. This allows the use of coarse meshes that need not resolve the gap, enabling efficient simulation. The film is coupled implicitly to the elastic surface displacement and to the rigid normal motion. The bulk fluid is coupled monolithically to the rigid body. For the axisymmetric case with vertical translation, the coupled step reduces exactly to a small dense nonlinear problem for the film pressure, with the bulk eliminated through a 2x2 affine map. The model is implemented in NGSolve and compared with the experiments of Hagemeier et al. (2021) and the Eulerian FSI simulations of Wahl et al. (2021a). For a PTFE ball the approach agrees with the Eulerian FSI to 1%. For a soft rubber ball (St approx 120) the purely elastic model gives about three times the measured rebound. Material damping is the most important missing effect: a Kelvin--Voigt compliance with loss factor tanδ=0.6 gives 4.0,mm, against 4.4,mm measured. A planar version of the model is compared with the recently published 2D benchmark of Corti et al. (2026). The radius of the film patch is the only numerical parameter of the splitting. It is fixed by one a-priori rule for all configurations, derived from a dry Hertz estimate of the approach, and the results depend only weakly on it.

articles.title: Tweezing microparticles by tightly focused optical skyrmionic fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The concept of skyrmions, once translated to the optical domain, provides a topological framework to investigate structured light-matter interactions. However, their practical use for the manipulation of material systems remains barely explored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate trapping and tunable orbital motion of dielectric microparticles in tightly focused skyrmionic polarization textures prepared using a compact spin-orbit optical element. We explore the tweezing capabilities at fixed topology either by varying the relative weights of the orthogonally polarized components or by switching between skyrmion and bimeron polarization textures. Vectorial focusing and optical-force calculations qualitatively reproduce the experimental observations. These results motivate extending skyrmionic light to the manipulation of micro-objects, including birefringent and chiral samples.

articles.title: Perturbation of CO A1Π by a3Π should have been undetectable: detection, mechanism, and surprises
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A direct perturbation between the a³Π and A¹Π vibrational levels of two electronic states that belong to the same electronic configuration of the carbon monoxide molecule should be unobservably weak because the vibrational overlap integral langle a³Π,v' mid A¹Π,v'' rangle for their near-degenerate levels is extremely small. Yet level-shift and transition-intensity signatures of the a³Π(v = 13) sim A¹Π(v = 2) perturbation are unmistakably present in the ¹³C¹⁸O isotopologue. A detailed study of, among others, the A¹Π - X¹Σ⁺(2, 0), B¹Σ⁺ - A¹Π(0, 2), and C¹Σ⁺ - A¹Π(0, 2) spectra, obtained by the VUV- and Vis-FT complementary techniques in the energy regions of the six crossing points (e- and f-symmetry, |Ω| = 0, 1, 2) between the a³Π(v = 13) and A¹Π(v = 2) states, reveal that the perturbation pathways are indirect, primarily facilitated by the e³Σ⁻(v = 4) state, and that quantum mechanical interferences via its F1e and F3e components occur.

articles.title: Quantum Tautochrone for photons and atoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The tautochrone problem, in which the travel time to a common point is independent of the starting position, has served as a foundational model in classical mechanics. Here we establish its quantum counterpart in engineered photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices, where nonuniform couplings drive photons and particles launched from different positions to converge simultaneously at a common site. Using higher-order correlation functions, we show that this quantum tautochrone effect holds for both bosons and fermions, with quantum statistics governing the character of the convergence: bosons converge onto the same site, while fermions, constrained by Pauli exclusion, gather at neighboring sites. For bosonic atoms, we further show how the tautochrone dynamics is shaped by lattice inhomogeneity, phase-space structure, and on-site interactions.

articles.title: Dynamic tuning of anisotropy-induced quasi-bound-states-in-the-continuum in liquid-crystal integrated dielectric metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry-protected quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs) in all-dielectric metasurfaces can be excited either by introducing a geometrical asymmetry into the unit cell or by illuminating the metasurface under oblique incidence. To date, tuning the coupling strength of such qBICs to the continuum has mainly relied on control of the geometrical asymmetry. Here, we show that qBICs can also be induced in a symmetric dielectric metasurface by embedding the latter into an anisotropic birefringent medium, and that they can be actively tuned by either rotating the anisotropy axis of the medium or by varying the degree of anisotropy. We experimentally implement a corresponding system by embedding a highly symmetric silicon nanocylinder metasurface into a nematic liquid crystal (LC) cell. Importantly, the LC does not only provide the desired birefringence, but also dynamic control of its strength as well as of the orientation of its anisotropy axis in response to different external stimuli. Specifically, applying voltage across the LC cell, where the LC molecules are pre-aligned along one of the lattice directions of the metasurface, enables out-of-plane rotation of the anisotropy axis of the LC medium. Meanwhile, its birefringence can be tuned by changing the temperature. In our experiments, the coupling of the qBICs to the radiation continuum is first maximized by the application of 25 V across the LC cell at room temperature. We then systematically tune the temperature and show that the resonance depth of the qBIC modes, which is associated with their coupling strength to the continuum, of the qBIC modes increases monotonously with birefringence. Our findings establish anisotropy-induced qBICs in LC integrated dielectric metasurfaces as a promising platform for actively reconfigurable metasurfaces and their applications in displays, optical modulation and tunable photonic devices.

articles.title: Determining the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode via X-ray spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper reports on a measurement to determine the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode. By measuring the spectra of several X-ray sources and comparing the response between the silicon-carbide diode and a commercial silicon diode, the electron-hole pair creation energy in 4H-SiC is determined to be (7.87 ± 0.09) eV. This is the first result obtained using X-ray spectra from several sources and including an estimate of the uncertainty. The result is in good agreement with studies of comparable devices.

articles.title: Integrated lasing and dual-band gain in neodymium-implanted silicon nitride
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lasers at wavelengths near 1 micrometer are used in quantum technologies, precision metrology, and sensing. Rare-earth gain at these wavelengths in photonic integrated circuits can reduce the size and enable the scalable fabrication of these lasers. We fabricate neodymium-based integrated waveguide amplifiers and a ring laser using neodymium-implanted LPCVD silicon nitride. The photonic integrated circuits were fabricated on a 200 mm commercial wafer platform, and individual dies were implanted with neodymium ions. We show that the amplifiers provide gain in two bands around wavelengths of 920 nm and 1100 nm, and we show lasing in a ring resonator. This demonstrates that neodymium-implanted LPCVD silicon nitride is a suitable gain material for integrated lasers.

articles.title: Nonlinear non-modal stability and minimal perturbations in electroconvection driven by unipolar injection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroconvection in a dielectric liquid subjected to unipolar charge injection is subcritical. Convection can be sustained well below the threshold of linear stability theory, and experiments report onset far below it. We use nonlinear non-modal optimization to determine the smallest charge perturbations that trigger convection below the linear threshold. The method, based on a direct--adjoint formulation of the full electrohydrodynamic equations, recovers the classical linear threshold in the limit of small amplitudes. At finite amplitude, the most dangerous perturbations are localized charge deficits rather than excesses, because a deficit relaxes more slowly under Coulomb repulsion. The minimal perturbation needed for transition grows from about 0.5% of the injected charge near the linear threshold to 3% at two thirds of it, where the convective branch ends, in agreement with direct numerical simulations. Near the critical amplitude, trajectories approach an unstable steady state, the edge state, that separates the basins of attraction of rest and convection and originates from the critical linear mode. The damped oscillatory modes involved in the growth of the optimal perturbations are transit-time modes of the ion drift. The convective mode is the first of them, made stationary by the coupling with the flow, which explains why the instability sets in as a steady motion. Small charge fluctuations can therefore lower the onset of electroconvection to about two thirds of the linear threshold, helping to explain the discrepancy between linear theory and experiments.

articles.title: Symmetry-constrained order hierarchy of connected optical responses in a five-level Rydberg-EIT medium
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Determining the connected many-body correlations required for a nonlinear optical response of a given order is a central challenge in interacting open quantum systems. We establish a symmetrybased selection rule for connected optical responses in a driven-dissipative Rydberg-EIT model. Under the specified Lindblad conditions, local phase covariance and zero-probe factorization imply that an n-atom connected contribution to the root optical coherence is forbidden below probe-amplitude order 2n-1. Consequently, optical-response coefficients through fifth order involve at most three-atom connected clusters, without assuming weak interatomic interactions. Direct finite-cluster calculations confirm the predicted lowest allowed orders, while an illustrative Maxwell-propagation calculation shows that triplet contributions can partially oppose pair-induced polarization rotation. Our results establish a rigorous connection between optical perturbation order and the connected many-body sectors that can contribute to it.

articles.title: Observation of programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent superposition allows information to be encoded in the geometry of physical states1-7. Preparing individual states, however, does not determine how they can be organized throughout a wave, because the wave propagation and modulation constrain the underlying interference. Here we observe programmable spatiotemporal quantum-inspired bits in a space-time metasurface. Coherent synthesis from four discrete responses per polarization channel produces two-component states with the projective geometry of a pure quantum bit. Joint state-space synthesis retains the interference constraints of the shared waveform while allowing distinct polarization states to coexist at different resolved frequencies. Paired spatial and temporal codes organize these states into the prescribed trajectories, reconfigurable Stokes skyrmions and distinct polarizations at 48 experimentally resolved nonzero harmonic orders generated by a shared code pair. This connects the local state preparation to programmable field organization, establishing a physical basis for quantum-inspired information carriers whose encoding can exploit the geometrical paths, spatial winding and coordinated spectral states.

articles.title: High-level, efficient ocean modeling at all scales with Oceananigans
articles.abstract: arXiv:2502.14148v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the user interface, governing equations, and numerical methods underpinning the ocean modeling software called "Oceananigans". Oceananigans development has been led by the Climate Modeling Alliance as part of a larger effort to build a trainable climate model with quantifiable uncertainty. Notably, Oceananigans is written in the Julia programming language, is optimized for GPUs, and can efficiently simulate all scales of ocean motion ranging from millimeter-scale turbulence in a small box to planetary-scale ocean circulation. We argue that a reusable finite-volume framework on structured staggered grids, GPU-efficient algorithms, and accessible interfaces and source code together enable efficient all-scale simulations and rapid innovation in model development. This design negotiates a dual mandate for highest-possible performance (to support state-of-the-art applications) and enhanced accessibility (to facilitate adoption and development). The dual mandate aims ultimately to accelerate the progress of Earth system science.

articles.title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22284v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory (DFT) to include a temperature dimension. The formalism unifies established hybrid functionals with information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation DFT, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. It further gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set of different organic molecules. The results clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.

articles.title: Asymptotic Analysis of Shallow Water Moment Equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.01886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Shallow Water Moment Equations (SWME) are an extension of the Shallow Water Equations (SWE) for improved modelling of free-surface flows. In contrast to the SWE, the SWME incorporate vertical velocity profile information. The SWME framework approximates vertical velocity profiles using a polynomial expansion with Legendre polynomials and polynomial coefficients, also called moment variables. The SWME have an increased number of variables that must always be incorporated, even when the flow approaches a viscous slip equilibrium state that could be characterised by vanishing moment variables. To reduce the complexity of the SWME in cases proximate to this equilibrium, we conduct an asymptotic analysis of the SWME. This yields the closed form Reduced Shallow Water Moment Equations (RSWME) for deviations from the equilibrium. The RSWME have fewer variables, compared to the SWME. The hyperbolicity of the RSWME is analysed. Numerical tests include a wave with a sharp height gradient, a smoother height gradient and a square root velocity profile. The numerical tests demonstrate that the RSWME reduce computational cost up to 77% compared to the SWME and improves accuracy up to 88% over the SWE.

articles.title: Ancilla-assisted multi-qubit quantum gates with polar molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.18972v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum error correction enables reliable quantum computation using imperfect physical gates, but its implementation often requires multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates CN(U) acting on N ge 3 qubits. Their direct realization is challenging, while decomposing them into standard one-qubit and two-qubit gates can increase circuit depth and error rates. Here, we present an ancilla-assisted scheme to directly implement CN(U) in optically trapped ultracold polar molecules. By appropriately selecting qubit states for the ancilla and data qubits, dark states can appear during two smooth π pulses. This can generate a controlled-phase gate with the phase set by the relative phase between the pulses; notably, a single 2π pulse yields a CN(Z) gate. Numerical analysis for a simple molecular spatial configuration demonstrates that the gate infidelity is dominated by qubit decoherence, yielding a C₂(Z) fidelity of 0.996 estimated with T₂^ast=1.5~s and a gate duration of T approx 4~ms. Furthermore, diabatic errors remain low, on the order of 10⁻⁴ for N=2,3 and 10⁻³ for N=4, even with dipole-dipole interaction strengths as low as 25hbar/T.

articles.title: infomeasure-rs: A High-Performance Rust Library for Information-Theoretic Measures and Estimators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.27951v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Information theory has become a standard tool across the natural and social sciences, yet practical use is limited by estimator choice, fragmented software, reproducibility, and computational cost. We present infomeasure-rs, an open-source Rust library that brings a broad set of information-theoretic measures and estimators into one self-contained, type-safe package. It covers entropy, mutual information, conditional mutual information, transfer entropy, conditional transfer entropy, cross-entropy, and the Kullback-Leibler and Jensen-Shannon divergences, with discrete (plug-in and bias-corrected), kernel, ordinal, and nearest-neighbour estimators, including the Rényi and Tsallis families, and exposes local and global values and significance testing through a consistent trait interface. It ships as a single portable binary with no runtime dependency and is continuously validated against a reference implementation. On a single central processing unit (CPU) core, and even without its GPU or parallel paths, it is the fastest of the packages we compared across languages, matching the closest packages only for plug-in discrete entropy and substantially faster for mutual information, the conditional and transfer measures, and the kernel, ordinal, and generalised-entropy estimators. The optional GPU and multi-threaded paths accelerate selected continuous estimators further. The library is open source and, to our knowledge, the most complete information-theory package for Rust.

articles.title: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intermediate layers often outperform final layers when foundation models are used as frozen feature extractors, but the source of this advantage is unclear. We study this question in EEG foundation models by separating three factors: how representations are read out, whether intermediate layers provide predictive utility beyond the final-layer interface, and whether useful depth structure transfers across datasets. Across five models and three tasks, improving the final-layer readout consistently recovers substantial predictive performance, yet intermediate layers remain advantageous within frozen extraction. We also find that layers selected on one dataset remain useful on another across five dataset pairs and four task families, and that a compact set of source-derived task directions retains predictive value after transfer in sleep staging. Together, these results show that predictive utility varies across depth, and its usefulness depends on how representations are read out and transferred. More crucially, source-selected layers provide a reusable feature interface across datasets, reducing the need for target-side layer search while outperforming final-layer baselines on target datasets.

articles.title: LatentLens: Rethinking Latent Interface in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Latent interfaces let agents in a multi-agent system communicate through continuous representations rather than decoded text. Prior work reports performance and efficiency gains, but neither separates latent communication from the agent harness nor examines its internal components, leaving its actual contribution unclear. We propose LatentLens, a framework that decouples the latent interface at two levels: externally from the agent harness, to measure its contribution to overall performance (RQ1), and internally into realignment compatibility, information accessibility, and propagation dynamics, to identify the benefits and limitations of each (RQ2). Across seven benchmarks with Qwen3 models, adding the latent interface to the same harness does not improve and can even substantially degrade accuracy. Internally, latent representations retain some domain information, but incompatible realignment can substantially degrade performance, and repeated latent steps can amplify representation-level failures. Thus, while latent representations may preserve information, they do not necessarily ensure effective communication, which also requires compatible realignment, information accessibility, and stable propagation.

articles.title: E(n)-Equivariant Spherical Decision Surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a constructive derivation of exactly E(n)-equivariant spherical decision surfaces by extending prior O(n)-equivariant hypersphere neurons to include translations. To achieve this, we present a decomposition of the features of the O(n)-equivariant neurons and provide explicit representations for translation and E(n)-transformations to fulfil the respective equivariance constraints. The resulting decision surfaces are exactly E(n)-equivariant without input centring or explicit pairwise differences, and admit explicit closed-form matrix representations. In addition, we numerically verify the correctness of the derivations and perform a downstream check of the resulting geometric primitives.

articles.title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for recommendation systems. However, their issued rankings require reliable instance-level uncertainty monitoring. In this scenario, comparing uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods becomes challenging because LLM rankers lack a standard item-classification head. Their scores may depend on option labels, prompts, generation procedures, and the available user and item evidence. Existing methods derive uncertainty from different sources and apply it at different stages of the recommendation process. Some methods evaluate an issued ranking, whereas others use uncertainty to change the ranking itself, making direct comparison difficult. Here we introduce a fixed-ranking benchmark which evaluates eight heterogeneous UQ signals as record-level monitors under a shared output contract. We evaluate these signals across four recommendation datasets and two LLM backbones under a shared fixed-ranking protocol. From the results, we draw three main observations. First, UQ method ordering changes across backbones even on the same reference instances. Second, ranking-aligned Top10Mass provides the strongest scalar Error@10 detection in several evaluation conditions, reflecting effective cutoff-aligned monitoring, while its advantage narrows for popularity-tail targets. Third, scalar UQ signals are weak at identifying which control has the larger clipped NDCG@10 difference, whereas source-specific signals, including Perturbation Rank Instability and simple listwise distances, provide stronger paired-control agreement, reflecting their sensitivity to the two controlled evidence sources. These findings motivate us to evaluate ranking-failure detection, robustness across recommendation conditions, and responses to controlled evidence changes as distinct properties of UQ.

articles.title: Sequential Monte Carlo approximations of Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.05905v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of sampling from a probability distribution π. It is well known that this can be written as an optimisation problem over the space of probability distribution in which we aim to minimise the Kullback--Leibler divergence from π. We consider several partial differential equations (PDEs) whose solution is a minimiser of the Kullback--Leibler divergence from π and connect them to well-known Monte Carlo algorithms. We focus in particular on PDEs obtained by considering the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao geometry over the space of probabilities and show that these lead to a natural implementation using importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo. We propose a novel algorithm to approximate the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao flow of the Kullback--Leibler divergence and conduct an extensive empirical study to identify when this algorithm outperforms other popular Monte Carlo algorithms.

articles.title: BridgeTwist: Twisting Schrödinger Bridges for Training-Free Conditional Sampling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18658v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative models are often required to serve many downstream conditional tasks. In the training-free setting, a pretrained unconditional model is reused as a prior and combined with a task-specific likelihood to sample from the corresponding posterior. While such training-free samplers have been developed for diffusion and flow models, their counterpart for Schrödinger bridge (SB) models remains unexplored, despite the growing appeal of SBs as flexible stochastic transport models between general source and target distributions. We propose BridgeTwist, a training-free conditional sampler for pretrained SB generative models, formulated as a tempered twisted sequential Monte Carlo scheme. The twist function employs a plug-in surrogate built on a closed-form endpoint predictor, which is derived by combining the velocity and score fields obtained from the SB pretraining. Since this surrogate is less reliable near the source, we temper the twist function with a time-varying exponent, downweighting its influence at early steps. We further introduce a bridge-shaped inference-time diffusion schedule that concentrates the proposal noise in the interior of the path. Telescoping importance weights then cancel all intermediate twist factors, yielding an asymptotically exact sampler for the posterior. Empirically, BridgeTwist outperforms training-free baselines on class-conditional and text-prompted image generation, and is competitive with specialized inverse problem solvers on inpainting, deblurring, and super-resolution.

articles.title: Evaluating Frontier-Model Agent Skills with Open-Weight Models in a Science Gateway
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific analyses that span many jobs and computing sites depend on workflow management systems to run reliably, but writing a production workflow requires expertise in such a system, which many domain scientists do not have. Coding agents can supply this expertise when they are guided by skills and packaged procedures for recurring tasks. We wrote skills and specialist agents for the Pegasus workflow management system with a frontier model, and the PegasusAI Studio science gateway offers them to scientists through a chat interface. New users without frontier-model credits need an open-weight model, served at no cost on research cyberinfrastructure, but skills written for a frontier model may not work with an open-weight solution. This paper presents a method for adapting such skills. An evaluation harness drives the real gateway as a user would, scores the workflows the agent builds, and feeds recurring failures back to the frontier model that maintains the skills. We evaluated 21 open-weight models on 17 tasks. The five highest-scoring models are close in quality after one trial per task, and their median response times differ twelvefold. In repeated trials with the best of the three open-weight models, we repeated scores of 0.76 on workflow building against 0.82 for Claude. The harness led to five changes to the initial skills. We also identify challenges in evaluating agents within operational systems: evaluation failures can be mistaken for model failures, and agents can circumvent experimental controls within their privilege domain. In a controlled ablation, an initially significant effect disappeared when the restrictions were properly enforced.

articles.title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively keeps, updates, or redecides pending actions. Compared with Agent S3, Chronotope reduces median end-to-end latency by 85.5% for a 27B model, expanding its performance envelope to 100% Live success at an 8-second deadline versus 0%. Chronotope enables real-time GUI control through compact interaction history, knowing when to preserve, revise, or replace actions, and an overall efficient architectural design that obviates verbose reflection, reasoning, and grounding calls.

articles.title: COGENT: A Modular Cognitive Architecture for Agentic User Simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based user simulation can support interface design, accessibility research, and interactive-agent evaluation, but standard computer-use agents are optimized for task completion rather than reproducing how people perceive, reason, and act. We introduce COGENT (COGnitive agENT), a modular cognitive architecture for simulating user interaction with desktop interfaces. COGENT draws on established cognitive theories, such as Norman's action cycle and ACT-R, to enable explainable, intervenable, and modular user simulation by decomposing the simulation process into cognitive modules with explicit representations of perception, memory, user state, intentions, and action selection. We begin by presenting six intervenability demonstrations, each tracing how a single edit to memory, a user attribute, or a processing module propagates through the cognitive pipeline to produce a behavioral change. We evaluate COGENT's behavioral and attributional fidelity across three benchmarks -- AgentNetBench, A11y-CUA, and SENSE-42 -- finding that it achieves statistically significant fidelity gains over computer-use baselines in reproducing recorded human behavior and recovers the relational structure among human self-reported psychological states. Together, these demos and evaluations demonstrate COGENT's utility toward more faithful, explainable, intervenable, and modular LLM-based cognitive simulations.

articles.title: LimoBench: How Street Smart Are Large Language Models?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed how humans interact with information, enabling natural-language interfaces across various domains. They are increasingly deployed for geospatial applications including map-based question answering, location-based services, and natural-language interfaces to spatial databases. But are LLMs truly location-aware, able to reliably interpret and precisely answer location queries involving real-world coordinates, points of interest (POIs), and geospatial distances? To answer this concretely, we present LimoBench, a street-level benchmark of 82 natural-language location queries over seven canonical spatial operations: geocoding, reverse geocoding, routing, directionality, range search, k-nearest-neighbor search, and spatial join. The queries are grounded in real map data of West Lafayette, Indiana, and are graded by location and semantic complexity. They are designed to probe LLMs' street-level spatial awareness, from simple lookups to multi-step spatial reasoning. We also present Limo, an approach based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that enhances the location awareness of LLMs. Limo grounds LLMs in PostGIS-backed spatial data through a compact set of tools. We find that ungrounded models mostly achieve single-digit accuracy (3.1% for GPT-6 Luna) across different spatial operations. In contrast, the same models achieve near-perfect accuracy (99.3% for GPT-6 Luna) when given access to Limo's spatial tools through MCP. Current LLMs thus have limited and unreliable street-level spatial knowledge, while grounding provides accurate answers at modest overhead (+0.2 s latency, 7.7× tokens, and 2.2× cost for GPT-6 Luna). We release the benchmark, Limo toolset, and evaluation code to encourage the community to evaluate their own location-aware LLM approaches.

articles.title: AGL-SKILL: Coding Harnesses as Agentic Optimizers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier models are increasingly used through harnesses as agents, with growing autonomy to do useful work. Agent performance can often be enhanced by the use of skills: reusable workflows, code, and prompts that provide task-related information or guide the behaviour of the model. Skills, being textual in nature, present themselves as another editable surface to be optimized; current methods have improved on handcrafting and one-shot generation by treating skill development as an iterative process, using score-driven search to tweak and improve performance. In this paper, we demonstrate the efficacy of the agents themselves as optimizers: across five benchmarks, a coding agent without guidance substantially improves every target and outperforms published skill-optimization methods. More broadly, this shows the capability of agents to do such work and to refine their own behaviour to provide task-specific context, as long as they are given a metric to measure against.

articles.title: RubikSQL-HB: Agentic Text-to-SQL with Knowledge in the Loop
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.32772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Database agents need more than schema structure: business meanings, stored values and reference queries supply knowledge that becomes relevant at different points in reasoning. We introduce RubikSQL-HB, which exposes these materials through queryable, database-specific knowledge workspaces built on the HeavenBase platform. Its knowledge interface remains available as an agent constructs and investigates an answer. Candidate agents interleave knowledge access with SQL construction and execution; a downstream Judge can reuse the same interfaces to investigate disagreements. A two-stage example interface separates discovering a reference question from expanding its SQL. On a 500-question BIRD Mini-Dev evaluation, the full pipeline reaches 75.2% execution accuracy, against 71.2% for first-candidate selection and 70.4% for execution-majority voting, with a correct candidate available on 79.0% of questions. The raw-knowledge condition, which also regenerates candidates without the built workspace, is 3.0 points lower, and adjudication with tools and revision accounts for most of the gain over selection baselines. A recorded execution probe shows how continued investigation resolves a candidate disagreement. Separate archived runs show semantic revision recovering answers absent from their original candidate pools. A versioned development study further illustrates how recurring corrections become reusable execution checks. The system and results connect knowledge-interface design to agent decision quality: queryable knowledge supports the construction of useful alternatives, and evidence-aware adjudication connects those alternatives to a final answer. Keeping knowledge in the loop lets agents acquire relevant observations as their reasoning develops.

articles.title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.33086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entity Resolution (ER) pipelines often collapse ambiguity into early hard decisions: upstream Named Entity Recognition (NER) selects a single span and type, and downstream Entity Linking (EL) treats that choice as ground truth. This discards valuable information about the ambiguity of the underlying data (e.g., span boundary disagreement and type confusion), leading to brittle systems that fail unpredictably when faced with uncertainty in inputs. Therefore, this work presents a proof-of-concept for uncertainty-aware ER that treats uncertainty as native data that should be preserved and exploited throughout ER pipelines. We (i) capture uncertainty signals in the NER stage and (ii) leverage these signals into the EL stage to improve candidate retrieval under ambiguity. Using a BERT-based NER model augmented with two auxiliary span-boundary prediction heads, we apply Monte Carlo (MC) dropout at inference time to derive three mention-level proxy signals: the MC-averaged start-boundary probability, the MC-averaged end-boundary probability, and De Luca-Termini fuzzy entropy computed over the Begin-Inside-Outside (BIO) predictive distribution. These signals are used to adapt the fuzzy cutoff in candidate generation (CG) for EL. Because CG is treated as a blocking step, we evaluate retrieval recall. On the AnnoCTR dataset linked to the MITRE ATTCK knowledge base, the boundary-aware and dual-signal fuzzy linking approaches improve Recall@10 from 0.6186 to 0.7966. The contribution lies not in an end-to-end optimised ER pipeline but in establishing uncertainty preservation as a viable and beneficial component of ER pipelines, enabling downstream EL to make better-informed decisions under uncertainty.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Iranian Doctoral Entrance Exams in Electrical and Computer Engineering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We evaluate four large language models (LLMs) on multiple-choice questions from the 2024 and 2025 Iranian national Ph.D. entrance examinations in Electrical Engineering (EE) and Computer Engineering (CE). Of the 440 questions in the four official booklets, 7 were excluded because the question statement or its figure was ambiguous, leaving 433 questions (186 EE, 247 CE), of which 171 (39.5%) depend on a figure. Each question was presented in the original Persian and in an English translation, giving 3,464 scored responses. GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Grok 4 were queried zero-shot, with reasoning enabled, through a single commercial web interface (Perplexity) in October 2025, using an automated script. Because every model answers the same items, all inferences use paired tests or question-clustered models. Accuracy separates into two tiers: GPT-5 (79.9%, 95% CI 76.6--83.1) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (78.4%, 74.8--81.9) are statistically indistinguishable, and both outperform Grok 4 (71.7%) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (71.3%) by 6.7--8.7 percentage points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). The English--Persian accuracy difference is small for every model (-0.2 to +2.5 points; exact McNemar p ge 0.28). For three models the 90% confidence interval lies within ± 5 points, so differences larger than this can be excluded. Questions with figures are much harder: the odds ratio is 0.30 (95% CI 0.21--0.43) after adjusting for discipline. The apparent EE deficit of two models disappears once the larger share of figure-based EE items is accounted for. We describe the dataset, the protocol and its limitations, including the uncontrolled web-retrieval and decoding settings of the interface, and release item-level responses and analysis code.

articles.title: When Successful Collaboration Becomes an Attack Surface: Insider Memory Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31307v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) increasingly use shared memory to store and reuse successful collaboration records, enabling teams to improve across tasks. However, this memory introduces a new attack surface for malicious insiders. Unlike existing insider attacks that inject misleading information directly into the current collaboration, misinformation stored in shared memory can later appear as successful team experience and gain greater credibility and influence. We propose MIMPA (Multi-Agent Insider Memory Poisoning Attack), which exploits this vulnerability using only normal participation privileges, without direct memory access. During an earlier task, the malicious agent embeds a target-specific payload while helping the team answer correctly, allowing the payload to be retained in a successful collaboration record. When retrieved for a later target task, this poisoned record can steer benign agents toward a designated wrong answer, further amplified by malicious triggering. Across three benchmarks and two LLM backbones, MIMPA substantially outperforms existing insider attacks and remains effective under hierarchical memory management, while auditing only partially mitigates it. These results reveal that shared memory intended to accumulate team experience can become a persistent channel for insider attacks. Our code is available at https://github.com/ahnji0520/MIMPA-code.

articles.title: Where is the Interface for the AI Harness?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31739v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Norman's gulfs of execution and evaluation have guided interaction design for forty years, but both assume a user who is present in the loop. Agentic delegation breaks that assumption: users describe an outcome and leave, while the agent takes hundreds of unseen actions. Starting from a 2026 incident in which a research agent circumvented an access refusal on an Australian government portal and went unnoticed for two months, we argue that delegation opens two new gulfs. The gulf of specification is the gap between what a user wants and their ability to express it, including how the agent should behave in situations nobody foresaw. The gulf of oversight is the gap between what an agent is doing and the user's ability to know, assess, and control it. We argue that both gulfs meet in the harness, the tools, permissions, checks, and loop that surround the model. Harnesses are currently written by developers and hidden from users. We call on HCI to decide which parts of the harness belong to the end-user, which should be visible and adjustable defaults, and which should be built in by design, and to create the interfaces that let ordinary people author and read them.

articles.title: TopoCryptoEEG: End-to-End Encrypted Framework for Brainprint Authentication
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Brainprint authentication enables continuous identity verification, but EEG data are privacy-sensitive. Existing feature-level encrypted authentication (FLEA) schemes protect extracted features under a trusted-client assumption. We show theoretically and empirically that a compromised client with access to plaintext query features and continuous authentication scores can exactly recover a registered template after finitely many interactions. To address this risk, we propose TopoCryptoEEG, a homomorphic-encryption-based framework that encrypts preprocessed EEG data at the client and performs feature extraction, template matching, score computation, and threshold centering on ciphertexts at the server. This extends protection from extracted features to preprocessed EEG data and removes the client-side plaintext-feature interface exploited by the attack. For efficient encrypted authentication, we develop Multi-Window Topology-Aware Encoding (MWTE) and a Topographic Branch Model with Linear Fusion (TopoFuse-MLP) to preserve EEG spatial information while limiting multiplicative depth. Query-Patch Coordinate Packing (QPCP) and Lane-Preserving BSGS Evaluation (LP-BSGS) further reduce ciphertext operations. Experiments on HGD and BCICIV-2a show high authentication accuracy, with homomorphic computation taking 1-2 s on CPUs and about 14 ms on GPUs. TopoCryptoEEG achieves over 18x average speedup over the EER (IMWUT 2025) baseline, supporting practical privacy-preserving brainprint authentication.

articles.title: Agentic Discovery of Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rust crates confine unsafe code, such as calls into C or C++ libraries or system calls, behind safe interfaces that must uphold Rust's invariants. If an interface encodes one rule of the code beneath it too weakly, a program written in purely safe Rust can cause undefined behavior. Static analyzers and fuzzers are bound to fixed patterns or to the paths they execute. We propose LLM agents as auditors of these interfaces, and study how well they do it. We first define a taxonomy of the defects of such interfaces, including undefined behavior, divergences from the wrapped library, and incomplete unsafe contracts. We then measure, in repeated audits of a real-world crate by a closed and an open model, Claude Opus 5.5 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, which defect classes agents find, how well they triage them, and what makes them find more. Agents find the first two classes unprompted, but find few incomplete contracts even when asked. Their findings are almost always real, even without an independent reviewer, yet they lack triage discipline: they seldom confirm with a sanitizer, and they stop early. With the same guidance, the open model finds as many defects as the closed one at a quarter of the cost. We integrate these insights in Crustify, an agentic system for automating C-to-Rust tasks, and run it at scale. In 16 widely used crates, including the bindings to the C libraries OpenSSL, SQLite, libgit2, and libcurl and to the C++ engine V8, Crustify found 225 undefined-behavior bugs, 23 behavioral divergences, and 36 incomplete unsafe contracts, between 3 and 61 per crate at a median cost under 50 per audit. In the Linux kernel's Rust abstractions, it found 11 more undefined-behavior bugs and 4 incomplete contracts. Maintainers have fixed 26 of the 83 findings that we reported.

articles.title: Rethinking Video Agents: When and Why Video Harnesses Work
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video understanding depends not only on how models reason about visual evidence, but also on which evidence they observe. Fixed observation policies determine this evidence in advance; agentic harnesses allow models to seek further observations as their understanding develops. This shift creates an opportunity to realize capabilities that fixed inputs leave untapped, yet the ability to request observations does not ensure their effective use. We investigate when and why video harnesses improve understanding, examining how task demands and models' capacity for interaction jointly shape their benefits. Using Video-Relook as an experimental framework, we let models adapt their temporal and spatial observations from a common default configuration, and analyze performance and interaction trajectories across models and tasks. Adaptive observation yields substantial gains on fine-grained action understanding, with benefits also extending to Video-MME-v2. Even under the same observation interface, gains differ substantially across models; interaction traces reveal corresponding differences in evidence seeking and the reliability of answer revision. The benefits also vary across tasks for the same model, ranging from substantial improvements to limited gains and regressions. Together, these findings support an account in which harness effectiveness depends on the alignment between opportunities for informative observation and the model's ability to turn interaction into reliable revisions. They motivate video harnesses that coordinate perception and reasoning, matching observational autonomy to task demands and model capabilities.

articles.title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce SPARK, textit{Semantic Probe-guided Adaptive Region seeKing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed to assess emerging hypotheses. Their spatial attention guides view placement, contextual responses determine crop extent, and observation history encourages complementary inspection. The resulting predictions are combined through uncertainty-weighted voting. On ScreenSpot-Pro, SPARK improves grounding accuracy over single-view inference by 13.9, 25.2, and 16.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and UI-TARS, outperforming all compared test-time methods for each backbone. Consistent gains across four additional benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse interfaces and grounding tasks. These results establish semantic probing as an effective mechanism for turning a frozen VLM's understanding of what to inspect into more accurate GUI grounding.

articles.title: Lightweight Rail Surface Defect Detection via Boundary-Distance Refinement and Shape-Aware Regression Reweighting
articles.abstract: Rail surface defects often exhibit weak contrast, elongated geometry, and ambiguous boundaries, making accurate localization difficult under class imbalance and textured rail backgrounds. This paper presents LBX-RSABR-YOLO26, a lightweight detector that couples inference-side boundary refinement with training-side regression reweighting. The LBX head aligns multiscale features, extracts differential detail cues, and introduces a zero-initialized residual branch that refines the four direct l/t/r/b distance outputs. RSABR complements this design by reweighting positive-sample regression using box area, aspect ratio, and class priors together with clipping, mean normalization, and task-assignment quality weighting. On a six-class dataset containing 7,400 images, the proposed model achieves 70.84% mAP50-95, while its training record peaks at 70.90%. Relative to YOLO26n, it reduces the parameter count from 2.6433 M to 2.5017 M and FLOPs from 6.3966 G to 6.2914 G. Ablation results identify LBX as the stronger standalone contributor, while the combined design delivers the best lightweight performance. These results demonstrate that boundary-distance refinement and shape-aware regression reweighting complement each other effectively for rail surface defect detection.

articles.title: Adsorption studies of malachite green dye on activated carbon prepared from cocoa biomass
articles.abstract: The dye malachite green (MG, CI 42000) is widely used in the textile industry to dye various materials and as an antiseptic to treat fish infections. Despite its applications, MG has high toxicity, which causes allergies and skin irritation. This study explored the application of activated carbon prepared from cocoa biomass residue in the removal of organic dyes. Thermogravimetric Analysis, Energy Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence Spectrometry, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy, and X-ray Diffraction characterized the biomass and the activated carbon. Adsorption isotherm studies were carried out using the MG dye. Dye removal was monitored spectrophotometrically. The Langmuir and Freundlich models were tested in equilibrium studies, and three kinetic models were evaluated: pseudo first-order, pseudo second-order, and intraparticle diffusion. The kinetic data were best fit to the PSO model, and the adsorption isotherm fit better to the Freundlich model. Those results suggested that chemisorption is the driven force for the process. Thermodynamic data, including a high adsorption enthalpy and a temperature-dependent Gibbs free energy, corroborated such an observation. The results showed that the methodology used to produce activated biochar from cocoa husks (agro-industrial waste) is efficient at removing synthetic dyes.

articles.title: Friction–wear antagonism in suspension-HVOF alumina–fluorapatite coatings on 316L stainless steel: sacrificial third-body lubrication and wear-based lifetime estimation
articles.abstract: Alumina (Al₂O₃) and alumina–fluorapatite (Al₂O₃–Fap) coatings containing 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 wt% Fap were deposited on 316L stainless steel by suspension high-velocity oxy-fuel (S-HVOF) spraying and tested in dry sliding against alumina balls (5 N, 0.1 m·s⁻¹, 400 m, three tests per composition). With increasing Fap content, the steady-state friction coefficient decreased from 0.65 to 0.55, whereas porosity increased from 4.96 to 6.71% and the specific wear rate from 3.1 × 10⁻⁵ to 4.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³·N⁻¹·m⁻¹. To separate friction from wear, an energy wear coefficient, defined as the wear volume per unit of frictional energy, was calculated. It increased by 72% between pure alumina and the 1 wt% Fap coating, in close proportion to the decrease in Vickers hardness from 556 to 319 HV: the product of the two quantities varied by less than ± 4% across the four compositions. The lower friction thus only partly offsets the loss of hardness. This loss is much larger than the small Fap fraction or the porosity increase can account for, and is attributed to weaker cohesion between splats. The worn surfaces showed smoothed plateaus crossed by fine cracks, with fine debris and no delamination. Wear-based lifetimes were estimated from Archard's law for critical wear depths of 10 and 20 µm, with Monte Carlo propagation of the wear-rate scatter: the 1 wt% Fap coating reached a given depth after about 31% less sliding than pure alumina. These dry-sliding data provide a reference for future tribo-corrosion tests in simulated body fluid.

articles.title: Calibration of Reported Uncertainty in State-of-Charge Estimation for Lithium Iron Phosphate Cells
articles.abstract: A battery management system acts on the state of charge (SOC) and on the uncertainty that its estimator reports, but estimators are usually evaluated by point accuracy alone. In lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, the flat open-circuit voltage (OCV) and its hysteresis make this uncertainty hard to trust. This paper examines when SOC estimators produce credible intervals with coverage consistent with their nominal levels. A preregistered simulation study with 144 primary and 96 control conditions, and an exact Bayesian reference in the controls, compares a Fisher-information estimator, an iterated extended Kalman filter (IEKF), an unscented Kalman filter (UKF), and a Rao--Blackwellized grid filter on a second-order equivalent-circuit model with hysteresis, whose state the estimators know, measured-current noise, and three voltage sensors.
