Yet their ability to recover population-level variable importance has received little attention. We design and conduct a Monte Carlo simulation study to compare variable importance recovery across tabular foundation models and established machine learning baselines. Our framework distinguishes multiple population estimands, pairs each one with an aligned model-agnostic importance estimator, and evaluates recovery in terms of ranking, support, and relative magnitude. Our results show that tabular foundation models are generally competitive with established machine-learning baselines in recovering population variable importance, and often more accurate. We thus extend the evidence for their capabilities to a previously underexamined dimension, further strengthening their appeal.

articles.title: A Novel Approach to Clustering Shape Data Using Iteratively Weighted Vectors with k-Means
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological data analysis provides a collection of methods for analyzing data with shape structure, including point clouds, graphs, and images. Recent advances in topological vectorization have enabled the embedding of shape data into Euclidean spaces, facilitating comparisons and machine learning tasks. Vector summaries that effectively capture topological structures are particularly useful for shape classification and unsupervised learning tasks such as clustering. We investigate the use of vectorized topological data for clustering through k-means, which partitions observations into a fixed number of groups by minimizing a squared-error loss function. By incorporating an element-wise weight-update step into the iterative k-means algorithm, we improve clustering performance on both simulated and real-world shape datasets. We show that estimating these weights reduces to a least-squares problem, requiring minimal additional computation while allowing flexible coefficient constraints. Our approach also substantially strengthens the negative correlation between the loss and clustering accuracy, improving the effectiveness of selecting among multiple clustering solutions based on the lowest loss. These improvements remain robust to changes in vector length and the number of initializations. Furthermore, weighted topological vector summaries exhibit stability under small structural perturbations, particularly when weight constraints are imposed. The proposed method offers a flexible alternative for clustering topological data, accommodating different k-means variants, vectorization methods, and weight constraints.

articles.title: Deep Negative Binomial Autoregression for Sparse Spatio-Temporal Counts: Estimation and Predictive Distribution Bounds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study estimation and probabilistic forecasting for sparse, overdispersed count panels using DeepNB-STAR, a negative binomial autoregression whose log-mean and log-size are outputs of a deep ReLU network of temporal and neighboring summaries of the past, fitted by maximum likelihood. We prove an oracle inequality for the Hellinger risk along the observed trajectory without mixing assumptions, rates governed by compositional smoothness with a matching lower bound for a Hölder subclass, geometric absolute regularity, and bounds on the error of h-step predictive distributions of order h¹/² times the root estimation risk plus a Monte Carlo term. All results hold for a size that depends on the covariates, and the estimation bounds hold under arbitrary dependence between sites, with the number of time points as sample size. On four Japanese surveillance panels, DeepNB-STAR has a weighted interval score 0.6% to 1.0% below that of a three-member ensemble of Temporal Fusion Transformers on every panel, distinguishable from zero only on the held-out panel. Fitted mean and size functions are reported with exploratory bootstrap intervals. Nominal 95% prediction intervals for national totals cover only 81% to 92% of weeks: the joint predictive law, unlike the estimator, relies on conditional independence across sites.

articles.title: RoFE: Rotated Frozen Embeddings for Low-Data Multimodal Tabular Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal tabular learning combines tabular data with images and text, often in settings where labeled data are scarce. Tabular foundation models such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) offer a promising solution via in-context learning without task-specific training. However, modern image and text encoders produce embeddings with hundreds or thousands of dimensions, far exceeding the number of features encountered during PFN pretraining. Existing approaches bridge this gap using principal component analysis (PCA) to compress frozen embeddings. Surprisingly, we find that this PCA interface can underperform simple linear classifiers when labeled examples are scarce, even though PFNs are designed for small datasets. We identify the underlying failure mechanism: the PFN's per-column standardization removes the variances of the PCA scores. When the PCA keeps every direction of the labeled examples, the examples collapse into a regular simplex in which all pairwise distances are equal. To address this problem, we propose Rotated Frozen Embeddings (RoFE), a training-free method that rotates PCA scores before PFN inference. We theoretically show that rotation makes the column variances nearly equal, so that standardization approximately preserves the embedding geometry. Across image and text classification tasks, encoders, and tabular foundation models, RoFE improves low-data performance over the PCA interface and outperforms baselines that require task-specific training. The improvements also extend to regression.

articles.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Can Decide the Outcome
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.15617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum machine learning is proposed to detect grid cyberattacks, but no study we could read tests quantum and classical detectors under white-box, transfer, and black-box attacks and random label flips in one protocol. We compare two quantum and six classical detectors on public grid-attack data under equal tuning budgets. Our main finding: evaluation choices can decide the outcome. On these data, seven choices each changed a reported result with model families fixed. Row-level splits inflate our best score by 0.31 macro-averaged F1 over held-out files, where matched-dimensionality classical and quantum models barely clear chance. Under its own white-box attack the quantum kernel's score falls from 0.56 to 0.01 (chance 0.50), while a transferred attack in the same run leaves 0.52. Trees admit no gradient-based white-box attack, so their attacked scores are upper bounds. These attack results use eight-dimension detectors under row-level splits. On gas-pipeline and simulated-grid data, neither quantum detector is more accurate or consistently more robust; three of the seven choices reproduce fully on gas data with one pressure feature log-scaled (two within noise), and none of the four checked on the grids does. Benchmarks should hold out whole files and give every model its own attack where possible. We release code and checklist.

articles.title: Specialized Large Language Models for Markovian Reasoning: Structural Cache Compression, Transition Pretraining, and Dual-Loop Transformers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard autoregressive large language models attend to the growing history of generated tokens, making the key-value (KV) cache a central memory and throughput bottleneck in long-chain reasoning and multi-branch sampling. Yet an important class of reasoning problems is naturally first-order Markovian: the next step depends on a sufficient representation of the current state, rather than on the raw sequence of all earlier steps. We develop a unified design paradigm for Markovian-reasoning specialized large language models. At the cache level, the Markovian state interface transforms history-dependent KV storage into constant-size state transfer with respect to the number of reasoning steps. At the learning level, we reformulate long-chain prediction as independently trainable one-step transition objectives, with explicit state bottlenecks, distillation, invariance, and drift-consistency losses. At the architectural level, we introduce a dual-loop Transformer: an outer loop advances the reasoning state, while an inner recurrent-depth loop allocates adaptive computation to each transition through shared weights and explicit memory tokens or recurrent matrix states. We connect this architecture to a three-region cache, step-relative positions, truncated backpropagation, branch-aware checkpoints, and a transition-centric evaluation protocol. The organizing principle is simple: the optimal reasoning system need not remember everything; it must carry forward exactly what the future needs. This principle opens a path toward specialized reasoning engines whose memory footprint is decoupled from reasoning-chain length.

articles.title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skill-augmented reinforcement learning enables LLM agents to reuse task-solving knowledge across episodes, but existing systems typically expose agents to a flat skill pool and update skills only from coarse, episode-level outcomes. This conflates two distinct uses of experience: a stable strategy that should frame the whole episode, and tactical know-how that should be retrieved only when the agent reaches a local execution gap. We propose STRIDE (Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-guided skIll Disclosure and Evolution), a framework that brings progressive skill disclosure into agentic reinforcement learning. STRIDE keeps the selected strategy visible as episode context, exposes a compact tactic menu, and loads full tactic content only after an explicit retrieval action. This interface turns each retrieval into an event-level credit unit: the same event provides process feedback for learning when to retrieve and supplies evidence for skill-bank evolution. On ALFWorld, STRIDE achieves a 92.7% average success rate with Qwen3-4B and a 94.9% average success rate with Qwen3-8B. On WebShop, it improves over the strongest reproduced skill-augmented baseline by 4.5 score points and 1.9 success-rate percentage points. These results show that skill reuse is most effective when persistent strategies preserve global task structure and tactics are disclosed only at local decision bottlenecks.

articles.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent frameworks typically orchestrate language models through prompt-and-response interfaces. We propose a harness design that exposes intermediate model states and layer-level execution controls to the agent runtime. By connecting state collection, policy fitting, and execution, the design enables policies to allocate computation within and across models based on intermediate states. We demonstrate the approach with a prototype that learns stitching bridges and state-conditioned execution policies from paired model states, then applies them during inference to select among continue, exit, and stitch. For dispatcher supervision, we select the least-computation action whose full-vocabulary next-token prediction matches the source model's full-depth prediction, using continue when neither early action matches. We train these components on a frozen proxy corpus of 5,000 typed-decision items authored using source texts sampled from WildChat conversations, then evaluate the prototype on JevBench measuring task accuracy, agreement with full-model predictions, and end-to-end latency including runtime overhead. Preliminary results show an approximately 15% reduction in mean latency while maintaining task accuracy comparable to full-model inference.

articles.title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution). We provide a normative second-order Langevin sampling framework wherein spike-frequency adaptation drives spatial exploration at the cost of speed, and momentum via dendritic input differentiation drives temporal compression. We numerically verify our framework via simulations of noisy RNNs trained on 2D triangular and T-maze navigation activity, and others trained on place cell activity of synthetic rats. Crucially, we observe that simultaneous adaptation and momentum increases both replay exploration and speed, and provide one of the first accounts for biologically plausible temporal compression in rate-based RNN replay. Our findings encourage experiments into whether dendritic input differentiation, or other mechanisms, may support temporal compression in memory circuits like the hippocampus.

articles.title: JaxNaviSim: A GPU-Accelerated, Data-Driven Simulator and Learning Benchmark for Maritime Navigation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coordinating vessels through the shared waterways of busy ports grows more challenging as vessel traffic increases. Port authorities need realistic simulations to assess how arrival schedules, anchorage assignments, and routes affect vessel throughput and navigation safety. Existing AIS-based trajectory models predict a vessel's track from its past trajectory in an open-loop fashion. They do not simulate step-by-step responses to other ships or test whether a vessel collides or reaches its goal. To address this problem, we introduce JaxNaviSim, a data-driven simulator and learning benchmark coupling Automatic Identification System (AIS) data with fast, controllable traffic simulation, in which learned models steer vessels through recorded traffic. First, we release a dataset of ~141 million AIS records from over 30K vessels across eight high-density regions of the Singapore Strait, among the world's busiest waterways, with ~6.7 million vessel-hours. Unlike several existing AIS datasets which mostly cover open seas, ours captures close-quarters vessel traffic in the narrow strait. Second, we define a navigation task for each recorded vessel trajectory. A model steers that vessel every 10 s from its recorded state to its anchoring point or region exit, while surrounding ships follow their recorded tracks or are steered by the model. We implement a JAX simulator that runs these tasks in large batches on a GPU. We also incorporate multiple vessel dynamics models and sea surface currents. Finally, we benchmark imitation learning (IL), offline and online RL, and include Predictive Action Refinement (PAR) as a safety baseline that cuts collision rates to 1-3%. The comparison shows that low tracking error does not ensure arrival, and learned policies can reach most destinations yet collide in 20-45% of episodes.

articles.title: AeroJEPA: A Two-Stage Framework for Aerosol Forecasting with Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aerosol forecasting requires integrating sparse ground observations and modeling meteorologically driven concentration evolution and spatial structure. However, analysis-initialized forecasts make limited explicit use of historical observations, while pointwise regression tends to smooth local variations and provides limited constraints on fine spatial structures. In this work, we propose AeroJEPA, a two-stage joint-embedding predictive framework for regional surface PM₂.₅ forecasting. Specifically, Stage I fuses historical observations, model backgrounds, and meteorological information to predict an initial future state, meteorological conditions, and multi-scale structures. Morphology-guided encoding and joint-embedding predictive supervision support learning future spatial representations, supplementing concentration regression with structural constraints. Stage II uses predicted meteorology to guide state refinement and incorporates coarse- and fine-scale structures into state updates and decoding to generate the concentration field at a single future time step. Experiments show that AeroJEPA reduces gridded and independent-station RMSE by 17.23% and 7.90%, respectively, relative to PFGNet, while improving spatial consistency with analysis fields. In a 48 h recursive forecasting case study, AeroJEPA generally achieves lower RMSE and MAE than the numerical forecasts across the forecast period, indicating promising short- to medium-range forecasting performance.

articles.title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally associated with greater social sycophancy, with odds ratios up to 7.56 (95% CI [6.22, 9.20]). However, UI-API differences varied significantly across models for all sycophancy dimensions, including a pronounced reversal for DeepSeek moral sycophancy (43% UI vs. 82.3% API). Overall, our results suggest that API-based LLM evaluations may underestimate the prevalence of sycophancy in corresponding consumer-facing systems, making access conditions consequential for the external validity of LLM evaluation. To facilitate research on access-mode effects, we release 57,000 model responses and SycoUI, a browser-automation pipeline for standardized cross-interface LLM evaluation.

articles.title: Effect of TiO2 nanotubes obtained from a Ti6Al4V alloy on the degradation of ciprofloxacin in aqueous solution by an electrochemical method
articles.abstract: The functional performance of anodic TiO₂ nanotube arrays depends on the relationship between their structural, chemical, and optical properties and their ability to support charge transfer. In this study, nanotubular oxide layers were formed by anodization on Ti6Al4V substrates manufactured by electron beam powder bed fusion (EB-PBF), and their electrochemical and photoelectrochemical behavior was evaluated. The nanotubes grew into a continuous layer approximately 850 nm thick, without delamination, with an average inner diameter of 59.79 ± 9.02 nm. Annealing at 350°C transformed the as-anodized amorphous oxide layer into the anatase phase. The anodic coating has a mixed-oxide structure in which alloy elements from the substrate modify optical absorption. The presence of Al2O3 and V2O5 species appears to shift the apparent bandgap to about 2.11 eV. The material showed no measurable photoelectrochemical activity under UV-C, simulated solar, or visible irradiation. Under galvanostatic polarization, the nanostructured electrode enabled approximately 49% removal of ciprofloxacin after 150 min, demonstrating its potential functionality under electrochemical treatment conditions. These findings show that anatase formation and an apparent optical absorption threshold in the visible range do not necessarily translate into measurable photoelectrochemical activation. The results highlight the need to assess optical properties alongside functional measurements when considering alloy-derived nanotubular oxides for water treatment applications.

articles.title: Regional screening of subsurface resource interactions in the northern Perth Basin, Western Australia
articles.abstract: Sedimentary basins can host multiple subsurface resources, creating potential for direct competition where activities target the same pore space and for pressure or fluid interaction where they occupy separate but connected intervals. In the onshore northern Perth Basin, Western Australia, these relationships may involve petroleum production, carbon geological storage (CGS), underground gas storage (UGS), geothermal development and groundwater abstraction. Regional spatial overlap can identify where potential resources interactions warrant closer assessment, but these resources may still be vertically and hydraulically separated. This study provides a data-driven framework for evaluating potential subsurface resource interactions and identifying potential risks and opportunities for regulators, industries and communities. The project uses a Geographic Information System (GIS)-based multi-criteria and hierarchy evaluation process to assess the suitability of different resources and quantify their spatial interactions with focus on petroleum and CGS operations and potential conflicts with groundwater usage. The overlap of suitable petroleum and CGS resources is most pronounced in the Permian succession, particularly on the Dongara, Beharra Springs and Donkey Creek terraces and in the northwestern Dandaragan Trough. Candidate areas where CGS could follow petroleum production and reservoir depletion extend south along the Cadda Terrace and Coomallo Trough. CO2 source–sink proximity screening identifies a western basin corridor, particularly between Dongara and Leeman, where prospective CGS areas lie relatively close to potential future gas-related CO₂ sources. The potential for vertical interaction between resources was also examined by considering faults and petroleum wells as possible vertical pathways between deep formation and to shallow groundwater aquifers. Water bore density was used as a proxy for evaluating the competition for groundwater. While groundwater resources are typically hydraulically isolated from deeper resources development activities by thick intervening shale aquitards, potential impacts of petroleum and CGS operations on groundwater resources are possible in heavily faulted areas in a central-western corridor inland of Dongara and extending south along the Cadda Terrace and Coomallo Trough. The presented framework provides a regional basis for more targeted, field-scale assessments and identification of resource development synergies, options for sequential development, and cumulative groundwater management.

articles.title: Generation of two-wavelength superscattering and super-forward scattering from degenerate electric modes in four-layered dielectric/epsilon-near-zero nanoshells
articles.abstract: Superscattering, induced by degenerate modes in a subwavelength particle, has attracted considerable interest due to its unique optical properties with potential applications in optical tagging, nanoantennas, and spectroscopy. However, most studies on superscattering have focused on intensity enhancement, the directional control of superscattering, especially superdirectional scattering at two or more frequencies, remains largely unexplored and constitutes a substantial challenge. We propose a concentric core-shell nanoparticle, consisting of four alternating dielectric and aluminium-doped zinc oxide (AZO) layers with two different epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) points, that can realize superscattering with super-forward scattering near two ENZ wavelengths. We demonstrate that two Al:ZnO shells can support two electric ENZ modes (ENZMs) with the same angular momentum but different mode orders near their ENZ wavelengths. Depending on the mode order of the excited ENZMs, we show that such nanoparticles can strongly confine the electric fields within different Al:ZnO shell layers. By flexibly varying the structural parameters, both dielectric dipolar and quadrupolar resonances can be tuned to overlap at two ENZ wavelengths (degenerate ENZMs), enabling two-wavelength superscattering in such subwavelength nanoparticle. Furthermore, we demonstrate that through the interference of degenerate electric dipolar and quadrupolar ENZMs, two-wavelength super-forward scattering can be achieved. This approach, relying on degenerate electric ENZMs in single subwavelength nanoparticle, offers a new pathway for constructing superscattering and superdirectional scattering, holding significant potential for applications in photovoltaic devices, biosensors, and nanoantennas.

articles.title: A Hybrid Particle Filtering and Local Optimization Framework for Solving Challenging Lennard-Jones Cluster Problems
articles.abstract: Lennard-Jones (LJ) cluster optimization is a demanding benchmark for global search because competing energy funnels can trap otherwise effective methods. We introduce a hybrid particle filtering (HPF) framework coupling population exploration with local refinement without problemspecific seeding. An Invertible Particle-Flow (IPF) operator transports particles toward promising configurations, while diversity-aware weighting, adaptive annealing, resampling and rejuvenation balance selection and exploration. Separate accessibility and target-concentration arguments motivate exploration and annealed selection in an idealized uncapped setting; they do not establish convergence of the implemented algorithm. Experiments on LJ38, LJ75–77, LJ98 and LJ102–104 use 30 distinct box-uniform initial populations per size, with independently recorded search seeds. Comparators include basin-hopping with occasional jumping (BH-OJ), genetic algorithms, particle swarm optimization, comprehensive learning particle swarm optimization and sequential Monte Carlo. Baseline evaluation caps were fixed from a separate HPF calibration and do not equal realized computational costs; all BH-OJ/LJ98 runs are time-limited. HPF achieves 100% target attainment on LJ38 and LJ102–104, and 96.7%, 86.7%, 56.7% and 20.0% on LJ75, LJ76, LJ77 and LJ98. BH-OJ succeeds only on LJ38 (10%); other baseline cells have no successes. Ablation on LJ75 and LJ102 identifies local refinement as the largest contributor to target attainment under the tested limits. Removing IPF preserves observed success but increases mean evaluations by factors of 3.32 and 9.11, respectively. These results concern the tested implementations and parameterizations, not their algorithmic families; validation is restricted to LJ clusters.

articles.title: Multisite exchange paths and zigzag antiferromagnetism in the Kitaev material RuI3 monolayer
articles.abstract: Monolayer RuI3, with heavy ligands, is expected to host intriguing Kitaev physics. We derive its jeff=1/2 pseudospin model up to thethird-nearest neighbors (3NN) using exact diagonalization (ED) of N-site clusters (N=1--6), with crystal-field and hopping parameters from density functional theory and Wannier functions. Our results well explain the spin-orbital levels from resonant inelastic x-ray scattering experiments. We find that two-site calculations are insufficient, and multisite exchange via intermediate Ru sites is important. Therefore, we focus on six-site clusters that preserve the bond symmetry, and find that the exchange paths through one intermediate Ru site reduce the 1NN ferromagnetic Kitaev coupling but enhance the 3NN antiferromagnetic Heisenberg coupling, making the two comparable in strength. Their competition, together with sizable 1NN off-diagonal couplings, removes the Kitaev spinliquid and stabilizes zigzag antiferromagnetic order, as predicted by our 24-site ED and 72-site density-matrix renormalization group calculations.

articles.title: PACSYLLM: natural-language access to an expanded PACSY database of protein structures and chemical shifts
articles.abstract: Chemical shifts are the first data obtained in protein NMR studies, and their relationship to three-dimensional structure underlies resonance assignment, secondary-structure analysis, and structure determination. In 2012, PACSY made this relationship searchable by integrating NMR structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB), chemical shifts from the Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank (BMRB), and fold classifications from the Structural Classification of Proteins (SCOP). Many analyses, however, still require SQL queries or custom scripts. Here, we describe a rebuilt, quality-controlled PACSY database and PACSYLLM, a natural-language interface to its data. The database holds 11,537 PDB/BMRB chain pairs, 10,881 of them protein chains, with 7.9 million chemical shifts and 239 million atomic coordinates, 1.6 to 3.9 times the 2012 content. It also stores derived annotations for shift-based secondary-structure and torsion-angle prediction, chemical-shift re-referencing, fold classification, ensemble quality, and covalent geometry. Chemical shifts are matched to the correct molecular entity and checked against their NMR-STAR source files. PACSYLLM keeps scientific computation outside the language model: deterministic programs handle well-defined outputs, while a self-hosted 27-billion-parameter model generates one validated, read-only SQL query and summarizes the returned data. PACSYLLM answered all 26 held-out questions correctly in three repeats and answered reworded versions correctly. The database queries of six published PACSY analyses, each posed as a single natural-language request, returned the published or independently verified results.

articles.title: Micro-topological and Micro-mechanical investigation of compressibility in polydisperse granular assemblies: a 2D DEM study
articles.abstract: The mechanical behaviour of granular materials depends on several parameters, including the properties of intergranular interactions at the particle scale and the fabric at the mesoscopic scale. This study investigates the micro-topological origins of macroscopic compressibility in granular assemblies, focusing on the combined impact of inter-particle friction and size polydispersity. 2D DEM simulations of isotropic compression were performed across a range of friction coefficients and distinct particle size distributions. The simulations show that increasing the confining stress decreases the global void ratio, increases the mechanical coordination number, and reduces the fraction of rattler particles, while the compressibility response is characterized by distinct recompression and virgin compression stages. Initially looser packings, whether induced by higher interparticle friction or a narrower particle size distribution, exhibit greater virgin compressibility. Contact-network analysis reveals that the global void ratio is governed by the topology of elementary loops, with interparticle friction promoting larger loop structures that preserve local voids. A wider particle size distribution enhances global packing through a pore-filling mechanism but also generates pronounced local packing heterogeneity, characterized by the coexistence of densely packed regions and local void pockets. Finally, force-chain analysis shows that the strongest contact forces are predominantly transmitted through well-confined particles in dense regions, although bridge particles spanning local void pockets may also participate in force transmission.

articles.title: Eco-Friendly Carbon Nanodots from Mango Peel Waste Combined with NPK Fertilizer: A Novel Growth Enhancer for Chili (Capsicum frutescens L.) Plants
articles.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to develop an eco-fertilizer by integrating carbon nanodots (C-dots) as a growth enhancer with NPK fertilizer for chili plants, evaluated through controlled pot experiments. Methods: The C-dots, synthesized from mango peel waste via the two-step low heating (TSLH) method yielded a dark brown solution. The C-dots were combined with NPK fertilizer to produce NPK/C-dots composites. The materials were characterized using UV–Vis spectrophotometer, PL spectrometer, FTIR spectrometer, TEM, and SEM. The evaluation was conducted on 25 chili plants under five treatments: well water, pure NPK, pure C-dots, and NPK/C-dots at 100% and 50% concentrations. Results: UV-Vis analysis revealed absorption peaks at 264 nm and 215 nm for pure C-dots and NPK/C-dots, respectively, with a maximum PL emission at 527 nm. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of C=C functional groups as the C-dots core. The surface morphology of the C-dots appeared as a continuous wrinkled sheet-like structure. The TEM analysis indicated that the C-dots had an average particle size of 2.6 ± 0.7 nm. Experimental results demonstrated that the 100% NPK/C-dots composite yielded the highest chili productivity of 174.9 g.  Conclusion: These findings highlighted the potential of C-dots as an innovative supplement for enhancing crop yield while supporting sustainable organic waste treatment.

articles.title: Antiferroelectric Fluids with Hierarchical Polar Organization
articles.abstract: The discovery of the ferroelectric nematic (NF) phase has accelerated research on fluids exhibiting polar order along the molecular long axis. However, their antiferroelectric (AFE) counterparts remain less explored. Here, we investigate how terminal alkyl-chain elongation competes with polar core–core interactions in a homologous series. This series exhibits modulated AFE order accompanied by SmC-type cybotactic correlations, with the AFE phase persisting in homologs bearing terminal alkyl chains of up to 17 carbon atoms. Three distinct phase sequences on cooling lead to two types of two-dimensional (2D) AFE lattices. Multiple sharp X-ray diffraction (XRD) peaks reveal rectangular and oblique lattice structures, supporting their classification as AFE columnar phases. XRD analysis and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations support a hierarchical structural model in which locally aligned polar molecules occupy thin segments of finite width within polar columns. The columns occupy the sites of a 2D lattice, with neighboring columns polarized in opposite directions. This model provides a structural framework for understanding the distinct precursor phase sequences and links packing between columns to the resulting AFE superstructures.

articles.title: A SHAP-Augmented Machine Learning Framework for Optimizing Iron-Carbon Micro-Electrolysis of PVA Wastewater
articles.abstract: While iron-carbon micro-electrolysis (ICME) is effective for treating polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) wastewater, its optimization remains notably constrained by two limitations of Response Surface Methodology (RSM): RSM's poor extrapolation capability and inability to reveal underlying governing mechanisms beyond local experimental domains. To break this bottleneck, this study establishes a triple-integrated paradigm that synergistically combines the experimental rigor of RSM, the predictive power of machine learning, and the mechanistic insights from SHAP interpretability analysis. A high-fidelity dataset of 1,423 samples was constructed via Box-Behnken design augmented with literature data. Among seven machine learning (ML)algorithms evaluated, XGBoost achieved superior predictive performance for COD removal rate(test set R² = 0.8045, RMSE = 6.06, MAPE = 11.25%), demonstrating robust generalization. Crucially, SHAP analysis decoded insights inaccessible to RSM: it identified the Fe/C ratio as the dominant structural factor governing system efficiency and delineated pH 2–3 as the optimal window for synergistic Fe/C ratio - pH interactions. The core innovation lies in the three-tiered methodological integration: RSM provides a rigorous experimental foundation; machine learning enables global, high-accuracy prediction; and SHAP transforms the "black-box" model into a discovery tool for extracting condition-dependent rules. This paradigm shifts the optimization strategy from local empirical tuning to system-level intelligent design, enabling a translatable framework for real-time control and the scale-up process of complex wastewater treatment.

articles.title: Validation of diffusion and exchange imaging biomarkers via simultaneous real-time NMR and optical microscopy
articles.abstract: Diffusion MRI can reflect features of tissue microstructure and homeostasis, but direct validation in living neural tissue remains challenging. Here we combine optical microscopy and NMR for real-time recording on viable ex vivo neural tissue during perturbations. Simultaneous high-temporal-resolution NMR and optical microscopy are used to monitor apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), apparent exchange rate (AXR), intrinsic optical signal (IOS), and intracellular calcium in ex vivo neonatal mouse spinal cord during osmotic and ionic perturbations. We find that ADC correlates strongly with IOS, while AXR decreases with metrics related to depolarization. ADC and AXR are sensitive to distinct features of cellular swelling, supporting their complementary roles in probing tissue viability and function.

articles.title: Bogoliubov-picture thermofield dynamics in anharmonic environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermofield dynamics (TFD) describes finite-temperature quantum relaxation through a purified wavefunction, without sampling thermally populated initial states. For harmonic environments, TFD is typically combined with a thermal Bogoliubov transformation to obtain a compact wavefunction representation. This transformation can also be useful for anharmonic baths, but preparing the corresponding thermal state in the transformed representation poses additional numerical challenges. Here, we explore TFD approaches tailored to anharmonic potentials and compatible with efficient tensor network methods for quantum propagation. We show that the conceptually appealing route of converting a harmonic-reference thermal state into the target anharmonic state by imaginary-time propagation can be numerically ill-conditioned. As a practical alternative, we formulate a multilayer multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (ML-MCTDH) protocol that separates thermal-state preparation from the harmonic-reference Bogoliubov transformation. We prepare the thermal purification in the bare representation and then apply finite-basis Bogoliubov unitaries to the physical--auxiliary mode pairs. For independent bath modes, direct construction of the thermal amplitude provides a complementary initialization procedure. We illustrate this protocol through vibrational relaxation and spatial-superposition decoherence of a harmonic subsystem coupled to a Morse-oscillator bath. We find non-monotonic energy relaxation, shifts in the dominant resonant response, and oscillatory energy exchange at zero and finite temperature. For decoherence, we recover the expected harmonic-bath scaling and find a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of the decay rate on anharmonicity at finite temperature in a low-frequency model, with a weaker dependence in a high-frequency model.

articles.title: Geometry-conditioned differentiable surrogate with adjoint Monte Carlo sampling for scintillator detector co-design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optimizing light-guide geometries for scintillator-based imaging detectors requires repeated photon-transport evaluations, making direct Monte Carlo simulation computationally costly. Differentiable surrogates can accelerate these evaluations and support detector readout co-design aimed at improving information extraction from particle interactions. In this work we describe a surrogate model for photon transport. We develop it starting from a modular, event-driven Monte Carlo model for the generation and transport of scintillation photons, and a reciprocal Monte Carlo construction (an adjoint model) of a spatially and temporally resolved optical response field. The latter evaluates the collectible light output and its temporal structure from a scintillator volume by launching weighted photon trajectories from the light-guide readout face. We apply this approach to a scintillator cell with two mirrored, curved, single-clad light guides. We employ the adjoint model to train a geometry-conditioned neural surrogate that predicts collection probabilities and conditional transport-time distributions across a constrained guide-design family. The surrogate is natively differentiable, lending itself to be an element of a differentiable pipeline for gradient-based optimization. A forward-reciprocal benchmark and validation on held-out geometries establish the accuracy of the trained model and identify its limitations. The developed tools provide a foundation for rapid optical-response studies and detector readout co-design.

articles.title: Classification of Thouless pumps with non-invertible symmetries and implications for Floquet phases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.01626v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study symmetry preserving adiabatic and Floquet dynamics of one-dimensional systems. Using quasiadiabatic evolution, we establish a correspondence between adiabatic cycles and invertible defects generated by spatially truncated Thouless pump operators. Employing the classification of gapped phases by module categories, we show that the Thouless pumps are classified by the group of autoequivalences of the module category. We then explicitly construct Thouless pump operators for minimal lattice models with Vec_G, Rep(G), and Rep(H) symmetries, and show how the Thouless pump operators have the group structure of autoequivalences. The Thouless pump operators, together with Hamiltonians with gapped ground states, are then used to construct Floquet drives. An analytic solution for the Floquet phase diagram characterized by winding numbers is constructed when the Floquet drives obey an Onsager algebra. Our approach points the way to a general connection between distinct Thouless pumps and distinct families of Floquet phases.

articles.title: Origin of Reduced Coercive Field in ScAlN: Synergy of Structural Softening and Dynamic Atomic Correlations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.18710v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Among wurtzite-type ferroelectrics, scandium-doped aluminum nitride (ScAlN) has emerged as a leading candidate for CMOS-compatible low-voltage memory, combining strong spontaneous polarization with process compatibility. A remarkable feature of this system is the pronounced reduction of the coercive field (E_c) with increasing Sc concentration; however, its microscopic origin remains poorly understood at the atomic scale, particularly under finite temperature and applied electric fields. Here, we employ an atomistic simulation framework that integrates a density-functional-theory-accurate machine-learning force field with an equivariant neural-network-based Born effective charge model to perform large-scale electric-field-induced molecular dynamics simulations at near-first-principles accuracy. The framework correctly reproduces key experimentally observed trends, including the decrease in the c/a ratio and the monotonic reduction of E_c with increasing Sc content. Beyond static structural softening, we uncover a dynamic mechanism underlying E_c reduction. Sc atoms exhibit larger thermal vibrations and begin to displace earlier during switching, acting as dynamic triggers for polarization reversal. Moreover, the displacement correlation between Sc and Al atoms evolves systematically with composition, enhancing cooperative atomic rearrangements and lowering the effective switching barrier. These results demonstrate that E_c reduction in ScAlN arises from the synergy of structural softening and dynamic correlation evolution, providing a new perspective for designing hexagonal ferroelectrics.

articles.title: Magnetism and symmetry of superconducting gap in LaFeAsO from dynamical mean-field theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.18582v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By employing a combined method of density functional theory and dynamical mean field theory (DFT+DMFT) we investigate the effect of electronic correlations on the magnetic and superconducting properties of the iron-based parent compound LaFeAsO. We find that the static non-local susceptibility χ(bf q) and the dynamical spin structure factor S(mathbf q,ω) exhibit a peak at the in-plane wave vector mathbf Q=(π,π), which is strongly enhanced upon inclusion of dynamical vertex corrections in the ladder approximation, leading to magnetic instability. Considering the eigenfunctions of the Bethe-Salpeter equation with the vertex, obtained within the second order perturbation theory, as well as the ladder approach containing dynamic interaction vertices, in agreement with earlier weak-coupling-based studies of LaFeAsO, we obtain a close competition between d-wave and s± order parameters, dominating in the second-order and ladder approach, respectively. We argue that the dominating s± instability in the ladder DFT+DMFT approach is related to the reduced degree of magnetic frustration by itinerant degrees of freedom due to only partially formed local magnetic moments. Our study shows that dynamic correlation effects do not change the type of the leading superconducting instability in LaFeAsO.

articles.title: Adaptive Slater Koster Parameters: Crossing Oxidation States with Density Functional Tight Binding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.19977v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose to adapt the confined pseudo-atomic orbitals underpinning the Slater-Koster (SK) tables in density functional tight binding (DFTB) to local atomic environments. Assigning optimal SK parameters to metal atoms in different oxidation states improves the electronic structure of a partially oxidized Ni surface and, with adapted repulsion, Li insertion energetics in graphite. Their smooth, interpretable response to chemical and spatial environment, independently observed for Ni and Co oxides, enables a simple, physically informed machine-learning scheme, here applied to Ni-O binaries.

articles.title: Dictionary learning approach to analytic continuation of imaginary-time quantum Monte Carlo data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.19205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many fields of physics use quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations to simulate quantum systems in imaginary-time τ and estimate imaginary-time correlation functions (ITCF). However, extracting dynamic ω-dependent quantities from ITCFs is a notoriously difficult task, known as analytic continuation (AC), that amounts to solving an exponentially ill-conditioned inverse problem. Within the AC literature, there are competing stochastic and regularized approaches, as well as an emerging collection of works using parameterized models like neural networks. Here we transcend the traditional divides between the communities, introducing the regularized stochastic optimization method (RSOM). This method reformulates AC as a dictionary learning problem, discovering a sparse dictionary to represent the solution. Our approach is motivated by the astounding results dictionary learning has produced in many scientific fields. Remarkably, RSOM discovers a sparse dictionary that maps a high-dimensional ill-conditioned inverse problem to a low-dimensional problem. We demonstrate that the method yields competitive results for common synthetic test problems as well as for authentic QMC data from the finite temperature electron gas. Due to the low dimensionality, there is reasonably finite uncertainty in the dictionary, which is leveraged to create an ad hoc post-processing estimate of the dictionary coefficients' sensitivity to perturbations. This work exposes that a dictionary exists within all stochastic and regularized methods and that dictionary learning provides a new angle of attack for future AC methods.

articles.title: Bridging electrode preparation and electrocatalyst performance with physics-based causal AI using Bayesian Structural Causal Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.30898v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: State-of-the-art artificial intelligence (AI) and Machine-Learning (ML) tools have not yet enabled rapid design of next-generation materials. Detailed physical understanding of how material properties affect device performance is required to advance materials development. For example, optimization of ink parameters for electrocatalysts has no known physical mathematical model and thus insights are difficult to translate from material studies to device studies. Herein, we demonstrate how to use the emerging AI tool, physics-based structural causal models (SCMs), to extract quantitative causative insights from complex heterogeneous electrochemical systems with small (n < 10), but multi-modal datasets. Our SCM quantitatively separates the role that varying the support-to-catalyst ratios and total material loadings plays on catalytic performance. The proof of concept model developed in this work enables root-cause-analysis on the cyclic voltammograms of manganese-antimony oxide oxygen reduction electrocatalysts on Vulcan carbon supports tested in alkaline media using a rotating disc electrode device configuration. Our computational causal analyses quantitatively disentangle how the catalyst performance is affected by the number of active sites versus the thickness of the electrode. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of SCMs with physical equations applied to electrochemical materials and their performance.

articles.title: Evolution of the electronic and superconducting properties of Re-based quinary high-entropy alloys under chemical and physical pressure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.23056v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a comparative study of chemical- and physical-pressure effects on the electronic and superconducting properties of the Re-based quinary high-entropy alloys (HEAs) [Nb0.67-xRex][TiZrHf]0.33 (x = 0.10, 0.20, and 0.56). Increasing Re concentration suppresses the superconducting transition temperature Tc from 5.4 to 3.9 K while producing positive, composition-dependent cocktail-effect ratios. Field-dependent transport and magnetization establish all three compositions as strongly type-II superconductors and identify x = 0.20 as the most distinctive composition, with the largest upper critical field and Ginzburg-Landau parameter and a Maki parameter close to unity. Most importantly, the pressure coefficient of Tc changes sign across the bcc-hcp structural change: dTc/dP is positive for the bcc x = 0.10 and 0.20 samples, with values of approximately 0.018 and 0.053 K/GPa, respectively, but negative for the hcp x = 0.56 sample, with a value of approximately -0.033 K/GPa. This systematic contrast within a single chemically related alloy series establishes a robust structure-associated superconducting response and identifies crystal structure as a key organizing variable under compression. Metallic transport and superconductivity remain robust up to approximately 8 GPa in all three compositions. These results reveal that chemical substitution and hydrostatic compression are complementary but nonequivalent routes for tuning superconductivity in Re-based HEAs.

articles.title: Rotational spectra and de-perturbation analysis for ground state ytterbium oxide, YbO
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.05905v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A combination difference analysis of Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (FTMW) measurements of ¹⁷⁴YbO combined with earlier near-infrared chemiluminescence data have resulted in much improved YbO rotational and centrifugal distortion constants. These have been confirmed in a multi-isotopologue analysis of further FTMW measurements of ¹⁷²YbO and ¹⁷⁶YbO and an analysis of nuclear-size-dependent Born-Oppenheimer breakdown effects in the molecule. Multiple excited electronic states overlap with low-lying excited vibrational levels of the electronic ground state leading to irregularities in its vibrational spacings and other previously observed electronic manifolds. This has been modeled with a matrix of the vibrational levels of the ground and multiple interacting states assuming Morse potentials and including electronic Hamiltonian matrix elements mixing the states. Vibrational level overlaps were calculated numerically assuming Morse vibrational wavefunctions. The resulting de-perturbed potentials for the states inform continuing experimental and theoretical work on this and other ytterbium-containing molecules.

articles.title: Autonomous Optimization of Complex Oxides for Thermochemical Fuel Production
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.06877v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-step thermochemical cycles for H2O and CO2 splitting offer a promising route to sustainable fuel production. Their performance depends on redox-active oxides that undergo cyclic reduction and oxidation reactions. Achieving high thermal-to-fuel conversion efficiency requires both favorable redox thermodynamics and sufficiently rapid reaction kinetics. These requirements have shifted materials design toward complex multication oxides, including mixed-cation fluorites, perovskites, and high-entropy oxides. Developing such materials requires the simultaneous optimization of their composition, defect chemistry, phase stability, and morphology. The resulting design space is difficult to explore through sequential trial and error. Thermochemical fuel production therefore provides a compelling testbed for autonomous materials design and optimization. In this study, we first examine why redox-active complex oxides are challenging to develop owing to their multidimensional phase spaces, harsh operating conditions, and competing functional targets. We then discuss how high-throughput computation, automated synthesis, characterization, and testing, together with machine learning, can be integrated into closed-loop workflows to address these challenges. Drawing on advances from broader oxide materials research, we define a capability roadmap encompassing complex-oxide synthesis, operando characterization, robotic testing, condition-aware computation, and multi-objective optimization. Finally, we identify the key experimental, computational, data, and artificial intelligence capabilities required to build self-improving optimization platforms for materials development in thermochemical fuel production

articles.title: Approximating thermodynamic equilibrium observables of quasi one-dimensional magnetic molecules and chains by thermal DMRG - a user perspective
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.24608v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Density matrix renormalization group methods or tensor network methods in general can not only be used to determine ground states but also to evaluate thermal equilibrium properties. Although convergence is superior for one-dimensional quantum spin systems with nearest neighbor exchange and open boundary conditions, the hope is that these methods can as well be employed to approximate magnetic observables of magnetic molecules with more complex interaction patterns. Here, we assume the position of a user and study the accuracy that can realistically be achieved for several archetypical quasi one-dimensional structures using the TenPy suite. In our study, we aim at systems that are too large for exact diagonalization or Krylov space methods.

articles.title: Positive Temperature Coefficient of Anisotropy due to d⁶L Groundstate in ϵ-Fe₂O₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.08927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Positive anisotropy temperature coefficients (dK/dT>0) usually arise from hybridization between magnetic 3d states and strongly spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) subsystems. Yet ϵ-Fe₂O₃ shows dK/dT>0 (125-200~K) without an obvious SOC partner. We study pure and Cr-doped ϵ-Fe₂O₃ across the transition from low temperature incommensurate to high-anisotropy magnetic phases. We identify a d⁶L groundstate in ϵ-Fe₂O₃ while reduced hybridization yields d⁶ + d⁶L² in the Cr-doped phase, highlighting metal-ligand hybridization as a route to tune magnetic, electronic and orbitronic properties.

articles.title: Stripe-Like Superconducting Enhancement and Coexisting Magnetic Texture in an Infinite Layer Nickelate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.15958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite their promise as structural and electronic analogs to cuprates, nickelate thin films consistently exhibit broadened superconducting transitions in many experiments that remain poorly understood. Local measurements are ideal for revealing the presence of defects or competing phases, which may cause this transition broadening through a phase-separation. Here, we use scanning SQUID microscopy to investigate local superfluid density and magnetic texture of optimally doped Nd₁₋ₓEuₓNiO₂ (NENO) (x=0.25) grown via molecular beam epitaxy. We observed a weakly-magnetic texture coexisting with superconductivity. Spatially resolved susceptibility imaging reveals a highly non-uniform superconducting state, characterized by a robust stripe-like enhancement pattern appearing near the phase transition. By resolving the mesoscopic landscape of electronic and magnetic inhomogeneities, these findings suggest that a competing magnetic phase is a primary contributor to the unusually broad superconducting transitions of these optimally doped NENO samples. Understanding the uncovered superconducting enhancement may provide a path to raising superconducting temperatures in these materials.

articles.title: t-J model at 50
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.35178v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: I briefly overview the original formulation of the t-J model starting from Hubbard model, as well as stress its unique features, i.e., advantages and shortcomings when discussing its physical properties. Particular emphasis is put on a brief characterization of connection between magnetism, unconventional superconductivity, and the Mott-Hubbard localization of the correlated carriers in a narrow band. In the second part I summarize the model generalization to the three--orbital situation. The main purpose is to list some basic features of the physics associated with t--J model.

articles.title: Beyond ideal cavities: quantifying the impact of cavity dissipation on light-matter strong coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities promises to reshape molecular reactivity and properties in a non-invasive and tunable way, yet cavity experiments remain notoriously difficult to interpret and reproduce, highlighting the need for accurate theoretical predictions. Significant progress has been made through ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) methods, but these generally assume ideal, lossless cavity fields, an approximation commonly justified by the assumption that cavity losses are negligible and by the need to keep the methods computationally tractable. Here we show that this approximation is far from innocent: incorporating cavity dissipation through the experimentally accessible quality factor Q reduces the Rabi splitting of p-nitroaniline by more than 10% and red-shifts the minimum polaritonic gap by 0.24 eV, even when the system remains firmly in the strong-coupling regime. This implies that convergence towards the ideal-cavity limit requires quality factors substantially larger than those needed to establish strong coupling itself. Our approach, based on a damped harmonic oscillator description of the cavity field and a time-dependent unitary transformation yielding a real Hermitian Hamiltonian, is demonstrated here within the quantum electrodynamics coupled-cluster singles and doubles framework (QED-CCSD). Its general formulation allows straightforward integration into existing ab initio QED frameworks without increasing the computational cost of the underlying methods, providing a practical and efficient route to quantitatively account for realistic cavity conditions in first-principles simulations of molecular systems in cavities.

articles.title: Local measurements reveal global quantum properties in a constant number of experimental runs
articles.abstract: A quantum device with more qubits is harder to verify. Describing a general quantum state takes an exponential number of parameters, and reconstructing it in full—a procedure known as state tomography—becomes impractical as the system grows. Yet most experiments do not need the full description. They need to know a few things: Is the state close to the target? Are the qubits entangled? And does the system carry the resources needed for quantum computation?

articles.title: Structural, optoelectronic, mechanical, thermodynamic and thermoelectric properties of kesterite Cu2ZnSnS4: A first-principles study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The structural, optoelectronic, mechanical, thermodynamic, and thermoelectric properties of kesterite Cu2ZnSnS4 were investigated using density functional theory. The mBJ and HSE06 approaches yield band gaps of 0.88 and 1.55 eV, respectively. Optical calculations reveal high absorption, with the onset in the 0.8-1.0 eV range. Hydrostatic compression from 0 to 30 kbar decreases the lattice parameters and increases the band gap. The elastic constants satisfy the Born stability criterion, and B/G > 1.75 indicates plastic behavior. Phonon calculations confirm dynamic stability. In the temperature range from 0 to 1000 K, the Helmholtz free energy decreases, the vibrational entropy increases, and the heat capacity approaches a plateau above 500 K. The thermoelectric properties were investigated in the temperature range from 100 to 1000 K. The Seebeck coefficient remains positive, peaking at approximately 310 μV/K at 250 K and decreasing to 239 μV/K at 1000 K. These results encourage the investigation of Cu2ZnSnS4 as a good candidate for thermoelectric power conversion.

articles.title: Multiorbital driving of quantum geometric nonlinear transport in oxide interfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum geometry plays a relevant role in determining the intrinsic non-linear transport properties of low-dimensional electron systems. Here, we theoretically investigate the quantum geometric contribution to the non-linear conductivity in SrTiO₃-based two-dimensional electron gases, comparing the prototypical (001) and (111) crystallographic interface orientations. Using a multi-orbital tight-binding approach, we uncover the crucial role of the multiband electronic structure in determining the quantum-geometric contribution to nonlinear transport. In particular, we show how the hybridization of t₂g orbitals near avoided band crossings shapes the momentum-space distribution of the band-normalized quantum metric and the resulting nonlinear conductivity. Furthermore, we reveal a strong dependence on crystal orientation: while the (001) interface exhibits sharp peak-and-dip features confined around Lifshitz transitions, the trigonal symmetry of the (111) interface promotes strong orbital mixing. Our results highlight how the interplay between orbital hybridization and crystallographic orientation gives rise to distinct quantum-geometric nonlinear transport responses in oxide interfaces.

articles.title: Nonequilibrium fluctuations could explain the hot mitochondria paradox
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several different experiments have found apparent temperature differences of up to 10 K between the interior of mitochondria and the rest of the cellular environment. The physics of heat conduction, however, precludes the steady-state existence of a temperature difference greater than the microkelvin scale within the cell, absent a far greater energy budget. Nearly a decade after the first reported measurement, this apparent paradox remains unexplained. Here, we propose an explanation which allows the elevated temperature measurements to coexist with the theoretical impossibility of a true 10 K steady-state temperature difference. We suggest that nonequilibrium fluctuations within the cellular environment, combined with molecular temperature probes sensitive to specific ranges of frequencies, can lead to apparent 10 K temperature differences with a biologically attainable power budget.

articles.title: Symmetry classes of hyperdeterminant wavefunctions: Application to phase transitions between a bosonic fractional Chern insulator and superfluids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a phase transition between a superfluid phase and a fractional Chern insulator phase in a hard-core boson model on the honeycomb lattice using symmetric hyperdeterminant (Hdet) wavefunctions. Combining projective symmetry group analysis with variational Monte Carlo, we construct and optimize Hdet states in various symmetry classes. Based on the associated effective theories, we show that different symmetry classes, i.e., representations of the projective symmetry group, describe specific quantum phases. Compared with traditional fermionic parton construction, the symmetric Hdet wavefunctions are shown to improve microscopics significantly, allowing quantitative investigation of quantum phase diagrams. We argue that, in contrast with the common belief, this putative continuous phase transition is described by a fluctuating SU(2)_g gauge field coupling with four Dirac nodes forming two SU(2)_g doublets (i.e., N_f=2 QCD).

articles.title: First-Principles Investigation of the ScSe2 TMDs Monolayer: Structural Stability, Electronic and Optical Properties
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an ab initio investigation of the ScSe2 monolayer using density functional theory (DFT), as employed in the CP2K code, to assess its structural stability and electronic properties. The electronic behavior of both phases is governed by the local coordination environment of scandium and the associated lifting of degeneracy of its 3d orbitals. The valence bands (VBs) are dominated by Se-4p states in both phases, while the states near the Fermi level distinguish the metallic 1T phase from the semiconducting 2H phase. Optical response calculations reveal markedly different spectral signatures for the two polymorphs. Two findings emerge from this study: a polymorphism-driven metal-to-semiconductor transition without any change in chemical composition and distinct optical responses relevant to phase-selective optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Persistent Neutron Irradiation Effects and Partial Recovery in Thin-Film CdS/CdTe Solar Cells
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thin-film CdTe solar cells are promising candidates for lightweight space power, but device-level studies of their response to neutron irradiation remain scarce. Here, we report the device performance of CdS/CdTe solar cells irradiated for 10 to 150 min in the thermal irradiator of a TRIGA reactor (90 kW), corresponding to nominal total neutron fluences of 3.3 x 10¹⁴ to 5.0 x 10¹⁵ n cm-2. The cells were characterized after 18 months of post-irradiation storage, once the residual activity has decayed to background levels. Co-irradiated FTO-coated glass reference substrates exhibit a wavelength-dependent transmission loss, with the transmittance at 500 nm decreasing from 80 % to 50 % after 60 min of irradiation. The irradiated cells retain rectifying behavior, but the reverse-bias dark current, photocurrent, and efficiency generally decrease with exposure time. Post-irradiation annealing at 70 degC under one-sun illumination initially improves Jsc and Voc, with the highest efficiency after 4 h. Prolonged annealing, however, causes substantial FF degradation despite continued photocurrent recovery. These trends suggest that irradiation-induced changes in the glass substrate, CdTe absorber, and contacts respond differently to annealing. Understanding underlying defect chemistry and correlating it with device behavior are necessary steps toward radiation-tolerant CdTe photovoltaics for space applications.

articles.title: Higher-Order Modulational Instability in Spin-Orbit-Coupled Bose-Einstein Condensates: Finite-Raman Effects and Branch-Resolved Spectral Redistribution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate higher-order modulational instability and the nonlinear spectral redistribution in a spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) binary Bose--Einstein condensate with equal interactions. For finite Raman coupling, the system is nonintegrable and exhibits both nonoscillatory and oscillatory instability regimes. Raman coupling reshapes the instability bands and changes what harmonics can grow. Direct simulations show that this reorganization modifies the subsequent nonlinear sideband dynamics. In the zero-Raman limit, SOC shifts successive harmonics between instability bands and stability gaps at a fixed carrier wavenumber. It thereby controls higher-order instability, distinct breather branches, and frequency-hopping sequences. We derive exact algebraic coefficients for the carrier and arbitrary-order sidebands. This yields an exact geometric power spectrum for the complete infinite sideband sequence and a unified description of carrier depletion, directional imbalance, and sideband decay, including an exact relation between the instability gain and the minimum spectral decay rate. For two coexisting breather branches with the same background and modulation wavenumber, the higher-gain branch can have a smaller maximum carrier depletion, a slower high-order spectral decay, and a weaker directional imbalance. SOC can also restore a symmetric sideband spectrum when the SOC-induced momentum shift compensates the carrier wavenumber, even when both k and k_L are nonzero. These analytical and numerical results clarify how SOC and Raman couplings organize higher-order instability and nonlinear spectral redistribution, providing a unified framework for studying coherent nonlinear-wave dynamics in multicomponent condensates.

articles.title: Ultrahigh Thermal Conductivity and Mirror-Parity Constraints in a Corrugated Two-Dimensional Oxide
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contrary to the expectation of poor heat transport in oxides, first-principles calculations predict an ultrahigh lattice thermal conductivity of 756 mathrmW,m⁻¹,K⁻¹ at 300 K in corrugated two-dimensional B₂O₂. Acoustic phonons dominate heat transport, with the flexural acoustic (ZA) branch contributing 40.62%. Triplet resolved analysis including acoustic and optical partners finds that mirror forbidden three phonon scattering is negligible within numerical precision for sampled ZA modes. These results highlight horizontal mirror symmetry as a constraint on phonon scattering in corrugated oxides.

articles.title: Tritium speciation and transport in molten FLiBe: parameters, uncertainties and validation priorities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molten lithium fluoride-beryllium fluoride (FLiBe) is a candidate liquid breeder material for fusion applications, but predictive modelling of tritium retention, transport and extraction depends on chemical and interfacial assumptions that remain only partly resolved. Tritium produced in lithium-bearing fluoride salts may occur in oxidised or fluoride-associated states and can exchange into molecular hydrogen-isotope species such as HT. The relative populations and apparent transport behaviour depend on salt composition and condition, redox state, and interactions at gas-liquid and salt-wall boundaries. This review assesses the evidence for tritium speciation and transport in molten FLiBe, with emphasis on the solubility, effective diffusivity, permeability, exchange and boundary-transfer parameters required by continuum models. The available evidence motivates a two-pool continuum description with separate oxidised or fluoride-associated and molecular-hydrogen pools, without assigning a unique microscopic species. This description applies where states omitted from these pools do not materially affect tritium inventory or transport in the salt. We distinguish directly measured quantities from fitted or inferred effective parameters, recommend how source-specific transport data should be reported and compared, and identify the measurements required to constrain the remaining uncertainties in speciation, exchange, bulk transport and boundary transfer.

articles.title: A High-Frequency Flux-Driven DC-SQUID Threshold Detector at the Single-Microwave-Photon Energy Scale: A Numerical Feasibility Study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our recent work (Phys. Rev. B 113, 224503 (2026)), we showed numerically that rapidly sweeping the bias current of a current-biased Josephson junction threshold detector (CBJJ-JTD) drives it out of equilibrium. This substantially reduces the effect of thermal noise on microwave detection and may enable threshold detection near the energy of a single microwave photon. The scheme requires very low damping (β ≤ 10⁻⁴) and a very fast bias-current sweep (v/β ≥ 1), both of which are difficult to achieve with available junctions and low-pass-filtered cryogenic measurement lines. Here we propose a more experimentally accessible nonequilibrium threshold detector based on a high-frequency flux-driven direct-current superconducting quantum interference device (DC-SQUID) and investigate it by numerically solving the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) equations. The applied flux drives a circulating supercurrent and sustains nonequilibrium phase dynamics throughout the bias-current sweep, removing the need for a fast sweep or for transient oscillations set by the initial phase. Using typical experimental device parameters, we calculate switching-current distributions (SCDs) with and without a microwave input for both driven and undriven SQUIDs. We quantify detection performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and their area under the curve (AUC). The simulations show that high-frequency flux drive reduces the impact of thermal noise and enables statistical discrimination of weak microwave pulses at the single-photon energy scale. We also numerically estimate detector characteristics such as phase selectivity and dynamic range.

articles.title: Spherical HgTe nanocrystal: a multi-band effective mass study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The size-quantized energies, eigenstates, and optical selection rules in a spherical HgTe nanocrystal are studied by solving the multi-band effective-mass equations analytically. The six-band Kane model, involving both the Γ₆ and Γ₈ bands within the spherical approximation, is employed in the derivation. The eigenstates can be classified by both the total angular momentum and the parity. As the nanocrystal radius varies, crossings occur not only between electron and hole energy levels but also among the hole levels themselves. The lowest two electron states (in each spin subspace) are surface states, one with even parity and the other with odd parity. The optical selection rules consist of two parts, namely, the parity selection and the angular momentum selection.

articles.title: Minimal Three-Band Model and d-Wave Superconductivity in La₄Ni₃O₈
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent observation of ambient-pressure superconductivity in Pr- and Y-substituted La₄Ni₃O₈, we combined density-functional theory (DFT), dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), random phase approximation (RPA), and fluctuation exchange approximation (FLEX) methods to study its electronic structure and superconducting pairing symmetry. DFT band analysis indicates that the low-energy states are mainly dominated by three Ni-3dₓ^₂₋y^₂ orbitals with weak d-p hybridization. Multi-orbital DMFT calculations yield an average dₓ^₂₋y^₂ filling of about 0.87, close to the optimal value for infinite-layer nickelates. By comparing the DMFT results of dₓ^₂₋y^₂ only and full Ni-3d models, we find that their electronic properties are almost completely consistent, demonstrating the effectiveness of the simplified dₓ^₂₋y^₂ model. RPA and FLEX calculations based on this model consistently indicate a dominant dₓ^₂₋y^₂-wave pairing instability. These results establish La₄Ni₃O₈ as a system whose electronic structure closely resembles that of hole-doped cuprates, suggesting that the electronic pockets near the Γ- and A-points, which are characteristic of infinite-layer nickelates, may not be essential for superconductivity. The calculated superconducting transition temperature (T_C) is approximately 10,K, in good agreement with experimental observations.

articles.title: Synthesis Method-dependent Resist-like Behavior of Liquid Crystalline Graphene Oxide Films Under Electron Beam Irradiation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Here, the electron-beam-induced structural evolution and patterning behavior of chitosan-functionalized GO films, specifically those using chemically vs electrochemically exfoliated GO, are investigated. Experimental results (supported by DFT calculations) revealed that electron irradiation drives controllable microstructure formation in GO by selectively triggering ablation and densification pathways, which are dictated by the GOs synthesis route and initial oxidation state. Furthermore, a comprehensive characterization study was conducted to compare the optostructural properties of the present system prior and subsequent to electron-beam irradiation. Moreover, a systematic study of the films mechanical properties across both micro- and macroscopic scales was also performed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms responsible for the observed phenomena. The results demonstrate that the integration of mask-free electron-beam patterning, multiscale characterization, and DFT modeling establishes a previously unexplored synthesis-structure-irradiation relationship in GO films, providing fundamental insights into irradiation-induced microstructure evolution and opening new avenues for the design of GO-based micro- and nanostructured materials.

articles.title: Large Deviations and Critical Scaling in the Finite-Population Granovetter Threshold Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a systematic asymptotic analysis of the exact finite-population solution of Granovetter's threshold model, in which a single initial instigator triggers a cascade among agents with independently distributed adoption thresholds.
