By expressing the propagation probability as an order-statistic boundary-crossing event, we formulate its macroscopic large-deviation rate as a constrained relative-entropy minimization problem. For Beta-distributed thresholds, we obtain explicit solutions for all shape parameters α and β, identifying four possible optimal empirical threshold profiles: fully free, fully pinned, pinned--free, and free--pinned. These profiles determine both the exponential probability of macroscopic cascades and the threshold configurations responsible for their occurrence. Importance-sampling estimates confirm the analytical rate functions, while sequential Monte Carlo simulations independently reproduce the predicted optimal profiles. We also revisit the critical scaling near α_c=1 and confirm the principal finite-size scaling laws: the mean active fraction decays as N⁻¹/² for uniform thresholds and as N⁻¹ for α=1 and 0<β<1. In the latter regime, we further derive an explicit scaling function for the logarithmic critical window from the microscopic branching-process limit. Our results provide a general framework for determining the probabilities and characteristic configurations of rare collective events in threshold-driven cascade processes

articles.title: Charge-fluctuation hot lines and superconductivity in Ba₁₋ₓKₓBiO₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The origin of superconductivity near 30~K in Ba₀.₆K₀.₄BiO₃ has remained a long-standing puzzle. Tunneling experiments give an electron--boson coupling λapprox 0.7--1.2, whereas density-functional calculations give λapprox 0.3, concentrated in the breathing mode near 50--70~meV. We propose that the missing coupling of about 0.7 comes from dynamical charge fluctuations at Q=(pi,pi,pi)/a, the ordering vector of the charge-disproportionated parent compound, and introduce an overdamped boson model to describe them. Using a tight-binding fit to the conduction band found from density-functional calculations at x=0.4, we show that such a boson scatters electrons strongly only on hot lines of the Fermi surface, small loops around the langle 111rangle directions where k and k+Q are both at the Fermi level. We derive closed-form self-energies, quasiparticle residues and band reconstructions, including shadow bands and hot-line pseudogaps for long-range correlations, and show that a sum rule fixes the Fermi-surface-averaged coupling independently of the boson frequency and correlation length. Combining the LDA phonon with an overdamped mode of frequency ωₘapprox 25~meV and coupling λapprox 0.7, anisotropic Eliashberg calculations reproduce T_capprox 25--30~K for correlation lengths of two to three lattice spacings and predict a gap enhanced by a factor of 3--4 on the hot loops. For longer correlation lengths an s-wave state competes closely with a sign-changing T₂g state confined to the hot loops. In the random-phase approximation for an extended Hubbard model, the boson emerges naturally near a charge instability at R, but purely electronic fluctuations are too weak and too long-ranged; coupling to the breathing-mode lattice distortion is one possible way to strengthen them.

articles.title: Observation of nonadiabatic quantum tunneling in a driven correlated insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many emerging solid-state platforms for Floquet engineering, nonlinear transport, and high harmonic generation operate near the Keldysh crossover, where optical fields are sufficiently strong and fast to reshape electronic states on sub-cycle timescales. Despite its importance, the microscopic pathways for photocarrier generation in this regime remain poorly understood, as neither perturbative multiphoton absorption nor adiabatic tunneling provides an adequate description. Here, we perform time-resolved optical spectroscopy on the correlated van der Waals insulator NiPS₃ while systematically tuning the drive electric field and frequency over a wide range. In the crossover regime, we observe multiphoton-like resonances that are blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects within an otherwise tunneling-dominated absorption channel - a clear spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown. Hubbard-model simulations based on a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach qualitatively reproduce these features. Together, our results elucidate the microscopic mechanisms of charge excitation in the Keldysh crossover regime and identify a key ingredient for controlling strong-field nonlinear dynamics in correlated materials.

articles.title: An informational interpretation of the reverse nonequilibrium molecular dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reverse nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (RNEMD) is an efficient simulation method for determining transport coefficients. In this method, a flux is imposed by a seemingly artificial nonlocal exchange operation and the corresponding thermodynamic gradient is induced as a result, apparently reversing the usual force-flux causality. Although this method is well studied as a simulation technique, developing an information-thermodynamic interpretation of its Maxwell-demon-type operation and the associated apparent reversal of force-flux causality would provide a solid physical foundation for algorithms of this type. Here, we develop an information-reservoir interpretation for a representative RNEMD scheme for determining self-diffusivity. We show that the statistical bias of the information reservoir defines an information affinity that sustains a concentration gradient and a diffusive flux in the steady state. We further derive the linear transport coefficient corresponding to the information affinity in the linear response regime. Using the large deviation functional for the steady-state densities and currents, we also establish a fluctuation theorem for entropy production and the thermodynamic uncertainty relation linking entropy production to the fluctuations of the particle current. Computer simulations are performed to corroborate our theoretical results.

articles.title: AgenticMM: A Material-Centered Multi-Agent Architecture for Scalable First-Principles Materials Modeling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent frameworks are attracting increasing attention as a means of autonomously driving complex, long-running workflows in first-principles materials modeling. However, such frameworks commonly organize AI agents by computational task or scientific role. When scaled across many materials, this organization can require repeated transfers of material-specific context and complicate persistent execution and resource coordination. Here, we introduce AgenticMM, a material-centered multi-agent architecture in which each material has a persistent agent that owns its complete workflow and retains its scientific context, while a persistent coordinator allocates shared resources, mediates communication, and tracks campaign progress. AgenticMM is designed to incorporate reusable, prompt-based skills as modular definitions of these workflows. Using DefectSkills prompts, we demonstrate the feasibility of AgenticMM through a multistage point-defect campaign in which material-specific agents concurrently perform host electronic-structure, phase-stability, and intrinsic-defect calculations for five chemically diverse semiconductors.

articles.title: Quantum-Metric-Driven Hollow Wigner Crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies have revealed the profound influence of Berry curvature on electron crystallization, yet the independent role of the quantum metric remains unclear. Here, we introduce a minimal three-band continuum model with separately tunable quantum metric and Berry flux. Employing the Hartree-Fock approach, we find that a conventional s-wave Wigner crystal can develop a hollow charge distribution with depleted density at lattice sites, without a change in symmetry or topology. We show that this density reconstruction occurs even at vanishing Berry curvature and arises from strong quantum metric and the nontrivial angular structure of the form factor. In our model, the continuous crossover between hollow and conventional WCs is accompanied by anomalous direct exchange interactions, nearly vanishing at intermediate quantum metric but enhanced by over an order of magnitude in the strong-metric regime. These results reveal how quantum metric can reshape both the charge distribution and exchange interactions of electron crystals beyond simple wave-function delocalization.

articles.title: Auditing a superconducting database built by a large language model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The data on superconducting materials are published as measurements and scattered across the literature, in prose, in tables and in figures, so that gathering them into one place means reading the papers themselves. Large language models (LLMs) can read those papers, and databases built that way are appearing. The difficulty is not the reading but the trust: a number lifted out of a sentence can belong to a neighbouring compound, a computed transition temperature can be recorded without saying that it is computed, and the paper itself may be wrong. This paper describes a pipeline that extracts superconducting materials from the published literature with an LLM, checks every value against its source, and asks how far that checking goes. The pipeline proposed 19,576 records; a cascade of gates rejected 659,252 field-level extractions, 644,438 of them for want of verbatim evidence, 13,121 because the text does not attach the value to the material, and 1,693 because the source sentence reads as a calculation. The database that survives holds 3,137 material records, each with the sentence its value came from. An audit of the survivors by two independent models, on 500 records drawn in proportion to the database, shows that the gates remove the errors that are mechanical: in 93.4% of the audited records the value is in the text and the text is about the compound the record names, and 91.8% of them are measurements rather than predictions.

articles.title: Engineering strategies for high-performance self-powered zinc oxide (ZnO) ultraviolet photodetectors: a design-oriented review
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-powered ultraviolet (UV) photodetectors generate a signal at zero applied bias, removing standby power and suppressing dark current, suiting battery-free Internet-of-Things sensing. Zinc oxide (ZnO) is the archetypal absorber for this task: UV-selective, earth-abundant, non-toxic, and processable at low temperature from solution. Operating it without bias, however, requires a built-in asymmetry that pristine ZnO rarely provides. Because the literature is organized by material or mechanism, the design logic remains obscured. Here we organize the field by engineering strategy, identifying five families of levers (junction and built-in-field engineering, doping and defect control, polarization coupling, interface/surface and photoelectrochemical engineering, and architecture and light management) and mapping each onto the metrics it serves and the trade-offs it imposes. A unifying lens is the zero-bias doping paradox: raising carrier density narrows the depletion region that zero-bias collection needs, so the self-powered optimum differs from the biased one. We flag the detectivity, speed, and active-area pitfalls that make zero-bias performance easy to overstate, and condense the synthesis into a decision tree linking target metric to strategy and growth route. The remaining bottlenecks (persistent photoconductivity, p-type ZnO, and reporting consistency) are problems of defect control and rigorous measurement, not of new materials.

articles.title: Ballistic propagation-mediated super-resolution light-element imaging: in-situ tracking dynamic hydrogen migration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transmission electrons - with few-picometer wavelengths - can theoretically resolve all atoms in solids. However, constrained by factors such as lens aberrations, Z-contrast dependence and poor temporal resolution, the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) fails to tackle the long-standing challenge of hydrogen dynamics on atomic scale. Here, our experiment-guided simulations reveal that unlike heavy-atom imaging - governed by wave-based imaging process - ballistic propagation of particle-like electrons in Cs-corrected TEM enables super-resolution imaging (SRI) of light atoms, achieving a resolution down to 14 pm and a robust hydrogen contrast of ~24%. Our in-situ SRI study not only uncovers polymetric hydrogen aggregation in TiHx and H-LaAlO3, but also inter-site migration, rotational displacement of hydrogen species and collective hydrogen tunneling-induced polarization surge in the oxide. By exploiting the novel electron-matter interactions, our findings offer an unparalleled approach to probe hydrogen dynamics and establish accurate structure-property relationships in diverse functional materials.

articles.title: Geometry Reorganizes Nonequilibrium States that Gate Topological Switching in an Active Polymer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Even under identical external conditions, a driven system can occupy distinct long-lived states with different susceptibilities to the same rare transition. We demonstrate this in a confined partially active polymer, where independent unknotted replicas occupy distinct mechanical states with different topological futures. Matched-control and event-resolved analyses reveal a susceptible reservoir and a short threading precursor. We test this state dependence prospectively by launching 2272 Langevin-noise branches from 71 preserved unknotted phase-space states using a classifier prespecified from independent data. Most strikingly, the same classifier strongly separates finite-time knotting at one pore radius, yet reverses its susceptibility ordering at a neighboring radius. Thus geometry does not merely shift an average knotting rate; it selects among long-lived nonequilibrium states and reorganizes the mapping between a pre-existing mechanical coordinate and future topological fate.

articles.title: Exact many-body scars of generic spin models from singlet covers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The square-lattice transverse-field Ising model has exact zero-energy eigenstates at any field: products of singlets on alternate plaquette diagonals. A longitudinal field isolates them from a symmetry-protected degeneracy. The mechanism is that a site coupled equally to both ends of a singlet annihilates it. The result thus holds for any spin s, anisotropic exchange, a large class of bond disorder and certain three-spin terms. This mechanism decides which lattices host such states: two of the 11 Archimedean lattices (four at s=1/2), bcc and quasicrystals with spins on the edges. Singlet pumping cools any state into them.

articles.title: Pyroelectric Harvesting from Steady Heat Sources via Active Piezoelectric Thermal Switching
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study demonstrates pyroelectric energy harvesting from a steady heat source using active piezoelectric thermal switching in a PZT/Si bimorph cantilever. The same PZT layer serves as both the mechanical actuator and the pyroelectric energy-conversion element. Dual output electrodes enable separation of the pyroelectric and piezoelectric signals. Pyroelectric energy harvesting is experimentally demonstrated at frequencies up to 110 Hz and temperature differences as small as 5 K. Comparison with the response predicted from the independently measured pyroelectric coefficient, together with transient thermal simulations, identifies dynamic interfacial heat transfer as a key limitation to high-frequency operation. This work demonstrates a compact MEMS approach for higher-frequency pyroelectric energy harvesting from low-grade steady heat sources.

articles.title: Geometric Polarization-Virial Theorems for Field-Induced Dipolar Interactions and Force Reversal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electric fields can turn attraction into repulsion between far-separated atoms, yet the complete angular mechanical structure governing this reversal has remained unknown. Here, we uncover an entropy-like geometric structure: the cubically weighted interaction free energy, r³ F(r), is nondecreasing under physical dilation. This structure unifies two exact polarization-virial theorems for arbitrary stable quasistatic dipole assemblies and fully retarded dipole pairs under stated conditions. Consequently, the free energy has at most one zero and energetic cancellation precedes mechanical cancellation. A force zero retains strictly positive energy, whereas an energy zero retains an attractive force. The resulting analytical angular fine structure is resolved by a quantum harmonic oscillator pair, yielding the complete arbitrary-angle interaction energy and radial force that recover quantum-perturbative results. The conventional dipolar magic angle splits into strictly ordered energy- and force-zero angles; the latter uniquely bounds the radially repulsive sector and carries a positive energy barrier. Derived scaling laws and finite-sphere calculations provide experimentally testable signatures from microscopic dipoles to macroscopic polarizable bodies.

articles.title: Domain advantage in two-dimensional quantum-device design with multi-modal agentic harness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-quality two-dimensional quantum devices are commonly fabricated from mechanically exfoliated crystals, whose irregular shapes and placement require a lithographic layout tailored to each specimen. Drawing these layouts remains largely manual. We introduce qlaybench, a benchmark that tests whether language-model agents can turn microscope images and experimental requirements into device layouts that fit the specimen. Agents with conventional tools often construct devices when material outlines are supplied, but struggle to identify those outlines from images. Modelled on the human workflow, qlaybot, a multimodal agentic harness, connects image interpretation to the tools used to align images, draw device features and inspect the resulting layout. We evaluate each layout with checks drawn from practical design experience, asking whether it fits the specimen and connects its intended components. With greater computational effort, an agent using qlaybot passes 81.5% of the benchmark tasks, compared with 24.1% when it uses conventional tools. This domain advantage highlights the importance of connecting scientific interpretation of a specimen to geometric design and provides a route towards reducing manual effort in two-dimensional quantum-device fabrication.

articles.title: Valence band, electron correlation, and possible temperature dependent change in the electronic structure near E_F of a candidate of ambient-pressure nickelate superconductors Sr₃Ni₂O₅Cl₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoemission spectroscopy (PES) studies of Sr₃Ni₂O₅Cl₂ (Sr3252), a candidate ambient-pressure bilayer nickelate superconductor, have been performed to investigate the electronic structure. Valence band spectra, which are compared with DFT and DFT+U calculations, reveal dominant Ni 3d t₂g-derived states located around 0.6 eV binding energy with a shoulder around 0.2 eV that can be attributed to states with a dominant Ni 3d₃z₂₋ᵣ₂ character. The overall valence band shape is better reproduced by the simulated spectrum of DFT+U (= 3 eV), providing an experimental estimation of the strength of electron correlation. High-resolution PES near the Fermi level (E_F) exhibits marked temperature dependence, which cannot be fully understood by a broadening due to coupling of a photo-hole to phonons alone and suggests change in electronic structure. The results provide fundamental electronic structure information of Sr3252, which is useful to further explore the superconductivity of Sr3252.

articles.title: Soliton Propagation of Zero Sound in Superfluid ³He-B
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear equations for zero sound interacting with the B-phase collective modes are derived by treating ³He-B as a medium of two-level ``molecules'' (Cooper pairs), The nonlinear equations reduce to known results from kinetic theory in the linear response limit. Soliton solutions to the nonlinear equations are discussed in context with the experiments of Polturak et al.

articles.title: Apparent thermal conductivity governed by interface-injected phonon spectra
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermoreflectance techniques such as time- and frequency-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR and FDTR) are widely used to measure the thermal conductivity of bulk materials, thin films, and interfaces. When phonon mean free paths Λ_ω become comparable to the thermal penetration depth, a Fourier analysis yields an apparent thermal conductivity κᵣₘ ₐₚₚ that deviates from the bulk value κᵣₘ bᵤₗₖ. Recent studies have highlighted the role of the phonon spectrum injected through the transducer interface, which is generally out of equilibrium owing to frequency-dependent transmission, and have shown that accounting for this nonequilibrium distribution can yield κᵣₘ ₐₚₚ>κᵣₘ bᵤₗₖ, unlike conventional suppression-function analyses that predict only κᵣₘ ₐₚₚ≤κᵣₘ bᵤₗₖ. However, the spectral characteristics governing whether κᵣₘ ₐₚₚ is enhanced or reduced remain unclear. Here, we resolve the surface-temperature response of semi-infinite Si mode by mode and show that short-Λ_ω-weighted injection raises the surface temperature, whereas long-Λ_ω-weighted injection lowers it. This behavior is governed by how deep the injected phonons travel before thermalizing with the lattice, which is set by their mean free paths, and by how effectively the substrate conducts the injected energy away, which is limited by its long-mean-free-path phonons. For an Al (70 nm)/Si structure, Fourier fits of synthetic TDTR phase signals give κᵣₘ ₐₚₚ of Si from about 93 to 360 W/(m K) for different interfacial transmission spectra, and κᵣₘ ₐₚₚ correlates with the heat-flux-weighted Λ_ω of the transmitted phonons. Thus, κᵣₘ ₐₚₚ from thermoreflectance reflects not only the substrate thermal properties but also the phonon spectrum injected across the transducer interface.

articles.title: Critical Topology: A New Perspective for Phase Transitions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Critical topology has emerged as a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm, challenging conventional approaches to classifying universality classes by introducing topological properties as an additional criterion. Despite substantial progress over the past five years, several fundamental questions remain open. Theoretically, can we establish a general criterion for the emergence of critical topology? Can a unified theoretical framework be extended beyond one-dimensional quantum many-body systems? What efficient numerical methods can be developed to investigate critical topological states in higher-dimensional strongly correlated systems? Experimentally, research has so far focused primarily on single-particle critical topology. An important next step is to realize and characterize many-body critical topology in quantum systems using platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays, superconducting quantum processors, and quantum materials. Major advances in statistical physics often arise from re-examining fundamental concepts. The theory of critical phenomena developed by Landau, Ginzburg, and Wilson, together with the topological phase transitions pioneered by Kosterlitz and Thouless, has now inspired new discoveries in artificial acoustic metamaterials. These experimental observations mark a beginning rather than an endpoint for research on critical topology, and further advances in this direction are anticipated.

articles.title: Correlated chemical and displacive disorder in a lithium-rich disordered rocksalt revealed by electron diffuse scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lithium transport in disordered rocksalt cathodes depends on local cation arrangements and atomic distortions that are hidden from average-structure analysis. Resolving both contributions experimentally remains challenging, particularly in powders where directional information is lost. Here, we use electron diffuse scattering and three-dimensional difference pair distribution function analysis (3D-ΔPDF) to resolve occupational and displacive correlations in the model lithium-rich rocksalt Li₂.5TiO₃F₀.5. We identify an unusual combination of like-cation first-neighbour and unlike-cation second-neighbour preferences with correlated anion displacements towards Ti and accompanying cation displacements. A minimal pair-interaction model incorporating these displacements reproduces the principal diffuse-scattering and 3D-ΔPDF features and improves agreement with powder-PDF measurements. The experimentally constrained cation configurations exhibit an above-random population of 0-TM lithium-migration environments. These results establish electron 3D-ΔPDF as a route to constrain atomistic models incorporating chemical order and local relaxation, providing a foundation for assessing their combined influence on lithium migration in disordered rocksalt materials.

articles.title: Asymmetrical transport distribution function: skewness as a key to enhance thermoelectric performance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How to achieve high thermoelectric figure of merit is still a scientific challenge. By solving the Boltzmann transport equation, thermoelectric properties can be written as integrals of a single function, the transport distribution function (TDF). In this work, the shape effects of transport distribution function in various typical functional forms on thermoelectric properties of materials are systematically investigated. It is found that the asymmetry of TDF, characterized by skewness, can be used to describe universally the trend of thermoelectric properties. By defining symmetric and asymmetric TDF functions, a novel skewness is then constructed for thermoelectric applications. It is demonstrated, by comparison with ab initio calculations and experiments, that the proposed thermoelectric skewness not only perfectly captures the main feature of conventional skewness, but also is able to predict the thermoelectric power accurately. This comparison confirms the unique feature of our proposed thermoelectric skewness, as well as its special role of connection between the statistics of TDF and thermoelectric properties of materials. It is also found that the thermoelectric performance can be enhanced by increasing the asymmetry of TDF. Finally, it is also interesting to find that the thermoelectric transport properties based on typical quantum statistics (Fermi-Dirac distributions), can be well described by typical shape parameter (skewness) for classical statistics.

articles.title: The effect of isotopically-enriched 70Ge on the Raman scattering in Cr2Ge2Te6
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The highest-energy A5g Raman-active vibrational mode in chromium germanium telluride (Cr2Ge2Te6, CGT) exhibits a unique lineshape comprising a series of remarkably narrow peaks. While this multiplet was attributed to the natural isotope distribution of germanium affecting Ge-Ge pseudo-molecular vibrations, direct evidence has been lacking. Here, we present a Raman spectroscopy study of CGT isotopically enriched with 70Ge to validate this hypothesis. Upon isotopic enrichment, both the E5g and A5g modes exhibit a pronounced blue-shift. At room temperature, the A5g peak undergoes significant narrowing, while low-temperature measurements reveal a single, well-defined line instead of the previously observed multiplet. These observations align precisely with density functional theory calculations, confirming that the multi-line profile originates from Ge isotope distribution. Our findings demonstrate that similar isotope-induced Raman splitting may occur in other structurally analogous layered tellurides containing Ge or Si.

articles.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and an ultralow holding voltage. Gate-pulse modulation and temperature-dependent measurements indicate avalanche-assisted thyristor operation and latching behavior. This 2D lateral heterostructure enables a new route to nonlinear and bistable switching, latching, ultralow standby power, and adaptive logic, opening the way for reconfigurable 2D electronics and photonic integrated circuits.

articles.title: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate electronic transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer with two quantum dots in the presence of finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. With the help of a diagrammatic technique, we derive, within linear perturbation theory in the tunnelling-coupling strength, analytic expressions for the occupations, current, and interferometric visibility in terms of a coherence measure that involves the sum of four off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix. The latter are calculated numerically from a master equation for arbitrary settings of the system parameters. For some symmetric setups, we obtain closed-form expressions for the linear conductance. We systematically analyse the impact of a finite Coulomb interaction on the interferometric visibility, and reveal a rapid suppression of destructive interference upon breaking of system symmetries. Our results are supported by alternative methods, including the TraSPI method.

articles.title: Geometry-controlled clogging and transport mechanisms in confined Y-junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate transport and clogging of hard particles in a confined symmetric Y-junction using off-lattice Monte Carlo simulations. The geometry is controlled by the channel width w and a truncation parameter s that modifies the inner vertex. The flow probability exhibits a sharp sigmoidal crossover, defining a characteristic width wc that depends non-monotonically on s. This non-monotonic behavior persists under variations of the transverse Monte Carlo step, although the absolute values of wc change. Microscopic analysis reveals two distinct blocking mechanisms: single-particle obstruction at small truncations and collective arch-like structures at larger truncations. Residence-time statistics and particle-order inversions provide additional evidence of this change in transport dynamics. Our results demonstrate that local modifications of junction geometry can strongly affect clogging and particle transport, even in a minimal model with excluded-volume interactions only.

articles.title: Janus Asymmetry Unlocks Rashba Spintronics and Chiral Phononics in Two-Dimensional Carbo-Chalcogenides
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spintronics and chiral phononics offer complementary routes for nanoscale control, yet realizing both functionalities within a common two-dimensional platform remains challenging. Here, using extensive first-principles calculations, we show that Janus asymmetry simultaneously drives both effects in transition-metal carbo-chalcogenides (JTMCCs) along two chemically distinct routes, through either chalcogen or transition-metal substitution. Remarkably, both Janus routes yield giant Rashba responses, with α_Rapprox2 eV Å in Ta₂CSSe and NbTaCS₂, exceeding those reported for Mo/W-based Janus transition-metal dichalcogenides. Furthermore, Janus asymmetry lifts the degeneracy of opposite-chirality phonons, producing splittings as large as approx28 cm⁻¹. More strikingly, asymmetry generates chiral carbon vibrations that were achiral in the centrosymmetric parent compounds, with splittings reaching approx8 cm⁻¹. Finally, we show external electric fields tunability over Rashba strength and chiral-phonon splittings, providing a common control knob for electronic spin and lattice angular momentum. Our work offers a unified strategy for realizing spintronic and chiral phononic in two-dimensional materials.

articles.title: Perfect Spin-to-Charge Signal Conversion via Inverse Spin Hall Effect in a Superconductor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-to-charge conversion is central to spintronics, but conventional spin Hall mechanisms are intrinsically limited by the small spin Hall angle. Here we show that superconductivity can overcome this limitation and enable near-unity spin-to-charge signal conversion. We consider a nonlocal spin-valve geometry in which a spin accumulation is injected into a superconductor and converted into a transverse charge signal through the inverse spin Hall effect. In the superconducting state, the strongly suppressed quasiparticle conductance below the gap allows the resulting charge imbalance to generate a voltage comparable to the injected spin bias, despite a small spin Hall angle. We derive the full nonequilibrium response including finite spectral broadening and finite temperature, and propose temperature and spin-bias-dependent measurements of the detector voltage to test our predictions.

articles.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches. For example, we show that it can further delay the production of tripartite entanglement. We build the quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap, and prove that it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement for crystal quenches. We discuss several key aspects of their tripartite entanglement dynamics through the lens of the Markov gap. We confront our results with exact lattice numerics and find perfect agreement in the hydrodynamic regime.

articles.title: Gallium at germanium surfaces: links to superconducting films and correlated adatom lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Epitaxial films grown on Ge(001) show that germanium hyperdoped with substitutional Ga is superconducting. In earlier implanted films, Ga-rich precipitates obscured the origin of the superconductivity. This review examines the sites Ga occupies on Ge(001) and Ge(111) and how it enters the growing film. The Ga fraction expected from the growth fluxes is 17.9%, yet the distribution of Ga among lattice sites is unknown. Comparisons include Ga on Si(001) and Si(111),In, Sn, Pb, Sb and P on Ge(001), and elemental and two-dimensional Ga. Where its surface coordination has been established, Ga has three bonds, whereas substitutional Ga in the films is fourfold coordinated and acts as an acceptor. Scanning tunnelling microscopy and X-ray standing waves have assigned Ga sites on Ge(111), but the dilute Ga site on Ge(001), where the films are grown, has yet to be measured. On Ge(111), Ga in the substrate may supply holes to the correlated Sn adatom lattice, as B supplies holes to the superconducting Sn lattice on Si(111). Whether Ga can supply holes depends on where it sits and whether it has three or four neighbours. On both surfaces, element-specific measurements and calculations comparing adsorption with substitution could settle the remaining site assignments.

articles.title: Interaction-driven ordering of multiple pseudospins and anomalous Hall metals in Bernal-stacked graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent observations of anomalous Hall states in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene raise a fundamental question: How do electron-electron interactions organize multiple low-energy pseudospin sectors within each spin-valley flavor? Within the Hartree-Fock approximation, we analyze interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and spin-valley polarization as functions of displacement field and carrier density. We find a rich phase diagram shaped by the interplay between the two pseudospin doublets, including mixed flavor orders at charge neutrality and anomalous Hall metals upon doping. In particular, we identify topological states with σₓy approx 6e²/h, consistent with recent experimental observations. Our results highlight the central role of multiple pseudospin doublets in the interaction-driven phases of even-layer Bernal multilayers.

articles.title: Statistical mechanics of noisy collisions in active matter: Dyson-Landau theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active systems and other coarse-grained descriptions are often modeled by generalized dynamics, effective equations of motion that are not bound by the constraints of genuinely microscopic physics. In particular, these equations are generally stochastic on the smallest resolved scale. This poses a challenge to first-principles statistical physics, which usually derives emergent noise on larger scales from deterministic interactions. Here, we show how to systematically incorporate microscopic noise into kinetic theory in the limit of weak noise, i.e., high activity. By means of a Dyson expansion of the noisy free propagator, we derive the leading correction to the Landau kinetic equation for weakly interacting systems. We find that the common practice of combining a deterministic collision integral with the diffusive terms of the Fokker--Planck equation is the correct leading order. For dry aligning active matter, however, the corrections are non-analytic in the noise strength, as nearly parallel particles interact for arbitrarily long times. For noise that acts only during interactions, a minimal model of stochastic interactions, noise and collisions do not decouple: the leading corrections are odd in the coupling strength, partly logarithmically enhanced, and amount to an orientation-dependent effective noise strength. Agent-based simulations confirm the predicted dependence on the sign of the coupling. Even in this minimal model, the effect of noise on collisions can thus not be inferred from symmetry alone.

articles.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. This counterintuitive result demonstrates that the success of CAM stems not purely from physical reasons, but also from a partial cancellation of errors. In contrast, for optical absorption spectra calculated within a model Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, GCAM systematically outperforms CAM, showing better agreement with the reference spectra obtained with the diagonal RPA screening in both peak positions and relative intensities. Our findings reveal the important role of error cancellation in dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals.

articles.title: Interface-Engineered Piezoelectricity and Electromechanical Coupling in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfaces between dissimilar two-dimensional (2D) materials provide a route to engineer electromechanical responses that are not intrinsic to the individual constituent layers. Here, we use high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate 461 van der Waals heterostructures constructed from 57 2D monolayers and establish a materials-design framework linking work-function mismatch, interfacial charge redistribution, dipole formation, and strain-dependent electromechanical response. We find that heterostructure formation generates out-of-plane interfacial dipoles via charge redistribution between the constituent layers, while biaxial in-plane strain systematically modulates them. The resulting heterostructures exhibit two distinct regimes: metallic interfaces with strain-tunable interfacial dipoles and semiconducting heterostructures with well-defined piezoelectric responses. For the latter, Berry-phase (BP) calculations independently validate the charge-density-difference (CDD) approach, which is generally applicable to all representative systems, with piezoelectric coefficients calculated via two methods agreeing to within 10%. Among 24 selected heterostructures, effective biaxial interfacial electromechanical coefficients reach 83.35 pCm-1 . These results demonstrate that the interface can serve as the active element governing electromechanical coupling and provide a computationally guided strategy for designing strain-tunable out-of-plane electromechanical responses in 2D van der Waals heterostructures.

articles.title: Lincege.jl: LINked Cluster Expansions on a GEneral GEometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numerical linked-cluster expansion (NLCE) is a powerful tool for studying properties of quantum lattice models directly in the thermodynamic limit. Here, we introduce Lincege.jl, a versatile, efficient, and easy-to-use package for generating the clusters needed to perform the NLCE on a general finite or infinite lattice. Lincege.jl takes as input only the Bravais lattice vectors, the basis information, and the expansion unit and uses a depth-first search to efficiently generate clusters, their lattice constants, and the sub-cluster information. It outputs final coefficients of the series, expressed in terms of the extensive properties of the clusters, in different orders. The package also contains tools for visualizing the lattice and the generated clusters as well as a classical Ising model solver that can be used as a template for interfacing Lincege.jl with solvers of other lattice models. This package can be installed using the Julia package manager and utilized with example scripts from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/rightleftspin/Lincege.jl. The online documentation, including examples, can be found at https://rightleftspin.github.io/Lincege.jl/stable/.

articles.title: Protected Charge Readout Scheme Utilizing Nonlinear Resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charge detection of nanoscale quantum devices commonly relies on dissipative sensors, where signal absorption causes measurement backaction. Recently, nonlinear resonators showed a near-unity readout signal through an induced frequency shift. We show that this frequency shift protects the sensor, as it detunes the resonator from the measurement signal. The resonator excitation reduces while an enhanced readout signal is maintained. Our results, supported by numerical modeling, show that nonlinear resonators can combine strong readout contrast with reduced measurement-induced backaction.

articles.title: Quantum-geometry-tuned Mott transition and emergent heavy fermions in a topological flat band
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.31242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A flat band with a nonzero Chern number has no localized Wannier orbitals, which raises the question of whether Mott physics is still possible. We place a Hubbard interaction U on coherent orbitals, which are localized but overcomplete, and develop a single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for this model. Within the flat band alone, DMFT reproduces the experimentally observed cascade and inverse-compressibility sawtooth without invoking Dirac revival or remote-band electrons. At nonzero integer filling we find an insulator-to-metal transition tuned by s², the fraction of the Brillouin zone that carries the Berry curvature. For N_f=8 flavors the Mott transition at ν=-2 occurs at s²_capprox0.025, where the top of the lower Hubbard band reaches the Fermi level and the local moments are Kondo screened, forming a heavy Fermi liquid (HFL). The HFL extends to the hole-doped side, ν=-2-x, but above the small Kondo temperature T_K the state is an incoherent bad metal without a Fermi surface. At low temperature, an anti-Hund's coupling J_Asim0.1U replaces the HFL with a pseudogap metal that has a small Fermi surface and is dominated by spin-polaron excitations at small x. We propose this pseudogap metal as the parent state of superconductivity in TBG. The framework may also be applied to other topological bands, such as those of twisted WSe₂.

articles.title: State-selective dynamical freezing in driven Rydberg atom chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamical freezing, the near-complete suppression of dynamics at special drive frequencies, offers a route to mitigating Floquet heating in periodically driven quantum systems. In interacting systems, however, the energy cost of each transition depends on the many-body configuration, so that the freezing condition itself becomes state dependent. We study this dependence in periodically driven Rydberg atom chains under single- and bi-frequency driving. Using Floquet perturbation theory, we show that each spin flip is characterised by a single interference amplitude set by its local interaction shift, and that a state freezes only where the amplitudes of all its available flips vanish simultaneously. This picture accounts quantitatively for the shift and proliferation of freezing frequencies with interatomic spacing and for the response of entire families of initial states, which are sorted by a single local motif. Freezing is strong only within a window of spacings bounded by interaction tails on one side and nearest-neighbour excitation facilitation on the other, outside of which the advantage of bi-frequency driving is lost. In the regime of large detuning amplitude, where freezing points are numerous and the perturbative description is controlled, this window leaves almost no room for the PXP limit.

articles.title: Dynamics of the Nuclear Envelope and Mitotic Spindle in Closed Mitosis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: During closed mitosis, large-scale deformation of the nuclear envelope is driven by the mitotic spindle and chromosomes contained within it. Previous models of closed mitosis have established that the spatial distribution of spindle-generated forces influences nuclear morphology, but have imposed axisymmetry and focused on equilibrium shapes. We introduce a three-dimensional biophysical model of nuclear envelope remodeling and spindle elongation that incorporates thermal fluctuations to examine how spindle-generated forces, chromatin distribution, and nuclear envelope elasticity control nuclear shape in fission yeast. The model reproduces features of both successful and aberrant nuclear shape change, including centering of mispositioned spindles, the dumbbell nuclear shape transition, and the formation of nuclear protrusions. A phase diagram of nuclear shape shows that insufficient spindle force produces elongated but undivided nuclei, while sufficiently large spindle forces produce either symmetric division or envelope tethers, depending on the size of the chromatin-envelope contact region. Near the boundary between symmetric division and tethering, nuclei develop asymmetric single-tether configurations. A reduced-order representation of the coupled envelope-spindle system shows a symmetry-breaking transition between symmetric and asymmetric nuclear shapes. Below a critical chromatin-envelope contact size, symmetric configurations lose stability during spindle elongation and thermal fluctuations drive nuclear shape trajectories toward one of two stable asymmetric configurations. These findings identify a growth-driven mechanical mechanism for spindle centering and alignment during early mitosis and reveal how asymmetric nuclear morphologies can arise during anaphase even in the absence of structural differences between the two spindle poles.

articles.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.

articles.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins. Semiclassical methods can reach these sizes, but their classical treatment of the bath cannot capture the sensor-bath entanglement that generates coherence revivals, especially under the application of refocusing pulses. Here, we resolve this tension. We introduce cluster spin-LSC, a method that clusters the sensor together with a few strongly coupled bath spins, treating them quantum mechanically in an otherwise classical spin bath. We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences. Our method converges systematically to the exact dynamics with cluster size, providing an internal consistency check when no exact benchmarks exist. We demonstrate that cluster spin-LSC recovers numerically exact coherence and population dynamics for a nitrogen-vacancy center and a molecular qubit, reducing day-long multi-GPU simulations to only minutes on a CPU. We further extend our method to systems with large spin baths that lie beyond the reach of exact methods. Our approach thus offers a scalable and systematically improvable route to accurately simulate the decoherence dynamics of sensors in realistic spin environments.

articles.title: Polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-refractive-index dielectric metasurfaces supporting optical modes are ideal candidates for achieving strong coupling with transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) materials. However, optical illumination with a specific polarization is always required to estimate the maximal coupling strength in such coupled systems due to the polarization-dependent optical modes. Here, we propose a self-hybridized strong coupling between Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBICs) mode and A excitons in the same bulk WS2 metasurface. By changing the thickness of the bulk WS2 metasurfaces, a typical anticrossing behavior with Rabi splitting of 165.9 meV is observed. Such Rabi splitting is unchanged when changing the polarization of the incident light from linearly to circularly polarizations, demonstrating the polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling. This work provides a novel method for realizing robust polarization-independent polaritons in bulk TMDCs metasurface and offers new insights for expanding the applications of polaritonic devices with arbitrary polarizations.

articles.title: Nonempirical Determination of the Optimal TAO-DFT Fictitious Temperature for Molecular Systems in the Lowest Singlet State
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) [J.-D. Chai, J. Chem. Phys., 2012, bf 136, 154104] has been developed to investigate the ground-state properties of large electronic systems exhibiting varying multi-reference (MR) character. As a central parameter in TAO-DFT, the fictitious temperature θ is closely linked to the degree of static correlation in an electronic system. While the conventional system-independent θ-scheme is computationally efficient and broadly applicable, a fixed, preassigned θ can be overly large for single-reference (SR) systems yet too small for strongly MR systems. To overcome this limitation, we propose a nonempirical scheme based on spin-symmetry restoration to determine the optimal system-dependent fictitious temperature θ* for molecular systems in their lowest singlet states. Across benchmark tests encompassing both MR systems (the bond dissociation of H₂, N₂, Li₂, and LiH, as well as the torsional rotation of twisted ethylene) and pure SR systems (the dissociation of He₂ and Ne₂), our nonempirical approach demonstrates superior overall accuracy compared with the conventional fixed-θ scheme. Furthermore, relative to standard Kohn-Sham density functional theory (TAO-DFT with θ = 0), TAO-DFT employing θ* yields substantial improvements for MR systems while preserving comparable accuracy in SR systems.

articles.title: Selecting Stable Sampling Dynamics for Compositional Diffusion: A Feynman-Kac Weight Reduction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.29764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given K separately trained diffusion models, how should one sample from a βₖ-weighted product of their terminal laws without jointly retraining the experts? Existing Feynman--Kac constructions provide many weighted stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with the correct target marginal. The consequential question is how to select useful proposal dynamics among them. We study an explicit family of weighted diffusions that realizes the same product-of-intermediate-experts trajectory. A scalar parameter λ controls how strongly the proposal drift follows the composed expert score, while an additional Langevin component can be varied independently. Writing B=sumₖ₌₁Kβₖ>0, we identify the distinguished choice λ=1/B. At this value, the aggregate squared-score term in the instantaneous Feynman--Kac log-weight rate cancels exactly. For positive expert exponents, the remaining score-disagreement contribution is non-positive. We call this structural cancellation Feynman--Kac reduction. Under bounded-divergence assumptions, it yields an upper bound on the instantaneous unnormalized log-weight rate for all λ≤ 1/B. For linear diffusion protocols with compactly supported expert data, λ=1/B yields two-sided bounds at every nonterminal time, for exponents of either sign. A corresponding result holds for a single expert under the same divergence assumption. In these two-sided settings, the selected value is unique within the specified family in a universal worst-case sense. Experiments on Gaussian mixtures and molecular sampling compare the analytically predicted stability with actual sampling quality, including instances in which parameter choices different from λ=1/B perform better empirically.

articles.title: Reconstructing Pure-State OTOCs from Forward-Time Linear Response
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the connected out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) of any pure state can be reconstructed exactly from commutator linear responses alone. The protocol requires no time reversal, no ancilla, no double copy, and no weak measurement: a unitary string pulse, forward many-body evolution, and a single local readout suffice. An average over a complete basis of pulse generators yields the OTOC exactly. We further show that the measurement can be made sparse by restricting the pulses to a fixed operator weight, which turns the truncation into an analytically controlled spectral filter: the deterministic bias can be computed before the experiment and cleanly separated from the statistical sampling variance. For Gaussian states, the finite-weight response is exactly proportional to the full OTOC after a known combinatorial rescaling. For quantum chaotic systems, the typical residual is suppressed as a power law in the sector size. Exact-diagonalization benchmarks in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and a nonintegrable Ising chain confirm these predictions.

articles.title: Liouvillian Quasiparticle Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quasiparticles play a central role in understanding closed quantum many-body systems, as they reduce complex many-body problems to effective single-particle descriptions and connect directly to spectroscopic measurements. In open quantum systems, the interplay between coherent dynamics and dissipation gives rise to unique phenomena, such as the Liouvillian skin effect and strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. This raises a fundamental question: how can the quasiparticle picture be extended to open quantum systems to account for such phenomena and enable the experimental probing of quasiparticle spectra? Here we introduce coherent and incoherent Liouvillian quasiparticles, defined by responses to perturbations acting on one side and both sides of the density matrix, respectively. We propose spectroscopy protocols that couple the system to auxiliary levels, either coherently or via a dissipative pulse, to measure the corresponding complex quasiparticle energies. Numerical simulations of Liouvillians with skin effects validate these protocols, revealing nontrivial spectral winding associated with unidirectional transport in real space. Notably, coherent and incoherent quasiparticles can propagate in opposite directions within the same system. Furthermore, in models exhibiting weak and strong-to-weak U(1) spontaneous symmetry breaking, our results unveil gapless Nambu-Goldstone modes in the coherent and incoherent quasiparticle spectra, respectively; the other quasiparticle spectrum remains gapped in each case. Our work provides a unified framework for theoretically describing and experimentally probing coherent and incoherent quasiparticles in open quantum many-body systems.

articles.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.30811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.

articles.title: Direct electron cooling at millikelvin temperatures with quantum-well heat pump
articles.abstract: arXiv:2207.14237v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Unconventional solid-state cooling is proposed whereby the electron subband degeneracy of a semiconductor quantum well is cycled at cryogenic temperatures. By "expanding" electrons to higher subband degeneracy and "compressing" to lower degeneracy in an Otto cycle, a stack of ultra-wide 150 nm GaAs quantum wells filling a 1 cm3 volume could be operated as a heat pump to pump 26 uW at 100 mK. Operated as a refrigerator, it can piggy-back onto dilution refrigerators to cool from T_base to T_base/4. Possible cooling applications include quantum computers and infrared detectors.

articles.title: P-adic numbers and kernels
articles.abstract: arXiv:2411.15377v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss the relation between p-adic numbers and kernels in view of a recent large deviation theory for mean-field spin glasses. As an application we show several fundamental properties of numerical bases in kernel language. In particular, we show that the Derrida's Generalized Random Energy Model can be interpreted as a (random) numerical base. We also show an application to the Primon gas and the Riemann Zeta Function by constructing a kernel representation of the Primon gas based on a finite p-base, thereby establishing a concrete link between number theory and kernel theory.

articles.title: Interaction-enhanced quantum to classical transport crossover temperature in a Luttinger liquid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.05356v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Strange metals are highly entangled gapless states of matter that exhibit anomalous transport, such as linear in temperature resistivity, over more than a decade of temperature. Why a single power law should be so robust is an open question. We propose a scenario in which interactions enhance the domain of certain scattering regimes, effectively suppressing other ``would-be regimes." We test this proposal in a one-dimensional Luttinger liquid coupled to a one-dimensional acoustic phonon. We use the memory matrix formalism to calculate the dc electrical and thermal conductivities at low and high temperatures, relative to the Debye cutoff on phonon frequencies, in both the ``clean" (umklapp scattering) and ``dirty" (disorder scattering) limits. We find the crossover temperature separating the low and high temperature regimes to be interaction-dependent, with repulsive interactions substantially increasing it, generally by more than an order of magnitude. This provides a concrete illustration for how interactions can extend a single transport regime over a wider temperature range.

articles.title: Characterization and Monte Carlo Simulation of Wavelength-Shifting Absorption Length in Plastic Optical Fibers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an experimental characterization of the wavelength-shifting (WLS) absorption length of the EJ-160I fiber core material from Eljen Technology. Fiber-core samples of different thicknesses were employed, and the transmitted intensity of incident LED light was measured to extract the WLS absorption length at 405.7 nm. The resulting value, (0.823 +/- 0.038) mm, was used to normalize the WLS absorption length spectrum derived from the absorption spectrum of the core material. An independent measurement at 392.5 nm yielded a WLS absorption length of (1.404 +/- 0.074) mm, differing from the value predicted by the reconstructed WLS absorption length spectrum by 3.16%, corresponding to 0.43 sigma. The resulting spectrum was implemented as an optical input in a Geant4-based optical Monte Carlo simulation of the EJ-160I fiber to examine the role of the WLS absorption length in light output, light attenuation, and the emission spectrum.

articles.title: Where does a molecule begin? Threshold masses of three-particle Coulomb systems and a predictive theory of their Born-Oppenheimer offsets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation serves as the foundational framework for the contemporary concept of molecular structure, which is central to chemistry and the molecular sciences. Its principal assumption is the treatment of nuclei as infinitely heavy particles. In this work, we test the boundaries of the BO approximation by examining systems with variable nuclear masses to investigate the emergence of molecular structure. We examine the three-particle family X⁺,X⁺,e⁻ as a function of the mass ratio M = m_X/mₑ, using deterministic variational calculations and the exact BO approximation. We accurately compute the threshold masses of all 23 excited levels bound below M = 100 with certified upper bounds. The BO approximation places every one of them too late by a nearly constant amount, 1.2 to 1.6 (0.23 to 0.54 with the adiabatic correction). We explain this constancy with a parameter-free theory, and test it with predictions frozen before the exact calculations: 18 of 18 symmetric levels pass (typical miss 0.003). For unequal nuclear masses none of 7 levels falls within the band, but the theory still captures over 90% of the offset. Where does a molecule begin? The ground state changes character gradually, over a crossover 2.3 decades wide in M. The sharp landmarks are the threshold masses: the first rotational level binds at M = 4.208, in the ortho-type nuclear-spin species, and the first vibrational level at M = 9.526; BO places them at 5.54 and 11.08. Thus, the BO picture orders the spectrum correctly at finite mass and shifts it by an amount that can be computed.

articles.title: Inverse design of polarization-analyzing gratings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurface polarization analyzing gratings have attracted increasing interest for polarization management and sensing in optical systems. Traditional strategies for the design of these gratings are based on a formalism combining the Jones calculus with Fourier optics. While this approach has achieved notable success in numerous applications, its validity is restricted to the paraxial regime. Here we introduce a differentiable topology optimization framework for these gratings which is free of this constraint. We show that this framework can yield designs which outperform the traditional approach, especially at high angles. Additionally, we provide preliminary experimental validation to corroborate these results.

articles.title: Excited-state lifetime and decay mechanisms in erbium-doped ZBLAN using Variable Excited-State dual-Pump Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a new technique for measuring excited-state lifetimes of rare-earth ions. This technique is particularly powerful for states that are very short lived or have a low photon yield because their de-excitation pathways are dominated by non-radiative processes. The technique uses dual optical parametric oscillators, whose pulses are separated by a variable delay. It reconstructs the excited-state decay curve from a series of delayed fluorescence intensity spectra rather than directly recording the fluorescence decay as done in conventional time-resolved laser fluorescence spectroscopy. The power of the technique is demonstrated by measuring the lifetime of the short-lived ⁴I₉/₂ level in Er³⁺-doped ZBLAN, which is well-known for its low photon yield. The technique enables accurate measurement of its lifetime and suggests a new depopulating mechanism involving the ⁴I₉/₂ level in ZBLAN glass. Its accuracy is validated by measuring the lifetime of the ⁴F₉/₂ state achieving excellent agreement with conventional time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy measurements. The approach is well suited for measuring lifetimes ranging from the sub-microsecond to the millisecond range. It provides a versatile platform for investigating excited-state dynamics and energy-transfer processes in RE-doped materials.

articles.title: Diurnal Warm Layer and Marginal Instability in the Ocean Surface Boundary Layer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-eddy simulations with high near-surface grid resolution are used to investigate the diurnal modulation of the ocean surface boundary layer (OSBL) at various latitudes for Coriolis frequencies corresponding to 15-70^circN. The OSBL, which is driven here by a low wind, surface waves and a diurnally varying heat flux, exhibits a diurnal warm layer (DWL) during daytime and a convective mixing layer at night. The DWL exhibits enhanced shear leading to daytime turbulence that is found in this study to exist in a state of marginal instability (MI) over a wide range of latitudes and convective heat fluxes. The MI is characterized by an intricate balance between the momentum input by wind, stable stratification owing to solar radiation and turbulent mixing in the DWL, such that the gradient Richardson number is maintained around the critical value of 0.25 from morning to late afternoon. The enhanced shear and stratification sustained by MI leads to a substantial deviation from Monin-Obukhov Similarity Theory. Turbulent mixing induced by MI is shown to be similar to isolated local Kelvin-Helmholtz shear instability events and to share a similar range of flux coefficients and flux Richardson numbers. The impacts of increasing rotation and nightly convection on OSBL variability at the inertial and diurnal timescales are quantified through a turbulent kinetic energy analysis. The interaction between inertial oscillations and diurnal shear is an important feature of the DWL at mid and high latitudes.

articles.title: Nonpremixed Flames Near the Leading Edge of Parabolic Cylinders
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonpremixed flames in the forward stagnation region of porous cylinders are classically described by the first-order stagnation-point boundary layer, which neglects the effects of surface curvature and boundary-layer displacement. In the present work, the description is extended to second order for a porous parabolic cylinder using the method of matched asymptotic expansions. The flame is assumed to be a sheet detached from the porous wall with unity Lewis numbers, and the model accounts for thermal expansion and displacement of the entire reacting layer. The expansion is verified against laminar Navier-Stokes solutions of the same idealized problem, and in the resolved cases the two-term errors decrease approximately as the square of the expansion parameter. At Reynolds numbers typical of laboratory-scale burners, curvature and displacement move the flame away from the wall and reduce the scalar dissipation rate, wall shear, and wall heat flux, whereas the flame temperature changes little. These effects increase with injection, and displacement contributes more over a longer porous section. The second-order terms considerably reduce the errors of the first-order theory in the flame stand-off distance and the scalar dissipation rate.

articles.title: Classifying detectability and time of emergence across different Stratospheric Aerosol Injection strategies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) can be deployed using different injection strategies with the same global-mean cooling target and result in distinct regional climate responses. The ability to identify the deployed strategy from observed climate depends on how large the regional differences are relative to internal variability. In this study, we ask whether five feedback-controlled SAI strategies from the GAUSS ensemble (CESM2(WACCM6), SSP2-4.5), all targeting 1.0^circC above pre-industrial levels, can be distinguished from annual global and regional means of near-surface temperature, precipitation, and polar sea-ice fraction, and when this distinguishability emerges. We use multinomial logistic-regression classifiers with leave-one-member-out cross-validation and define the emergence year using a family-wise error rate threshold computed from a restricted-permutation null, combined with a calibrated persistence requirement. We find that the strategies become distinguishable in the mid-to-late 2040s, about 8-14 years after deployment, with a peak accuracy of 0.87 on a model using both global and regional features. Additionally, we find that no model trained on a single region-variable pair performs as well as the models using global and regional means, suggesting the discriminative signal is small and distributed across regions and variables. The equatorial and high-latitude injection strategies are the most distinguishable. The classifier is able to recognize the multi-latitude strategy more easily at lower temperature targets. Our results suggest that annual climate features can identify with confidence which coordinated injection strategy has been deployed roughly a decade or more after deployment.

articles.title: How Brine Pockets Evolve and Release in Ice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liquid inclusions migrate through solids by melting at one end and freezing at the other, but how a macroscopic phase boundary regulates their deformation and release remains poorly understood. Here, we track individual brine pockets in saline ice through bulk migration, elongation, and release at the ice-water interface, resolving the motion of both ends. In the bulk, temperature-dependent thermomigration gradually elongates the pockets. Near the ice-water interface, the front slows, whereas liquid connection is followed by accelerated rear freezing and rapid shortening. These opposing responses arise from distinct changes in thermal-solutal transport: proximity to the boundary suppresses the local thermal-gradient enhancement and slows front-end melting, while liquid connection enables salt exchange with the surrounding liquid and accelerates rear-end freezing. A quasi-steady diffusion-resistance model captures the dependence of the half-length release time on the pocket length at connection and identifies an effective external exchange length consistent with a salt-balance estimate. Our results identify thermal proximity and liquid connectivity as distinct controls on inclusion evolution and release, providing a framework for understanding liquid redistribution in multicomponent solids.

articles.title: Transient coupling of Marangoni spreading and interfacial waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How does an initially non-uniform distribution of surfactant generate waves on a de- formable interface, and how do those waves then govern the redistribution of the surfactant? We answer this question for the linear Cauchy-Poisson problem of an axisymmetric interface between two viscous fluids, released from rest with independently prescribed distributions of surfactant and of interface displacement, by Hankel and Laplace transforms. In Stokes flow the pressure and the viscous normal stress of the Marangoni flow cancel in the nor- mal traction on the interface, for any viscosity ratio, so that the surfactant relaxes without displacing the interface: the coupling between surfactant redistribution and interface de- formation is inertial. With inertia, the Marangoni flow initiates a capillary-gravity wave whose polarity, at leading order for thin boundary layers, is set by the sign of ρₗ μₗ - ρᵤ μᵤ , and the surfactant is then carried by the wave, so that its concentration performs weakly damped oscillations at the wave frequency after the Marangoni relaxation of a flat surface has ended. The amplitude of these oscillations is given in closed form at small viscosity; its maximum does not coincide with that of the familiar resonant damping, and the surfactant and the interface shape decouple exactly only when the two fluids have equal densities and viscosities. A localized displacement radiates a wave packet that the surfactant damps, and a localized surfactant redistribution initiates a wave on an initially flat interface. Direct numerical simulations with sharp geometric surfactant transport verify these predictions.

articles.title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Balancing Causation, Correlation, and User Intent
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.28794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turbulence states vary widely in modeling difficulty, requiring distinct paradigms; thus, no single AI or data-driven approach suits all flows. We propose an operational framework classifying data-driven turbulence modeling by balancing physical causation and statistical correlation via non-equilibrium flow memory and user intent. Using the Mori--Zwanzig projection formalism, we decompose unclosed turbulent stress into a local response (τᵢⱼ^L) and a spatio-temporally non-local memory integral (τᵢⱼNL).
