Applications to prototypical one- and two-dimensional tight-binding models, including disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model and its Floquet and non-Hermitian variants, graphene and Haldane models, demonstrate that Koopman-DMD provides a unified route for the data-driven analysis of wave propagation, localization, and topological phases in condensed matter, photonics, and related fields.

articles.title: The role of different nonlinearities and potential vorticity conservation in two-dimensional fluid ITG models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.01414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The nature of turbulent energy cascade of simple two-dimensional fluid models of ion temperature gradient driven turbulence is studied in detail. Notably, it is observed that a minimal two-field model of toroidal ITG behaves qualitatively differently with or without the diamagnetic nonlinearity. In its absence, the zonal flows always dominate and the system never reaches a high-transport state. In contrast, when this term is included, zonal flows dominate only near marginality, while away from it, an inverse cascade with high levels of transport is observed, requiring large-scale dissipation (hypoviscosity) to saturate and hyperviscosity to regularize small scale instability associated with this nonlinear term. However introducing such a term, together with the existence of the curvature term, breaks potential vorticity conservation, which is one of the key symmetries of drift-wave turbulence. This can be remedied by considering a more complete model that retains higher-order terms in the pressure equation. This form of the model, with four nonlinearities, conserves potential vorticity and behaves similarly to the original model, requiring hyperviscosity to saturate since the added nonlinearity generates small scale instability also for the pressure equation. To characterize the roles of potential vorticity conservation and higher-order terms in the pressure equation, the behavior of both the standard ITG system, and the potential vorticity conserving system, is studied by analyzing their spectra, turbulent cascades, and sensitivity to viscosity. Finally, the direction of turbulent cascade due to the different nonlinearities is investigated by examining their contributions to the spectral energy transfer and by considering the triadic instability assumption for each of these nonlinearities separately.

articles.title: BEAM3R: Beam's-eye-view architecture with Mamba-3 for implicit dose reconstruction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.04747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To enable accurate and rapid photon control point and proton beamlet dose calculation in the DoseRAD2026 challenge, we present BEAM3R, a dose estimation framework operating in beam's-eye-view (BEV). Our core innovation combines a Mamba-3 state-space depth-sequence core with physics-based transport conditioning to model long-range depth transport without expensive 3D convolutions. BEAM3R shares a 2D CNN encoder-decoder architecture for photon and proton dose tasks, processing per-plane BEV slices. Proton beamlets are conditioned on water equivalent thickness and remaining range, encoding the parameters determining Bragg peak position. Photon models use a bidirectional Mamba-3 core to capture dose contributions from materials downstream of the calculation point, while the proton model uses a forward core with learned energy-prefix tokens and a Bragg-peak refinement module. To reduce interpolation artifacts and support high spatial resolution, we introduce axial grid alignment of BEV lattices with CT slices and an implicit super-resolution representation arranged as channels, evaluated by a differentiable Triton-accelerated resampler that reconstructs packed cubic B-spline coefficients directly in CT space. For MRI-based tasks, synthetic CTs (sCT) are generated using a conditional GAN with a SwinUNETR generator and a PatchGAN discriminator. On the preliminary DoseRAD2026 test set, CT-to-photon and CT-to-proton models achieved 1%/1 mm local gamma pass rates of 96.8% and 96.0%, with stratified plan-level MAEs of 0.0041 and 0.0079. Substituting sCT reduced gamma pass rates to 89.7% for photon and 75.4% proton plan level doses, with stratified plan-level MAEs of 0.0093 and 0.0336. Standardised runtimes were 23.4 s and 18.4 s for CT-to-photon and CT-to-proton prediction, increasing to 39.7 s and 42.8 s for the corresponding MRI-based pipelines.

articles.title: FlowMLLab: An open-source framework for reproducible computational-fluid-dynamics and scientific-machine-learning experiments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.27975v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: FlowMLLab is an open-source Python framework for scientific machine learning in thermal-fluid and aerospace engineering, covering incompressible, compressible and rarefied flows. Its 22 weeks comprise 51 notebooks and 35 lectures. Solvers and molecular sampling underpin field prediction, uncertainty quantification and reduced-order modeling. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and deep operator networks (DeepONets), including POD-DeepONet, connect operating conditions to flow fields alongside Fourier neural operators. Physics-informed neural networks infer solutions and constitutive coefficients. Geometry-conditioned models, including the point-cloud DeepONet variant Geom-DeepONet, handle changing domains. Aerospace applications address airfoil shock/vortex identification, rarefied-gas modeling, nozzle flow prediction and supersonic body design. Complementary thermal-fluid examples cover unsteady wakes, hydrofoil vapor clouds and noisy particle observations. Attention mechanisms support sparse-sensor reconstruction, autoregressive prediction and transfer assessment, alongside character-level language modeling. Complete-case evaluation excludes tests from selection; execution notes identify retained research outputs. A worked extension embeds a learned monotone relation for a fixed manufactured Carreau fluid in channel momentum balance. At three unseen in-support pressure gradients, it outperforms profile-interpolation and fitted-Newtonian controls with different information or priors.

articles.title: Quasi-symmetric error field correction and applications to ITER
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.29849v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reliable correction of nonaxisymmetric error fields (EFs) is essential to the safety and performance of tokamak operation. Although resonant error field correction (EFC) is well established, supported by an improved understanding of 3D plasma response, the residual fields left after resonant EFC remain an open question: they are expected to be predominantly nonresonant, yet can still degrade both confinement and stability. Here we introduce a systematic EFC scheme that minimizes resonant and nonresonant EF effects simultaneously, based on neoclassical torque response computed from self-consistent perturbed equilibria. The scheme extends the method developed for designing quasi-symmetric magnetic perturbations to the case where actual error fields are present. Application to standard ITER target plasmas with a range of intrinsic EF scenarios demonstrates the advantages of this quasi-symmetric (QS) EFC scheme for controlling residual EFs. QS EFC consistently yields low-torque solutions while strongly suppressing resonant response, outperforming single-mode resonant overlap EFC in most cases and approaching the performance of multimodal resonant EFC. We also show that the QS EFC solution varies only tolerably between half- and full-Iₚ ITER scenarios, despite the greater sensitivity expected from its higher-order nature.

articles.title: Stein Kernelized Molecular Dynamics for Active Learning of Interatomic Potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.04100v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) enable efficient and accurate atomistic simulations but depend critically on the quality and diversity of the training data. We introduce Stein kernelized molecular dynamics (SKMD), an enhanced sampling method that uses interacting particle dynamics to acquire informative training configurations for the fine-tuning of MLIPs. SKMD corresponds to a stochastic variant of Stein variational gradient descent that is adapted for molecular dynamics by incorporating asynchronous particle updates and a kernel of global atomic descriptors, which provides a symmetry-aware measure of configurational similarity. Unlike other enhanced samplers used in molecular dynamics, SKMD maintains the Boltzmann distribution as a stationary distribution of its dynamics in the appropriate asymptotic limit. This property enforces a balance between the exploration of diverse configurations and attraction toward high-probability regions of the energy landscape. We further propose an approach to efficient online data acquisition using an adaptive stopping criterion that selects non-redundant training data over the course of simulation. We demonstrate SKMD for the active learning of a neural network model of the Müller--Brown potential, a MACE interatomic potential for alanine dipeptide, and a MACE foundation model with a DFT oracle for predicting the Pandey reconstruction of the Si(111) surface. Compared to active learning baselines, our method achieves higher model accuracy in fewer training iterations.

articles.title: Efficient targeting of arbitrary excited states with quantum inverse power iteration through filtering polynomials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.28255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we introduce a quantum inverse power iteration (QIPI) algorithm based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) to target arbitrary excited states. Given an energy shift ω, QIPI prepares the target excited state by iteratively applying an approximation of the shifted inverse Hamiltonian (H-ω I)⁻¹ to a trial state. Prior quantum inverse power approaches typically relied on Fourier decompositions of the inverse Hamiltonian, with numerical quadrature used to reconstruct the transformation, but such methods are highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices and have been observed to be numerically unstable, effectively restricting their use to ground-state preparation. To enable robust excited-state targeting, we investigate two alternative transformation techniques: a Chebyshev decomposition of the inverse (Cheb-inv) and an eigenstate filtering (EF) approach based on QSVT. We find that EF-based QIPI is substantially more robust than Cheb-inv and other decomposition-based approaches due to the symmetry of the applied filtering polynomial, avoiding divergence with respect to the choice of ω and efficiently suppressing off-target eigenstates even in closely spaced spectra. Numerical simulations for molecular Hamiltonians of H₂, LiH, and BeH₂ show improved convergence and enhanced access to higher excited states relative to other quantum power methods. Assuming standard oracle access to the Hamiltonian, we further provide logical resource estimates in fault-tolerant settings in terms of T gate counts, and conclude that QIPI can achieve high target state amplification with modest polynomial degrees, thereby making it a promising candidate for scalable excited-state preparation in fault-tolerant quantum chemistry applications.

articles.title: The muon Moonshot: Moon subsurface tomography with upward-going muons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.10403v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a novel muon Moonshot concept for lunar subsurface tomography based on upward-going muons originating from the lunar regolith. Unlike Earth, the Moon lacks an atmosphere, leaving dense regolith below and a near-vacuum environment above. Consequently, most downward-going hadrons are absorbed before decaying, while upward-going hadrons escaping the regolith can decay in flight, producing a significant flux of lunar muons. These muons can be detected by instruments on the lunar surface or in near-lunar orbit. We perform Monte Carlo simulations to investigate their energy spectra, angular distributions, and integrated fluxes under various theoretical and detector configurations. The results indicate that the lunar muon flux is sensitive to detector altitude under idealized geometry. This dependence demonstrates its potential as a novel, non-invasive probe of shallow subsurface voids. We also present case studies on the detection of underground cavities and water resources. For shallow overburden, large cavity signals remain detectable with estimated backgrounds and systematics. Weaker water signals remain challenging. Potential implementations in future lunar missions are also discussed.

articles.title: Proof-of-principle long-distance Sagnac twin-field quantum key distribution network
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.04447v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Twin-field (TF) quantum key distribution (QKD) offers a promising approach to long-distance QKD networks due to its superior performance over large channel losses. Due to specialized hardware requirements, nearly all long-distance TFQKD demonstrations have only two users exchanging keys, rather than a network with three or more users. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate a proof-of-principle three-user-pair Sagnac TFQKD network spanning 127-km using single-photon avalanche detectors without any active phase stabilization or postcompensation. We implement efficient procedures for maintaining polarization stability and circumventing Rayleigh backscattering noise to achieve a stable Sagnac interference visibility of 93±1 % over one hour. Using measured data for the signal basis and simulated data for the decoy basis, an asymptotic secure key rate of 1.398×10⁻⁵ bits per pulse is achieved over an asymmetric communication channel with 102-km fiber and 45-dB overall loss. To our knowledge, this is the first TFQKD network without active phase stabilization or postcompensation achieved over long fibers. Our results represent a highly practical and cost-effective approach to long-distance QKD networks.

articles.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13634v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at sqrts = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb⁻¹. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high p_T. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

articles.title: Compositional neural networks for multimodal X-ray and neutron scattering inversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.29362v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: X-ray and neutron scattering are indispensable for structural characterization across condensed-matter physics and materials science. Yet, because scattering experiments generally record intensities without phase information, distinct structures can yield similar scattering patterns, rendering the corresponding inverse problems non-unique. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining complementary measurements, but their integration into machine-learning frameworks remains challenging. Here we introduce a modular framework for probabilistic multi-measurement analysis based on prior-amortized flow matching. Single-observation posterior estimators are trained separately for individual observation types or physical probes and combined only at inference time through a compositional sampler. This late fusion approach allows pretrained single-observation models to be reused without dedicated joint retraining. As a case in point, we consider reflectometry, which provides depth-resolved, nanometer-scale information about thin films and interfaces. Our single-observation demonstrations span X-ray, time-of-flight neutron and polarized neutron reflectometry. In separate co-refinement studies, task-matched estimators enable homogeneous composition across multiple neutron contrasts and heterogeneous multimodal composition of X-ray and neutron measurements. Together, these results establish compositional flow matching as a modular approach to uncertainty-aware inversion and co-refinement, with potential applicability to other scattering problems in which multiple observations constrain a common physical structure while retaining measurement-specific parameters.

articles.title: Hybrid Quantum Selection of Learning Rates in Language-Model Training: Termination Criteria and an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-rate choices strongly affect language-model fine-tuning, but the best joint profile across layer groups is generally unknown. This paper studies quantum minimum finding for layer-group learning-rate selection within a hybrid classical-quantum training framework. It combines Durr-Hoyer minimum finding with BBHT search and compares fixed-budget and confidence-based stopping policies using a lookup oracle built from measured profile scores at fixed training checkpoints. The paper then introduces an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle that scores and marks joint schedules in superposition without a precomputed score table. Classical one-step loss measurements supply the main, pairwise and three-way interaction effects between layer groups. The circuit adds the effects for each schedule, compares the resulting score with the current baseline score, and marks improving schedules for amplitude amplification. Measured candidates are checked classically before acceptance. Uniform-rate training supplies the initial baseline; using schedules from classical adaptive methods as baselines for joint refinement is left for future work. In closed-loop fine-tuning of a 1.5-billion-parameter language model, each selected schedule drives the next 200 classical training steps. Benchmark accuracies lie within the range observed across five uniform-rate seeds. The results give a working example of how quantum superposition can support adaptive learning-rate selection during training; the remaining quantum limitations are discussed in the paper.

articles.title: When Does Discrete Ricci Curvature Help? An Edge-Level Analysis of Curvature-Enhanced GCNs for PPI Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Curvature-enhanced graph convolutional networks (CGCN) incorporate Ollivier-Ricci curvature (ORC), grounded in optimal transport theory, into message passing, motivated by the claim that curvature-weighted edges alleviate "over-squashing" at structural bottlenecks. But does CGCN's improvement actually come from mitigating over-squashing? We investigate this on four real-world protein-protein interaction (PPI) datasets, comparing CGCN against a standard GCN at the level of individual edges rather than aggregate metrics alone. While CGCN improves aggregate AUC, AUPR, and F1 across all four datasets, this gain is concentrated almost entirely on low-degree edges, while performance on low-curvature (bottleneck) edges systematically degrades in three of four datasets, the opposite of what the over-squashing motivation predicts. Examining the learned edge-weight function directly, together with clustering-validity metrics, edge-distance ratios, and a layer-depth ablation across four depths, we find evidence for an alternative account: curvature-weighting sharpens the separation between clusters, which improves intra-cluster predictions at the cost of inter-cluster (bottleneck) ones. We test this account against topologically defined communities rather than the classification labels used elsewhere. Additionally, we offer practical guidance on when to prefer CGCN over standard GCN, depending on whether intra- or inter-cluster predictions matter most.

articles.title: tmol: a GPU-accelerated implementation of the Rosetta energy function for machine learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-inspired forcefields complement generative machine learning models, showing better generalization beyond the training distribution. However, these forcefields are typically slow to evaluate, and their derivatives are difficult to integrate into ML frameworks. We introduce tmol, a GPU-native PyTorch library implementing the state-of-the-art RosettaGenFF forcefield. tmol supports efficient batched differentiable scoring and whole-structure refinement with up to 362-fold throughput increase (batched). Used as a reward in generative protein design, tmol increases hydrogen bonds and water bridges at designed interfaces.

articles.title: World-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Pollution-Aware Bird Movement Modeling Using a Multi-Instance DQN Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Birds are modeled as environmentally sensitive agents whose movement reflects real-world air quality conditions, where AQI serves as a measurable world feedback signal representing pollution-driven consequences. Instead of relying on human preference or synthetic rewards, the system uses environmental outcomes as the primary training signal, enabling policy learning grounded in ecological impact. We propose a multi-instance reinforcement learning simulation in which agents navigate a 2D grid representation of India integrated with a precomputed AQI matrix and geographic state boundaries. The framework combines bird call metadata from the Xeno-canto dataset, spatial discretization, and real environmental data to learn adaptive navigation strategies under pollution constraints. To ensure scalability and efficiency, repeated real-time API queries are replaced by a structured AQI mapping that enables fast lookup during training and execution. Multiple baselines, including Monte Carlo, Q-Learning, and Value Iteration, are evaluated for comparison. Deep Q-Network demonstrates stronger stability, adaptability, and cumulative performance across varying environmental conditions, establishing a scalable foundation for world-feedback driven ecological decision modeling.

articles.title: Physics-informed neural networks for spacecraft trajectory optimization with exact boundary conditions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use neural networks to optimize trajectories by modeling the position as a function of time and minimizing the thrust with respect to the network parameters. This corresponds to an unsupervised training procedure in which physical laws are incorporated directly into the optimization objective. In standard physics-informed neural networks, initial and terminal states are enforced through additional weighted loss terms, resulting in a multi-objective optimization problem that is highly sensitive to the choice of loss weights and can lead to poor convergence and reduced accuracy. To address this challenge, we construct a simple transformation, exploiting the mathematical structure of trajectory optimization problems, to enforce boundary conditions exactly a-priori. This transformation can be interpreted as a reparameterization of the solution space that embeds the boundary conditions directly into the function. This converts the original constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one over admissible trajectories. I.e. the transformation eliminates the boundary condition penalty terms and reduces the problem to a single-objective optimization. Crucially, trajectory optimization comes with a low-dimensional boundary, which allows particularly simple and stable constructions of distance functions compared to general domains in partial differential equations. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach meaningfully improves convergence behavior and solution accuracy.

articles.title: Higher-Order Interaction Reconstruction via Integral Physics-Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstructing higher-order interactions is a fundamental challenge in complex networked systems, with applications in ecological, social, and biological networks. This inverse problem is inherently difficult due to the combinatorial complexity of higher-order structures, the strong nonlinearity of the underlying dynamics, and the prevalence of noisy and sparse observations. In this article, we propose a novel integral physics-informed neural network (IntegralPINN) framework for higher-order interaction reconstruction. Instead of { penalizing derivative-based physics residuals,} we adopt an integral formulation over temporal intervals, which naturally suppresses high-frequency noise and mitigates derivative-induced instability. We further introduce a continuous parameterization of interaction tensors, enabling tractable identification of higher-order structures via gradient-based optimization. We provide theoretical analysis establishing a noise-robust error bound that is independent of derivative amplification when the integration window satisfies an excitation condition. Extensive experiments on ecological dynamics, social contagion, and neuronal synchronization systems demonstrate that IntegralPINN achieves accurate and robust reconstruction under noisy and sparse observations, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.

articles.title: An AI-Based OSSE Framework to Evaluate Learned Physical Consistency: A Multi-Model Study Using FourCastNet, Aurora, Prithvi WxC, and GraphCast
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Observing System Simulation Experiments (OSSEs) are a central methodology for evaluating future atmospheric observing systems. We present the first AI-based OSSE framework to test whether different AI weather models can reproduce comparable physical impact from new observations that traditional physics based models generate. We evaluate four distinct architectural AI models on the Charney conjecture that incomplete historical observations can infer the present state of the atmospheric. We considner- FourCastNet V2, GraphCast, Aurora and Prithvi WxC and integrate each autoregressively over a 60-day forecast horizon. After a 30-day spin-up, we insert ERA5 temperature fields to infer winds and related atmospheric fields. Similar OSSE experiments are conducted for wind insertion. We measure the performance of each model's response to observational information on a 30-day data assimilation cycle forecast with and without data insertion. Distinct architectural AI weather models respond differently to the same OSSE observations. Foundation models (i.e. Prithvi WxC and Aurora), produce the strongest impact. For example, while GraphCast is the weakest, all three of the four models capture the temperature-to-geopotential height response. The two foundational models retain a positive, non-trivial, tropical zonal wind at 500 hPa response to temperature insertion. Various data insertion experiments can vary significantly even within a given architecture. We identify an architecture-specific numerical instability in GraphCast's full 37-level configuration that produces a runaway feedback concentrated at the uppermost levels with ERA5 temperature insertion correctable by excluding levels at or below 100 hPa.

articles.title: VTT: Reading Vehicle Size and Powertrain Type from Motion Trajectory Across Unseen Car Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vehicle size and powertrain information can enrich trajectory data for traffic analysis and simulation. We present VTT, a dataset and benchmark for identifying these attributes from motion and controller area network (CAN) signals across unseen car models. The dataset contains 9,062 drives, about 3,950 h, from 1,431 vehicles and 174 car models. It provides three footprint-based size classes, powertrain labels, and evaluation on unseen car models and unseen drivers. Using 60-s windows, we compare four sequence architectures, statistical features and physical features proposed by large language models. Training with auxiliary physical targets, data augmentation and task-specific weighting raises drive-level macro-F1 to 92.6-93.0% for battery-electric versus combustion vehicles and from 62.9% to 67.1% for size classification. On public logs from 4,061 additional drivers, the full-input model identifies powertrain correctly for 86 of 88 car models; size accuracy is 63.2%, close to the internal vehicle-level result of 63.5%. Physical-feature analysis links powertrain recognition to deceleration behaviour and size recognition to steering response. Errors near size-class boundaries and limited gains from longer observations highlight the importance of label resolution and training-fleet coverage for cross-model generalisation.

articles.title: What Does Weight-Space Programming Add to Diffusion Editing? Program Construction versus Score-Guided Refinement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weight-space programming (WSP) lets a language model construct executable weight updates for another network. We study diffusion concept editing through an interface in which programs define training contexts, preservation constraints and update directions, while a shared numerical fitter selects their coefficients. We compare generated programs with published editors, a shared-panel hand-written baseline and budget-matched search over conventional edits on 24 TIMED test edits for Stable Diffusion 1.4. The preregistered rewrite pipeline shows no advantage over the strong baseline. In an exploratory comparison, one-shot Astra programs improve fresh-scene VLM joint success, which requires subject presence together with whole-image target matching, by +10.0 points over the shared-panel baseline, while CLIP relative match shows no detectable change. These programs organise adjustable directions around protected text-state subspaces. Probing and rewriting the Astra programs then raises CLIP by +6.2 points while joint success changes by -9.7. On a fixed 144-image sample, five additional evaluators give point estimates in the same directions under whole-image target matching; checks of subject-local change give less decisive differences. Together, these results identify useful behaviour in complete generated programs and show that score-guided revision need not preserve it: program construction and revision should be evaluated as distinct stages of a WSP pipeline.

articles.title: DLS: Dual-Logic Graph Neural Networks with Chaos-Fuzzy Residuals for Robust Link Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Link prediction is a fundamental task in graph mining, critical for applications ranging from biological interaction discovery to recommender systems. While Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) have achieved state-of-the-art results, they are fundamentally limited by the inadvertent suppression of high-frequency signals, as the recursive aggregation that stabilizes structural learning inherently leads to over-smoothing, rendering node representations indistinguishable in deep layers. This limitation is particularly severe in heterophilous graphs, where structural proximity does not imply feature similarity. In this paper, we propose DLS (Dual-Logic SAGE), a novel inductive framework designed to break the over-smoothing barrier via a "controlled instability" mechanism. Unlike conventional methods relying on static structural heuristics, DLS introduces a dynamic residual pipeline. First, a Chaotic Injection Module utilizes the Logistic Map to diversify the feature manifold, exploiting sensitivity to initial conditions to separate topologically similar but semantically distinct nodes. Second, to mitigate the aleatoric uncertainty introduced by chaotic dynamics, a Fuzzy-Logic Gating Mechanism applies soft-thresholding to filter noise and retain only high-confidence signals. Experimental results on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that DLS effectively balances feature discrimination with robustness, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in heterophilous settings while maintaining competitive efficiency on standard homophilous graphs.

articles.title: Where Should Physics Enter? Information, Identifiability and Calibration in Probabilistic Sea Surface Temperature Forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advection-diffusion priors are a common way to make neural sea surface temperature (SST) forecasts physics-informed. We test where such a prior must enter a heteroscedastic ConvLSTM to help, using daily NOAA OISST v2.1 for the Bay of Bengal (1982-2024) and a synthetic benchmark on the same grid with known currents of controlled strength. (i) On real data, a soft advection-diffusion residual with a learned velocity gives no reliable benefit (lead-15 CRPS -0.007 degrees C, 95% interval [-0.022, +0.008]); a plain temporal-smoothness penalty matches it, and equivalence within 3% is not established either. (ii) Learned velocities do not recover the currents, whether placed in the loss, in an explicit transport step, or in a transport step without neural correction: they correlate with the reference no better than a shuffled-date null, even on synthetic data where knowing the currents would improve day-15 forecasts by 16-23%. (iii) Supplied currents help on synthetic data, but mostly as information: giving them to the network as input channels, without transport, recovers 92% of the transport design's lead-5 gain, and a frozen-current numerical forecast does as well as either. (iv) With GLORYS12 reanalysis currents on real data, the transport design is 6% and 4% worse at leads 1 and 5; reanalysis advection explains essentially none of the daily OISST change (correlation 0.02), and frozen-current transport is worse than persistence. (v) The defect that matters is lead-dependent miscalibration shared by every model. One variance multiplier per lead, fitted on validation data, brings 90% coverage to 0.85-0.91 at all leads and lowers day-1 CRPS by 13-21%; fine-tuning on 15-day rollouts fixes long-lead coverage but costs short-lead skill. This version withdraws an earlier claim of an 81% CRPS reduction that came from an uncontrolled comparison.

articles.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce EJBench, a benchmark of engineering judgement: whether a model can predict how a design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier results, and decide on it. Unlike engineering benchmarks that test whether an agent can operate simulation or CAD software, EJBench is software-agnostic and asks what an engineer would conclude without running a simulation. Its tasks come from a conjugate heat transfer design campaign for battery cold plates, in three families: matching unlabelled test results to their operating points, choosing which stored runs to reveal before signing off a design, and ranking new duties by peak cell temperature. Every answer is taken from a converged simulation, not from an LLM judge. The best of ten frontier models, GPT-6 Astra, scores 0.71, and models state almost the same confidence on tasks they get wrong as on tasks they get right. We also post-train Qwen3.5-9B with LoRA and reinforcement learning, rewarded by the share of answer criteria the simulation results confirm; on the held-out test split its score rises from 0.071 to 0.106. We release the train, validation and test splits, the evaluation harness and the leaderboard.

articles.title: Better Calibrated, Better Planned: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-ASV Informative Path Planning for Oil Spill Monitoring
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21783v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monitoring oil spills with fleets of Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) requires mapping a heterogeneous pollutant field from sparse, noisy measurements under tight time and energy budgets. Informative Path Planning (IPP) addresses this problem by coupling a reconstruction model, which infers the field and its uncertainty, with a planner that decides where to sample next. Prior work has focused on planning strategies and has largely relied on Gaussian Processes (GPs), leaving the calibration of the model's uncertainty underexplored. We study how uncertainty calibration conditions multi-vehicle IPP with a fleet of ASVs that coordinates online through a shared uncertainty map. We introduce Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) as an uncertainty-calibrated information model. We benchmark EDL, Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensembles against a GP in closed loop with five planners on physics-based oil spill simulations. Across 60 maps, the choice of model dominates the outcome, explaining 80% of the variance of the final reconstruction error, against 1% for the planner among the deep models. EDL achieves the lowest error and the highest IoU under every planner, is the best calibrated model and runs at 3.9 ms per step. With 50 cells per vehicle it reconstructs the spill better than MC Dropout and Deep Ensembles with 150. Deep Ensembles become more confident as their error grows, whereas EDL is unaffected. Robustness of the information model to the data its own planner collects is therefore a requirement of uncertainty-aware IPP.

articles.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning from human demonstrations has enabled robots to acquire a wide range of manipulation skills, but learned policies typically execute far slower than ordinary humans. This speed gap is mainly due to lack of an interface for collecting demonstration data at high speed, and the difficulty in training policies that can robustly execute high-speed motions. In this paper, we present ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA), a system for learning fast and precise robotic manipulation. Our system uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories. We also present a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action smoothing and aligns the visual data distribution between data collection and deployment with masking. Given 50 demonstrations for each task, ALOHA Lightning autonomously completes bimanual tasks such as ball tossing and catching, folding shorts, battery insertion, and bussing tables for over 80% success rates while close to human speed. Project website: https://flash-aloha.github.io/

articles.title: Discovery of new antiviral agents through artificial intelligence: in vitro and in vivo results
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22230v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this research, we employed a deep reinforcement learning (RL)-based molecule design platform to generate a diverse set of compounds targeting the neuraminidase (NA) of influenza A and B viruses. A total of 60291 compounds were generated, of which 86.5% displayed superior physicochemical properties compared to oseltamivir. After narrowing down the selection through computational filters, nine compounds with non-sialic acid-like structures were selected for in vitro experiments. We identified two compounds, DS-22-inf-009 and DS-22-inf-021 that effectively inhibited the NAs of both influenza A and B viruses (IAV and IBV), including H275Y mutant strains at low micromolar concentrations. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed a similar pattern of interaction with amino acid residues as oseltamivir. In cell-based assays, DS-22-inf-009 and DS-22-inf-021 inhibited IAV and IBV in a dose-dependent manner with EC50 values ranging from 0.29 uM to 2.31 uM. Furthermore, animal experiments showed that both DS-22-inf-009 and DS-22-inf-021 exerted antiviral activity in mice, conferring 65% and 85% protection from IAV (H1N1 pdm09), and 65% and 100% protection from IBV (Yamagata lineage), respectively. Thus, these findings demonstrate the potential of RL to generate compounds with promising antiviral properties.

articles.title: From Temperature-Limited to Battery-Limited Legged Locomotion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On legged robots, sustained locomotion often ends in thermal shutdown rather than battery depletion: the heat of walking concentrates in a few joint motors, which overheat long before the battery is empty. We train thermally aware locomotion policies by reinforcement learning without ever observing temperature, and demonstrate this on a Unitree Go2 quadruped. We first identify a coupled 13-node lumped RC thermal network, fitted on two runs of a single robot and calibrated against the measured electrical power, that predicts all twelve motor temperatures with a mean RMSE below 1 ^circC across different robot instances, gaits, payloads, and speeds. Under a sustained gait, the temperatures the motors will settle at follow directly from the gait-averaged squared torques and joint speeds. Our core contribution is a reward that drives down the hottest predicted asymptotes: thermal time constants exceed the credit-assignment horizon of reinforcement learning by orders of magnitude, but predicted asymptotes respond to torque and joint speed within a single gait cycle, so the policy learns to lower and spread heat with no temperature input. On the robot, the policy turns sustained locomotion from temperature-limited to battery-limited: with a 5 kg payload at 1 m/s, a learned baseline reaches thermal shutdown after 19 minutes (1.1 km), whereas our policy runs the battery down after 174 minutes (10.0 km) with its hottest motor 14 ^circC below the shutdown threshold in a 26 ^circC room; on an unloaded factory circuit with stairs and ramps, the baseline overheats after 25 laps (6.2 km), while our policy completes 47 (11.2 km) on one battery with 22 ^circC of margin.

articles.title: A Quantum Support Vector Regression Framework for Missing Data Imputation in Ship Performance Data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Internet of Ships enables vessels to generate vast amounts of data, yet missing values remain a persistent issue. To the best of the authors' knowledge, existing imputation techniques in this domain rely exclusively on classical machine learning. This study investigates quantum support vector regression (QSVR) for imputing missing values in ship performance data. Classical support vector regression and QSVR models based on different quantum feature maps are compared for estimating marine fuel consumption under varying levels of data availability. The case study uses real-world data from a Panamax bulk carrier, covering 37 variables across six categories. Three experiments are conducted: exploratory analysis with three input features, scalability analysis with increasing dimensionality (3 to 18 features), and comparative evaluation under a selected representative configuration. Across all scenarios, both classical and quantum approaches captured the relationship between the inputs and the main-engine fuel-flow rate, maintaining strong imputation performance even under severe data scarcity. ZZFeatureMap₁ achieved the highest average R2 (0.991 in the performance comparison conducted with 60% of the dataset, 90% missing data, and 14 input features, for instance) and the lowest aggregate imputation errors, while the radial basis function kernel was the strongest classical baseline, delivering highly competitive results.

articles.title: Magflow: Differentiable Simulation of Industrial-Grade 6D Magnetic Levitation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic levitation with six-degrees-of-freedom enables frictionless transport and micrometer-scale positioning in principle, but low-level control is inherently challenging due to its complex and unstable dynamics. Industrial systems typically rely on deep hardware-software co-design, where mover and stator geometries are jointly designed to enable a compact, hand-crafted approximation of the electromagnetic force computation, thereby keeping control computationally tractable at kilohertz rates. However, this approach imposes overly conservative constraints on the operating workspace and the range of supported mover topologies. Instead of reducing the underlying physics to a hand-crafted approximation, we compute the physics directly. We introduce Magflow, a fully differentiable, GPU-parallel simulator for 6D magnetic levitation. It is used to train the first neural controller for an industrial-grade 6D magnetic levitation system that is learned purely from simulated physics. We show that the learned neural controller transfers zero-shot from simulation to real hardware while satisfying hard real-time constraints at 4 kHz. The learned controller achieves qualitatively new behaviors and even levitates a mover topology for which no hand-crafted solution exists. These results demonstrate that co-design is not a physical necessity for 6D magnetic levitation control. More broadly, control learning from simulated physics can find solutions beyond the reach of control engineering in demanding industrial domains. Source code and demonstration videos are publicly available at https://sites.google.com/view/magflow.

articles.title: Amortizing Tempered Sampling with Corrected Self-Training
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning a neural sampler can reduce the cost of repeated sampling from an un-normalized distribution, but obtaining good training data remains difficult. We develop a corrected self-training scheme across a sequence of tempered targets, making use of importance sampling and Markov chain Monte Carlo to correct the samples and replay buffers to store them. We introduce Sequential Score Sampler (SSS) as a particular case. In SSS, the proposal is a score-based diffusion trained by regression on energy gradients; and the samples are corrected by importance weights on the path space. After training, samples can be collected directly from the model, from its importance-corrected proposals, or from the final-temperature buffer. The method amortizes repeated sampling by encoding the global structure of the target in the model. SSS achieves competitive sampling accuracy across the benchmarks and, on several targets, uses shorter runtimes with fewer energy evaluations than competing samplers.

articles.title: Representation Learning with Quantum Signal Processing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.28828v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Representation learning begins when training changes the features that define similarity between data. A frozen-kernel model only reweights a fixed geometry. We establish quantum signal processing (QSP) as a solvable quantum model of the representation-learning regime. At arbitrary depth, we compute the exact mean and variance of its quantum neural tangent kernel, revealing an input-dependent angular geometry whose diagonal remains non-self-averaging even when the underlying unitary approaches Haar randomness. We also prove a sparse-data guarantee for the full nonlinear gradient flow without freezing or ensemble-averaging the kernel: the realized dynamics converges to an integrable scalar flow with a time-dependent kernel closure and explicit convergence times. A finite-depth speed limit holds for every data set and trajectory. At higher data density, numerical results show coupled evolution beyond both the scalar and frozen-kernel descriptions. These results give a controlled theory of learned quantum data geometry with provable training dynamics beyond the frozen limit.

articles.title: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We study this capability as reconfigurability, the ability to realize new behaviors by cost-efficiently restructuring existing components and relations under sparse governing information, where task specifications provide high-level goals and procedure specifications expose a limited set of reusable factors, leaving the concrete bindings and compositions required for execution underdetermined. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and materializes executable skill sequences by composing stored transitions to realize task-specific changes. RecPo maintains a procedure knowledge base of skill-induced transitions, with each view exposing a reusable factor and preserving local skill connectivity. At deployment, it interprets task specifications through the same views and resolves the resulting compositional queries over the stored relations to bind skills for execution. On long-horizon tasks in an extended Franka Kitchen benchmark, RecPo achieves 91.9% ordered completion with 1.0 ms of task inference per episode across varying procedure support and task-record sparsity. Real-robot studies further demonstrate adaptation through local memory edits without task-specific retraining.

articles.title: Learning Regions of Attraction for Transverse Feedback Linearization under Controller Singularities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transverse feedback linearization (TFL) achieves path following by exactly linearizing the error dynamics, but its controller is undefined on a singular set, such as zero speed for a unicycle or zero thrust for a quadrotor. The constrained region of attraction, the set of initial states from which the closed loop converges to the path without violating state or regularity constraints, determines where the controller can be safely activated. Exploiting the exact linear error dynamics, we show that this region is the largest forward invariant subset of the admissible set. We then decompose its state-constrained Zubov value function into an analytically known quadratic cost-to-go and a safety value function. We learn only the latter, by fitted value iteration without infinite-horizon trajectory labels. The resulting estimate combines an inner layer verified by interval branch and bound with a learned outer layer tested on samples. On a unicycle following a circle and a sinusoid and on a planar quadrotor, it covers on average 72.0%, 83.4% and 19.1% of the simulated region of attraction. In comparison, the quadratic cost-to-go and two physics-informed neural network (PINN) solvers of Zubov's equation cover at most 11.3%, 4.0% and 0.0% on average. Code and animations are available at https://gradslab.github.io/roa_tfl

articles.title: MCTS Is Counting the Wrong Thing: Learning Exploration Counts for LLM Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) has powered landmark successes in reinforcement learning, yet its gains in LLM reasoning can remain modest despite substantial search effort. We identify an overlooked bottleneck: what MCTS counts. Standard UCT assigns independent visit counts to textual branches, allowing different formulations of the same reasoning strategy to repeatedly receive exploration bonuses. Our theoretical analysis shows that this count fragmentation can impair exploration efficiency, as quantified by increased cumulative regret. To address this problem, we introduce Learned Pseudo-Count MCTS (LPC-MCTS), which changes only the exploration statistic in UCT. A lightweight Coin-Flipping Network head on the policy's hidden representations estimates representation coverage, enabling related branches to share exploration evidence. Across 5 mathematical-reasoning and 7 search benchmarks, LPC-MCTS consistently outperforms strong MCTS baselines. Holding each LPC-MCTS-trained policy fixed, replacing standard MCTS counts at inference improves average mean@16 accuracy across 5 mathematical benchmarks by 3.79 percentage points on Qwen2.5-7B and 2.71 points on Qwen3-4B. Applying LPC-MCTS during both training and inference yields gains of 4.96 and 4.37 points over standard MCTS, respectively. Together, our theory and experiments show that changing what MCTS counts can substantially improve its exploration efficiency and reasoning performance.

articles.title: EmbedGym: Letting Coding Agents Develop and Debug Embedded Firmware Without Physical Hardware
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern coding agents perform well on general software benchmarks because they can run code and unit tests in a closed loop. Embedded firmware development, however, breaks this loop: a program that compiles can still fail on real hardware due to pin polarity, bus protocol, timing, or networking bugs that an agent at a text terminal cannot observe. Existing embedded coding agents either skip hardware execution, drive GPIO-only simulators with multi-second delays, or test on physical boards in a static environment. In this paper, we present EmbedGym, an interactive virtual hardware environment that lets coding agents develop and debug embedded firmware without physical hardware. EmbedGym uses instruction-level microcontroller unit (MCU) emulators to execute the same binary that would be flashed onto a physical board, connects them to 41 peripheral models, an analog circuit simulator, and virtual WiFi/Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) endpoints, and exposes an interface for agents to change sensor inputs, press buttons, and inspect hardware states. On top of it, we build EmbedGym-Bench, which consists of 598 tasks across 6 MCU-framework pairs graded by hidden timed test vectors, using a five-stage multi-agent workflow that synthesizes peripheral models and tasks from datasheets and driver libraries. We expose EmbedGym to a coding agent at three levels and evaluate eight models over more than 14K trajectories. Even when compilation succeeds 99.7% of the time, 19.9% of compiled firmwares fail at runtime (up to 73% on individual targets). In contrast, interactive hardware testing in EmbedGym increases pass rates across models by +4.9% to +14.7% (up to +31% on individual targets). Our results also show that an agent with EmbedGym outperforms prior embedded agent frameworks, and lightweight models with EmbedGym match frontier models without it at 30-70x lower cost.

articles.title: Segmentation-Guided Direct Capacity Estimation of Rooftop Photovoltaics from Aerial Imagery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distribution planners need installation-level inventories of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) capacity, but interconnection records may be incomplete or spatially aggregated. Conventional image-based estimators segment PV arrays, convert the mask to physical area, and multiply by an estimated power density, coupling capacity prediction to mask-derived area. We propose Direct Head, a segmentation-guided architecture that retains U-Net segmentation and soft-mask pooling while directly regressing nonnegative capacity from PV-region features and area descriptors. We evaluate three independent runs on 7,590 French rooftop installations under the original split and a department-based holdout. Relative to a parameter-matched area-density neural model, Direct Head reduces mean absolute error by 8.7% and 12.5%, and symmetric mean absolute percentage error by 14.0% and 20.7%, respectively. Comparisons with conventional estimators, controlled architecture variants, auxiliary-loss ablations, and representative cases show that segmentation provides useful spatial evidence without requiring capacity to be determined by an area-density product.

articles.title: QAOA for Layered Architecture Recovery: Feasibility, Limits, and the Role of Decomposition
articles.abstract: Layered architecture recovery (LAR) reconstructs a system's architectural layers from its package dependencies, and is defined as a combinatorial optimisation problem solved with classical search. We investigate whether the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can be applied to LAR, and with what practical limitations. We formulate LAR as a Quadratic Semi-Assignment Problem, transform it into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimisation (QUBO) problem in which each package is penalised unless it is assigned to exactly one layer, and encode it as an Ising Hamiltonian solved by QAOA. To reach instances beyond the qubit budget of a single circuit, we also apply an impact-guided decomposition that solves the problem as a sequence of smaller sub-problems. We evaluate the approach on three real Java systems (15, 18, and 24 qubits), studying the effect of circuit depth and sampling budget (RQ1), a comparison with a classical Tabu Search baseline (RQ2), robustness to simulated quantum noise (RQ3), and the decomposition (RQ4). We find that monolithic QAOA is feasible and accurate on the two smaller systems but fails on the 24-qubitinstance. The sampling budget rather than circuit depth governs its accuracy and that it is competitive with but does not outperform Tabu Search. Decomposition restores reliable recovery on the 24-qubit instance, raising the optimal rate from 6.7% to 93.3%; its accuracy is governed by the size of each sub-problem and, unlike the monolithic pipeline, improves as the samplingbudget is reduced. Our results indicate that, in the current noisy intermediate-scale regime, problem decomposition, rather than larger circuits or more sampling, is the key to applying QAOA to software architecture recovery

articles.title: Non-Volatile Tunable Chiroptical Responses of GSST-Ge Hybrid Quasi-BIC Active Metasurfaces in the Mid-Infrared Regime
articles.abstract: Dynamic polarization state manipulation at the nanoscale is highly desirable for emerging photonic applications. Here, we theoretically demonstrate a reconfigurable chiral metasurface based on quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BIC) and the chalcogenide phase-change material Ge2Sb2Se4Te (GSST). By combining Ge and GSST elliptical dimers, the proposed structure achieves a quasi-BIC resonance with Q ≈ 8390 dominated by magnetic dipole resonances, ensuring strong near-field enhancement. Benefiting from the substantial and near-lossless refractive index contrast of GSST (Δn ≈ 1.5), the metasurface delivers a dramatic circular dichroism (CD) modulation ranging from − 0.3 to -1 across the 6∼8 µm mid-infrared band. Crucially, the phase change induces a large resonance wavelength shift of Δλ = 1.2 µm, which drives a continuous polarization evolution across the Poincaré sphere. By dynamically tuning the crystallization ratio (C from 0 to 1), we achieve continuous polarization conversion from elliptical toward near‑circular polarization states. This high-performance platform provides a promising paradigm for active infrared meta-optics, including tunable lenses, dynamic holography, and polarization-encoded computing.

articles.title: Development of a Lignin-Based Bio-Binder for Particleboards Applications from Organosolv Lignin Extracted from Mixed Cameroonian Wood Sawdust
articles.abstract: This study aimed at developing a lignin-based bio-binder from organosolv lignin extracted from mixed wood sawdust composed of three local wood species, namely Cordia, Iroko, and Passi, collected in Ngaoundéré, Cameroon, for application in particleboard manufacturing. The mixed sawdust was first sampled and characterized. Lignin was then extracted using the organosolv process, characterized, and modified by phenolation. The bio-binder formulation was optimized using response surface methodology based on a central composite design with three factors (lignin, furfural, and glycerol) and four responses (pH, viscosity, gel time, and insoluble fraction). The optimized bio-binder was subsequently used in the manufacturing process of particleboards produced from the mixed sawdust. The results showed that the mixed sawdust contained 45.6% lignin, with an extraction yield of 55.75% and a lignin purity of 91.1%. The optimized bio-binder exhibited a pH of 5.1, a viscosity of 342 mPa·s, a gel time of 3.35 min, and an insoluble fraction of 79.56%. The optimized particleboard exhibited a thickness swelling of 2.94%, an impact resistance of 100%, and a water absorption of 254%. Finally, the developed bio-binder contains 87.6% wood sawdust. When incorporated at 8.00% into particleboards containing 90.48% sawdust, it results in a final material with a wood sawdust content of 97.28%. These findings highlight the economic and industrial potentials of mixed wood sawdust as an abundant and readily available resource for the development of lignin-based bio-binders and more sustainable particleboards in Cameroon to promot local technology and economic development.

articles.title: Mechanistic and kinetic insights into secondary phenol formation from cresol and toluene: A combined quantum chemical and machine learning study
articles.abstract: Context In this study, the reaction mechanisms and kinetics of four pathways leading to phenol + CH3 formation were systematically investigated, including the reactions of o-, m-, and p-cresol with H atoms and the reaction of toluene with OH radicals. The results show that the addition of H atoms to the three cresol isomers requires activation energies of 7.6, 8.4, and 8.6 kcal/mol, respectively, leading to the formation of the corresponding intermediates IS1, IS2, and IS3. In the toluene + OH reaction, a pre-reactive complex is formed before the system proceeds via a submerged transition state to generate IS4. All four intermediates subsequently undergo CH3 elimination to yield the same bimolecular product, phenol + CH3. The transition-state energies predicted by the machine learning (ML) model are in good agreement with the corresponding quantum chemical results, with deviations of less than 1 kcal/mol. The calculated rate coefficients indicate that the o-cresol + H reaction is the fastest among the four pathways over the investigated temperature and pressure ranges. In addition, the rate coefficients obtained for the toluene + OH reaction agree well with the previous theoretical results of Wu et al., with a mean absolute relative deviation of 6.3%. These findings provide insights into the competing pathways for phenol formation and their temperature- and pressure-dependent kinetics, with implications for understanding aromatic oxidation and combustion chemistry.Methods The geometries of all reactants, intermediates, transition states, and products were optimized at the B3LYP/6-311 + + G(3df,2p) level of theory. Single-point energies were subsequently calculated using the CCSD(T) method with the same basis set. The ML model was employed to predict transition-state energies and evaluate their agreement with the quantum chemical calculations. Temperature- and pressure-dependent rate coefficients were calculated using RRKM/master equation (ME) theory, as implemented in the MESMER software package. All quantum chemical calculations were performed using Gaussian 16.

articles.title: The relevance of the Joule–Thomson effect to CO2–geothermal operations, with reference to production and injection wells
articles.abstract: The CO2-geothermal (CO2 Plume Geothermal) process has been the focus of research for over a decade. The efficacy of the system in terms of heat extraction has been demonstrated, while its potential benefit in terms of CO2 storage has been highlighted. Nevertheless, further elucidation is required in the context of field applications, including the flow behaviour of supercritical CO₂ within the wellbore, which is directly related to energy extraction. The objective of this study is to demonstrate the significance of the Joule-Thomson (JT) effect in CO2 well flow and to determine its potential impact on the engineering components of such systems, particularly on energy extraction.A theoretical evaluation of the CO₂ flow within a wellbore suggests that temperature fluctuations are also impacted by the JT effect, in addition to variations in kinetic and gravitational energies, and the heat transfer from adjacent formations. The numerical results demonstrate that, although the role of heat transfer from the surrounding formations via the well integrity component is relatively minor, the other thermal components — including the JT effect and gravitational energy conversion — have a significant impact on production conditions at the wellhead. While the extent of CO2 cooling is certainly due to the thermodynamic conditions in the borehole, the temperature may still be low enough to significantly reduce energy extraction performance at the surface. Numerical assessments indicate that energy extraction could be reduced by 80–90% due to enthalpy losses in the wellbore.The thermal effects are also relevant during injection and result in a warming effect. While the warming has been shown to reduce the cooling of the reservoir, it does not offset the negative impact of the JT effect on energy extraction during production. Consequently, the design and engineering of CO2-geothermal systems must incorporate reservoir-well coupled modelling to ensure a realistic assessment of energy extraction.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal CNN LSTM Based Multi Class Stability Assessment of Renewable Integrated Power Systems Using PMU Measurements
articles.abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources and the resulting variability in power-system operating conditions have created significant challenges for reliable real-time stability monitoring and corrective control. Conventional stability assessment methods often require extensive computation and may not satisfy the low-latency requirements of Wide Area Monitoring Systems (WAMS). To address these challenges, this paper proposes a spatiotemporal deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for multi-class stability assessment using synchronized Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data streams. The CNN layers learn spatial correlations among measurements from different buses, while the LSTM layers capture the temporal evolution of disturbance dynamics. The proposed framework simultaneously classifies four stability conditions: Stable, Transient Instability, Voltage Instability, and Frequency Instability. The methodology is evaluated on the IEEE 9-bus, IEEE 39-bus, and IEEE 118-bus benchmark systems under diverse disturbances, including three-phase faults, generator disconnections, line contingencies, and sudden load changes. A total of 5,150 operating and disturbance cases are considered. The proposed CNN-LSTM model achieves an overall classification accuracy of 97.4%, with an average model inference latency of 17.3 ms for each 500 ms PMU observation window, outperforming standalone SVM, ANN, CNN, and LSTM models. Because the classifier requires a complete observation window, a stability decision becomes available 519.2 ms after disturbance onset, and the corrective action is applied at 0.649 s for STATCOM, 0.769 s for SVC, and 1.019 s for battery dispatch, excluding communication delay. All closed-loop results reported in this paper use these actuation instants. For transient instability on the IEEE 39-bus system, STATCOM support limits the critical generator to a peak rotor angle of 75.0 degrees, against loss of synchronism at 1.33 s without control, and synchronism is retained for communication delays up to approximately 334 ms. For voltage instability on the IEEE 118-bus system, SVC support limits the weak-bus voltage to 0.894 p.u. and the excursion below the 0.90 p.u. ANSI limit to 0.18 s, against collapse to 0.621 p.u. without control. For frequency instability following a 650 MW generator trip, the decision delay places the battery dispatch after the rate-of-change-of-frequency peak, so the maximum ROCOF is unchanged at 1.48 Hz/s and the nadir improves only from 48.79 Hz to 48.89 Hz; the measurable benefit is a shorter recovery, 4.3 s against 7.5 s to return above 49.8 Hz. The results therefore establish a mechanism-dependent latency limit: measurement-window-based deep-learning control is effective for rotor-angle and voltage mechanisms, which evolve over the first one to two seconds, and cannot act on the inertial phase of a frequency event. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach for data-driven stability monitoring and coordinated corrective control in renewable-integrated power systems, with the latency constraint quantified for each mechanism.

articles.title: MatOS: An Agent Operating System for Materials Research
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34203v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Materials research relies on scattered and growing data, knowledge, and simulation tools, and a single study often spans multi-day workflows across literature analysis, computation, and experiment. Large language model agents can now retrieve materials data, operate simulation codes, and close design-synthesis-characterization loops with autonomous laboratories. However, extending these agents with new capabilities, keeping long-running tasks on track, and letting them learn from past tasks and user feedback remain difficult. Here we present MatOS, an agent operating system for materials research with three core components: (1) a layered scientific asset graph that organizes data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles, and workflows as reusable assets; (2) a stateful adaptive workflow that runs tasks as explicit execution graphs with scientific checks, so that they can be resumed and traced; and (3) evidence-driven asset evolution, which revises these assets from execution records and user feedback. On ResearchClawBench, MatOS improves on the previously best-performing agent by 11.15% with the same base model and extends the cost-score Pareto frontier. With a common base model, it outperforms Codex CLI and Claude Code, exceeding Codex CLI by 2.13% on MatTools and 4.17% on SciAgentGym. In eight research cases, MatOS narrowed more than 30 million candidate structures to 97 solid-electrolyte candidates, identified 89 halide variants with higher computed conductivity than their parent structures, linked the force errors of 11 pretrained interatomic potentials to local atomic environments, and supported two new methods that reduce errors by 3.1% and 13.6% relative to their baselines. These results show that organizing research capabilities as reusable, evolving assets enables agents to carry out long, multistage materials studies. Code is available at https://github.com/DingyangLyu/MatOS.

articles.title: An energy-based conservative–dissipative latent neural evolution operator for magnetization dynamics
articles.abstract: We introduce a reduced-order learning framework that couples a convolutional autoencoder to a structured latent neural ordinary differential equation. A learned scalar generates the latent dynamics through an antisymmetric operator and a positive-definite dissipative operator. The antisymmetric component permits motion along scalar level sets, while the dissipative component decreases the scalar. Adding a coercive quadratic term gives bounded continuous-time latent trajectories and approach to the scalar’s critical set under the stated assumptions. The scalar provides a structural constraint rather than an approximation of physical energy. The encoder, decoder, scalar, and operators are trained jointly on short snapshot windows without time-derivative supervision, physical-energy labels, or dissipation penalties. At inference, one initial state is encoded and evolved continuously in latent space, with decoding only at requested times. We demonstrate the framework on micromagnetic magnetization trajectories from NIST MAG Standard Problem 4 and compare it with dissipative-only dynamics and an unstructured latent neural differential equation. Repeated training runs show competitive observed-horizon accuracy, while selected longer rollouts illustrate improved retention of approximately stationary states relative to the unstructured baseline. These results motivate scalar-generated latent dynamics as an inductive bias for reduced-order prediction and other learning tasks where bounded evolution and equilibrium behavior are important.

articles.title: Richtmyer-Meshkov instability induced by a Gaussian-kicked rotor-like potential in a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This research investigates the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability within a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate. We offer a kicking potential that replicates the impulsive shock across both interfaces of the three-component BEC to trigger the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability. We propose a hydrodynamic model that indicates the essential criteria for the onset of hydrodynamic instability in the BEC through the application of the hydrodynamic pressure equation. We utilise the split-step Crank-Nicolson method to numerically solve the coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations, with the objective of obtaining the immiscible ground state of all components in a quasi-2D harmonic trap. Following this, we introduce a Gaussian-like disruption instigated by the kick rotor model at both interfaces of the confined three-component BEC to explore the time-dependent development of nonlinear hydrodynamic instability patterns, culminating in quantum turbulence and nonlinear configurations at the interfaces. The kinetic energy spectra of both the incompressible and compressible elements of the system exhibit scaling in the low-wavenumber domain with power-law exponents of -5/3 and 1, respectively. Conversely, the high-wavenumber domain is defined by k⁻⁴ and k⁻⁷/² scaling for the incompressible and compressible elements, respectively, aligning with the established spectral characteristics of quantum turbulence. This research offers fresh perspectives on the mechanisms of hydrodynamic instability, vortex generation, non-equilibrium pattern evolution, and quantum turbulence in superfluid systems comprising multiple interacting elements.

articles.title: Tailoring pore architecture and residual carbon ordering in vat-photopolymerized SiC ceramics via debinding temperature
articles.abstract: Vat photopolymerization (VPP) of SiC ceramics produces green bodies that contain about 45 vol% organic phase, so thermal debinding does not simply remove a fugitive binder but defines the pore architecture on which both the subsequent solid-state sintering and the pore-related functionality depend. This work examines how the debinding temperature (450–650°C) governs the open pore structure, the structural ordering of the residual carbon and the porosity–strength relationship of pressureless-sintered SiC ceramics. Mercury intrusion porosimetry shows that the open porosity rises from 27.25% at 450°C to a maximum of 35.92% at 600°C, with a single pore-size peak between 100 and 300 nm, while the total pore area falls from 9.07 to 2.67 m² g⁻¹, indicating that a tortuous, high-surface-area pore network is replaced by a coarser and better-connected one. EDS and Raman spectroscopy show that the residual carbon is progressively enriched and reaches its highest structural order at 600°C (ID/IG = 0.63). The ceramic debound at 600°C combines a sintered porosity of 13.99%, a density of 2.77 g cm⁻³ and a flexural strength of 290.2 ± 24.3 MPa, and the strength–porosity data follow the Ryshkewitch–Duckworth relation (σ0 = 394.9 MPa, b = 2.36, R² = 0.949). The debinding temperature therefore provides a single processing lever for the design of porous VPP-SiC components with a controlled open pore fraction and load-bearing capacity.

articles.title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomic sequencing delineates the spatial atlas of dental pulp aging
articles.abstract: Aging induces profound degenerative changes in dental pulp, yet its spatial molecular basis remains unclear. Here we performed Visium HD spatial transcriptomics on healthy pulp tissues from three young (18–34 years) and three aged (≥ 60 years) donors to map the high-resolution spatial transcriptomic landscape of pulp aging. We identified eight major cell populations and found that aged pulp exhibited a pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic shift, with broad suppression of vasculature development, biomineralization, and regenerative programs. The fibroblast subcluster (high SERPINA3/DEPP1) was markedly reduced, with parallel reductions in progenitor (high SERPINA3/SOCS3) and endothelial (high ACTG2/PLN) subclusters, all sharing enrichment of extracellular exosome and apoptotic pathways. Neural cells showed mild stress responses, while immune remodeling featured monocyte/macrophage reduction and plasma cell increase. Senescence-associated gene overlap identified 14 candidates, revealing downregulation of protective genes (e.g., SOD2, TNFAIP3) and upregulation of pro-inflammatory/pro-apoptotic genes (e.g., CXCL8, NGFR). Furthermore, spatial interaction analysis suggested that intercellular communication was markedly weakened in aged pulp, with reduced MPZ–MPZ interactions between neural cells and altered PTN–SDC3 and COL1A2–CD44 patterns. These findings provide the first spatial molecular framework of pulp aging, revealing that coordinated loss of pro-regenerative subclusters and emergence of a pro-inflammatory microenvironment critically compromise pulp vitality, and offering an exploratory basis for targeted therapies.

articles.title: SDH-LGCNet: Static–Dynamic Hybrid Spatio-Temporal Graph Learning With Factorized Spatial Priors for EEG Emotion Recognition
articles.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals can directly reflect neural activity and are an important source of information for affective computing. However, using only static or dynamic graphs makes it difficult to accommodate both stable sensor-space priors and input-adaptive dependencies. Electrode-level local modeling also lacks global integration and feedback guided by region and lateralization priors. We therefore propose SDH-LGCNet, a static-dynamic hybrid three-dimensional (3D) graph convolutional network with factorized prior-guided local-global collaborative learning.
