Within local temporal windows, the static-dynamic hybrid 3D graph convolution module (SDH-G3D) constructs a static spatio-temporal prior graph and an input-adaptive sparse dynamic graph. Through residual gating and multi-order propagation, SDH-G3D learns local spatio-temporal representations. The factorized prior-guided local-global collaborative learning module (LGCL) encodes five scalp-topographic regions and left, midline, and right lateralization positions as factorized prior tokens. Local-to-global aggregation, token context learning, and global-to-local feedback jointly integrate local details with global context. On the public Shanghai Jiao Tong University Emotion EEG Dataset (SEED) and Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals (DEAP), SDH-LGCNet achieves competitive recognition performance under both subject-dependent and subject-independent settings. Ablation experiments on SEED further validate the effectiveness of static-dynamic graph fusion, cross-time propagation, and joint modeling of region and lateralization priors. The approach provides a modeling framework for the collaborative learning of local spatio-temporal relations and global spatial information in EEG.

articles.title: Bioaccumulation of essential and toxic elements in natural populations of Caiman latirostris: sentinels of pollution in a hypereutrophic urban tropical estuary
articles.abstract: The broad-snouted caiman (Caiman latirostris) is widely distributed throughout Brazil and, despite being classified as Least Concern, faces increasing anthropogenic pressures. Crocodilians are promising sentinel species for ecotoxicological studies, yet research on free-ranging populations in anthropized tropical estuaries remains scarce. This study investigated caiman ecotoxicology in an Atlantic Forest and mangrove remnant within the eutrophic Capibaribe River estuary (Recife, northeastern Brazil), adopting a One Health approach. Two field surveys during the dry and rainy seasons of 2024 yielded 22 individuals (19 adults and three subadults; 14 males and eight females). Scales, muscle, liver, and kidney samples were analyzed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to quantify 13 essential and potentially toxic trace elements (Al, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, As, Se, Cd, Hg, and Pb). Fe, Zn, Al, and Cu had the highest concentrations overall, with the kidney being the primary bioaccumulation organ. Females had higher hepatic Zn and renal Mn concentrations, whereas males had higher muscular Cu, Cd, and Pb concentrations. Subadults had higher hepatic Mn, Zn, Se, and Cd; renal Co, Cu, As, Se, and Cd; and muscular Al, Se, and Hg concentrations. Adults had higher Mn and Zn concentrations in scales. Hepatic melanomacrophages occurred in all individuals, with moderate frequency in 54.5%. Trace-element exposure may threaten caiman health, conservation, estuarine biota, and human populations. These findings support the species’ potential as a sentinel for environmental monitoring and for informing biodiversity conservation and environmental management under a One Health framework.

articles.title: Peak Proton Flux of Solar Energetic Particle Events from Soft X-Ray Flares: The Garcia–Balch Relations Compared with Quantum Regression
articles.abstract: We extend the peak-flux relations of Balch (2008) and Garcia (2004a), last verified on solar cycle 23, to 111 events of cycles 23–25 (1997–2026), and compare them with variational quantum regression (VQR). With published coefficients the Balch relation keeps its original skill on these independent data, including the first GOES-R cycle (correlation 0.49, root-mean-square error 0.83 dex). The peak flux depends on the flare fluence in a curved way: the local exponent is 0.85 at 0.1 J m⁻², close to the published 0.82, and steepens for the largest flares. Emission measure and temperature add no information beyond the integrated emission. The scatter is organized by the time of the proton maximum. Events peaking within 12 hours lie near the nominal connection (median W58) and follow the fluence law, whereas those peaking after a day lie near central meridian (median W11) and are underestimated by 0.4–0.7 dex, as expected if their maximum is set near shock passage. VQR matches the best classical models. With only fluence and connection it reaches a mean absolute error of 0.567 dex, against 0.705 dex for climatology and 0.636 dex for the published law, a difference from the latter that is within the uncertainties. It captures the curvature of the law without an assumed form and with a small generalization gap. Compact classical models do equally well, a small neural network (0.550 dex) and a ridge regression on four Fourier features (0.542 dex), and entanglement brings no gain, so no benefit specific to quantum effects is found. Adding the proton flux observed 3–6 hours after onset lowers the error of events still rising from about 0.6 to 0.4 dex, so the accuracy at the flare end is limited by missing information on the shock at 1 AU rather than by the model.

articles.title: Safety-gated graph-attention compensation backstepping control for multi-UAV formation flight in obstacle-rich environments
articles.abstract: This paper develops a safety-gated graph-attention compensation backstepping architecture for multi-UAV formation flight among static and dynamic obstacles. Each follower is represented by a three-dimensional double-integrator model with bounded acceleration. A sliding-surface law tracks the desired formation; an obstacle-distance authority factor and a safety-conflict projection coordinate tracking and avoidance; a graph attention network (GAT) generates risk-aware additive compensation; and a safety gate redistributes authority among tracking, obstacle avoidance, inter-UAV anti-collision, altitude constraint, and compensation channels. Smooth saturation enforces the input bound. A Lyapunov analysis of the smooth nominal control law establishes uniform ultimate boundedness in the unsaturated operating region, while restart-enabled covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) tunes the ten coupled gains offline. In a dense dynamic scene, the tuned controller attains 90.0% obstacle-avoidance success, 66.7% joint success, a mean minimum obstacle clearance of 0.249±0.020,m, and a tracking RMSE of 0.879,m. Removing GAT compensation increases RMSE to 2.40,m, and CMA-ES tuning increases dense-scene joint success from 3.3% to 66.7%. Ablations identify obstacle avoidance and predictive avoidance as safety-critical modules, nominal tracking and GAT compensation as performance-critical modules, and the residual inter-UAV margin as the dominant remaining bottleneck.

articles.title: Recycled LiMn₂O₄ Cathode–Graphite Composite as an Electrochemical Sensor for Hydrogen Peroxide
articles.abstract: The direct reuse of spent lithium-ion battery cathodes as functional electrochemical materials offers a promising strategy for waste valorization. In this study, LiMn₂O₄ recovered from discarded mobile phone batteries was investigated for electrochemical hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) detection. The recovered material, characterized by a predominantly spinel structure, was incorporated into a simple graphite–mineral oil composite without noble-metal catalysts or advanced carbon nanomaterials. In 0.1 mol L⁻¹ NaOH, the electrode exhibited a pronounced cathodic response near −0.39 V vs. Ag/AgCl upon H₂O₂ addition, whereas the graphite control showed no comparable enhancement. A highly linear response was obtained over 0–1.370 mmol L⁻¹ (R = 0.99986), with a sensitivity of 980.65 µA mM⁻¹ cm⁻² and an estimated detection limit of 29.11 µmol L⁻¹. The enhanced response may involve peroxide reduction facilitated by manganese redox-active sites. These findings demonstrate the potential of recycled LiMn₂O₄ as an electroactive sensing material, providing a simple route for converting spent battery cathodes into value-added electrochemical devices.

articles.title: Inhomogeneous spin states as an indicator of the tomographic structure of paramagnetic multielectronic (molecular) structures
articles.abstract: The paper substantiates the existence of inhomogeneous electron spin states in heterospin systems – coordination compounds of paramagnetic ions, including molecules containing unpaired electrons as ligands. It is noted that compounds containing atoms with unfilled , and shells are characterized by strong interactions of uncompensated electrons with the electron subsystem of ligands. Due to the interconnection of magnetic and spin moments, it is also possible to assert the existence of inhomogeneous magnetic states within the molecules of these compounds due to the manifestation of interelectron correlations. As an example, the article discusses the nature of the exchange magnetic interaction in a tetranuclear cluster of nickel containing a nitroxide radical as a ligand. The structure of the Heisenberg spin-Hamiltonian of this cluster is discussed using the concept of a magnetic polaron or ferron. Methods of visualization (detection) of inhomogeneous electron spin states in heterospin systems using magnetic resonance methods (EPR and NMR) are discussed. The reality of the existence of such inhomogeneity opens up new opportunities for obtaining detailed information about individual parts of a paramagnetic molecule.

articles.title: Molecular Dynamics Investigation of Solid Methane Crystal Storage in Coal Matrix Confined Pores: A Potential Trigger Mechanism for Coal Outbursts
articles.abstract: Coalbed methane (CBM) outbursts pose critical safety risks, with incompletely clarified mechanisms for anomalous gas storage. This study proposes that interfacial growth-driven solid methane storage in coal matrices arises from lattice-matched crystallization at NaCl-CH₄ interfaces—enabled by the near-identical face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice constants of NaCl (5.640 Å) and CH₄ (5.665 Å)—which potentially trigger outbursts. To verify this, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations probed methane crystallization in FCC-NaCl nanopores under four pressures (S1–S4: 50, 97, 145, 176 MPa) during 400 K→30 K thermal quenching. Results reveal a hierarchical crystallization pathway: methane first forms dense wall monolayers, followed by bulk FCC lattice nucleation at ~140 K (confirmed by radial distribution function, RDF), driven by interfacial lattice compatibility that induces symmetry-aligned molecular ordering; pressure governed phase distribution, with lower pressures (e.g., S1) favoring surface adsorption and higher pressures (e.g., S4) promoting bulk crystallization (evidenced by plateaued mean-squared displacement, MSD, indicating long-range crystalline order). Between 140–92 K, structural entropy and diffusion coefficients dropped sharply as methane stabilized into ordered FCC configurations within NaCl-structured nanopores, and notably, metastable methane accumulation at ~140 K caused localized near-vacuum conditions that stabilized clathrate-like structures, enabling coal methane storage capacities far exceeding Langmuir adsorption model predictions by orders of magnitude.

articles.title: Computational Taxonomy for visualizing and exploring systems with functional response dynamics: soybean's O2-respiration example.
articles.abstract: A collective of 1684 O2-respiration curves of 183 dimensions are collected along soybeans' germinating process with 72 covariate feature-measurements. We develop a computational thematic platform for first discovering and exposing heterogeneous typical-shapes and then extracting readable, visible and explainable pattern information with biological implications when comparing between them. Via existing knowledge on seeds of much smaller sizes, such collective of O2-respiration curves are expected to generally embrace the two-stage or sigmoidal patterns. However, due to Soybean's relatively large surface area with harder to control and retain experimental conditions, much diverse and heterogeneous shapes are highly expected. Shannon entropy is applied to capture potential categorical nature across the 183 time-points, while scaled mutual information is used to evaluate pattern-consistency. Three motifs are determined to partition the temporal time-points into three regions: W1 on [1, 20], W2 on [21, 60] and W3 on [61, 183]. Each curve is partitioned into three segments accordingly. Hierarchical cluster algorithm is applied onto these motif-region-specific curve-segments, respectively. Five clusters of shapes on W1 are selected, four on W2 and four on W3. We computationally build a tree-geometry-based Taxonomic Hierarchy to organize these 80 curve-shapes into 15 typical shapes. Then we compare among these typical shapes to extract and display their differences through block-sustained heatmaps. Each focal block is expressed va a network of covariate features to reveal dominant interacting effects of various orders. Scientific explanations and understanding are to be rested on the collected heatmaps and coupled networks collectively.

articles.title: Evaluation of two different 3D electrodes in the electrogenerative removal of tin(II) from chloride solutions using a flow-through reactor
articles.abstract: This study investigates the electrogenerative removal of tin(II) from SnCl2/NaCl solutions using carbon felt (CF) and reticulated vitreous carbon (RVC) cathodes coupled to a sacrificial zinc anode in a flow-through reactor. Cyclic voltammetry on CF showed a cathodic wave and an anodic stripping peak attributable to Sn(II)/Sn(0) deposition and dissolution, superimposed on hydrogen evolution at negative potentials. The influence of the cathode material, initial Sn(II) concentration, dissolved oxygen and pH were examined. With 500 mg L − 1 of Sn(II), CF and RVC removed 99.6% and 98.6% of the dissolved Sn(II) concentration, respectively, after 4 h. CF performed slightly better than RVC at all sampling times, but the differences (1–4 percentage points) were within the experimental scatter. Nitrogen purging increased the 4 h removal from 82.3% to 99.6%, and removal was faster at pH 7 than at pH 4 or 5. The concentration decay followed apparent pseudo-first-order rather than zero-order kinetics (k1 = 1.35 h− 1 for CF and 1.07 h− 1 for RVC), but the strong dependence of the rate on dissolved oxygen and pH indicates that the process was not controlled by mass transport alone. Scanning electron microscopy showed a cracked deposit on the CF fibres. Because the cell current, the tin mass balance and the composition of the deposit were not determined, the results establish efficient removal of dissolved Sn(II) but not the faradaic efficiency or the purity of the recovered tin; these quantities are identified as priorities for further work.

articles.title: Broadband photodetection in an AgI-poly(1H-pyrrole)/TiO₂-MXene-I₂ heterostructure from 340 to 730 nm
articles.abstract: The development of simple heterostructured architectures capable of sustaining photoresponse across a broad spectral range remains an important challenge in optoelectronic photodetection. Here, an AgI–poly(1H-pyrrole) (P1HP)/TiO₂–MXene–I₂/P1HP multilayer device was developed to combine photon absorption, interfacial charge separation, and carrier transport within an ITO/FTO-free architecture. Structural and spectroscopic characterization confirmed the coexistence of AgI, Ag-containing species, TiO₂–MXene-derived components, iodine species, and P1HP within the integrated heterostructure. Incorporation of the TiO₂-MXene component increased the photocurrent density from approximately 0.45 to 1.25 mA cm⁻² relative to the AgI–P1HP–I₂/P1HP reference device. Under monochromatic illumination at 340, 440, 540, and 730 nm (3.6, 2.8, 2.3, and 1.7 eV), the device maintained photocurrent densities of approximately 1.20, 1.12, 1.08, and 1.00 mA cm⁻², respectively, demonstrating a sustained photoresponse across the investigated spectral range. The corresponding responsivity and specific detectivity values indicate effective conversion and extraction of photogenerated carriers across the coupled interfaces. The enhanced response is attributed to the complementary functions of the AgI-containing photoactive phase, TiO₂-MXene-derived charge-transport pathways, iodine-containing interfacial species, and P1HP. These results demonstrate the potential of the coupled heterostructure as an ITO/FTO-free platform for broadband optoelectronic photodetection.

articles.title: TiO₂–Hydroxyapatite Nanocomposite: A High-Performance Sensing Material for Volatile Organic Compound Detection
articles.abstract: In this study, the synthesis, characterisation and VOC sensing behavior of TiO₂–Hydroxyapatite (HaP) nanocomposites have been systematically explored. Using chemical co-precipitation technique, HaP was obtained in a simple and economical manner. To achieve enhanced crystallinity and stability, the sample was subjected to sintering at 800°C for 6 hours in a muffle furnace with a controlled heating rate of 5°C/min. Subsequently, the TiO₂ nanomaterial was integrated into the HaP matrix at incremental proportions (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 wt%) via the solid-state processing approach. Detailed evaluation of pure and composites samples covering structural, morphological, and chemical aspect were subjected to (XRD), X-ray diffraction, (FESEM), Field emission Scanning electron microscope, (EDX), Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and (XPS) X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The incorporation of TiO2 modified the phase and surface features of HaP composites. These composite samples were subjected to analyse for (VOCs) volatile organic compounds (ethanol, methanol, propanol, and acetone) sensing in ambient atmosphere. Notably, among all the composite samples, composite one wt% TiO2 loaded had strongest performance against acetone vapors due to better surface reactivity and charge transport behaviour of TiO2 and HaP. As the result 1.0 wt% TiO₂–HaP composite is a cost-effective, biocompatible material with strong potential for real-time acetone sensing.

articles.title: Radiation of sine-Gordon equation solitons in a model with an extended attractive impurity, damping and a periodic external force
articles.abstract: The radiation of sine-Gordon equation solitons in the presence of an impurity, damping, and an external force has been studied by numerical methods. The case of an extended impurity with a rectangular profile is considered; it acts as a potential well for a moving topological soliton (kink) and as a generator of localized oscillations. The finite difference method was used to solve the initial-boundary value problems. Localized waves of soliton type excited at the impurity, even in the absence of an external force and damping, are accompanied by a gradual decrease in their amplitude due to energy loss to wave radiation. Fourier spectral analysis of the emitted waves revealed the presence of two main frequencies at all observation points studied: the first corresponds to the lower boundary of the linear phonon spectrum, and the second is related to the natural oscillation frequency of the soliton. It is shown that the impurity parameters and the magnitude of the external force directly affect the characteristics of the solitons themselves and of the waves they emit, which makes it possible to control their amplitude and frequency. The dependences of the amplitude and frequencies of radiation on the system parameters, the distance from the soliton, and the frequency and amplitude of the periodic external force have been found. It is shown that for the sine-Gordon equation, the use of a variable external force of small amplitude leads to the radiation of stable quasi-monochromatic waves, while the choice of the external force frequency leads to a change in the type of soliton dynamics and in the frequency characteristics of the radiation.

articles.title: Obstacle immune super resolution CMOS integrated THz imaging system based on a freeform caustic lens
articles.abstract: While terahertz (THz) radiation's ability to penetrate dielectrics holds great promise for non-destructive testing, opaque materials such as metals and large obstacles fundamentally limit this capability, particularly at higher frequencies. Endowing THz waves with obstacle-bypassing capabilities remains a formidable challenge for practical applications. Although conventional bottle beams can route energy around a central obstacle, their low spatial resolution precludes high-fidelity imaging of fine details. To address this, we propose an achromatic super-resolution bottle beam. Using caustic theory, we derive a phase profile that can theoretically circumvent a metallic disk obstacle with a 12 mm diameter and map it onto gradient-index (GRIN) and freeform lens designs. Here we report the experimental generation of a broadband super-resolution THz bottle beam spanning 0.5–1 THz, enabled by integrating a 3D-printed freeform lens with a compact 65-nm CMOS oscillator–radiator array. The beam features a sub-diffraction full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.8λ and a robust 4-mm depth of focus. This integrated system achieves high-precision recognition of sub-millimeter features (down to 0.2mm) in complex targets, such as USAF 1951 charts and a biomimetic network structure resembling biological tissues. Crucially, the super-resolution imaging performance is flawlessly maintained even in the presence of the 12-mm metal disk. Furthermore, volumetric 3D imaging through highly scattering media is also validated. Our work establishes a robust paradigm, highlighting the transformative potential of super-resolution bottle beams in complex non-destructive imaging scenarios.

articles.title: Transient Burst Dynamics in Resource-Constrained EEG Decoding: A Systematic Review of Single-Channel Adaptive Deep Learning for Wearable BCIs
articles.abstract: Single-channel electroencephalography (EEG) is increasingly favored for wearable brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) due to reduced hardware complexity and power consumption. However, single-channel decoding faces limited spatial information, cross-session non-stationarity, and severe resource constraints on embedded platforms. Transient burst dynamics—brief oscillatory events such as gamma bursts and ERD/ERS—have emerged as neurophysiologically meaningful features that may compensate for the loss of spatial resolution. Yet, the literature on burst-centric adaptive deep learning for single-channel EEG remains fragmented, with no systematic synthesis of methods, adaptation strategies, and reported performance. This systematic review will follow PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching IEEE Xplore, PubMed, SpringerLink, and ScienceDirect for peer-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2026. The search strategy will combine terms related to single-channel EEG, transient oscillatory features, adaptive deep learning, and wearable deployment. Two reviewers will independently perform screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. Extracted data will include channel configuration, feature type, adaptation method, dataset, performance metrics, computational cost, and limitations. Findings will be synthesized narratively and, where homogeneity permits, quantitatively. This review will provide the first systematic synthesis of burst-centric single-channel adaptive decoding as a distinct technical route, clarifying validated features and adaptation strategies, identifying generalization gaps, mapping computational constraints, and deriving a research agenda for resource-efficient wearable BCIs.

articles.title: Non-Destructive Quality Assessment of Permanent Magnets inPedelec Drive Systems via Magnetic Field Mapping and SupportVector Machine Classification
articles.abstract: This paper presents a non-destructive methodology for quantifying irreversible permanent magnet degradation inpermanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) used in pedelec drive systems, using spatially resolved magnetic-field-mapping [MFM] combined with machine learning classification. Fourteen NdFeB magnets from a daum electronicImpulse2 e-bike drive system were characterized before and after 5,000 km of endurance testing on a biomechanicalHardware-in-the-Loop test bench at Aalen University. Spatially resolved magnetic field mapping was used to obtain fluxdensity distributions for comparison of fully magnetized and degraded magnet states of the permanent magnets. Theresulting difference field maps indicate small but measurable field deviations in the order of a few milliTesla (0.3 to 7.6 mT)across the magnet selection. While these deviations are modest relative to the nominal flux density of over 300 mT, theobserved spatial patterns, concentrated at peripheral magnet regions, show localized demagnetization effects.Twenty-five statistical, spatial, and texture features were extracted from each grayscale field map, including intensitydistribution moments, gradient magnitude statistics, Gray-Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture parameters, andpercentile distributions. A comparative classification study employing five machine learning algorithms (SVM with linearand RBF kernels, Decision Trees, k-Nearest Neighbors, and Bagged Tree Ensembles) was evaluated using Leave-One-Outcross-validation. The results demonstrate that the proposed methodology is capable of detecting and classifying these smallfield deviations, establishing a baseline framework for non-destructive permanent magnet quality assessment.

articles.title: Allocation in Manufacturing: Handling Operational Variability, Exceptional Events, and Process Changes
articles.abstract: Product-related CO2 values are increasingly required in manufacturing, but direct attribution of production emissions to individual products can create distorted Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) values under real operating conditions. Machine failures, scrap, material losses, fluctuating quantities, changing product mixes, or process changes such as new electricity mixes or photovoltaic systemscan strongly affect product-level results. This paper proposes an allocation-oriented approach for product-related CO2 calculationin manufacturing. It decomposes production-related PCF contributions into materials, consumables, energy use, maintenance, asset and infrastructure shares, and waste treatment and defines allocation strategies for products, batches, product types, accounting periods, and future periods. A forecastand-reconciliation mechanism compares expected and actual emissions and distributes deviations through correction factors. A gDEZ-based data foundation provides the energy-related accounting context, while an exemplary BaSyx-based deployment illustrates how allocation choices, calculation inputs, correction parameters, and traceability information can be represented in Asset Administration Shells for adaptable PCF calculation.

articles.title: Multi-Slotted Hexagonal-Core Resonant Architecture for an Ultra- Efficient Graphene THz MIMO Antenna with Exceptional Diversity for 6G Wireless Systems
articles.abstract: This paper presents a low-profile graphene-based hexagonal-core resonator 1×2 multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for future sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems operating in the terahertz (THz) band. The antenna consists of a graphene radiating patch on a flexible polyimide substrate with an annealed copper ground plane. The designed antenna is optimized by evolving its geometry while simultaneously optimizing the feed, substrate thickness, and ground thickness to improve impedance matching, gain, bandwidth, efficiency, isolation, and diversity performance. The patch resonates at 2.61, 3.50, 4.4531, and 6.25 THz, with impedance bandwidths of 0.6156, 0.7822, 0.815, and 1.5226 THz, respectively, and a reduced pattern of 1.827λ₀ × 0.783λ₀. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 13.1076 dB and a radiating efficiency of 99.038%. The designed antenna achieves port isolation greater than − 30.668 dB and − 67.4517 dB due to its orthogonal, anti-parallel feeding configuration. The envelope correlation coefficient is found to be insignificant (0.012) and diversity gain is 10 dB which shows satisfactory MIMO multiplicity functionality. The graphene patch radiator is conductive enough for electricity, and the extensible polyimide base and reduced surface area for THz operation allows for a loss-free deployment. We created and verified an analogous RLC circuit for the designed antenna using CST full-wave and ADS circuit simulators. The simulation resonances match the proposed equivalent RLC circuit model well. The designed antenna can be used for 6G communication, THz sensing, imaging, spectroscopy, the Internet of Things (IoT), emerging industrial applications, and innovative wireless technologies. The electromagnetic and circuit-level simulations provide insight into the resonance mechanism, impedance behavior, and frequency-selective response.

articles.title: Electrical Characterization and Modeling of Reverse Leakage in Cubic and Hexagonal GaN Schottky Diodes
articles.abstract: This work investigates reverse leakage current in Ni/Au Schottky diodes based on cubic GaN (c-GaN) and hexagonal GaN (h-GaN) using experimental characterization and technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations. Simulations were performed in Silvaco Victory Device using Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, Fermi–Dirac statistics, Schottky tunneling, and barrier-lowering effects to assess their ability to reproduce the measured reverse current–voltage (I–V) characteristics. The simulated results did not fully reproduce the experimental behavior, and variations in trap density and interface charge had a limited effect on the calculated leakage current within the investigated parameter ranges. The measured reverse current exhibited an approximately linear dependence on reverse voltage, which was not adequately described by the conventional transport models considered. An equivalent shunt resistance was therefore introduced to represent this non-ideal behavior, resulting in improved agreement between simulation and experiment. These findings highlight the limitations of the investigated transport models and the potential utility of an equivalent shunt resistance representation for modeling reverse leakage in c-GaN and h-GaN Schottky diodes.

articles.title: How electrons find their way to diamond's quantum defects
articles.abstract: A diamond's most useful quantum properties come from defects, places where the regular arrangement of carbon atoms is broken. One of these, a nitrogen atom situated next to a vacancy caused by a missing carbon atom, has become a key component in quantum technology.

articles.title: Using a microwave link to transfer a three-level quantum state
articles.abstract: Quantum technologies, devices and systems that process, store, transfer or collect information leveraging the laws of quantum mechanics, could outperform their classical counterparts on some real-world tasks. Many of these technologies encode quantum information in qubits, which can exist in either of two basic states or a superposition of them.

articles.title: Quantum-gas microscope resolves the 'color' of individual atoms in a single shot
articles.abstract: In 2024, researchers at the Ultracold Quantum Gases group at ICFO built a quantum-gas microscope capable of imaging individual atoms in strontium quantum gases for the first time, marking a key enabling step for quantum simulation. At that time, the researchers imaged strontium-84, a boson that has no spin.

articles.title: Quantum observers can 'agree to disagree,' but within limits, new theorem shows
articles.abstract: Two observers can start with the same description of a quantum system, follow the same probability rules and still disagree about the chance of the same outcome—even while being certain of each other's assessments.

articles.title: The Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic PBC clusters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct and solve the three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions. We describe a self-contained procedure which uses finite quotients of orientation- preserving triangle groups to generate regular maps on compact genus-g surfaces. From these, one can extract their lattice connectivity, plaquette structure, homology cycles and Wilson sectors while implementing consistent boundary conditions. On the example of 8, 3 and 12, 3 lattices, we enumerate a selection of quotients with up to 72 vertices, which constitute the discrete steps in a finite-size scaling analysis. For the isotropic point, corresponding to the spin-liquid phase in the thermodynamic limit, we identify the ground state superselection sectors, quantify their deviation from the homogeneous π flux sector and show how the selected flux background depends on the quotient geometry. We then discuss how the resulting ground state sector degeneracies are entirely generated by physical lattice symmetries acting on both the plaquette fluxes and non-contractible Wilson loops. Finally, we study the behaviour of the finite-size two-vison gap and matter fermion correlations. We find that the gap does not decrease monotonically with increasing system size, while one still recovers the expected algebraic decay of the correlations at the isotropic point, even for the considered modest system sizes.

articles.title: Probing Phase Fluctuations in Cuprates by Multidimensional Josephson Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The normal state of cuprate superconductors is believed to host precursor electron pairing above the superconducting transition temperature. These pre-formed pairs, which extend over an unknown temperature range, are expected to lack long-range phase coherence. Because spectroscopic evidence for this hypothesis is only indirect, new methods to probe these physics are needed. Nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy allows one to probe high-order time correlation functions and is therefore sensitive to fluctuations. Measurements of third-harmonic generation along the superconducting planes have revealed responses persisting above Tc, but a clear relation between these optical responses and specific properties of the fluctuating state has not yet been established. Here, we apply angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz spectroscopy to probe the optical nonlinearity of the Josephson tunneling resonance in La1.83Sr0.17CuO4 across the superconducting to normal state transition. We find that among all third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is especially sensitive to non-mean field fluctuations of the order parameter. We measure a crossover occurring at T ~ Tc between a mean-field optical nonlinearity that dominates at low temperatures and one that is mediated by short-range superconducting fluctuations. We present a theoretical framework that connects the out-of-plane optical response in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state, and contrast the sensitivity of different types of terahertz nonlinearities to fluctuating order.

articles.title: Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by ρ, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after ρ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to ρ -1 (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.

articles.title: Optical characterization of Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe₂ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Amorphous silicon nitride is the leading low-loss, CMOS-compatible platform for wafer-scale integrated photonics. Encapsulating transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers within this platform offers a promising route towards scalable TMD-photonic circuits. Yet the effect of this amorphous dielectric on the optical response of the monolayer remains poorly understood. Here, we compare monolayer MoSe₂ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride with a hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated reference, using differential reflectivity and photoluminescence. Whereas the reference is dominated by the neutral exciton, the nitride-encapsulated monolayer shows attractive and repulsive polaron resonances separated by sim31~meV, with emission dominated by the attractive branch. A quantitative comparison of temperature-dependent reflectance with a microscopic finite-temperature Fermi-polaron theory shows that the nitride induces substantial electron doping in the monolayer, with an electron density of (0.8--0.9)×10¹²~cm⁻². Using the extracted density and trion binding energy as the only input parameters, the theory reproduces the photoluminescence spectra up to sim80 K in excellent quantitative agreement with experiments, thus corroborating the Fermi-polaron description of the observed excitonic response.

articles.title: Frame Based Inelasticity for Strength and Fracture in Anisotropic Media
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A field theory is presented for predicting damage and fracture in brittle materials. Four concepts are used: a new nonlocal deformation gradient for dynamic stress analysis in anisotropic media, a new type of phase field coming from a constitutive law, the evolution of material displacement from Newton's second law, and a new incorporation of scaled strength surfaces into constitutive laws for predicting dynamic and quasi-static fracture patterns. The elastic softening is governed by the strain dynamics through the constitutive law and in this way we provide the two way coupling between strain and fracture. Simulations validating the approach for both dynamic and quasi-static fracture analysis are compared to experimental results and other simulation methods. The model is capable of predicting material strength in titania and the competition between strength and energy in soda lime glass and titana and captures dynamic crack branching in soda lime glass and concrete.

articles.title: Exact Dynamic Scaling of Quantum Jump Statistics in Monitored Many-Body Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum measurement has opened a new frontier in nonequilibrium many-body physics, revealing striking phenomena such as measurement-induced entanglement transitions, whose experimental observation typically requires costly postselection. Quantum jump statistics offer another route to studying such measurement-induced many-body phenomena without postselection, motivating the search for universality in measurement outcomes themselves. In this Letter, we discover that fluctuation of the number of quantum jumps within a subsystem exhibits novel dynamic scaling, characterized by diffusive time scale and anomalous super-Poissonian system-size scaling that depend on the subsystem size in monitored many-body systems. For free fermions under continuous monitoring, we exactly determine the scaling exponent and the scaling function by deriving an exact finite-size solution of the Liouvillian autocorrelation function. We also analytically show that the dynamic scaling with the same scaling exponent and the scaling function even holds for interacting fermions in the limit of large measurement strength. Our work provides a novel framework to classify measurement-induced nonequilibrium many-body universality through experimentally friendly, postselection-free quantities.

articles.title: Apparent contact angle equation for a dielectric droplet on a conductive hydrophilic surface in an electric field
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A dielectric droplet resting on a conductive substrate elongates when a voltage is applied across the surrounding gap without touching the upper electrode. We construct a closed form theory of the equilibrium shapes by approximating the interface as a truncated spheroid with a single shape parameter and obtain the dimensionless electrostatic prefactor that corrects the free-space depolarization, based on the mirror symmetry across the substrate. Minimizing the resulting free energy along voltage ramps reproduces the boundary-element-method (BEM) equilibria, both the droplet height and the contact-line radius, with and without gravity, at negligible computational cost. An explicit apparent contact angle equation is found that collapses all the numerical calculation data. The configuration shows a behavior of fixed contact angle and an increasing apparent angle with the applied voltage, which is completely different from that of the Young--Lippmann equation.

articles.title: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states in boron-doped/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boron-doped diamond (BDD) enables the integration of electrical functionality with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, but the influence of junction electrostatics on NV charge-state stability remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the equilibrium electrostatics of BDD/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions using self-consistent Poisson-Fermi calculations. The results reveal two distinct electrostatic length scales in the nitrogen-doped substrate: a near-interface region of ionized donors that produces dominant band bending and determines the NV⁰/⁻ charge-state boundary, and a much longer screening tail associated with weak donor ionization in the neutral bulk. The resulting NV⁻ depletion depth depends strongly on the nitrogen concentration but exhibits a more moderate dependence on boron doping. At N_B = 10²¹ cm⁻³, varying the interface grading scale w from 0.5 to 8 nm changes the depletion depth by approximately 22 nm, whereas variations in the modeled bulk BDD charge response produce a shift of only 1.27 nm. These results indicate that, under the conditions studied, the nitrogen donor concentration and local interface structure primarily govern the equilibrium NV charge-state profile, rather than the bulk electronic response of BDD alone.

articles.title: Swift Heavy Ion Tracks in Polymorphs of Titanium Dioxide: The Effects of Electron Beam and Crystal Structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Swift heavy ion (SHI) irradiation generates nanoscale damage in materials, offering opportunities for controlled modification of structural properties. Understanding the fundamental processes governing damage formation in altered regions remains a longstanding challenge. This work explores how crystal structure influences swift heavy ion-induced damage formation and evolution in rutile and anatase TiO2. Combining transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate how differences in atomic arrangement govern track morphology and structural recovery. Although irradiation produces amorphous tracks in both polymorphs, their morphologies differ considerably. In rutile, tracks develop pronounced diameter variations, forming hourglass-like structures, whereas in anatase they retain a relatively uniform cylindrical shape. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that these differences arise from the distinct recrystallization behavior of the two crystal structures during rapid cooling, leading to different pathways of track evolution and recovery. Particular attention is paid to electron beam induced effects during TEM characterization, which can substantially modify the structure and apparent morphology of ion tracks. Prolonged electron beam exposure promotes the recrystallization of initially amorphous tracks and surface hillocks, accompanied by the development of Fresnel contrast. These findings highlight the importance of understanding beam-induced transformations for the reliable interpretation of TEM observations of radiation-damaged materials.

articles.title: Reconfigurable 2D Lateral Heterostructure Platform for Unified Detection, Emission, and Logic
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heterogeneous integration of sensing, light generation, communication, and computation typically requires specialized devices, resulting in complex interconnects, fabrication overhead, parasitic losses, and energy penalties. Developing a monolithic, reconfigurable device capable of controlling carrier generation, transport, and recombination remains a longstanding challenge. Two-dimensional (2D) lateral heterostructures offer a promising approach by combining spatially distinct domains of different charge polarity with a dynamically tunable electrostatic landscape. Here, multifunctional bilayer MoSe2-WSe2 lateral heterojunctions are demonstrated, integrating photodetection, reconfigurable electroluminescence (EL), and CMOS logic operation within a unified platform. The photodetector exhibits a responsivity of 35 A W-1, a specific detectivity of 5 x 10¹³ Jones, and a noise-equivalent power of 6.3 x 10⁻¹⁸ W Hz⁻¹/2, enabled by efficient charge separation and photoconductive gain. Under electrical injection, electrostatic gating dynamically switches the radiative recombination zone among the MoSe2 domain, lateral heterointerface, and WSe2 domain, enabling spatially programmable EL, optical multiplexing, and ternary optical logic. Furthermore, the complementary transport characteristics of the two domains enable CMOS inverter operation at 0.25 kHz. These functionalities originate from a common electrostatic framework in which the gate-tunable depletion region governs carrier extraction, recombination, and transport. This work establishes 2D lateral heterostructures as multifunctional building blocks for monolithically integrated electronic and optoelectronic systems combining light sensing, generation, and information processing.

articles.title: Mapping phase competition in GaAs under pressure and temperature
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pressure-induced transformations in GaAs offer a means to investigate the interplay between crystal structure, electronic behaviour, and phase stability in a technologically important III-V semiconductor. Here, we have used structure search algorithm combined with first-principles calculations and identified high-pressure competitive phases. The previously proposed Imm2 structure lies above the calculated minimum-enthalpy envelope. The static enthalpy calculations with the PBEsol functional predict the transition sequence Fbar43m → Cmcm → Ibar4m2 → C2/m → Amm2, at approximately 12, 14, 34, and 69 GPa, respectively. The initial zinc blende to Cmcm transition is accompanied by a volume reduction of approximately 17.5 % and metallization within the PBEsol description. Phonon calculations support the dynamical stability of all five phases at representative pressures, while elastic calculations characterize their mechanical response. Vibrational free energies are incorporated within the quasiharmonic approximation to examine phase competition over 0-80 GPa and 0-1000 K. These results identify competing high-pressure structures and connect their relative energetics with the electronic, vibrational, and elastic responses of compressed GaAs.

articles.title: Thermal radiation of nanowires and near-field interaction with substrates: exact computation and proximity approximation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radiative heat transfer involving complex nano-objects is difficult to evaluate due to their sub-wavelength size, which induces deviation to macroscopic Planck's opaque surface-to-surface formalism, and due to the small distances involved, which lead to near-field radiative (photon tunneling) effects. As a result, thermal radiation has mostly been neglected in analyses of thermal transport in nanowires. Here, we report on calculations of thermal emission by single nanowires and on the radiative interaction between suspended silicon nanowires and flat substrates. We observe that metallic nanowires can be particularly emissive in comparison to wires made of other materials. While thermal emission from an isolated silicon nanowire is lower than Stefan-Boltzmann's prediction, the radiative exchange with a substrate can be larger by one order of magnitude. The considered configurations also allow benchmarking various levels of common or original approximations, including, in near field, the proximity approximation, the thickness-dependent PA, the electrostatic approach, and the effective emissivity in the far field.

articles.title: Burgers vectors from Voronoi topology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated dislocation analysis is standard in atomistic simulations, yet current tools are limited to a handful of crystal structures. We introduce an algorithm without adjustable parameters, based on Voronoi topology, that identifies dislocations in a broad class of crystals. Each face shared by two cells that match the ideal crystal is taken as a step in it, and summing these steps around closed circuits of such cells yields exact Burgers vectors, without geometric templates. Tested on dislocations inserted into all 9,610 Materials Project structures whose Voronoi cells are stable with a wide margin, the algorithm finds every dislocation with its correct Burgers vector. In raw molecular-dynamics snapshots, including eleven dislocation types in θ-Al₂Cu and bcc iron up to its melting point, every Burgers vector it returns is correct, although near melting the dislocations merge into one cluster. Voronoi topology thus provides a natural language in which a crystal, its defects, and their Burgers vectors are all described.

articles.title: From the Full Fermionic Hilbert Space to the BCS Paired Subspace
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer (BCS) and number-projected BCS variational treatments are formulated within a paired Hilbert subspace, where modes with opposite momenta and spins are either both empty or both occupied. Here we ask whether this paired subspace can itself be selected energetically from the full fermionic Hilbert space of the attractive reduced BCS model. Using conserved projectors that distinguish singly occupied states from empty and doubly occupied ones, we decompose the full Hilbert space into invariant sectors. A direct energy comparison between sectors shows that, at zero temperature, every ground state at fixed average particle number lies in the paired subspace. The same holds at fixed even particle number, with the comparison preserving the total particle number, while at fixed odd particle number one fermion remains unpaired, as required by parity. Within the resulting paired subspace, minimization over positive generalized-P representations of pseudospin coherent states selects a common phase for the nonzero pair amplitudes and determines their magnitudes. BCS and number-projected BCS states arise as particular minimizers under the respective particle-number constraints.

articles.title: Solvent/Antisolvent-Driven Etching of 2D Layered Halide Perovskite Microcrystals toward Endo-Epitaxial Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Engineering internal interfaces within single crystals remains challenging, particularly in soft ionic materials such as layered halide perovskites (LHPs), for which conventional lithographic approaches are difficult to implement. Here we report a solvent/antisolvent-driven strategy for controlled etching of LHP microcrystals, producing well-defined rectangular cavities. Etching initiates at the top surface and proceeds preferentially along the crystallographic [100] and [010] directions. Cavity dimensions are tuned through etching time, temperature and etchant composition. The reaction can be interrupted and resumed, enabling stepwise cavity evolution through successive etching cycles. The resulting cavities serve as confined templates for regrowth of compositionally distinct LHPs, yielding endo-epitaxial heterostructures with designed internal architectures. The approach extends across diverse LHP compositions and antisolvent systems, while sequential precursor addition controls the extent of internal regrowth. This strategy establishes a route to engineering internal heterointerfaces in single-crystal perovskites through controlled chemical etching and confined growth.

articles.title: Preformed excitons in the excitonic density-wave state of monolayer 1T'-MoTe₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-incoherent preformed excitons have long been anticipated in excitonic insulators, yet their characteristic signatures and underlying physics remain elusive, as the electrical neutrality of excitons hinders direct probes of condensate phase coherence. Here we exploit the emergent excitonic density wave driven by phase-coherent pairings in systems hosting momentum-separated electron and hole Fermi pockets, such as monolayer 1T'-MoTe₂, as an experimentally accessible probe of excitonic phase coherence. We observe in 1T'-MoTe₂ that the density-wave order and its associated emergent collective excitations, as revealed by Raman spectroscopy, vanish above T_capprox80~K, whereas the excitonic-insulator state, characterized by a single-particle gap in transport and tunneling measurements, persists up to T_gapprox100~K, revealing an intermediate pseudogap-like regime of preformed excitons without long-range phase coherence. Theoretically, we attribute this intriguing separation to two distinct processes governing the loss of excitonic order by its own emergent excitations: boson-driven phase decoherence and fermion-driven pair breaking. Specifically, we identify an emergent low-lying collective excitation as a lattice-pinned phason (phase mode), whose heating-induced gap softening enhances phase fluctuations and drives condensate phase decoherence above T_c, while thermal excitations of fermionic quasiparticles gradually suppress and ultimately destroy pairing amplitude at the higher T_g. The self-consistent microscopic calculation quantitatively captures our key observations, establishing an excitonic realization of preformed-pairing physics.

articles.title: Targeted material doping to enable the formation and coherent propagation of Laser Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS): the ZnO paradigm
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work explores how the initial free carrier density governs the formation and coherent propagation of Low Spatial Frequency Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LSF-LIPSS). As a paradigm we have analyzed the behavior of ad-hoc-doped ZnO films. ZnO is a multifunctional Transparent Conducting Oxide (TCO) with many scientific and technologic uses including applications in biomedicine, photonics, sensing or photocatalysis. Many of them would benefit from the use of large area, electrically anisotropic surfaces. By introducing small amounts of Yb3+ as donor dopant in ZnO films grown by Pulse Laser Deposition (PLD), we have substantially improved its carrier density at room temperature (RT) and its electrical conductivity while preserving the functional properties of pure ZnO. For RT carrier densities ne > 1019 cm-3, coherent propagation of LSF-LIPSS has been successfully achieved upon irradiation with 350 fs laser pulses at 1030 nm at high repetition rate (500 kHz) and for laser scanning speeds well above 1 m/s. However, the ablation mechanism (ZnO sublimation at the LIPSS valleys) and the large melting temperature of ZnO, make the thermal conductivity of the substrate, the film thickness and the irradiation pulse duration to play a crucial role in determining the morphology of the LSF-LIPPS propagated over large areas, especially in avoiding film cracking. The results achieved upon optimization fully confirm the role of free carrier density in the large-scale propagation of high quality LSF-LIPSS in doped ZnO and enable using these structures to easily generate large electrical anisotropies over macroscopic regions with conductivities along the LIPSS several times larger than transversally.

articles.title: A Variational Description of the Adsorption Phenomenon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The adsorption of particles dispersed in a liquid is analyzed introducing a variational approach. While traditional adsorption models rely on localized, discrete site-binding kinetics, we treat the system as a binary mixture consisting of adsorbate particles (APs) and the host liquid within a continuous framework. An expression for the variation of the mixing entropy arising from an inhomogeneous distribution of the APs, of density n(z) is derived. The interactions between APs are modeled by a bulk free energy functional containing a term proportional to the square of the density, nabla n, and a bulk compressibility term which exhibits a minimum at the equilibrium bulk density of APs, n₀, in the absence of adsorption. This approach offers the distinct advantage of capturing non-local fluid structures and particle-particle correlations near interfaces that discrete models overlook. The profile n(z) is obtained analytically by linearization of the Euler-Lagrange equilibrium equation for a sample confined between two parallel walls under the constraint of particles number conservation. The surface density of adsorbed particles, σ is then calculated for the simplified case in which the interaction with the substrate is short-ranged and decays exponentially into the bulk. For a semi-infinite sample limited by a planar wall, the analysis predicts that σsim n₀ for small values of n₀, whereas it saturates at a constant value for large n₀, in agreement with the predictions of the classical Langmuir model, thereby providing a thermodynamic foundation for phenomenological adsorption isotherms. In case a localized surface energy is present, an effective adsorption energy is derived in the limiting cases of vanishing and very large anchoring strength, offering a predictive tool for tailoring surface modifications in experimental soft matter systems.

articles.title: VQkit: A Unified and Extensible Framework for VASP and Quantum ESPRESSO Pre- and Post-Processing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: VQkit is a Python-based computational toolkit developed to streamline the pre- and post-processing of density functional theory calculations performed using Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP) and Quantum ESPRESSO (QE). The framework employs a unified representation of lattice vectors, atomic coordinates, chemical species, and positional constraints, enabling cross-code structure conversion, geometry manipulation, crystallographic reconstruction, and code-specific input generation. Its pre-processing capabilities include symmetry-dependent reciprocal-space path generation, atomic constraints, and automated preparation of simulation inputs. The post-processing framework provides calculation convergence inspection, extraction of total energies and Fermi levels, electronic band-structure and density-of-states analysis, orbital-resolved electronic-structure processing, charge-density analysis, and evaluation of application-specific materials properties. The computational implementation is evaluated through elastic-property benchmarks for HfC, ZrC, ZrO2, Ti, and diamond, showing close agreement between VQkit and VASPKIT for VASP-based calculations, with differences observed in the corresponding QE results. By integrating cross-code interoperability, automated simulation preparation, standardized post-processing, and quantitative property evaluation within a common computational environment, VQkit reduces workflow fragmentation and facilitates consistent pre- and post-processing of first-principles calculations.

articles.title: Effects of probe size, shape, and probe-surface interactions in imaging multilayer island growth, coalescence, and formation of a smooth film
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies of deposition onto weakly interacting substrates have revealed multilayer island growth, followed by smooth-film formation upon island coalescence. However, for C60 films, the roughness peak measured by atomic force microscopy (AFM) was significantly lower than that obtained by X-ray reflectometry (XRR), suggesting tip-sample convolution effects. We investigate this problem using kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations of such films and models of probe-surface interactions for AFM imaging modes. To model the non-contact mode, surface profiles are transformed by averaging heights over regions matching the probe-tip width. A roughness peak remains if the probe width L is smaller than the average island distance, but its height decreases with L and its position is slightly displaced. In the contact-mode model with cylindrical probes and hard-core interactions, the peak also decreases and shifts significantly to smaller thicknesses, indicating apparently faster island coalescence. Thus, SPM images under these conditions may underestimate film-thickness nonuniformity in deposits with coalescing islands. Instead, models of sharp pyramidal or conical probes with hard-core interactions produce deviations in the roughness peaks only for large L, although such sharp tips are difficult to realize experimentally. A geometric model of cuboid island growth and coalescence quantitatively confirms the effects of contact modes and probe shapes observed in the simulations. The results suggest that post-growth processes, such as island coarsening and dewetting, may have occurred in the recently studied C60 film between the XRR and AFM measurements.

articles.title: Mechanically induced self-propagating reactions within the realm of mechanochemistry: Fundamentals, overview, in situ monitoring and perspectives
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanically induced self-propagating reaction (MSR) represents a promising but rather underexplored phenomenon within mechanochemistry, a solvent-free alternative to classical solution-based chemistry. In contrast to the gradual mechanochemical reactions, MSRs are sub-second combustive-like processes bringing about substantial benefits such as faster product formation, time efficiency, and lower energy consumption. Despite the fact that the mechanochemical field is in the research spotlight, MSR investigation remains on the periphery. This review aims to catalyze a renaissance in MSR fundamentals investigation by reviewing the current state-of-the-art. This is done via systematically reviewing the reaction systems that were reported to react via a MSR in the past twenty years, such as metal-metalloid ones (carbides, borides, silicides, and carbonitrides), metal chalcogenides, metal oxides, and other specific types of reactions. A couple of case studies are briefly reviewed for each system, and the comprehensive table follows afterward. The review also revisits the factors impacting the MSR course from milling conditions and reagent's properties point of view, showing either a direct or inverse relationship with MSR ignition time. The recent development in the in situ monitoring of mechanochemical reactions allowed to obtain some mechanistic insights into the MSR process, which are summarized in the last chapter.

articles.title: Non-Invertible Quantum Cellular Automata I: Microscopic Definition of Non-Invertible Symmetries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce non-invertible quantum cellular automata (QCAs), defined as locality-preserving quantum channels that are dualizable and pure. This provides an operator-algebraic definition of non-invertible symmetries of quantum lattice systems, formulated in terms of their action on local operators. Focusing on quantum spin chains, we motivate these defining conditions and conjecture that every such quantum channel admits a realization by dualizable topological defects or, equivalently, by dualizable sequential quantum circuits. We construct a broad class of examples, including on-site non-invertible symmetries that are anomalous, as well as higher-dimensional examples. In Part II of this work, we reconstruct topological defects whose boundary algebras yield an index theory that classifies non-invertible QCAs up to blend equivalence.

articles.title: From quasiperiodic three-colour order on a triangular lattice to covalent carbon sheets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can the quasiperiodic colouring of a lattice be encoded in the bonds of a single carbon sheet? We construct golden-, silver- and bronze-mean three-colour patterns on a triangular lattice. The positions of one colour determine the other two through a nearest-neighbour rule. The three patterns have eight, nine and seven first-shell environments, respectively. A triangle of three identical motifs frustrates the alternating bond ports of each of the three molecular alphabets in the golden and silver patterns. The bronze pattern admits four designs with direct or ethynylene connections. Three periodic structures reproduce its infinite environment frequencies in a local-energy model. For a 708-atom sheet with independently matched environment counts, the predicted energy lies 0.295 meV per carbon below the density-functional result. Across four periodic cells initialized from two smaller donors, relaxation changes the bond lengths by at most 0.00113 angstroms in root-mean-square terms. Fitting one 60-degree sector to relaxed periodic geometries gives complete sixfold-symmetric fragments with up to 22,140 carbon atoms. In the 13,950-atom directly linked sheet, a π doublet places 79.05% of its weight in a boundary shell comprising 7.96% of the atoms, whereas the lowest unoccupied doublet places only 0.124% there. These calculations connect a testable motif-selection rule to the energetics and finite-patch spectra of candidate quasiperiodic carbon sheets.

articles.title: Pair distribution function oscillations at electrostatically stabilized nanocrystal surfaces reflect nanocrystal lattice periodicity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanocrystals (NCs) stabilized electrostatically by short, multivalent inorganic ligands exhibit rich interactions and phase behavior believed to hinge on the configuration of ions at the NC surface, yet these molecular details have not previously been measured. Here we use double-difference pair distribution functions (ddPDFs) of total X-ray scattering to determine the configuration of Sn₂S₆⁴⁻ ligands on PbS NCs suspended in multivalent electrolyte. The measured ddPDFs exhibit a sim3-mathringA wavelength oscillation that extends sim10 mathringA. Comparison with a PbS NC model decorated with Sn₂S₆⁴⁻ ligands indicates ligands are aligned simradially, suggesting bidentate binding. Calculated partial PDFs show that the oscillatory signal is dominated by nanocrystal-Pb to ligand-Sn correlations. A simplified model that replaces the ligand with a strongly scattering Pt atom near the NC surface confirms the oscillation period in the ddPDF originates from the NC lattice constant. Nanocrystal lattice periodicity therefore merits consideration when interpreting ddPDFs of colloidal NCs.

articles.title: Polymer adsorption on vicinal surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While polymer adsorption is theoretically well established on flat surfaces --- and somewhat understood on rough surfaces --- the common and practically relevant case of nearly flat stepped surfaces remains poorly studied. Here, we address this gap via extensive simulations of flexible polymer chains grafted at the step edge of vicinal surfaces. For wide terraces, the polymer-step interaction yields a stable step-attached (SA) phase, alongside the desorbed and terrace-adsorbed (TA) phases, all of them separated by continuous transition lines that meet at a multicritical point previously unanticipated in polymer thermodynamics. This scenario is observed for terrace widths W gtrsim 3 R_g⁽²D⁾, being R_g⁽²D⁾ the radius of gyration of TA polymers. Simpler phase diagrams, absent this multicriticality, are found for W lesssim 3 R_g⁽²D⁾, where a simple crossover exists between the SA and TA phases. The presence of kinks at the steps does not alter these behaviors. Besides their theoretical relevance, these findings unveil an interesting route to produce polymer nanowires and control polymer conformation via step attachment-detachment on designed stepped surfaces.

articles.title: Quasiconformal geometry and elastic anisotropy in liquid crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.22978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unequal splay and bend elastic constants endow planar nematic liquid crystals with a director-dependent anisotropic geometry. Here, we show that this geometry is quasiconformal: the magnitude of the associated Beltrami coefficient is fixed by the elastic constants, while its phase depends on the director relative to a compatible rotating frame introducing an SO(2) spin connection. We construct explicit maps for a hybrid-aligned film and isolated defect textures, generalizing the conformal construction of isotropic defects. These results provide a new insight into the classical Dzyaloshinskii defect solutions, which are shown to define an auxiliary reference cone on which the defect texture is quasiconformally distorted before being projected conformally into physical space. Numerical simulations of constrained +2 defects reveal core morphologies consistent with the quasiconformal geometry. Our results suggest that quasiconformal maps provide a broader geometric language for anisotropy in liquid crystals and other materials.

articles.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. II. A path-probability formalism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a dynamical theory of the East model---a one-dimensional, hierarchically constrained kinetic Ising model---based on path-probability densities. This theory yields an infinite but closed set of equations for single-spin path-probability densities, which, after Laplace transformation, become algebraic difference equations. To render the theory tractable, we introduce a systematic factorization approximation in which the joint probability densities of consecutive flip intervals are factorized into lower-order joint probability densities. We implement the first-order single-interval factorization approximation, obtain a closed set of four equations for the persistence functions, and solve them numerically. The resulting time correlation functions and relaxation times agree closely with Monte Carlo simulations and with the two-domain-basis approximation of the Zwanzig--Mori formalism over a wide range of temperatures, although both approximations fail to capture the exact low-temperature asymptotic super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time. The present formalism provides a plausible foundation for a complete and rigorous theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model and offers a promising route toward generalization to other systems.

articles.title: Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Textures at Chiral Molecule-Metal Interfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral molecular adsorption can modify the spin and orbital character of metal surface states, providing an electronic-structure basis for interpreting spin-dependent interfacial phenomena. Using first-principles calculations with spin-orbit coupling, band unfolding, and an atom-projected orbital angular momentum (OAM) analysis, we investigate spin and OAM textures at chiral heptahelicene/Au(111) interfaces and compare them with clean Au (111) and an achiral coronene/Au system. Adsorption changes the orientations of the spin and OAM vectors and reduces the sampled OAM magnitudes of Au-derived surface states near the Fermi level. The two heptahelicene enantiomers exhibit textures related by mirror and time-reversal symmetries, whereas the comparison with coronene identifies changes that also occur without molecular chirality. These results clarify how molecular adsorption modifies interfacial spin and orbital character and establish symmetry constraints relevant to chirality-dependent photoemission.

articles.title: Spontaneous axis formation through defect fusion in active nematics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Initially spherical embryos break symmetry to establish a body axis. Topological defects in tissue nematic order have been implicated in axis formation, but the physical mechanisms underlying defect organization in active materials remain unclear. We study an active nematic fluid on a sphere using a fully covariant hydrodynamic theory that ensures thermodynamic consistency in the passive limit. We find that, in compressible systems, active nematic traction drives a spontaneous transition from the equilibrium configuration of four separated +1/2 defects to two antipodal +1 defects through pairwise fusion. The resulting state defines an axis, with aster or vortex textures at the poles depending on the flow-nematic coupling. These results identify a physical mechanism by which active forces reorganize topological defects to establish an axis on a spherical surface.

articles.title: Specific heat in the BCS-rashbon BEC crossover regime of an ultracold Fermi gas with a 3D spherical spin-orbit coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically investigate strong-coupling properties of an ultracold Fermi gas with a tunable spherical (isotropic) spin-orbit interaction. In this spin-orbit coupled system, it is known that a two-body bound state, called rashbon, can be formed even in the coupling regime where a pairing interaction alone cannot form such a two-body bound molecule. In this paper, we evaluate the specific heat at constant volume C_V, including pairing fluctuations in the presence of SOC within the framework of the strong-coupling theory developed by Nozières and Schmitt-Rink, to show that this thermodynamic quantity is very useful to see how system properties vary from a Fermi gas to a rashbon gas with increasing spin-orbit coupling strength. At the superfluid phase transition temperature Tᵣₘ c, C_V is found to exhibit a peak structure in the intermediate spin-orbit coupling regime between the weak-coupling Fermi gas regime and a strong-SOC rashbon gas regime. In the normal state above Tᵣₘ c, from detailed analyses of the temperature dependences of C_V, we also identify the regions where system properties are dominated by (1) a Fermi atomic gas, (2) a Bose gas of stable rashbons, and (3) fluctuating rashbons. Combining these results with the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS)--Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) crossover physics realized by tuning the strength of a pairing interaction, we present a unified description of the BCS--BEC and BCS--rashbon BEC crossover phenomena.

articles.title: Localized corrosion resistance of ultrafine-grained austenitic steel 321 obtained by Rotary Swaging: The role of annealing conditions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The object of this study was austenitic steel 321, which has an ultrafine-grained (UFG) structure formed by Rotary Swaging (RS). RS leads to the formation of a two-phase macroscopically heterogeneous and, at the same time, a microscopically homogeneous UFG structure with an increased content of martensite. It has been shown that secondary TiC nanoparticles form in the annealing at 450-550C, the reverse transformation of martensite into austenite occurs at 550-650C, and recrystallization begins at 700C. Electrochemical studies of the resistance of the UFG steel to general corrosion, intergranular corrosion (IGC), and pitting corrosion (PC) have been carried out. It has been shown that the UFG steel after RS has a reduced IGC resistance. The surface of steel rods after RS has a reduced hardness and corrosion resistance compared to the central part of the rods. It has been shown that in the temperature range of 450-550C, there is a slight increase in the microhardness, and a significant decrease in the IGC and PC resistance of the UFG steel. Recrystallization at 700-800C leads to an increased PC resistance and IGC resistance. Annealing conditions have been determined that ensure a good combination of strength, ductility and corrosion resistance of the UFG steel. It was demonstrated that to explain the non-monotonic variation in the localized corrosion rate of UFG steel during annealing, it is necessary to consider not only the well-known effects of martensite and delta-ferrite, but also the precipitation of TiC particles and the changes in the free energy of non-equilibrium grain boundaries.

articles.title: Effect of superplastic deformation on the intergranular corrosion resistance of austenitic steel 321 with different types of UFG structure: A case of homogeneous and heterogeneous microstructure obtained by ECAP
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.23183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effects of superplasticity (SP) on the structure, hardness, and intergranular corrosion (IGC) resistance of UFG 321L steel are reported. By increasing the number of the ECAP cycles (N) and varying the ECAP temperature, and annealing temperature, the degree of the microstructural heterogeneity was changed. Regardless of the microstructural homogeneity degree, UFG steels demonstrated the possibility of realizing the SP effect at temperatures below the onset temperature of dynamic recrystallization. The dependence of ductility of the UFG steel on the test temperature is non-monotonic with a minimum at 450-600C. The maximum elongation to failure (~250%) was achieved at a SP temperature of 800C. The SP deformation of the UFG steel is controlled by the power law creep. It is shown that the hardness of UFG steel samples after SP is equal than the hardness of UFG steels annealed at the same temperature. It is also shown what SP leads to a decrease in the IGC resistance of the UFG steel. Heterostructured steel have reduced ductility, as well as lower resistance to IGC after tension tests at room temperature (RT). The minimum IGC resistance is ensured at N=2, and the maximum - at N=4. The IGC resistance of homogeneous UFG samples after tension testing exceeds the IGC resistance of coarse-grained steel. Tension test at a RT has the greatest negative effect on the IGC resistance of heterostructured steel, and the least negative effect on the IGC resistance of homogeneous steel.
