Together with the absence of an additional chemical component or distinct band manifold in photoemission, these observations support an electronic origin of the kagome-like contrast. Comparison of local tunneling spectra with calculated orbital projections suggests an energy selective change in the relative spectral contributions of Sb p states. Interface separation tests reveal sensitivity to Al-Sb coupling, while vacuum local density of states calculations identify states with enhanced bridge density. These results suggest that local interface changes could alter the balance between atomic and bridge contributions to tunneling within β-Sb. For a reference β-Sb model retaining the epitaxial geometry after Al removal, spin-orbit coupling modifies local band dispersions while the structure remains metallic. The model exhibits a finite intrinsic spin Hall response that varies with chemical potential.

articles.title: Orbital antiferromagnetic currents in a frustrated fermionic ladder
articles.abstract: arXiv:2407.19232v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a spinless t-t' ionic Hubbard chain at 1/2 filling and large hopping ratio t'/t. In this limit the model adequately maps onto a weakly coupled triangular ladder with a potential interchain bias. The low-energy properties of the system are formed due to the interplay of geometrical frustration, correlations and charge imbalance. We derive the effective field-theoretical model to study universal properties of the model in the scaling limit. We show that at full dynamical frustration the ground state of the ladder represents a repulsive version of the Luther-Emery liquid with dominant orbital antiferromagnetic correlations exhibiting the slowest power-law decay in the ground state. Pairing correlations also display algebraic order but are subdominant. At an incomplete dynamical frustration a finite commensurability gap is dynamically generated, and the fluctuating OAF transforms to a long-range ordered state with a spontaneously broken time reversal symmetry. The mass gap in the spectrum of relative density fluctuations gets suppressed upon increasing the potential bias.

articles.title: The large |U| expansion for a half-filled asymmetric Hubbard model on a triangular ladder in the presence of spin-dependent magnetic flux
articles.abstract: arXiv:2412.13657v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a half-filled system of spin-1/2 fermions on a triangular ladder with spin-dependent hopping in the presence of spin-dependent flux. Using the Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, we derive an effective spin Hamiltonian describing the infrared properties of the system in the limit of strong on-site repulsion. The expansion is performed up to the third order in the hopping amplitude over on-site interaction energy. It is shown that the low-energy spin excitations are described by an anisotropic XXZ Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and an unconventional three-spin (correlated exchange) term in the presence of an extended magnetic field. The latter couples not only to z-projection of the total spin on a triangular plaquette but also to the product of z-components of three spins located on vertices of the triangle. In the case of strong attractive interaction, the corresponding effective model is derived from the repulsive one using the one-spin-component particle-hole transformation. The effective Hamiltonian is given by the same XXZ Heisenberg model, as in the repulsive case, but in terms of pseudospin (charge) operators.

articles.title: A General-Purpose and Efficient Machine-Learned Potential for SiC from Ambient to Extreme Environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.01827v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) polymorphs are widely employed as nuclear materials, mechanical components, and wide-bandgap semiconductors. The rapid advancement of SiC-based applications has been complemented by computational modeling studies, including both ab initio and classical atomistic approaches. In this work, we develop a computationally efficient, general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potential (ML-IAP) capable of multimillion-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Building on the tabulated Gaussian approximation potential (tabGAP) framework, we introduce an additional embedding term that captures local atomic coordination, improving accuracy and generality, while retaining high computational efficiency. Using this ML-tabGAP model, we map a broad pressure-temperature phase diagram, simulate the threshold displacement energy distributions for the 2H and 3C polymorphs, and simulate primary irradiation damage in 3C. Across a benchmark covering conditions from ambient to extreme, including high-pressure/high-temperature states and high-energy cascade damage, tabGAP provides a favorable balance of accuracy, robustness, transferability, and computational cost among the tested empirical and ML-IAPs.

articles.title: Experimental methods to measure thermal hysteresis of martensite-austenite transition in bulk beta-Cu-Zn-Al composition gradient single crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.17297v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Improvement of functional and structural fatigue endurance for applications of ferroelastic materials requires an optimization of their composition. We propose an experimental methodology to explore the model beta-Cu-Zn-Al system. It is based on an original route to process bulk gradient composition single crystals to investigate fine variation of composition range coupled with local measurements of the austenite-martensite microstructure by light microscopy during the transformation. The latter method is compared with differential scanning calorimetry measurements. The methodology is applied to different narrow ranges (up to 4 at%) of composition of standard CuZnAl shape memory alloys where local fluctuations of hysteresis of 3 K are observed.

articles.title: Pseudospin order of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.26128v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional superconducting system with a smoothly and periodically varying order parameter, which is modulated along one direction while remaining uniform in the perpendicular direction, leading to a spatially periodic superconducting phase. It is known that the phase of the order parameter determines the relative phaseof the quasiparticle components. Here we demonstrate that the latter becomes observable through the associated Bloch vector, which provides a topological invariant that links the Bloch vector to an integer winding number. The Bloch vector can be understood as the expectation value of the pseudospin, for which the physical manifestation of the winding number is a helical ordering. For the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian with an edge we have both plane-wave solutions describing bulk states and exponentially localized solutions that correspond to edge modes. The analytic bulk-edge connection is employed to identify the conditions under which the edge states emerge from the bulk spectrum. The pseudospin ordering rotates under the energy change of the edge modes but is energy-independent for the bulk modes, except for the opposite sign in the upper and the lower band. These results establish a direct connection between the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the topological structure of the Bloch vector, as well as the relation between the order parameter phase and the pseudospin orientation of the edge modes.

articles.title: Giant enhancement of attosecond tunnel ionization competes with disorder-driven decoherence in amorphized silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.14678v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) and tunnel ionization in solids are strong-field phenomena sensitive to the attosecond dynamics of laser-driven electron-hole pairs. While HHG has been used extensively as a spectroscopic probe in crystalline systems, its potential as a probe of disorder on the length scale of electron-hole trajectories remains relatively unexplored. Furthermore, with the advent of petahertz electronics, there is a growing need for controlling ionization on the nanoscale. Here, we show how focused-ion beam driven amorphization of silicon leads to a giant enhancement (>250 times) of yield for lower-order harmonics and quenching of higher-order harmonics, consistent with a dramatically enhanced tunnel ionization yield and disorder-induced decoherence, respectively. Modelling the real-space quantum dynamics, we show how electron-hole coherence in the amorphous phase is lost over a characteristic length of approximately five lattice sites. HHG spectroscopy also reveals remnant order inherited from the original cubic structure. Our results establish HHG spectroscopy as a probe of medium-range order and pave the way for new opportunities in lightwave nanoelectronics.

articles.title: jahn-teller-dynamics: Python package to determine vibronic interaction demonstrated on molecules and trigonal defect qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.05704v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Trigonal solid-state defects are often subjects of spontaneous symmetry breaking driven by the Eotimes e Jahn-Teller effect, reflecting strong electron-phonon coupling. These systems, particularly paramagnetic defect qubits in solids are central for quantum technology applications, where accurate knowledge of their fine-structure parameters - shaped by the complex interplay of spin-orbit and electron-phonon interactions - is essential. We introduce the mathttjahn text - teller text - dynamics package, a Python code that implements the first-principles approach of [Phys. Rev. X 8, 021063 (2018)] to accurately compute the spin-orbit-phonon entanglement in trigonal defects utilizing the output from density functional theory calculations (DFT) to predict fine-structure parameters of zero-phonon lines (ZPLs), including Zeeman shifts under external magnetic fields. We demonstrate its capabilities on negatively charged Group-IV-vacancy (G4V) defects in diamond: SiV⁻, GeV⁻, SnV⁻, PbV⁻ and the neutral N₃V⁰ defect in diamond, and the CH₃O⁰ methoxy radical. Additionally, we implement a generic electron-phonon code that is capable entangling an arbitrary amount of (i) vibration modes and (ii) electronic levels by (iii) arbitrarily high order of vibronic interaction terms. Exemplarily, we demonstrate the Jahn-Teller multimode problem on the CH₃O⁰ methoxy radical and the Pseudo Jahn-Teller case on the C₄H₄⁺ butatrien cation.

articles.title: Electric-field-controlled altermagnetic spin-momentum locking and ultrahigh tunneling magnetoresistance in Bilayer Cr₂SeO
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.23253v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnets offer a promising platform for spintronics by combining zero net magnetization with nonrelativistic spin splitting, yet efficient electrical manipulation of their spin-dependent transport remains challenging. Here, using first-principles calculations, we show that an out-of-plane electric field induces spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr₂SeO, gives rise to a magneto-optical Kerr effect, and drives a semiconductor-to-metal transition at sufficiently high field magnitudes. Reversing the field direction switches the spin-momentum-locking pattern, which reverses the sign of the Kerr rotation angle as well as that of the longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Leveraging this electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking, we propose a dual-gate altermagnetic tunnel junction in which high- and low-resistance states are realized without reversing the Néel vector. The resistance switching originates from the matching and mismatching of spin-polarized conducting channels in momentum space, yielding a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio on the order of 10⁸. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for realizing electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr₂SeO and developing all-electrically controlled altermagnetic spintronic devices.

articles.title: A Quantum Many-Body Approach for Orbital Magnetism in Correlated Multiband Electron Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.14372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Orbital magnetism is a purely quantum phenomenon that reflects intrinsic electronic properties of solids, yet its microscopic description in interacting multiband systems remains incomplete. We develop a general quantum many-body framework for orbital magnetic responses based on the Luttinger--Ward functional. Starting from the Dyson equation, we reformulate the thermodynamic potential in a weak magnetic field and construct a controlled expansion in powers of B applicable to correlated electron systems. A key technical advance is a modified ``Fourier'' representation using noncommutative coordinates, which allows the thermodynamic potential to be expressed in an effective momentum space where the magnetic field acts perturbatively. This formulation makes analytic progress possible within the Moyal algebra. As an application, we derive the spontaneous orbital magnetization for approximations whose skeleton diagrams contain no fermion loop enclosing magnetic flux (e.g., Hartree--Fock, self-consistent RPA, and single-site dynamical mean-field theory). Vertex corrections consistent with the self-energy are included automatically, without a separate diagrammatic analysis, and the result is expressed entirely in terms of the zero-field Hamiltonian renormalized by the self-energy. For frequency-dependent but Hermitian self-energies, we generalize the orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvature to momentum-frequency space and identify two gauge-invariant contributions built from these quantities. For frequency-independent self-energies the result reduces to the familiar geometric formula for noninteracting systems. This framework provides a unified foundation for computing orbital magnetic responses in correlated multiband materials.

articles.title: Band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.15131v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnets are a class of metallic magnets characterized by spin-split electron bands. Like an- tiferromagnets they lack spontaneous bulk magnetisation. The initial description of the momentum dependent spin splitting of electron bands in altermagnets was based on the spin groups approach, which is valid when relativistic interactions are neglected. Then the spin-orbit coupling has been taken into account according with time-reversal-odd, even-parity irreducible representations of cen- trosymmetric point groups formally considered by R.M.Fernandes et al, Phys.Rev.B 109, 024404 (2024). The problem of electron band splitting should be discussed based on crystal symmetry of concrete altermagnet material. Here, the band spin-splitting in hexagonal altermagnet CrSb is established using magnetic groups formalism that allows to find the additional spin splitting missed in frame of exchange approximation. Another type of spin splitting takes place in so called hidden altermagnets. This type materials do not possess symmetry in respect of space and time inversion but are symmetric in respect of the product of these operations known as toroid symmetry. There is demonstrated the real space spin splitting in materials with toroid symmetry.

articles.title: The Z_N× ³ symmetry protected boundary modes in two-dimensional Potts paramagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.00910v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct and analyze a class of one-dimensional boundary Hamiltonians arising from two-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases with Z_N× ³ symmetry on a triangular lattice. Using a cohomology-based transformation, the lattice models for the edge modes are explicitly obtained, and their structure is shown to be governed by the arithmetic properties of N. For prime N, the boundary theory admits a formulation in terms of mutually commuting Temperley-Lieb algebras. For the composite values of N, the models exhibit hierarchical or factorized structures. We demonstrate that the phases can be understood in terms of primary models augmented by local defect degrees of freedom that partition the system into independent segments. Finally, the global symmetry is realized on the boundary in a non-on-site and anomalous manner, directly realizing the corresponding 't Hooft anomaly.

articles.title: Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in PT antiferromagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.11128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Surface altermagnetism extends spin splitting beyond bulk altermagnets through symmetry reduction at surfaces and interfaces. An existing classification applies to the local symmetry of atomically flat surface terraces. Here we address the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue class. Because rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet with antitranslations, the classification reduces to PT-symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations or suppress spin splitting. Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in PT-symmetric antiferromagnets offers a route to combine bulk electrical switchability with altermagnetic surface transport.

articles.title: Lattice dynamics and the spectroscopic signatures of H-bond disorder in δ-AlOOH
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.14590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Compression of δ-AlOOH produces a multistage evolution of H-bond configurations, average symmetry, and proton centering. Raman and infrared anomalies at 5-10 GPa mark early changes in phonon frequencies and linewidths within this sequence, while static harmonic phonons soften only at much higher pressure. We combine harmonic phonon calculations with strongly constrained and appropriately normed (SCAN)-based deep-potential molecular dynamics and phonon quasiparticle analysis at 300 K. Vibrational spectra show branch reorganization and linewidth growth during H-bond disordering. Loss of coherence in a coupled proton-lattice mode develops before the bulk compression anomaly and the change in average symmetry near 9-10 GPa; full proton centering occurs later, at 16-18 GPa. Quasiparticle renormalization and directional longitudinal-optical--transverse-optical (LO-TO) splitting reproduce the three higher-frequency components of the ambient-pressure OH-stretching Raman multiplet; the lowest-frequency component remains unresolved. Finite-temperature H-bond dynamics and loss of spectral coherence are necessary to explain the early spectroscopic anomalies.

articles.title: First-principles calculation of electron-phonon spectral functions for defects using phonon interpolation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.20788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate optical lineshapes of point defects require dense sampling of lattice vibrations, which is challenging for direct first-principles supercell calculations. We introduce a phonon-interpolation method for calculating Huang-Rhys spectral densities and optical lineshapes within the harmonic Franck-Condon framework. By exploiting the spatial localization of transition-induced forces, the method obtains electron-phonon coupling from a tractable defect supercell and samples its vibrational response on dense reciprocal-space grids, avoiding explicit construction and diagonalization of large hypercell dynamical matrices. Applied to the negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, the method resolves low-energy acoustic contributions, the dominant phonon sideband structure, and finer optical-phonon features. The resulting temperature-dependent photoluminescence lineshapes reproduce the main features of experimental spectra after accounting for additional broadening. The approach offers an efficient route to high-resolution defect spectra and can, in principle, complement embedding and machine-learning methods.

articles.title: Electronic and magnetic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals from an ab initio approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.26858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an ab initio method to study the electronic properties of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. In particular, we focus on the calculation of the electronic charge distribution. Our theoretical studies are motivated by the experimental observation of few-electron Wigner crystals in a carbon nanotube [Science 364, 870 (2019)]. We model the experimental setup by confining electrons in a one-dimensional potential well with hard-wall boundary conditions. We represent the Hamiltonian of the system in a basis of Slater determinants and perform full configuration interaction to ensure we capture all the electron correlation for a given basis set. As the one-particle basis set we use particle-in-a-box wave functions which by construction satisfy the boundary conditions. With our approach, we obtain accurate electronic density profiles of small one-dimensional Wigner crystals. These profiles clearly show the localisation of the electrons. Moreover, we calculate the exchange coupling constant of the Wigner dimer by mapping our ab initio method on a Heisenberg Hamiltonian. We obtain a reasonable agreement with a result in the literature.

articles.title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.26888v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs), with their unique compositional-complexity and tunable surface chemistry, have emerged as promising electrocatalysts for energy conversion. The catalytic activity of HEA often arises from the interplay between the intrinsic activity of the individual elements and the synergistic effects generated at the interfaces. Even a single-element substitution in a multicomponent HEA can substantially alter the surface-chemistry and electrochemical kinetics of the active surface. Here we investigated the structure-property relationship of CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) and MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) HEAs by comparing the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Under the same experimental condition, HEA-Cu outperforms HEA-Cr towards both HER and OER. Substituting Cr with Cu significantly enhances the bifunctional activity, where HEA-Cu achieved a lower overpotential (538 mV) and Tafel slope (165 mVdec-1) when compared with HEA-Cr. Computational analysis corroborates these findings, showing that Cu substitution modulates the electronic-structure to provide favorable binding energies for reaction intermediates (H*, O*, OH*, and OOH*). Interestingly, unlike HER, recovered HEA-Cu after OER showed migration of Cu forming a Cu-rich outer layer shell with a multimetallic core. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-element substitution in HEAs as a strategy for designing high-performance, cost-effective catalysts for efficient water electrolysis.

articles.title: New theoretical framework free of ghostlike instabilities expands the possibilities of symmetry in particle physics
articles.abstract: Elementary particles and the forces governing their interactions are described by relativistic quantum field theory, in which symmetry serves as a fundamental guiding principle. For more than half a century, the possible symmetries of such theories were believed to be restricted by the Coleman–Mandula theorem and its supersymmetric extension, the Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius theorem.

articles.title: Elusive optical effect paves the way for advanced lidar and nanophotonic technologies
articles.abstract: An international research team, led by scientists from Skoltech, has experimentally demonstrated for the first time the photonic spin Hall shift for light scattered off an optically small particle. This work, published in the Advanced Photonics journal, overcomes a long-standing challenge in optics and could contribute to the development of next-generation optical technologies, advanced radar and lidar systems.

articles.title: Reading superconducting qubits while suppressing unwanted state transitions
articles.abstract: Recently an artificial intelligence proved an 18-year-old conjecture in computer science, called the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture. The proof settles a long-standing conjecture (educated guess) that eliminates one proposed route to enormous quantum computer speedups, ruling out one particular variant of "quantum supremacy," the term for the hypothesis that a programmable quantum computer can solve a problem that no classical computer can solve in any "feasible" amount of time.

articles.title: Lower Bound of Thermal Conductivity in Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The intrinsic thermal conductivity (κ) of graphene remains highly controversial because of physical and metrological complexities. Although the thermal bridge method enables reliable measurements, sample fabrication remains challenging. Here, we develop a highly efficient patterning and transfer technique to systematically fabricate and characterize suspended bilayer graphene (BLG) thermal bridges with lengths of 1-30 μm. Suspended BLG with unavoidable polymer residues exhibits length-independent thermal conductivity of approximately 570 W/(m K) at room temperature, remaining nearly constant from 250 to 350 K and robust to rigorous surface cleaning and amorphous silicon nitride substrates. Homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations show that amorphous carbon coverage of only approximately 0.01 monolayer is sufficient to suppress out-of-plane flexural acoustic (ZA) phonons. These findings challenge the prevailing view that rigid substrates suppress ZA phonons more strongly than surface contamination and identify a robust lower bound of κ governed by amorphous surface scattering. This lower bound reflects heat conduction in graphene under realistic device conditions and provides a reference for fundamental phonon transport studies and the integration of graphene into thermal management applications in electronic devices and chips.

articles.title: Adaptive nonorthogonal atomic orbitals refine charge transfer and bonding descriptors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19023v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: First-principles calculations implicitly encode bonding and charge transfer, but converting periodic electronic structure into interpretable and transferable descriptors remains challenging. Recently, we introduced Crystal Orbital Guided Iteration To atomic-Orbitals (COGITO), a tool for mapping plane-wave DFT back to an interpretable, minimal basis of adaptive atomic orbitals. Here, we show how the high-dimensional bonding information from COGITO can be reduced into chemically useful descriptors of covalent bonding, charge transfer, and crystal-dependent atomic chemistry without collapsing the real-space origin of the interactions. Compared to methods that use static or orthogonal orbital bases, COGITO descriptors of short- and long-range bonding show more stability and a better ability to distinguish between ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding regimes. Lastly, COGITO reliably decomposes band dispersion into range-resolved contributions, allowing us to verify and add to the orbital origins of silicon's low-symmetry conduction band minimum. Overall, the adaptive COGITO-based descriptors encode electronic structure, offering a well-structured route to expose the orbital interactions and charge transfer responsible for electronic properties.

articles.title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-1/2 XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.

articles.title: A mesoscale damage model for void nucleation and growth in shock loaded microstructure informed by computer vision
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spallation in ductile materials under high strain rates occurs through the process of void nucleation, growth, and coalescence. Void nucleation is known to depend on factors ranging from microstructural to stress state. The criteria for void nucleation in damage models are stochastic, and microstructural awareness is often neglected. Recently, it was shown that nucleation propensity can be estimated using computer vision. In the present work, this is integrated with a continuum damage model framework for comprehensive simulation of spallation in tantalum under plate impact. Void nucleation probability is governed by a susceptibility field, predicted from grain orientations and grain boundary (GB) energy, with a mechanical barrier set by the local maximum principal stress. This is coupled to a crystal plasticity model within a Lagrangian shock simulation, with microstructure selectively resolved to reduce computational cost. The model is calibrated at a flyer velocity of 196 m/s, where the simulated free surface velocity (FSV) matches experimental measurements of shock arrival, peak state, release and the pullback signal measured in flyer impact experiments, with some deviations confined to the late time ringing. With no further parameter changes, the model transfers to a 214 m/s case and accurately reproduces the FSV. To demonstrate the microstructure-awareness of the nucleation model, a selection of synthetic microstructures is presented for comparison. In the resolved microstructure, voids nucleate predominantly (though not exclusively) at GBs and triple junctions. It is shown that the FSV differs significantly based on the incorporated microstructure, yielding the correct FSV prediction only in the case of representative microstructures.

articles.title: Optical response of quantum metals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strongly interacting quantum systems display puzzling electrical transport properties whose interpretation remains controversial. Many theoretical and phenomenological analyses assume that the complex behaviour observed in such `quantum materials' originates either from quasi-particles dressed with an anomalous electron self-energy or from collective excitations associated with hydrodynamic flow. Despite their distinctly different starting points, the underlying assumption is that dissipation of electrical current arises from the relaxation of the total momentum of charge carriers. This classical description breaks down in the absence of long-lived charge carriers. In such strange metals dissipation seems to be governed by the rate at which equilibrium is thermally restored, and it has been suggested that this constitutes an upper bound, known as the `Planckian limit'. Here we show that in this quantum regime a description of the conductivity in terms of relaxation rates no longer suffices: strange metal transport is carried instead by fast-decaying current fluctuations, which together with quantum detailed balance give rise to the widely observed Planckian dissipation. The distinction between classical and quantum metals becomes transparent when experimental data is analysed in terms of the current-current correlation function instead of the optical conductivity. When applied to the cuprate superconductors, such analysis uncovers that the strange metal response is present at all doping levels, and that a second, classical component develops above optimal doping. This simple, but powerful, approach further highlights essential features associated with superconductivity, (pseudo-)gaps, provides fresh insight in the properties of metals, and identifies key areas where progress in our theoretical understanding is needed.

articles.title: Thermal-energy relaxation in chiral quantum Hall edge mode
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nonequilibrium state generated by a real Ohmic contact (ROC) in the charge-fractionalization regime. We then investigate its thermal-energy relaxation along a quantum Hall edge mediated by a fictitious Ohmic contact (FOC) with large capacitance and perfect coupling to the edge. For cold Ohmic contacts, the electron distribution function and current noise are fully described by their equilibrium forms and the corresponding Fermi-Dirac distribution. In contrast, in the case of hot Ohmic contacts, strong thermalization effects do not drive the outgoing state into complete equilibrium. Both the distribution function and the noise retain signatures of the initial nonequilibrium state and therefore cannot be characterized solely by the effective contact temperature, contrary to common assumptions.

articles.title: Porosification of the dielectric layer in alternating-current electroluminescence devices enables high-resolution tactile imaging
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-based tactile sensing enables high-resolution contact perception, yet bulky optical architectures consume valuable space and constrain the functional design of dexterous robotic hands. Here we introduce a self-emissive tactile imaging strategy based on alternating-current electroluminescence (ACEL) devices, in which a compressible porous dielectric encodes contact pressure into spatial emission patterns without external illumination or discrete sensing pixels. We identify a nonlinear capacitance-dependent emission window that provides a basis for tunable pressure-to-light conversion. Pore-size engineering further suppresses local emission deficiencies, reducing spatial intensity variation by nearly ninefold and enabling faithful imaging of contact features down to 100 μm. The continuous electroluminescent interface also reproduces complex contact patterns without computational reconstruction of electrical fields. Direct lamination of the ACEL device onto a complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensor is expected to enable compact contact imaging in an assembly less than 5 mm thick, substantially thinner than conventional vision-based tactile sensors. This approach could reduce the space required for high-resolution tactile imaging, offering greater design freedom for dexterous robotic hands.

articles.title: Charge-Transfer Energy Governed by f-d Coulomb Interaction in Rare-Earth Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The f-d Coulomb interaction (Uᵣₘ fd) plays a central role in low-energy theories describing valence fluctuations and quantum valence criticality in rare-earth systems. In contrast, core-level spectroscopies have conventionally been analyzed using the phenomenological charge-transfer energy (Δ), and the relationship between these two descriptions has remained unclear. Here, we develop a spectroscopic framework demonstrating that the charge-transfer energy contains an f-d Coulomb contribution Uᵣₘ fdn_d arising from the d-electron occupation (n_d), leading to the charge-transfer energy Δ'. We apply this framework to the prototypical valence-transition compound YbInCu₄ and demonstrate, from combined analyses of core-level photoemission and L-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy, that the observed spectroscopic evolution across the first-order valence transition is consistently interpreted in terms of the variation of Δ'.

articles.title: Electrical transport of surface-bound electrons on annealed solid neon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dc transport of electrons bound to the surface of solid neon using the conventional Sommer-Tanner method. First, we find that the capacitive cross-talk for the thickness of solid samples on the order of a millimeter varies substantially with the temperature and is strongly affected by the sample annealing. Second, we find that, even for the annealed samples, the observed response of electrons differs significantly from that of the surface-bound electrons on liquid helium and cannot be satisfactorily described by conventional models. Despite this, we managed to extract the resistance of the electron system from its in-phase response and investigate the temperature dependence in a wide range between 1.4 and 20 K. In a high-temperature range between 16 and 20 K, the resistance behavior is found to agree very well with the vapor-atom scattering mechanism, while at lower temperatures it is consistent with temperature-dependent scattering by surface roughness. Our analysis indicates a high electron mobility of electrons on solid neon but two orders of magnitude lower density than expected. These results suggest surface electrons as a suitable probe for studying the morphology of the neon surface but call for a better understanding of the experimental method applicable to such systems.

articles.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. Using a diagrammatic formulation of the exciton-polaron problem, we derive exact relations between the spectral and quasiparticle properties of current-biased exciton-polarons and their finite-momentum counterparts in an equilibrium Fermi sea. These relations show that absorption measurements with drifting electrons can reconstruct the momentum dependence of the quasiparticle properties for both branches. We estimate that experimentally accessible currents can probe a broad momentum range while remaining within the linear-response regime.

articles.title: Chirality-polarized superradiance induced by quantized orbital-angular-momentum transfer in a ring cavity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a spin-1/2 Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to two counterpropagating modes of an optical ring cavity and driven by Laguerre-Gaussian Raman beams carrying quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). We demonstrate that competition between OAM-selective Raman scattering channels controls collective superradiance through self-consistent atom--cavity feedback, linking atomic orbital motion to cavity-chirality selection. For unequal OAM transfer, one cavity mode dominates the superradiant response, with its chirality switchable by the Raman pump strengths. In contrast, equal OAM transfer allows both counterpropagating modes to coexist. The resulting chirality-polarized phases support distinct vortex and vortex--antivortex configurations with reconstructed synthetic gauge-field textures. Remarkably, contact interactions can reshape the vortex topology without changing the dominant cavity chirality, revealing distinct responses of atomic and photonic degrees of freedom. The predicted mode switching and vortex ordering can be probed through cavity output and spin-resolved imaging in a proposed ⁸⁷Rb implementation. Our results establish quantized OAM transfer as a mechanism for controlling collective cavity emission beyond conventional atomic SOAMC.

articles.title: Giant Raman Optical Activity in Chiral and Polar Ni₃TeO₆
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Raman optical activity (ROA) measures the difference in Raman scattering intensity for right- and left-circularly polarized light and reflects the chirality of excitations. In solids, ROA is commonly very weak. For the phonons of chiral and polar Ni₃TeO₆, we find a giant ROA with magnitude 100 times higher than commonly reported for molecules. The systematic analysis based on phonon selection rules allows the chiral and achiral scattering channels to be separated. First-principles calculations of the Raman tensor at finite phonon momentum relate the effect to the phonon modulation of the band-geometric and band-dispersion contributions to optical gyrotropy. This establishes Raman optical activity as a probe of electron--phonon modulation of the band geometry in an insulator.

articles.title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H₂-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H₂ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

articles.title: Multi-symmetry projected coupled cluster theory with triples corrections
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry projection and coupled cluster theory provide complementary descriptions of static and dynamic correlation. We introduce two approximate perturbative triples corrections to spin- and point-group-projected coupled cluster with single and double excitations (PCCSD). The coherent (T) correction combines triples intermediates over the projection grid, whereas +(T) evaluates the conventional triples expression using PCCSD amplitudes. Both recover conventional (T) in the absence of projection. We assess these corrections for N₂ and C₂ dissociation, 3d transition-metal monoxides, and Cr₂. Projection improves the singles-and-doubles description and distinguishes selected low-lying symmetry sectors. For the six-monoxide benchmark subset, coherent (T) reduces the PCCSD mean absolute error from 13.4 to 3.0~mEh, achieving accuracy comparable to conventional CCSD(T). Both triples corrections restore the short-bond minimum missing from the PCCSD curves of Cr₂, with coherent (T) giving a well depth closer to extrapolated DMRG. In contrast, +(T) provides more balanced N₂ and C₂ dissociation curves. These results demonstrate the benefits of perturbative triples in PCC, while their system-dependent performance highlights the need for a more systematic treatment.

articles.title: Calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains from local conserved charges and currents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a simple algebraic method for calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains. We introduce current minors, antisymmetrized products of local conserved charge densities and their currents, and prove that their expectation values are determinants of density and current mean values. Decomposing local operators into current minors, we derive factorized formulas for correlation functions in terms of current mean values, valid in any nondegenerate eigenstate. Applying the method to the spin-1/2 XXZ chain and, more generally, to every representation of the Temperley--Lieb algebra, we prove previously conjectured factorized formulas for short-distance correlation functions.

articles.title: Interface-Selective Extreme Ultraviolet Second Harmonic Generation Away from Linear Absorption Edges
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (XUV) second harmonic generation (SHG) combines interface selectivity with core-level element specificity but has so far been limited to linear absorption edges. Here, we measure XUVSHG from an indium tin oxide capped MoO₃/SiO₂/Si photovoltaic heterojunction for fundamental energies of 60--76,eV, below the Si L₂,₃-edge. Where linear absorption is a featureless valence background, we observe a strong, structured XUVSHG response with maxima near 70 and 76,eV. Layer-resolved first-principles calculations reproduce both maxima and assign them to the Si/SiO₂ interface, the 76,eV peak to the bridging Si monolayer and the 70,eV peak to the near-interface substrate. Bethe--Salpeter calculations for bulk Si connect the signal to Si 2p excitons at 140--160,eV. At the Si L₂,₃-edge, the calculated response is instead governed by MoO₃-induced asymmetry at the oxide interface. These findings establish off-edge XUV SHG as a powerful approach for selectively probing distinct buried interfaces within complex material heterostructures.

articles.title: Logarithmic thermodynamic cost of prediction from rare observations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A memory predicting changes in its environment from rare observations must spend energy on sampling and recording. We consider autonomous chemical memories driven by a sample-and-hold sensor observing an environment that switches at rate gamma, with sampling frequency f<

articles.title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe₂/HfS₂ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe₂/HfS₂ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the Γ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. We further show that external vertical electric fields, twist engineering, and both out-of-plane and in-plane strain provide efficient means to tune the band alignment, charge transfer, and Rashba parameters. In particular, electric fields and mechanical strain can drive reversible transitions between type-II and type-III band alignments while simultaneously modifying the Rashba spin texture and the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) window. The twisted heterostructure with θ = 21.79^circ exhibits similar tunability, including strain-induced transitions between distinct band-alignment regimes. These findings establish MoTe₂/HfS₂ vdWHs as versatile multifunctional platforms combining electrically tunable Rashba spin splitting with controllable type-II/type-III band alignment, offering promising opportunities for next-generation TFETs and spintronic devices.

articles.title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Based on temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction measurements and first-principles calculations using the experimental lattice parameters, we found that the contribution of thermal expansion is negligibly small compared with the observed band-gap variation. Furthermore, first-principles phonon calculations for the optimized crystal structure revealed peaks in the phonon density of states near these two characteristic energies. These results suggest that electron-phonon interactions play an important role in the anomalous temperature dependence of the optical band gap in TiNCl, with low- and higher-energy phonons contributing to the low-temperature decrease and the higher-temperature increase, respectively.

articles.title: Nitrogen Defect Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3 From Structural Reconstruction to Water Oxidation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth-abundant ABO3-type perovskite oxides provide a versatile platform for understanding how anion chemistry and defects govern electrocatalytic behavior. Here, we use epitaxial LaFeO3-xNy thin films to reveal how dilute N incorporation (<0.8% N/O) couples to defect formation, structural reconstruction, and water oxidation. Nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition introduces N and is accompanied by reduced oxygen content, localized Fe-metal exsolution, and pronounced lattice expansion, while preserving predominantly Fe3+ in the bulk of the film. Ab initio calculations identify a plausible charge-balanced extended defect configuration involving coupled oxygen and Fe vacancies with substitutional N incorporation, reproducing the experimentally observed lattice expansion while preserving the bulk-average Fe oxidation state. The resulting electronic-state redistribution is accompanied by substantially modified electrical transport and nearly two orders of magnitude higher initial oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity than undoped LaFeO3. Under OER conditions, however, the highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface N depletion and Fe0 oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay toward a quasi-steady state. pH-dependent kinetics and post-OER anion redistribution are consistent with possible lattice-oxygen participation. These results establish relationships among dilute anion incorporation, coupled defect reconstruction, electronic properties, and electrochemical behavior in perovskite oxides.

articles.title: Kinetic and Thermodynamic Limits of Sodium Pore Filling in Hard Carbon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-voltage plateau-like capacity of hard carbon anodes is widely regarded as a key signature of sodium storage in closed pores, often defining the performance of Na-ion batteries. Here, we combine first-principles calculations with a grand canonical Monte Carlo pore-filling model to show that Na storage in closed pores is not governed by a single equilibrium-plateau mechanism but by a distribution of pore-specific thermodynamic and kinetic activation processes. Thermodynamically, the voltage at which Na pore filling becomes favorable decreases with increasing pore size. Kinetically, pore filling involves Na nucleation, coalescence, growth, and bulk diffusion. While small pores fill rapidly, large pores exhibit both a smaller thermodynamic stimulus and significant kinetic limitations. Nucleation can be accelerated by introducing defects at the pore walls, although an excessively high defect concentration slows bulk diffusion. This work shows that not all closed pores contribute equally to Na storage: some may be thermodynamically favorable but kinetically inactive under realistic charge/discharge rates. Because of this, the inverse design of hard carbon electrodes should target a kinetically accessible pore-size and defect-density window that balances high plateau-like capacity with fast-charging performance.

articles.title: Vortex solitons in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our previous study of a three-dimensional (3D) atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) with quadratic nonlinearity and spin-orbit coupling (SOC), stable solitons are realized as semi-vortex (SV) or mixed-mode (MM) states, with SOC applied solely to the atomic component. In the SV state, the molecular part forms a pure vortex, while the atomic part remains a hybrid of fundamental and vortex modes. This prevents the overall self-bound state from achieving a fully pure vortex configuration, with the total vortex component always less than 100%. Here, we extend the study to two dimensions (2D) and uncover a qualitatively different behavior: purely quadratic 2D systems support not only ground-state (GS) SV solitons, but also higher-order excited-state (ES) solitons that are genuine full vortices (a feature absent in the 3D counterpart). For both GS and ES solitons, stable vortex states exist only when the SOC strength λ exceeds a minimum threshold λₘᵢₙ, which increases monotonically with S₁. Conversely, the critical detuning α_c decreases monotonically with S₁, indicating that higher-order vortices are more susceptible to destabilization. For λ < λₘᵢₙ, the system forms MM states instead of vortex solitons. Our results demonstrate that dimensional reduction to 2D enables the emergence of pure-vortex excited states, establishing a new pathway for stabilizing high-charge topological excitations in ultracold molecular gases.

articles.title: Model-free stiffness measurement of microscale soft contacts by far-field traction force microscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The microscale stiffness of soft materials governs their contact mechanics, adhesion and friction, yet it is surprisingly difficult to measure. Micro or nanoindentation is typically used, but extracting stiffness from these measurements requires using contact mechanics models (e.g. JKR), whose assumptions often break down for soft adhesive contacts. Here, we introduce far-field traction force microscopy (FF-TFM) to extract stiffness without using any contact model. We drag a colloidal probe mounted on an atomic-force microscope across a soft surface, measuring the friction force while imaging the displacements of fluorescent tracers on the substrate. Far from the contact, in the elastic limit, these lateral displacements depend solely on the friction force and the substrate stiffness, and fitting them with the point-force solution thus gives the substrate's Young's modulus directly. We successfully match bulk rheology moduli with FF-TFM for six different silicone elastomers, where JKR fits to indentation data underestimate moduli by as much as 40% of their bulk values. Our approach also enables tracking how the probe slips across the surface. We find that soft contacts can "pre-slip" with no detectable signature in the force signal, unlike stiffer contacts. FF-TFM thus offers a contact-model-free route to measuring microscale stiffness and slip behavior in soft materials.

articles.title: Polymorphism and crystal suppression in symmetric mixtures with entropic interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the phases of a binary mixture of hard spheres with equal diameter and negative non-additivity, favoring hetero-coordination in dense samples. By performing extensive swap Monte Carlo simulations, we show that in an interval of small non-additivities, close to the eutectic point, the mixture fails to crystallize and the compressed fluid gets stuck in an amorphous state. The onset of glass at intermediate compositions is associated with the competition between FCC and B2 (CsCl-type) crystal structures. As the propensity of particles to hetero-coordinate grows further, however, the B2 crystal gives way to a B1 (NaCl-type) crystal at equimolarity, and again the mixture orders for all compositions. We argue that this happens because of the underlying FCC symmetry of the B1 crystal. These results, pertaining to a model with excluded-volume interactions only, point to the key role of entropy in generating amorphous structures in multi-component metallic, inorganic, and soft-matter glass formers.

articles.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.

articles.title: Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Layered palladates provide a 4d platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO₂, RbSr₂PdO₃, BaLaPdO₂Cl₂, La₄Pd₃O₈, and La₅Pd₄O₁₀. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-dₓ^₂₋y^₂ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-dz^₂ orbital. LaPdO₂ and BaLaPdO₂Cl₂ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr₂PdO₃ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La₄Pd₃O₈ and quadlayer La₅Pd₄O₁₀ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-dₓ^₂₋y^₂ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO₂Cl₂ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr₂PdO₃ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-dz^₂ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

articles.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain ce(H2)ₙ. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

articles.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. Equilibrium temperatures are given for both a theoretical lumped body and for a slab body, in which thermal conduction is considered. All data are limited to the solid state, up to a material-specific upper temperature limit. Currently, the database applies to extraterrestrial (AM0) sunlight only. A graphical App is also provided for exploring and visualizing the database.

articles.title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze. We introduce a local disordered spin-1 chain in which a single domain wall explores an exact binary tree of configurations. Random fields create strongly correlated disorder on this tree, as in generic interacting systems, while the absence of loops keeps the problem tractable. We rigorously bound the spreading of the domain wall at strong disorder, and efficient numerics on exponentially large trees indicate a localization transition at finite disorder strength.

articles.title: Emptiness formation in quantum fluids: a hydrodynamic solution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an auxiliary-kernel method for constructing the hydrodynamic instantons that govern macroscopic emptiness formation in one-dimensional Galilean quantum fluids. The key step is to represent the equation of state by an auxiliary integral kernel inspired by the Bethe ansatz. For equations of state admitting such a representation, we reduce the imaginary-time hydrodynamic problem to a single integral equation. Its solution determines the full density and current profiles, the vacuum boundary, and the leading emptiness rate. Notably, the construction does not require microscopic integrability. For the Lieb--Liniger gas, we derive the previously conjectured integral equation for the leading rate and use a known elliptic solution to obtain explicit expressions for the rate and vacuum boundary. Direct hydrodynamic numerics support the predicted boundary. We also recover known instanton solutions for a family of polytropic fluids.

articles.title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. For several impurities in a strongly reflecting chain, transmission peaks at an intermediate mean level splitting. At small splittings, energy exchange with the impurities can weaken constructive interference between backscattered paths, consistent with the initial rise in transmission. As excitation channels close, virtual transitions can enhance reflection and drive transmission below its purely elastic value T₀. At larger splittings, these virtual processes weaken and transmission approaches T₀. We discuss how gate-controlled transmission measurements in quantum-dot arrays could test these predictions.

articles.title: Rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models from a tetrality web
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising (TIM) models by using different chiral symmetries to prepare their folded boundary states. We use a moving up procedure which extends the product theory to an auxiliary coset with an S₃ automorphism group, where permutations give twisted Cardy states. We complement this with a moving down approach which reduces to the S₃ invariant algebra. Overall, these procedures uncover a tetrality web relating four different theories. Pulling back ordinary Cardy states of the smallest theory in the web to the physical tensor product system gives eighteen factorized interfaces and six transmitting interfaces. The latter agree with four transposition and two 3-cycle twisted boundaries in the largest theory. They include Gaiotto's RG wall and the interface obtained by fusing an Ising duality line into it. The six interfaces carry the regular action of the TIM fusion ring and have the same energy transmission coefficient, 35/48. Their boundary entropies, bulk correlations and operator spectra distinguish them. We calculate these observables and the complete annulus amplitudes between the twenty four boundaries.

articles.title: The Z₂ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere from multi-target density matrix renormalization group
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The fuzzy-sphere regularization provides a powerful framework for studying three-dimensional (3D) conformal field theories (CFTs) through radial quantization, but conformal defects have so far been studied with it only by exact diagonalization (ED) of small systems. In this work we realize the Z₂ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere by imposing antiperiodic boundary conditions on the Z₂-odd fermion flavor, and solve it with a multi-target density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm that optimizes several low-lying states of each symmetry sector in a common matrix-product basis. This gives the defect spectrum at system sizes well beyond the reach of ED (up to 2s+1=25, or 49 spinless orbitals). The spectrum obeys the spin-parity selection rule of the twist line and organizes into conformal multiplets along the line. Using the displacement operator as an intrinsic ruler, its protected descendant as a test, and the bulk stress tensor as an independent cross-check, we identify the leading finite-size corrections and obtain controlled continuum extrapolations, which sharpen the dimensions of several known defect primaries and resolve four higher-lying ones. This study establishes the fuzzy sphere combined with multi-target DMRG as a framework for precision studies of conformal defects.

articles.title: Dressed higher-form symmetries in mixed state quantum matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe how to construct emergent strong higher-form symmetries in mixed quantum states that act unitarily on Hilbert space. Our construction uses (quasi-)local recovery channels from quantum error correction to some nearby simple (stabilizer) model. We prove that when the recovery is done in an appropriate (deterministic) manner, the resulting operators continue to be unitary. When applied to operators acting on topologically non-trivial sub-manifolds (loops, surfaces), the resulting unitaries inherit the logical algebra of the fixed point model. More generally, the unitarity of the emergent symmetries allows one to define emergent excitations whose statistics follow those of the fixed point limit.

articles.title: Computing rare events in Lévy-driven systems via optimal control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the optimal control formulation of sample path large deviation theory, which has proven effective for numerical computation of instantons and sharp probability estimates in stochastic differential equations with Gaussian noise, to systems with light-tailed Lévy noise. In the scaling limit of small jumps and high intensity, such systems satisfy a large deviation principle of Freidlin-Wentzell type, with a running cost given by the Legendre transform of the noise cumulant generating function. We propose to numerically minimize this cost over noise realizations subject to the system dynamics, which yields the instanton without having to solve Hamilton's equations, and naturally handles degenerate and multiplicative noise. When the cumulant generating function has a bounded domain, the cost grows only linearly for large noise, and instantons can contain jumps. We analyze when jumps are not only admissible but optimal, depending on the subleading behavior of the cost and on the drift, and show how jumps can be resolved numerically through a time reparameterization that freezes physical time. For continuous instantons, we derive Riccati and Fredholm determinant expressions for the leading-order prefactor, and we discuss the modifications needed when the instanton jumps. We illustrate and validate our methods against Monte Carlo simulations in several examples: a two-dimensional nonlinear model, an active run-and-tumble particle with non-Gaussian tumbling noise, and the Ghil-Sellers energy balance climate model with Lévy-perturbed solar forcing.

articles.title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent ν>0, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of 1.5×10⁻¹³ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.

articles.title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90^circ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C₆₀ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per μA of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

articles.title: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching. Linearizing the coherence-vector equations of the intercellular Hartree approximation (ICHA) about the unpolarized state gives a lattice dispersion with a low-frequency cutoff, an evanescent band below it and a Klein-Gordon long-wavelength limit, and relaxation toward the instantaneous equilibrium damps the waves at a rate that depends on the wavenumber. The exact Jordan-Wigner solution and exact diagonalization confirm the mode as a sharp quasiparticle, with ICHA frequencies within 6% of the exact ones once the tunnelling energy is at least twice the kink energy, and show that the exact chain also carries waves over a range of couplings where the ICHA predicts latching. A leading low-temperature estimate of thermal dephasing sets a ceiling on the operating temperature of about 13.6 K per terahertz of gap for a carrier that keeps its phase over 30 periods. At junctions the waves scatter through a lattice scattering matrix that reaches the familiar transmission-line value only at mid-band.

articles.title: Matching two-dimensional statistics does not certify three-dimensional transport in battery electrodes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Three-dimensional battery electrode structures reconstructed from two-dimensional micrographs are routinely used to predict transport, assuming that matching the measured 2D statistics reproduces the relevant 3D properties. We test this premise on X-ray tomograms of three all-solid-state cathodes. With a differentiable conductivity solver, we optimise voxel structures that match the real electrode in phase fractions, boundary density, two- and three-point correlations and lineal-path functions, on all section planes, slab by slab and layer by layer, within measurement noise. Every sample has statistical twins conducting 10-88-fold less than the real electrode, robust to 5³ majority filtering, whereas the most conductive are at most 3.3-fold above it. The twins rearrange rather than remove material, severing or funnelling through-plane paths. A classifier on 2D sections detects them, as it does current 2D-to-3D generators: the information is in the images but not in the statistics. Matching standard 2D statistics therefore does not certify 3D transport.

articles.title: Mixed-state topological transitions with hidden long-range correlations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20159v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a decoherence-driven transition from a one-dimensional symmetry-protected topological state to a trivial product state. The decoherence acts onsite while preserving the protecting symmetry on average. Although conventional local correlations remain short-ranged across the transition, we uncover hidden nondecaying long-range correlations in a symmetry-twisted ensemble that weights states according to their symmetry charge. At the transition, the twisted correlation length diverges and the twisted partition function becomes singular. These signatures can be directly extracted from symmetry-resolved measurement outcomes, making the hidden critical behavior accessible on current quantum platforms at mesoscopic system sizes.
