articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motor imagery (MI) enables a brain-computer interface (BCI) to decode movement intentions without overt movement. Hybrid electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) classification combines complementary signals, but inter-subject variability and the design of information exchange between modalities affect generalization to new subjects. We propose a framework that combines Cross-Subject Class Mixup (CSCM) with Selective Attention. CSCM aims to construct new training data to make the model robust against inter-subject variability. It independently selects EEG and fNIRS donor trials from other training subjects within the anchor class and mixes each modality while preserving the original label. Selective Attention provides an effective way to simultaneously model the temporal signal characteristics and fuse the two modalities. It retains causal temporal self-attention for EEG and uses a classification token (CLS) to integrate both modalities, without fNIRS attention updates or direct cross-modal temporal-token attention. Leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) evaluation across 28 subjects on a public EEG-fNIRS dataset yields a mean balanced accuracy (BA) of 76.85% and a macro-averaged F1 score (Macro-F1) of 76.58%. The proposed model achieves the highest mean performance among five reimplemented baselines. We also examine the contributions of CSCM and Selective Attention through modality-specific mixing and donor-policy comparisons, temporal-policy comparisons, interventions on direct cross-modal paths, and component ablations.

articles.title: The Manifold-Index Model: provably and efficiently avoiding the statistical and computational curse of dimensionality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study vector-valued regression with predictors filling a tube around an unknown m-dimensional manifold M in R^D. In the Manifold-Index Model, the mean response is F=fcircΠM, where ΠM is the nearest-point projection onto M and f:MtoR^p is a possibly non-injective link function. Multiscale ANisotropic lOcal Regression (MANOR) estimates tangent planes by multiscale PCA of predictors with similar responses, then refines them by pooling outer products of local slopes. The neighborhoods narrow tangentially while retaining complete normal fibers. We assume a Lipschitz link differential and bounded response noise. For pge m, under our geometric and sampling conditions, n independent observations give mean tangent-space error of order n⁻²/⁽m⁺⁴⁾ and integrated squared prediction error at the m-dimensional nonparametric rate n⁻⁴/⁽m⁺⁴⁾, up to logarithmic factors. In a scaling regime with fixed intrinsic dimension, model and scale parameters, and ratio of manifold volume to the m-th power of its reach, the required sample size grows polynomially in D+p, and computation is polynomial in n, D and p. Numerical experiments on curves with non-monotone links and surfaces with vector-valued responses compare observed convergence rates with the theoretical bounds; a Langevin dynamics example tests prediction of hitting probabilities under an approximate manifold-index model.

articles.title: PMR: MoE Routing with Shared Prototypes and Congestion Pricing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional linear routers in sparse mixture-of-experts models select experts directly from token-expert matching scores, coupling input matching with expert allocation. We propose Prototype-Mediated Routing (PMR), a two-stage router with shared prototypes. PMR first computes each token's distribution over prototypes, then uses it to mix prototype-conditioned expert distributions according to the law of total probability. This formulation models input matching and expert allocation separately, explicitly represents many-to-many associations between prototypes and experts, and provides separate interfaces for context adaptation and load regulation. Within this framework, short-term states summarize preceding tokens to adapt the prototypes, while congestion prices updated from dispatch feedback achieve loss-free load balancing by adjusting the conditional expert distributions. We use a two-pass blockwise approximation to accelerate short-term state processing, achieving over 20 times the training throughput of the eager tokenwise PMR implementation while maintaining high agreement in routing decisions. Across three pretraining configurations with 0.43B, 1.18B, and 0.48B total parameters, PMR improves mean zero-shot accuracy on seven benchmarks over linear routing baselines with matched expert architectures by 1.54, 2.65, and 1.45 percentage points (pp), respectively. The corresponding gains on ARC-Easy are 6.71, 5.80, and 3.92 pp. In parameter-efficient fine-tuning of 7B-8B backbones, PMR's improvements over MixLoRA vary across backbones, with gains of up to 1.76 pp in mean accuracy across four tasks.

articles.title: Behavioral Assurance for Socially Deployed AI Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.19564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, yet existing evaluations provide limited assurance that they behave consistently with their intended characteristics across diverse interactions. We introduce an evaluation framework for measuring the behavioral consistency of socially deployed AI agents. The framework operationalizes agent behavior along five measurable axes and uses a standardized evaluation battery spanning six socially salient interaction settings to assess behavioral differentiation, consistency, and drift. Controlled persona configurations serve as experimental anchors, enabling systematic testing of whether intended behavioral differences persist across contexts rather than appearing only as stylistic variation. Preliminary analyses demonstrate measurable differentiation across configurations and suggest associations between behavioral profiles and interaction outcomes. By shifting the focus from persona design to behavioral assurance, this work provides a foundation for evaluating whether socially deployed AI agents behave as intended, consistently and measurably, across the situations in which users encounter them.

articles.title: The Logic Chain Breaking Point: A Controlled-Variable Benchmark for Reasoning Degradation in Open-Weight Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce The Logic Chain Breaking Point, a controlled-variable benchmark for deductive reasoning in open-weight language models. It spans three phases: (i) pure modus-ponens chain scaling, (ii) distractor resilience with a fixed core chain, and (iii) contradiction detection under primacy versus recency placement. Independent variables follow a powers-of-two sequence v in 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128, with ground truth known by construction. We evaluate sixteen open-weight models across instruction-tuned and reasoning-tuned panels, including a small-model suite and a larger local-model extension. All models are evaluated with greedy decoding under model-appropriate context and output budgets, while context- and length-limited trials are quarantined from the valid accuracy denominator. Our results reveal a sharply non-monotonic difficulty surface: pure deductive chains up to L=128 remain near saturation for most models, and distractor noise causes only model-specific degradation at high D, while the inconsistent premise condition has the lowest accuracy. Instruction-tuned models, including larger 24B--27B baselines, score essentially zero on inconsistent premise sets, while reasoning-tuned models recover only partially and remain below reliable accuracy. Within this benchmark, inconsistent premise sets are associated with the strongest degradation under the benchmark's abstention-based scoring rule.

articles.title: EVIDENT: Evaluating Evidence Grounding in GUI Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI agents are increasingly evaluated by whether they complete web tasks, but surface success can hide a critical failure: the final answer may not be supported by evidence observed during navigation. We introduce EVIDENT, an evidence-driven benchmark for evaluating whether GUI agents ground their decisions in observable web evidence. EVIDENT contains 220 real-world English and Korean tasks spanning semantic grounding, contextual inference, and visual grounding, each paired with human-curated evidence metadata specifying what must be verified. We further separate surface task completion from evidence-grounded success using three metrics: TSR, ESR, and GSR, which respectively measure outcome success, required evidence observation, and claim-level evidence support. Experiments on commercial and open-source GUI agents reveal substantial gaps between surface success and evidence-grounded success, especially in contextual and visual tasks. These results show that current evaluations can overestimate agent reliability and highlight the need to assess not only whether agents answer, but whether they verify.

articles.title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory for Long-Horizon Task-Solving Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent that carries memory across tasks is only as good as the entries it keeps. We begin from an observation that is easy to reproduce and uncomfortable for the field: naively accumulating cross-task experience can make an agent emphworse than one with no memory at all. On AgentBoard, a workflow-induction memory solves fewer tasks than a memoryless ReAct agent in seven of eight domains, and a per-step procedural store with no surrounding structure loses half of ReAct's completions on Jericho. We argue that the missing ingredients are per-action credit assignment and an explicit life cycle for stored entries, and present AdMem, which supplies both. Before each action the actor commits to an expected outcome; a concurrently running critic scores the realized outcome against that expectation and writes a procedural entry carrying a binary reward and a reflection, so credit lands on the action that earned it and no environment reward is required. Each entry then carries a scalar utility, updated online under a noisy-OR reward model, that ranks retrieval jointly with context similarity and drives eviction and merging, giving the store a forgetting and consolidation policy instead of unbounded growth. Across 707 tasks in eight AgentBoard domains AdMem solves 441 against 388 for ReAct and 312 for the workflow-induction baseline --- a pooled gain significant under a two-sided Fisher exact test, concentrated in the domains that supply transferable cross-task structure. All memory stays human-readable text, which is what makes the failures above diagnosable --- and, as we discuss, also makes the store an auditable but attackable surface.

articles.title: Hivemind: A Federated Protocol for AI-Mediated Tacit Knowledge Sharing in Organisations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.20988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents Hivemind, a federated protocol that enables AI agents to exchange tacit knowledge on behalf of their users, asynchronously and without requiring any direct human interaction. Individual AI memory systems capture the decisions, reasoning, and contextual knowledge that surface during AI-assisted work. Hivemind creates the shared space in which this captured knowledge can flow between individuals across team and departmental boundaries, addressing a structural gap that neither centralised knowledge repositories nor existing AI tooling closes, even where partial solutions such as expert-finding systems exist. The paper evaluates centralised versus decentralised design approaches, proposes a federated architecture grounded in Nonaka and Takeuchi's (1995) Socialisation, Externalisation, Combination and Internalisation (SECI) model, and demonstrates a proof-of-concept implementation using Design Science Research (DSR) methodology. Measuring the enterprise benefit of federated tacit expertise sharing remains an open task for future work.

articles.title: VisualArtifactSpec 1.0: Evaluating Visual Artifacts under Task Specifications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual artifact tasks test agents' ability to translate task specifications and source materials into outputs that meet practical needs. Evaluation across artifact families helps distinguish broadly applicable authoring capabilities from strengths confined to a particular medium. We introduce VisualArtifactSpec 1.0 (VAS), a benchmark of 211 creation and modification tasks spanning presentations, static graphics, animations and videos, and web interfaces. Each task specifies authoring objectives, source materials, constraints, and deliverables. Existing benchmarks provide limited support for systematically evaluating how authoring choices suit different audiences, purposes, and media across artifact families. VAS evaluates two aspects separately: Task Fulfillment verifies explicit requirements and applicable functionality, while Artifact Performance assesses Content, Organization, Visuals, and Delivery. Task-specific rating anchors instantiate shared criteria for the intended audience, purpose, and medium, with judgments grounded in source materials and artifact inspection records. We evaluate nine model-harness configurations on all 211 tasks. Overall scores range from 42.12 to 70.52, with Artifact Performance accounting for 73.4% of the gap between the highest- and lowest-scoring configurations.

articles.title: Shaping AI's Beliefs Before It Generates: Human Sense of Agency in Creative AI
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems for creative media generation expand human capabilities yet risk diminishing human agency. A core problem is anchoring, where the user's thinking becomes anchored to a polished, generated artifact, shifting the user's role from active authoring to reactive editing. We propose pre-generation belief controls that can empower creators to inspect, revise, and steer the AI's interpretation before any media is generated, so that the initial anchor is set by the human. We formalize four design principles and instantiate them in the Proactive Co-Creator (PaCC), a system for early-stage conceptual ideation and prototyping that proactively surfaces its assumptions and uncertainty through clarifications, belief graphs, and media attributes, inviting users to shape the AI's beliefs before generating the final outcome. Using PaCC as a design probe in a small-scale, single-arm exploratory user study, we observed that participants reported directionally positive sense of agency and process control relative to their familiar prompt-based AI tools, noting that surfaced assumptions helped them think through details they had overlooked, whereas their feelings about ownership and authorship diverged

articles.title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When AI agents relay information to one another, an output can preserve an injected instruction's effect on downstream agents even after its wording changes, yet legitimate quotation and template reuse can produce high textual overlap with the source, so text-similarity guardrails that attempt to flag the former risk conflating these two cases. We test this distinction using DonkeyRail, a public classifier combining BLEU, ROUGE-L, and METEOR features, deployed in a controlled three-agent email relay, defining a behavioral measure in which an output counts as functional (the injected procedure induces fresh computations in two subsequent agents) independent of the detector's score, alongside legitimate controls that explicitly authorize quotation and reuse. At its default threshold the classifier misses 8 of 19 functional outputs while flagging 70 of 192 legitimate replies, with every completed quotation and template-reuse reply triggering a false alert; calibrating for low false positives on one template set does not transfer, as the recalibrated threshold detects only one functional output and still produces 15 false alerts on new templates. We also identify an operating-point error in all 21 published classifier configurations, where ROC interpolation replaces direct threshold application, and show formally that high AUC against a surface-level text criterion provides no distribution-free guarantee of high AUC against the behavioral target, while the existing evaluation labels lack the joint observations needed to estimate the gap. An authorization analysis further shows that identical visible transcripts can require different safety decisions depending on the governing policy, a distinction no observation-only classifier can resolve. These results argue for behavioral and policy-grounded evaluation over text-similarity guardrails.

articles.title: Swarm Shepherd: Securing Multi-Agent Ecosystems Against Persistent Latent Compromise
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic ecosystems are emerging as a new platform layer in which agents maintain persistent memory, retrieve from shared knowledge bases, execute through tool interfaces, and coordinate through shared states. These capabilities create a security problem that per-turn defenses miss: compromise can accumulate across sessions, agents, and system layers before visible failure. We define this threat as Agentic Sleeper, a system-level adversary that first behaves legitimately, gains routing trust, and later activates across memory, agent logic, and infrastructure. We formulate defense as inference under partial observability and propose Swarm Shepherd, a system-level defense framework centered on an inference filter for early warning, paired with a backward trace-back module for entry attribution. Our analysis yields a two-scale deployment rule that balances longer event histories against broader agent coverage. Across LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen, Agentic Sleeper drift begins 2.7--8.9× faster than natural baselines, propagates across agents on most topologies, and evades per-turn and stateful defenses above 80%. Swarm Shepherd warns at least three sessions before visible degradation (2.6 sessions when failure is scored by the benchmark's own task grader), while trace-back reaches 0.69 top-1 accuracy and 0.72 macro-F1 over 24 variants. The two-scale deployment rule is empirically confirmed, and in live end-to-end runs on LangGraph and AutoGen the posterior-guided defense stack drives cross-agent propagation below the self-sustaining regime, which removing only the visibly compromised agent does not achieve.

articles.title: KUDEX: A Zero-Shot Decompositional Framework for Logical Analysis in Natural Language
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at generating fluent text, they often struggle with multi-step logical reasoning with inferential connections among statements. We introduce KUDEX (Knowledge-Upward-Downward Reasoning Extension), a novel zero-shot, decompositional framework for analyzing and verifying logical relationships in natural language. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on surface-level entailment checks, KUDEX leverages LLMs to decompose reasoning into atomic primitives and constructs transparent reasoning graphs that serve both as execution traces and audit logs. Our framework includes a general prompt adaptation pipeline that adapts to diverse reasoning tasks without additional fine-tuning or domain-specific pipelines. Through comprehensive experiments on benchmarks across four domains, we demonstrate that KUDEX provides superior performance compared to existing methods, offering a more granular and robust framework for assessing logical relationships between statements.

articles.title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as recommenders in e-commerce and conversational shopping systems, where they select a product from a set of retrieved candidates described in natural language. Their decisions should depend on relevance to the user query, but may also be influenced by surface-level properties of the descriptions, such as their length. Detecting such structural biases is difficult because relevance labels are rarely available. We propose a label-free framework to audit LLM-based recommender systems for structural bias. Candidate descriptions are rewritten by randomly assigned paraphrasing models and presented in random order. We prove that, if the recommender's choice is invariant to these rewritings, every paraphraser is selected with equal probability, yielding a statistical test that requires no relevance labels. A four-step statistical pipeline tests this property and quantifies the contribution of each description feature while controlling for query-product relevance. We apply the framework to verbosity bias on 20,000 product queries and nine recommender LLMs from five model families. After controlling for the measured relevance signals, description length has a positive effect on selection in all nine models, increasing the odds of selection by up to 38% per standard deviation of length. Relevance remains the primary driver of recommendations, while verbosity acts as a consistent secondary signal whose strength depends on the model family. Since the framework needs only black-box access and no annotations, it can be run as a routine audit of deployed shopping assistants, and we provide an auditing protocol with cost and sample-size guidance.

articles.title: Infodynamic insights applied to effervescent sprays
articles.abstract: The characterization of effervescent atomizers, useful for atomizing viscous liquids , and that of sprays in general, often reduce droplet size distributions to mean diameters that cannot express the diversity and indeterminacy inherent to atomization. This study introduces an infodynamic characterization layer built on known information theory parameters, such as informature H I , differential informature H ∆ , and newly developed, as the Representation Index R (j). Infor-mature quantifies the amount of information carried by number-, area-, and volume-weighted droplet size distributions, but depends on the measurement alphabet (i.e., statistical classes). The differential informature proves essentially alphabet-independent, and is an intensive descriptor of the spray informational structure. The Representation Index quantifies the invariance between regular and variable size classes to locate the dominant information carried by droplets, among that of number, interfacial area, and liquid volume. R (j) depends on the resolution scale of the measurement technique, and its spread across these carriers reveals whether they reside at separated scales. Applied to Phase Doppler Interferometry measurements of an effervescent atomizer at several gas-to-liquid ratios (GLR), the framework uncovers an “info-hollow-cone” informational structure: differential informature peaks at the spray/ambient interface, locating the spray boundary from the droplet size distribution alone, while R (j) profiles resolve three radial regions and a progressive depletion of volume carriers from the spray axis as GLR increases, which follows the decrease of their geometric mean diameter below the reference scale of the measurement.

articles.title: Sol-Gel Synthesis of Nitrogen-Doped Titanium Dioxide (N-Tio2) Nanoparticles as a Nano-Fertilizer for Plant Growth in Agriculture
articles.abstract: Nitrogen-doped titanium dioxide (N-TiO2) nanoparticles were synthesised using the sol-gel method for sustainable agriculture as nano-fertilisers, which help plants to uptake soil nutrients. Pure TiO2 nanoparticles and nitrogen-doped TiO2 nanoparticles in different ratios (1:1 and 1:2) were synthesised. The structural, optical and morphological properties of nitrogen-doped TiO2 (N-TiO2) nanoparticles were investigated by X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV-vis Diffusion Reflectance Spectroscopy (UV-DRS), Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and Electron Dispersive X-Ray analysis (EDX). XRD peaks confirm the presence of anatase and brookite structures for the pure TiO2 and N-TiO2. The FT-IR analysis shows the presence of TiO2 in the respective vibration. The SEM studies were carried out to examine the cube-shaped morphological features of N-TiO2 nanoparticles. The purity of the sample and the atomic percentages of O (30.31) and Ti (69.69) were confirmed by compositional studies of EDAX analysis. The pH value and the total NPK availability were analysed for the pure and nitrogen-doped TiO2 nanoparticles in different ratios (1:1 and 1:2), and the morphological and biological growth of the plants were observed.

articles.title: Electrochemical Impedance Analysis on Hydrated 3YSZ and 8YSZ Nanopowders
articles.abstract: The effect of humidity on the electrical impedance of zirconia nanoparticles stabilized with two different yttria contents (3 mol% and 8 mol% Y2O3), both with a size distribution ranging from 7 to 10 nm, as confirmed by TEM (Transmission Electron Microscopy), was examined. Impedance measurements were performed after four different exposure times (4, 32, 54, and 70 minutes), maintaining a constant relative humidity of 100%. A combined model was developed that links the charge carrier transport mechanisms (proton conduction via Grotthuss and vehicular mechanisms) with an equivalent circuit representation of the impedance response. To monitor the evolution of the impedance response, an equivalent circuit was developed, incorporating bulk (high-frequency), grain boundary (intermediate-frequency), and diffusion (low-frequency) contributions. The results are consistent with the formation of a proton conduction pathway via these mechanisms in the physisorbed water layers for both 3YSZ and 8YSZ compositions. These results contribute to the understanding of humidity-induced proton conduction in YSZ nanopowders, establishing the basis for their application as humidity-activated gas sensors at room temperature (26 to 30°C).

articles.title: Influence of dipping heterogeneous layers and contact strength on dyke ascent: Observations from analogue models
articles.abstract: Magma intrusions approaching the surface commonly encounter dipping, mechanically heterogeneous layers in folded sequences, composite volcanoes and calderas, yet most models used to interpret volcano deformation assume a homogeneous or horizontally layered crust. In analogue dyke experiments, we injected water into two layers of elastic gelatine solid separated by a 45°-dipping interface, sing polarised light and particle image velocimetry to track the ascent dynamics. The stiffness ratio (EU/EL=0.4-2) of the gelatine, the contact strength (weak or strong) between layers, and the lateral offset between the injection point and the interface were varied. A penny-shaped dyke formed, and its geometry, ascent velocity and eruption location changed depending on whether, and at what depth, it intercepted the interface, and what the stiffness contrast was. Contact strength controlled whether the dyke crossed the interface or deflected along it. When interface interception occurred at depth, lateral growth almost stopped, the upper part of the dyke narrowed and ascent rate increased until eruption, independent of contact strength. Deflection occurred only where a weak contact was combined with an offset injection point, for stiffness ratios above and below unity, and caused the eruption site to be displaced laterally. Asymmetric stress and strain fields developed both around a vertical dyke beneath a dipping stiffness contrast, depending on which layer was stiffer, and around dykes deflected near a weak interface. As both configurations produced asymmetric surface displacement, we suggest an asymmetric deformation signal detected in nature may not by itself distinguish between them. Interception of a dipping contact could also appear as a late acceleration of precursory seismicity and deformation, which may be relevant to hazard assessment.

articles.title: Wave-to-water energy balance of an S-shaped buoy and ball-screw power take-off driving small-scale batch reverse osmosis
articles.abstract: Small wave energy converters can supply fresh water off the grid only if every link between the sea and the membrane is accounted for. This study couples a time-domain model of the S-shaped buoy SB-1.5 and its ball-screw power take-off (PTO), both experimentally verified in earlier work, with a batch seawater reverse osmosis (RO) model based on solution–diffusion transport, film-theory concentration polarisation, and Pitzer osmotic pressure. The PTO law is anchored to the published bench power and to a mean-to-peak ratio of 0.26 measured from the oscilloscope records, and the buoy follows the Cummins equation calibrated to the published 22 W full-scale absorbed power. In the ShiDao wave climate (2.0 kW/m), the unit absorbs 54.0 W (capture width ratio 1.83%), delivers 19.2 W of electricity and passes 7.3 W of hydraulic power to a 0.6 m² membrane element. With a batch cycle at 30% recovery, this gives about 142 L/day (51.7 m³/yr) at 0.83 g/L, whereas a fixed-pressure once-through module on the same chain gives 10.5 L/day. The hydraulic energy of 1.23 kWh/m³ is about 1.4 times the least work of separation, and the motor–pump set, at 48% stage efficiency, is the weakest link. Monte Carlo and Sobol analyses bound the output at 115–171 L/day (5–95%), with motor–pump efficiency alone explaining 58% of the variance. The simulation is calibrated to published bench tests and full-scale values, and sea trials are the next step. An unconstrained linear damper would absorb 2.6 times more power than the rating-limited PTO, and a 100 W generator raises the annual permeate from 51.7 to 79.6 m³. One unit provides 15 L/day per person for about nine people (volume only, before post-treatment), and eleven units cover a village of one hundred.

articles.title: Chloroform Occurrence and Drivers of Disinfection By-Product Formation in Drinking Water in the Tropical Andean Region: Evidence from Four Colombian Municipalities
articles.abstract: Chloroform (CF) is one of the most prevalent disinfection by-products (DBPs) generated during drinking water chlorination, yet field-based evidence about its occurrence in Colombian water supply systems (WSSs) remains limited. This study quantified CF concentrations and characterized their relationships with key water quality indicators for the first time in four Colombian municipalities: Montería, Cereté, Tunja, and Soracá. Drinking water samples were collected from six points within each WSS during the dry season. Field and laboratory measurements included turbidity (TB), pH, water temperature (WT), electrical conductivity (EC), free residual chlorine (Cl), ultraviolet absorbance at 254 nm (UV254), and CF concentration. TB remained below 1.0 NTU in all municipalities, indicating compliance with Colombian and international guideline values. Cl exhibited spatial variability and frequently fell below the Colombian recommended minimum of 0.3 mg L-1 in Tunja and Soracá. Mean CF concentrations from highest to lowest were Montería (54 ± 8.28 µg L-1) > Tunja (33 ± 6.62 µg L-1) > Soracá (31 ± 8.07 µg L-1) > Cereté (28 ± 8.31 µg L-1). Response surface and correlation analyses indicated that CF occurrence was modulated by municipality-specific combinations of WT, EC, Cl, and UV254, with WT and EC more relevant in Montería and Cereté and UV254 more influential in Tunja and Soracá. However, correlations were generally weak to moderate, indicating that CF formation was governed by the interaction of source water, treatment, and distribution system conditions rather than by a single predictor. These findings provide baseline evidence of CF occurrence in Colombian WSSs, and support routine DBP monitoring that integrates water quality, natural organic matter (NOM) reactivity, and WSS conditions.

articles.title: Small-scale mixing regulates the reconfiguration of the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone
articles.abstract: Oxygen minimum zones limit marine habitats and influence climate through carbon sequestration and greenhouse gas production. Studies suggest that long-term shifts in the balance between oxygen consumption and supply may “reconfigure” these regions across oxygen classes, with moderately oxygenated waters expanding while the most oxygen-depleted cores shrink. However, the mechanisms responsible for redistributing oxygen across classes remain unknown. Here we show, using high-resolution glider observations in the Arabian Sea, how distinct oxygen sources and small-scale mixing together act to shape the oxygen-class structure. Subsurface oxygen production at a deep chlorophyll maximum, mixed-layer deepening, and laterally advected Persian Gulf Water preferentially ventilate different oxygen classes, with seasonally varying contributions. Double-diffusive convection, a type of ocean mixing, accounts for > 70% of the estimated oxygen redistribution. Idealized diffusion experiments show that mixing alone can produce changes in oxygen-class structure comparable in magnitude to longer-term modeled and observed shifts, with the resulting distribution strongly dependent on how mixing is represented. Reliable projections of oxygen minimum zone reconfiguration require Earth system models to represent local oxygen sources and the spatial relationship between small-scale mixing and oxygen gradients.

articles.title: Conventional compliance masks heavy metal exceedances in a lead-acid battery effluent treatment plant
articles.abstract: Lead-acid battery manufacturing generates complex effluents, yet conventional compliance monitoring often fails to capture the full toxicological load. This study provides a critical assessment of a treatment facility in the Ishwardi Export Processing Zone,Pabna, Bangladesh, using a split-dataset approach. The first campaign (June and July 2025) utilized effluent-only grab samples to establish baseline compliance for conventional pollutants and lead. The second campaign (November 2025) utilized six paired influent-effluent events to calculate treatment performance and generate a comprehensive eleven-metal toxicity profile. The November paired data demonstrated effective physicochemical treatment, neutralizing highly alkaline influent (mean pH 9.68 to 7.97) and recovering dissolved oxygen (2.58 to 5.87 mg L⁻¹). However, total dissolved solids (TDS) removal was highly inconsistent, averaging only 22.8% (R² = 0.51). This indicates that November TDS compliance was an artifact of lower influent loading rather than stable treatment efficacy. Critically, this conventional compliance masked severe heavy metal exceedances. Seven metals complied with ECR 2023 limits: Pb (0.015 mg L⁻¹), Zn (3.423 mg L⁻¹), As (0.0345 mg L⁻¹), Cr (0.0085 mg L⁻¹), Mn (0.0131 mg L⁻¹), Ni (0.0231 mg L⁻¹), and Hg (0.0023 mg L⁻¹). In stark contrast, three metals failed: Cu (2.075 mg L⁻¹), Cd (0.14 mg L⁻¹), and Fe (2.3 mg L⁻¹) exceeded limits by 107%, 40%, and 15%, respectively. Furthermore, Sb was detected at 0.0746 mg L⁻¹, yet lacks a defined numerical limit. Because influent metals were not measured, true metal removal efficiency could not be quantified. The findings expose a critical regulatory blind spot: conventional treatment compliance does not guarantee protection from heavy metal toxicity. The facility currently relies on influent dilution to achieve regulatory compliance, leaving the ecosystem vulnerable to episodic toxic shocks. Future monitoring paradigms must mandate paired influent-effluent metal sampling to accurately assess treatment efficacy and protect downstream aquatic ecosystems. The findings directly contribute to SDG 6 (Clean Water) and SDG 3 (Good Health) by providing the evidence base needed to modernize discharge limits and protect the Padma River ecosystem from neurotoxic and carcinogenic metal loads.

articles.title: Molecular-scale tough adhesives based on the Lake–Thomas model
articles.abstract: High interfacial fracture resistance commonly relies on finite-thickness adhesive layers that dissipate energy through deformation, whereas molecularly thin interfaces provide little volume for such toughening. Here, we report a molecular-scale bonding strategy connecting opposing surfaces through covalently interlinked molecular bridges whose load-bearing backbone length is systematically controlled. Guided by the Lake–Thomas framework, we show that bridge backbone length controls interfacial fracture resistance through the fracture work of individual load-bearing connections. The optimized system reaches an interfacial fracture energy of approximately 500 J m⁻² with a sub-5-nm interphase for polyimide–polyimide bonding. Surface analysis and molecular-dynamics simulations support the primary role of backbone length while suggesting that surface-tethered chain organization modulates length-dependent toughening through bridge density. The strategy strengthens dissimilar interfaces and maintains interfacial reliability under environmental exposure. These results establish backbone length as a design parameter for tough molecularly thin interfaces, providing a route to mechanically robust heterogeneous integration.

articles.title: Soliton Dynamics and Stability Analysis in Fractional Modified Kawahara and Landau- Ginzburg-Higgs Models
articles.abstract: In this study, the nonlinear time-fractional modified Kawahara and the space-time fractional Landau-Ginzburg-Higgs models are investigated to explore nonlinear wave propagation in shallow water and higher-order dispersive media with memory effects, as well as nonlocal phase-transition dynamics in superconductors and wave phenomena in plasmas. To transform the governing equations into ordinary differential equations, the appropriate fractional wave transformation called beta-derivative is implemented. By employing the new generalized (:left(Gprⁱme:/Gright))-expansion method, a broad class of exact analytical solutions is effectively formulated. This procedure yields three separate solution types: hyperbolic, trigonometric, and rational forms. Therefore, a variety of physically relevant wave shapes are derived, including kink, anti-kink, singular soliton, singular periodic, bell-shape, compacton, W-shape, flat parabolic, parabolic, and other types of wave profiles. Additionally, stability analysis is conducted to examine the persistence of the solution. Symbolic calculations and mathematical analysis have been done by Wolfram Mathematica software. The results show that the suggested method is efficient, reliable, and competent for generating a wide variety of intricate nonlinear wave shapes. Overall, the obtained solutions are essential for comprehending nonlinear wave propagation and the dynamics of complex phenomena in the fields of science and engineering.

articles.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.21397v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from -155;dBm to -130;dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from -95;dBm to -55;dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of 6.0;GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of (74.7± 0.2) ;dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of (75.4± 6.8) ;dB. The larger uncertainty of the dispersively coupled qubit measurements indicates that these qubits are less reliable for power sensing than the directly coupled qubits, most likely, due to the additional coupling resonator, whose transfer function is difficult to estimate accurately. Our results constitute the first step towards validation of qubit power sensing in dilution fridges, leading towards traceability for cryogenic microwave measurements.

articles.title: Effect of Mangosteen Peel (Garcinia mangostana L.) and Grass Jelly Leaf (Cyclea barbata L. Miers) Natural Dye Mixing Ratio on the Optical, Morphological, and Photovoltaic Properties of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSC)
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.26622v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) are promising low-cost and environmentally friendly photovoltaic devices. This study explores the effect of the mixing ratio of natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL) on the optical, chemical, morphological, and photovoltaic properties of DSSCs. Dye solutions were prepared from crude extracts at a fixed concentration of 0.6 g/mL, with MP:GJL volume ratios varied from 3:1 to 1:3. UV-Vis absorption spectra showed that MP contributes to the UV-blue region (350-450 nm) and GJL to the red region (600-700 nm), giving the mixtures a broader, more panchromatic absorption. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra confirmed that both extracts share hydroxyl (-OH) and carbonyl/carboxyl (C=O, C-O) groups capable of anchoring the pigments onto TiO₂, with a stronger glycosidic C-O-C band for MP. Optical and FESEM imaging revealed that balanced and GJL-rich mixtures form more uniform, crack-free films than single dyes. Current-voltage (J-V) measurements of three independently fabricated cells per composition (n=3) under identical white-light illumination showed that the 1:3 (MP:GJL) ratio gave the highest apparent power conversion efficiency, about 1.3 and 1.7 times that of the single MP and GJL dyes, respectively. Because the input power was estimated photometrically (lux) rather than with a calibrated AM1.5G source, these efficiencies are apparent (relative) indicators for comparing samples, not absolute values. The improvement is attributed to the complementary absorption of the two pigments, while direct electrochemical confirmation of the charge-transfer mechanism remains for future work.

articles.title: Monte Carlo Sampling for Wave Functions Requiring (Anti)Symmetrization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.20577v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many strongly correlated states, such as those arising in the fractional quantum Hall effect and spin liquids, are described by wave functions obtained by dividing particles into multiple clusters, constructing a readily evaluable wave function in each cluster, and (anti)symmetrizing across these clusters. We introduce a method to compute quantities such as energies and correlators, using Monte Carlo simulations for these states. Our framework overcomes the factorial scaling of explicit (anti)symmetrization, allowing for studies of systems beyond the reach of exact diagonalization.

articles.title: Towards superior van der Waals density functionals for molecular crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.20738v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ubiquitous van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a subtle yet crucial role in determining the precise atomic arrangements in solids, particularly in molecular crystals where these weak forces are the primary link between constituent building blocks. Within density functional (DF) theory, the most natural approach to address them is the use of vdW-inclusive density functionals. Through a detailed analysis of the underlying formalism, we have developed a computational scheme that combines vdW functionals of type DF1 and DF2 providing a readily tunable framework to improve the theoretical description and prediction of molecular crystals and other sparse materials. The proof of principle is demonstrated by benchmarking our method on the X23 dataset of molecular crystals.

articles.title: Electronic structure, phase stability, and transport properties of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy: A computational study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.16528v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the thermodynamics and phase stability of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy using a combination of ab initio electronic structure calculations, a concentration wave analysis, and atomistic Monte Carlo simulations. In alignment both with experimental data and with results obtained using other computational approaches, we predict a B2 (CsCl) chemical ordering emerging in this alloy at comparatively high temperatures, which is driven by Al and Ti moving to separate sublattices, while V and Cr express weaker site preferences. The impact of this B2 chemical ordering on the electronic transport properties of the alloy is investigated within a Kubo--Greenwood linear response framework and it is found that, counter-intuitively, the alloy's residual resistivity increases as the material transitions from the A2 (disordered bcc) phase to our predicted B2 (partially) ordered structure. Our results give fresh insight into the atomic-scale structure and consequent physical properties of this well-studied, technologically relevant material.

articles.title: Time-resolved observation of conversion of spin and orbital currents to charge currents in spintronic and orbitronic terahertz radiation emitters
articles.abstract: Author(s): Basem Y. Shahriar and Abdulhakem Y. Elezzabi Spintronic and orbitronic emitters are promising tabletop sources of pulsed, ultrabroadband terahertz radiation. Due to their ultrathin nature and compatibility with various materials, they are prime candidates for on-chip integration with preexisting material platforms. However, certain properties of these emitters, such as the femtosecond-scale onset time from the moment of laser excitation to emission, still need to be studied. This Letter presents a simple method to do so, and demonstrates how the choice of material has a surprisingly significant impact on switching time, potentially due to differences in excited-carrier population between spin and orbital angular momenta. articles.title: Ab initio reaction pathways and nonadiabatic cycloreversion dynamics in 2-styrylthiophene
articles.abstract: We report a combined electronic-structure and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics investigation of the excited-state nonradiative decay processes in 2-styrylthiophene (2-STTP). The ground and excited state conformational landscapes were characterized at second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation and the algebraic diagrammatic construction to second-order [ADC(2)] levels with the aug-cc-pVDZ basis set. To identify the key relaxation channels governing ultrafast deactivation, minimum-energy conical intersections between the S 1 and S 0 states were optimized at the complete active space self-consistent field level. Twisted-pyramidalized and cyclized-like MECIs relevant to photoisomerization and photocyclization are located and analyzed. The connectivity between conformers and MECIs was further explored using geodesic interpolation reaction paths, which reveal that isomerization channels originating from cis conformers are more favorable than those from trans conformers, and the cyclized MECIs can be accessed with comparatively small or even barrierless energy profiles. To complement these static insights, trajectory-based ab initio molecular dynamics simulations were carried out to study the cycloreversion reaction for CYC1 . The dynamical results demonstrate rapid internal conversion within 100 fs and highlight a strong competition between reactive and nonreactive decay pathways, leading either to open-ring photoproduct formation or recovery of the initial reactant structure. Overall, the combined approach provides a comprehensive mechanistic picture of the excited-state behavior, emphasizing the decisive role of conical intersection accessibility and excited-state potential energy surface topology in controlling photophysical and photochemical outcomes.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Resonance formation patterns of conserved fragments in dissociative electron attachment to diethyl disulfide and 2-hydroxyethyl disulfide
articles.abstract: To elucidate how substituent identity modulates fragmentation induced by dissociative electron attachment (DEA) to symmetric disulfides, DEA was performed on gas-phase diethyl disulfide (DEDS) and 2-hydroxyethyl disulfide (2-HEDS). Anionic fragments resulting from these processes were detected by quadrupole mass spectrometry, and ion yields of those fragments as a function of incident electron energy were rendered. Our study demonstrated that both systems yielded the principal anionic fragment classes reported across prior DEA studies of symmetric disulfides—S − , (R–S) − , (R–S minus H) − , and (R–S–S) − , where R denotes the substituent branches affixed to the central disulfide bond, i.e., C 2 H 5 for DEDS and HOCH 2 CH 2 for 2-HEDS. This conserved fragmentation pattern suggests that the dominant DEA pathways proceed primarily through S–S and S–C bond cleavage, with certain channels additionally involving cleavage of hydrogen-containing bonds. We employed density functional theory and composite wavefunction methods to compute thermodynamic threshold energies for potential dissociation channels, including those for the dehydrogenated and disulfide-sparing anions. Although DEDS and 2-HEDS yielded analogous fragment classes, their corresponding ion-yield profiles were distinct: the number, relative intensity, and energetic positions of resonance peaks differed between the two molecules. Thus, our findings indicate that the resonance features governing DEA to disulfides exhibit strong substituent dependence.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Calculation of interfacial tensions between solid, liquid, and vapor phases in metals by molecular simulations
articles.abstract: The interfacial free energy is a key determinant of material behavior, governing phenomena such as wetting, adhesion, nucleation, and phase coexistence. Despite its importance, experimental measurements remain challenging, particularly for liquid metals and solid–liquid interfaces under extreme conditions. Classical molecular dynamics (CMD) provides a versatile alternative, enabling atomistic evaluation of interfacial properties beyond experimental reach. In this work, we systematically compute solid–vapor, solid–liquid, and liquid–vapor interfacial free energies across multiple metals, applying and comparing established atomistic methods, including both the mechanical and thermodynamic routes, free energy perturbation, and thermodynamic integration. This unified framework allows cross-validation between methods and interfaces, revealing consistent trends and highlighting the influence of interatomic potentials on accuracy. Our results demonstrate the robustness of CMD for interfacial predictions and emphasize the importance of careful potential validation. These findings provide a coherent picture of metallic interfacial thermodynamics, with implications for mesoscale modeling, materials design, and high-temperature applications.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: A multiscale description of electrical double layers in alkaline hydrogen evolution: From continuum theory to molecular dynamics
articles.abstract: A molecular-level understanding of electrical double-layer (EDL) structure is essential for establishing a physically realistic description of electrochemical interfaces. In this work, we develop an experiment-informed continuum-atomistic framework that integrates experimentally derived hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) kinetics, Poisson–Nernst–Planck (PNP) transport modeling, and atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate interfacial structure evolution under alkaline HER conditions. Unlike many continuum EDL models in which electrostatic boundary conditions are specified independently of interfacial reaction kinetics, the present framework incorporates experimentally extracted HER kinetic parameters through reaction-derived ion-flux boundary conditions, establishing a direct connection between electrochemical kinetics and interfacial ion transport, electrostatic potential, and electric-field distributions. Quantitative comparisons among classical PNP, sterically modified PNP, and MD simulations reveal the progressive influence of finite ion size and molecular-scale hydration on interfacial ion redistribution. While modified PNP recovers physically bounded ion concentrations and improves continuum predictions, they remain unable to capture the nonmonotonic ion distributions and molecular-scale solvent organization resolved by MD simulations. Atomistic simulations further reveal hydration-dependent ion positioning and pronounced water layering near the electrode surface, defining a reaction-relevant interfacial region where molecular effects become dominant. These results quantify the applicability and limitations of continuum descriptions under alkaline HER conditions and provide a framework for connecting electrochemical kinetics with molecular-scale interfacial structures across different length scales.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Conservative phase-field modeling of fully Eulerian fluid--structure interaction
articles.abstract: We present a fully Eulerian, one-domain method for fluid--structure interaction (FSI) between incompressible fluids and hyperelastic solids, in which the solid indicator is transported by a conservative phase-field equation of Allen--Cahn type. Solid deformation is described by an Eulerian left Cauchy--Green tensor whose phase-weighted elastic stress enters a single momentum balance. Because the interface transport is written in flux form on a staggered Cartesian grid, the phase integral is conserved to machine precision and different regularization strategies can be exchanged without modifying the mechanical solver. The method thus adds conservative phase-field transport to the volume-of-fluid, level-set, reference-map and Cahn--Hilliard formulations available for fully Eulerian FSI. We instantiate it with three regularizations (CDI, ACDI and UWCDI) and assess them on two benchmarks. For a deformable disk in a lid-driven cavity, all variants reproduce the reference centroid path under grid refinement while differing in contour regularity and effective interface width. For a wall-supported filament under Kolmogorov forcing, severe bending creates narrow connections whose discrete topology depends on the regularization and, for CDI, strongly on resolution. Global observables are therefore robust to the choice of interface flux, whereas the geometry and connectivity of near-grid-scale features are not, with direct implications for FSI in strongly forced and turbulent flows.

articles.title: FLC genomic occupancy as a biological benchmark for plant ChIP-seq: a complete workflow from crosslinking to motif validation
articles.abstract: Background Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) is widely used to identify genomic regions associated with a protein of interest, including transcription factors and other chromatin-associated proteins. However, the reliability of ChIP-seq experiments is questionable, because they often do not recover expected transcription factor-DNA binding sites. A robust workflow is essential for reliably detecting protein-associated genomic regions, particularly in plant tissues.Results Here we present a complete and robust plant ChIP-seq workflow from tissue harvest to annotated peaks, generating high signal-to-noise ratio, developed for approximately 2–3 g of 7-day-old Arabidopsis thaliana seedlings expressing a tagged protein of interest. The wet-lab procedure comprises formaldehyde crosslinking under vacuum infiltration, isolation of nuclei, detergent-assisted chromatin extraction, sonication, and affinity enrichment using RFP-Trap Magnetic Agarose beads. A particularly critical, yet often overlooked, parameter for achieving a reproducible high signal-to-noise ratio is the optimization of the balance between the amount of input chromatin containing the tagged protein and the volume of affinity beads used for immunoprecipitation. Then, affinity enrichment is followed by stringent sequential washing, reversal of crosslinks and column-based purification of ChIP DNA, with input chromatin and mock IP samples processed in parallel as controls. Purified DNA is converted into dual-indexed Illumina libraries using the TruSeq DNA Nano kit, quantified by qPCR and sequenced in paired-end mode (2×151 bp) on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus. Reads are then quality-trimmed with fastp, aligned to the TAIR10 reference genome with Bowtie2, and peaks are called against matched input controls with MACS3 and annotated with ChIPseeker (https://github.com/mhajheidari/FLC-ChIP-seq-analysis). We benchmarked the workflow using the Arabidopsis MADS-box transcription factor FLOWERING LOCUS C (FLC), for which the workflow identified 1183 reproducible peaks called in all four biological replicates, narrowing to 957 peaks after mock IP-based specificity filtering. We identified peaks located at or near all previously reported FLC direct target genes, as well as at several additional developmentally important genes not previously reported as potential FLC targets, including the FLC locus itself. De novo motif discovery and central-enrichment analysis (CentriMo) confirmed strong, significant enrichment of the known FLC binding motif at the called peaks (E = 3.1×10⁻⁴⁰), matching the published FLC position weight matrix (TOMTOM E = 1.3×10⁻²³).Conclusions The protocol provides detailed buffer formulations, incubation conditions, computational parameters, and practical handling recommendations, and can be readily adapted to different plant lines expressing the tagged protein of interest. The FLC motif benchmark demonstrates the robustness of the workflow and its ability to reliably capture biologically relevant and specific transcription factor-DNA interactions, addressing a key challenge in approaches for identifying protein-DNA interactions, including ChIP-seq. Overall, this workflow provides a practical and reproducible framework for conducting and validating ChIP-seq experiments in plants.

articles.title: Hybrid dynamical simulation reveals apparent stiffening of flexible protein lattices driving membrane bending
articles.abstract: Membrane-deforming protein lattices play a central role in essential and pathogenic remodeling processes, including clathrin-mediated endocytosis and viral budding. Simulating these systems at biologically relevant length and time scales requires mesoscale approaches that preserve structural detail while avoiding the computational cost of atomistic resolution. Here, we present a hybrid simulation framework that couples a particle-based flexible protein lattice to a continuum membrane model, enabling systematic investigation of how lattice geometry and rigidity influence dynamic membrane remodeling. We validate the coupled model by comparing simulation results with theoretical predictions for membranes under increasing tension. Using buckling-based deformations of pre-assembled clathrin lattices, we quantify the lattice flexural rigidity and establish a direct relationship between the force constants in the coarse-grained energy function and the emergent lattice mechanics. We then compare this flexural rigidity, κ l ,flex , with an effective rigidity, κ l ,eff , commonly used in continuum descriptions of sphere-forming protein assemblies. Although κ l ,flex is set solely by the energy function, κ l ,eff depends on lattice size and connectivity, with the two measures converging only for weakly connected lattices. As a result, with lattice growth, the effective rigidity relevant for spherical bud formation increases and the relaxation timescale decreases. This size-dependent stiffening highlights the importance of structural details in interpreting lattice mechanics and cautions against assuming a single constant stiffness. We further demonstrate the generality of the method by applying it to pre-assembled viral lattices generated with reaction–diffusion simulations. Overall, this work provides a validated framework for simulating how deformable protein assemblies of diverse geometry couple to membrane dynamics and remodeling.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Post-relaxation ring-opening dynamics of 1,3-cyclohexadiene following 1 1 B-state excitation revealed by time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Photoinduced electrocyclic ring opening of 1,3-cyclohexadiene (CHD) has long served as a benchmark reaction for nonadiabatic molecular dynamics. Although the prompt formation of 1,3,5-hexatriene (HT) through excited-state relaxation at conical intersections is well established, the subsequent fate of CHD molecules that return to the electronic ground state without immediate bond cleavage remains less directly characterized. Here, we report time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopic evidence for post-relaxation ring-opening dynamics of vibrationally hot ground-state CHD following 1 1 B-state excitation. Using high-harmonic-generation-based extreme-ultraviolet time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy, supported by molecular-orbital analysis based on ground-state density functional theory, we resolve two temporally distinct stages in the evolution of HT-associated spectral features: a prompt component within ∼200 fs and a delayed component appearing between ∼700 and 1100 fs. This two-stage assignment is supported by correlated transient changes in the highest occupied molecular orbital region and a deeper valence region sensitive to the C–C bonding framework. These changes provide orbital-sensitive signatures of CHD depletion and HT formation. The prompt component corresponds to the established photochemical ring-opening pathway, whereas the delayed component is attributed to secondary ring opening of vibrationally hot ground-state CHD produced by internal conversion without immediate bond cleavage. Harmonic microcanonical Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus calculations indicate that statistical ground-state ring opening is too slow to account for the delayed component, suggesting a role for nonequilibrium nuclear motion following internal conversion. These results provide evidence that product formation in this benchmark electrocyclic reaction is not limited to the initial nonadiabatic relaxation pathway but can continue through nonequilibrium structural dynamics on the electronic ground-state surface.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: The fluid-lattice gas isomorphism with application to liquid–vapor equilibrium in physisorbed monolayers
articles.abstract: Liquid–gas equilibrium is described using a pair of Ising-like thermodynamic variables. The first is a combination of density and energy fields that is even under phase coexistence, derived from the Gibbs–Duhem and Clausius–Clapeyron relations. The second is the normalized density deviation M = ρ / ρ d − 1, which distinguishes the coexisting phases and serves as an odd ordering variable. Combining these variables with the empirical linearities of the binodal diameter and the Zeno line leads to a projective mapping between continuum-fluid and lattice-gas states. The implications of such mapping are tested against coexistence-density and saturation pressure data for the two-dimensional Lennard-Jones fluid, as well as physisorbed molecular monolayers of simple molecular fluids like argon and methane. Finally, a heuristic microscopic interaction-variable formulation that motivates continuous fluids vs lattice model description is also discussed.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Simulating catalytic resonance with molecular dynamics
articles.abstract: Static heterogeneous catalysts are constrained by the Sabatier principle, where their overall turnover is limited by balancing the kinetics of reactant binding, surface reaction, and product unbinding. Modulating the surface binding energies between a strong binding state and a weak binding state can overcome this limit. For such a dynamic catalyst, a maximum turnover is achieved at a catalytic resonance modulating frequency. Here, we demonstrate that classical molecular simulation approaches can be used to study this phenomenon. Our method introduces a generic classical model for a surface reaction with time-dependent surface binding energy. Using a non-equilibrium molecular simulation in which reactants tend to be added to the system and products tend to be removed, we can simulate many catalyst cycles. Our approach reproduces catalytic resonance, with the dynamic catalyst providing up to a three-order-of-magnitude boost in turnover compared to the static catalyst. We further demonstrate the presence of a second resonant frequency in the gas phase, associated with resonance of the reacting bond. The general approach outlined here can be extended to more detailed models and used to study the molecular-scale effects of surface modulation and to computationally test input frequency, amplitude, and waveform for programmable catalysts.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Effect of Liquid Metal Velocity during Low-Pressure Casting on the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Al12Si Alloy
articles.abstract: In this study, low-pressure die casting (LPDC) of the Al12Si (LM6) alloy was experimentally fabricated. For the Al12Si alloy, the velocity of the liquid metal in the gate cross sectional area was selected as 0.25, 0.50, and 1.00 m/s. To ensure the liquid metal's velocity, the metal was injected into the mould cavity using the required Argon gas, in accordance with Bernoulli's principle. Microstructural investigations and mechanical properties of an Al12Si alloy at different liquid metal velocities were evaluated. Microstructural analyses were performed using optical microscopy (OM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Tensile and hardness tests were applied as mechanical tests. In microstructural examinations, it was determined that Al dendrites morphologically changed from linear-colonial to star-shaped as the liquid metal velocity increased. In addition, it has been determined that, during the solidification process under pressure, the liquid metal velocity and the Al-Si eutectic yield finer grains and a decrease in porosity. According to the density test results, the highest density was 2,465 g/cm³ at a liquid metal velocity at the gate of 0.5 m/s, and the lowest was 2,324 g/cm³ at a liquid metal velocity at the gate of 0.25 m/s. The change in hardness values could not be determined. According to the average tensile test results, the highest tensile strength was obtained at a liquid metal velocity at the gate of 0.5 m/s, 143 MPa (4.47% elongation), and the lowest tensile strength was obtained at a liquid metal velocity at the gate of 0.25 m/s, 125 MPa (3.48% elongation).

articles.title: Streamlining V-T Flash: A Simple, Robust and Reliable Algorithm Built on PT-Flash
articles.abstract: Volume-Temperature equilibrium calculations (VT-Flash) are essential for simulating confined fluids in reservoir grid-blocks, rigid vessels, and separators. This work presents an approach, robust VT-Flash algorithm that enhances the efficiency and reliability of the indirect PT-Flash method. Two modifications are introduced: first, a nested stability analysis loop provides reliable initial equilibrium constants (k-values) before the equilibrium calculation, overcoming the limitations of Wilson’s correlation at high temperatures. Second, three numerical manners (Bisection, Levenberg-Marquardt Algorithm (LMA), and Trust-Region Quasi‑Newton (TRQN) methods) are employed to solve the molar volume objective function with improved convergence speed. The results are compared with constant composition expansion (CCE) test data for a synthetic gas condensate and a live oil, yielding R2 values of 0.926 and 0.983, respectively, and cross-validated with the Helmholtz free energy minimization approach, showing very good agreement (R2> 0.9999). Comparative analysis demonstrates that all three proposed mathematical methods reduce the number of iterations and elapsed time by up to 70% and 92% relative to the reference method, introduced by Cisomandi et al. [1], while maintaining almost constant iterations across a wide temperature range, also in high temperatures. The approach produces smooth, physically consistent isochoric lines, phase envelopes, and three‑dimensional pressure-temperature-volume surfaces. The Bisection method offers the lowest computational cost but requires a predefined operational pressure range; LMA and TRQN eliminate this need by initializing it with the ideal gas law. The proposed framework thus provides a simple, accurate, and robust PT‑based VT‑Flash tool suitable for diverse fluid systems and operating conditions.

articles.title: Experimental Study and Response Surface Modeling of the Combined Effects of the Process Parameters on the Thermal and Mechanical Properties of Friction Stir Welded 3003 Aluminum Alloy
articles.abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) of AA3003 aluminum alloy is governed by the tool rotational speed (𝑁), feed rate (𝑆), and tilt angle (𝜃). Earlier studies on this alloy have used these parameters to model either the tensile properties or the welding temperature, but these responses have rarely been analyzed together with the hardness of the weld zones. In this study, a three-level full factorial design and response surface methodology (RSM) were used to model four responses: the ultimate tensile strength (𝜎U), the maximum temperature (Tmax) recorded 10 mm from the weld centerline, and the hardness of the nugget zone (NZ) and the heat-affected zone (HAZ). Within the tested ranges, the tilt angle had the largest effect on Tmax, whereas the rotational speed had the largest effect on NZ hardness and 𝜎U. Increasing 𝑁 or 𝜃 raised Tmax and lowered the hardness of both zones, while 𝜎U increased with 𝑁 and varied nonlinearly with 𝑆, with a minimum near the intermediate feed rate. A multi-response optimization that maximized 𝜎U and hardness gave 𝑁 = 1000 rpm, 𝑆 = 400 mm/min, and 𝜃 = 0.5°. At this setting, the predicted 𝜎U and the NZ and HAZ hardness reached about 77%, 89%, and 80% of the base metal values, respectively. Eight independent validation tests gave coefficients of determination (R²) between 0.818 and 0.919. The models describe the parameter effects within the tested domain and can support the selection of welding conditions for AA3003 joints.

articles.title: Effect of Recycled Concrete Aggregate on the Elastic Modulus of Concrete at Different Replacement Ratios
articles.abstract: This study investigates the effect of recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) on the mechanical properties of concrete, with particular emphasis on the modulus of elasticity (Ec), at replacement levels of R25, R50, R75, and R100, compared with a reference concrete mixture containing natural aggregate (R0). An experimental and analytical investigation was conducted using cylindrical specimens measuring 150 × 300 mm, in which the modulus of elasticity, Poisson’s ratio, splitting tensile strength, and compressive strength were evaluated at different curing ages. The tests were complemented by a nonlinear finite element model of the cylinders in ABAQUS (concrete damaged plasticity) and by a statistical analysis of the compressive strength results (one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s HSD post hoc test). The experimental results demonstrated that the use of recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) resulted in a progressive reduction in the cylindrical compressive strength of concrete as the replacement level increased. At the ages of 7, 28, and 120 days, the reductions in compressive strength for the R25, R50, R75, and R100 mixtures ranged from 6.96–20.50%, 6.51–17.11%, and 3.80–18.40%, respectively, compared with the reference concrete containing natural aggregate (R0). ANOVA showed that the replacement level had a significant effect on compressive strength at 7 and 28 days (p < 0.001); the 25% replacement did not differ significantly from the reference concrete, significant reductions appeared from 50% replacement, and R75 and R100 were not significantly different from each other. Increasing the proportion of RCA at the investigated replacement levels resulted in a 10–27% reduction in the modulus of elasticity of concrete (Ec), a 5–7% increase in Poisson’s ratio, and a 15–26% reduction in splitting tensile strength, compared with the reference concrete (R0). The numerical model reproduced the increase in axial strain with increasing replacement, and its splitting tensile strengths were 5–16% higher than the experimental values. An empirical equation based on the ACI 318 relationship, with reduction factors for the compressive strength ratio and the unit weight, was proposed to estimate the modulus of elasticity (Ec) of concrete containing RCA. It reproduced the measured moduli with differences between − 3.6% and + 2.5%, and for 9 of the 11 data points from previous studies the predictions were within ± 15% of the reported values.

articles.title: Experimental Investigation of Sodium Citrate Assisted Electrolyte in Electrochemical Machining of AISI 304 Stainless Steel
articles.abstract: This study experimentally explores the influence of adding sodium citrate (Na3Cit) to a sodium nitrate (NaNO3) electrolyte in electrochemical machining (ECM) of AISI 304 stainless steel when using a palladium-coated tool electrode. The machining voltage, duty cycle, and electrolyte concentration were adjusted, while the machining rate (MR) and overcut (OC) were assessed. Raising the voltage from 6 to 11 V increased the MR from 0.20 to 0.42 µm/ s for NaNO3; however, NaNO3 + Na3Cit reached 0.52 µm/ s at 11 V, which is about 24% higher. Within the same range, OC dropped from 343 to 221 µm for NaNO3 and from 302 to 204 µm for the mixed electrolyte. At a 90% duty cycle, the NaNO3 + Na3Cit mixture achieved an MR of 0.35 µm/s, compared to 0.30 µm/s for NaNO3 alone; meanwhile, OC dropped to 220 and 240 µm, respectively. At an electrolyte concentration of 0.41 mol/L, the MR was 0.46 µm/ s for the mixed electrolyte and 0.44 µm/ s for NaNO3, with corresponding OC values of 210 and 230 µm. SEM observations showed cleaner, nearly circular holes with less sludge and sharper edge definition when using NaNO3 + Na3Cit. The results show that citrate-enhanced electrolyte boosts MR, dimensional accuracy, and electrochemical stability by enhancing complexation, optimizing current distribution, facilitating removal of reaction products, and better localizing anodic dissolution.

articles.title: Reusable operators for irreducible Cartesian tensor decomposition and coupling
articles.abstract: Molecular and material properties, from the polarizability to the elastic constants, are described by tensors. Their behavior under rotations is made explicit when a tensor is decomposed into irreducible parts that transform independently. In Cartesian form, these parts are the symmetric and traceless irreducible Cartesian tensors (ICTs), whose decomposition and coupling underlie selection rules, orientational averages, and the use of symmetry. The decomposition is a textbook result at rank two, but higher rank and the intrinsic symmetry of physical tensors make it nontrivial. What has been lacking, unlike in the well-established spherical formalism, is a general construction for a given intrinsic symmetry, together with reusable operators that extract the ICTs and rebuild the original tensor exactly. Here, we develop such a construction and obtain these operators explicitly. These operators depend on rank and symmetry alone, and therefore, each need only be built once and then applied to any tensor of that class. Building on them, we further obtain the Cartesian harmonics of a vector and the operators that couple two ICTs into a third, both central to equivariant machine learning. The construction is demonstrated on the elastic tensor, in both its second-order form of rank four and its third-order form of rank six. The ICTs of the rank-4 tensor also define a rotation- and scale-invariant measure of anisotropy, which we evaluate across the first-principles elastic tensors of crystalline materials from the Materials Project. The construction is implemented in the open-source package natto, which produces the operators in both exact symbolic and numerical form.

articles.abstract: Author(s): Iryna Knysh, Anton Charkin-Gorbulin, Claudio Quarti, David Beljonne, Igor Poltavsky, and Alexandre Tkatchenko Can a machine learning model trained on surface slabs accurately describe bulk phase transitions? The authors show that the choice between pairwise and beyond-pairwise dispersion treatments significantly affects the predicted phase transitions. The authors attribute these differences to the strong sensitivity of Cs and I atomic forces to the treatment of van der Waals dispersion. Their findings highlight the potential of surface-trained machine learning models for transferable atomistic simulations and the crucial role of dispersion interactions in perovskite dynamics. [Phys.
