By separately resolving the two circularly polarized components, rather than relying solely on the total SHG intensity, we extract the degree of polarization as a direct optical indicator of defect-induced valley depolarization. The measured response tracks the structural, optical, chemical, and electronic evolution of plasma-induced defects revealed by complementary characterization and distinguishes subtle defect variations that are not readily resolved by conventional optical techniques. The method is non-destructive, ultrahigh sensitivity, operable at room temperature, compatible with rapid large-area mapping, and potentially suitable for real-time quality monitoring and scalable defect engineering in 2D materials.

articles.title: Structural Context Collapse in Deep-Learning Predictors: A Benchmark of Outer Membrane Protein Loop Decontextualization and a Backbone-Centric Filter for Surface Epitope Identification
articles.abstract: Deep-learning structure predictors (AlphaFold2, ESMFold) require global context. Modeling outer membrane protein (OMP) loops without transmembrane scaffolds creates an out-of-distribution challenge. Across 28 non-redundant OMP crystal structures (1.40–3.10 Å), isolated loops collapsed, inverting core solvent accessibility (native core RSA: 3.6 ± 0.7% inverted to 58.7 ± 4.5% [AF2] and 62.1 ± 4.8% [ESMFold] for buried positions; mean loop RSA: 32.1 ± 10.0%), yielding 0.00% true negative rate (0/28 retaining core burial; 95% Clopper–Pearson CI: [0.00%, 10.15%]) across RSA thresholds 5%–20%. Intact models preserved burial (AF2: 27/28 [96.43%], residue TNR 96.89% ± 5.6%; ESMFold: 26/28 [92.86%], residue TNR 93.21% ± 4.2%). Mean pLDDT fell from 83.0 ± 5.1 to 66.9 ± 4.8, correlating with backbone Cα RMSD (r = − 0.68, p < 0.001; 4.83 ± 1.92 Å); 27/28 intact proteins (96.4%) maintained pLDDT > 70. Mixed-effects modeling confirmed core RSA increases (β = +28.5%, p < 0.0001). A backbone-centric Cα contact density filter (CDα ≤ 10.17; ≤ 10 neighbors at rc = 8.0 Å) identified exposed loops, achieving pilot residue-level macro-averaged AUC of 0.80 ± 0.08 (pooled AUC = 0.96; n = 3 test proteins). Prioritized Pseudomonas aeruginosa epitopes were assembled into a 93-residue chimera. Explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (4 systems × 5 × 300 ns; 6.0 µs CHARMM36m + 6.0 µs Amber ff14SB = 12.0 µs total; 6.0 µs/force field) preserved epitope exposure (41.8 ± 1.2 vs. 28.3 ± 3.1 nm²; Cohen’s d = 4.8). Predictors require intact scaffolding for OMP loop modeling; CDα provides an exploratory filter for full-length prioritization.

articles.title: Valorization of pistachio shell waste into a biochar/Zeolite-13X composite for CO2 adsorption: Role of porous structure and surface chemistry
articles.abstract: In the present investigation, a biochar-based adsorbent was prepared from pistachio shell waste-derived biochar (BPS). The obtained biochar was modified with Zeolite-13X particles to prepare a BPS/Zeolite-13X composite. The adsorbents were used to capture carbon dioxide from a gas stream. SEM-EDX, FTIR, BET, and XRD analyses were performed to characterize the obtained adsorbents. According to the results, the surface area of BPS and BPS/Zeolite- 13X was 184.74 and 357.05 m2/g, respectively. The increase in surface area after the modification suggested that the surface properties of BPS were improved by adding Zeolite- 13X particles. Under the selected experimental conditions (80% CO₂ and 60 min), the experimental equilibrium CO2 adsorption capacities (qe) of BPS and the BPS/Zeolite-13X composite were 0.869 and 1.237 mmol g⁻¹, respectively. The highest adsorption capacity of the BPS/Zeolite-13X composite was obtained at a BPS/Zeolite-13X mass ratio of 70:30. The Sips isotherm predicted maximum adsorption capacities (qm) of 1.04 and 1.54 mmol g⁻¹ for BPS and BPS/Zeolite-13X, respectively. The isotherm and kinetic models demonstrated that the adsorption of CO2 was best described by the Sips and pseudo-second-order models for BPS and BPS/Zeolite-13X adsorbents. The mechanism of CO2 adsorption was clarified on the example of the BPS/Zeolite-13X composite, which revealed the presence of van der Waals forces, electrostatic attraction, and possible hydrogen bonding. Therefore, the fabricated adsorbent showed promising performance for CO₂ capture, demonstrating the potential of pistachio shell waste-derived materials.

articles.title: Novel (R)-Camphor-Derived Thiosemicarbazones and Thiazolidinones as Potential Antiparasitic Agents: Synthesis, Biological Evaluation, Molecular Docking, ADMET, and DFT Studies
articles.abstract: This study reports the synthesis of a novel series of (R)-camphor-based thiosemicarbazones and thiazolidinones derivatives. We obtained the compounds through heterocyclization and Knoevenagel-type condensation reactions, and characterized them by HRMS and NMR spectroscopy. Several derivatives exhibited promising in vitro antiparasitic activity against Leishmania major promastigotes and amastigotes, as well as Toxoplasma gondii tachyzoites. Compound 1 showed activity against L. major amastigotes and promastigotes, with EC₅₀ values of 0.5 and 11.9 µg/mL, respectively. Compounds 2a, 6a, 6b, 5a, and 3a–c were active against L. major promastigotes (EC₅₀ < 10 µg/mL), while 4a–c and 5a–c exhibited antitoxoplasmal activity (EC₅₀ < 11 µg/mL). Molecular docking identified 2a, 3a, and 3b as compounds with multiple interactions with the active site of trypanothione reductase and N-myristoyltransferase. We performed DFT calculations at the B3LYP/6-311 + + G(d,p) level to investigate their optimized geometries and HOMO–LUMO gaps, and used SwissADME to assess their pharmacokinetic properties. The results identify selected (R)-camphor-derived thiazolidinones as promising starting points for further antiparasitic investigation.

articles.title: Reading Royalty Risk at Scale: LLM-Assisted Construction and Reliability Analysis of an Offset- and-Deduction Clause Corpus from SEC-Filed Technology Licences
articles.abstract: We introduce RODEO, a corpus of 5,111 royalty offset and deduction clause spans from material-contract exhibits filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (709 exhibits, 417 filers), labelled for their economic function under a seven-function taxonomy. Because exhaustive human annotation is costly, we build the resource with a protocol assisted by a large language model (LLM): independent double classification, adjudication of substantive disagreements, and a stratified human spot-check. We release the corpus with source identifiers and privacy-screened excerpts, together with the per-pass and adjudicated labels, prompts and code. As a quality-control analysis we examine how far the model can be trusted. It is highly self-consistent on the surface (82.4% exact-set agreement across passes) yet poorly calibrated: 82% of predictions carry the maximal confidence score, even that top bin flips label across passes 13.8% of the time, and the model’s own uncertainty flag recovers only 1% of genuine disagreements. On a deliberately hard subset, a model from an independent family agrees with the adjudicated label only 36.6% of the time, whereas on a broad stratified sample the two LLM annotators agree substantially (macro Cohen’s κ = 0.78). Inter-pass disagreement, not self-reported confidence, is therefore the more useful signal for triaging hard cases when full human labelling is infeasible. Supervised baselines show that the labelling is learnable (a bag-of-words logistic-regression classifier reaches macro-F1 0.80; the notice-and-documentation condition is hardest). The released labels are LLM-generated with a human spot-check (“silver”), and we set out the path to a fully human-adjudicated version.

articles.title: Thermal stress ahead of arrested dyke tips with implications for the reinitiation of dyke propagation
articles.abstract: Understanding the movement of magma within the crust is essential for interpreting volcanic unrest signals and ultimately forecasting volcanic eruptions. Magma ascends through the crust by generating pressure-driven fractures at the leading tips of dykes and inclined sheets. The vast majority of studies investigating the mechanics of magma propagation neglect the influence and effect of temperature on the rock surrounding intrusions during emplacement. However, magma can disrupt temperature fields, leading to thermal expansion or contraction of the surrounding host rocks and to the generation of thermal stress and thermal fractures. This study uses a thermo-mechanical approach to investigate thermal stress perturbations around dyke tips and considers how insight from numerical experiments may be utilized to interpret geophysical signatures. Despite limited data on rock physical properties at elevated temperatures, existing data suggest a non-linear relationship between temperature and thermal expansion/contraction co-efficient. A two-dimensional nonlinear thermo-mechanical transient model was implemented using the finite element method (FEM). Results show that thermal stress in the direction parallel to dyke propagation suppresses tensile stresses predicted by purely elastic models, potentially creating stress conditions that are more favourable for mixed-mode failure involving both tensile and shear components near the dyke tip. The results become particularly salient for magma sheets that become stalled and are given time to heat and alter the surrounding host rocks. In these circumstances, sheets may resume their propagation, following arrest, if the combination of magma pressure and thermal stress overcome the local rock strength.

articles.title: Defect-mediated carrier transport in tin oxide transparent electrodes via post- annealing atmosphere engineering for silicon heterojunction solar cells
articles.abstract: Silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cells are promising for high-efficiency terrestrial and low-Earth-orbit photovoltaics owing to their high efficiency, low temperature coefficient, and high bifaciality. However, conventional indium tin oxide transparent electrodes rely on scarce and costly indium, hindering the sustainable development of SHJ technology. In this work, tantalum-doped tin oxide (TTO) was employed as an alternative transparent conductive material, and the effect of post-annealing atmosphere on the optoelectrical properties of TTO films is investigated. After post-annealing at 220 ℃, N2 and vacuum annealing yields the highest carrier concentration and mobility, respectively. Vacuum annealing improves crystallinity and reduced localized defect states, thereby suppressing carrier scattering and enhancing mobility; whereas N2 annealing increases the concentration of oxygen-vacancy-related defects, resulting in a higher carrier concentration. The 100 nm TTO film annealed in N2 achieves a minimum sheet resistance of 244 Ω sq− 1 and a figure of merit of 2.99 × 10− 4 Ω−1. Indium-less SHJ solar cells are subsequently fabricated using TTO transparent electrodes. Compared with the device based on as-deposited TTO film, this device employing post-annealed TTO film exhibits improved fill factor and power conversion efficiency. These results provide insights into the mechanisms governing the electrical properties of tin oxide-based transparent conductive films and demonstrate the potential of TTO for indium-less SHJ solar cells and other optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Dynamic Pulsed Magnetic Field Treatment Alters Germination Physiology, Transcriptomic Profiles, and Phytohormone Dynamics in Hulless Barley and Is Associated with Increased Grain Yield
articles.abstract: Dynamic pulsed magnetic-field seed priming represents a non-invasive physical approach associated with modifications in seed physiology and crop performance, yet its multi-layered effects remain poorly characterized in plateau‑adapted hulless barley. Hulless barley (cv. Kunlun 14) seeds were assigned to a magnetic field treatment group (CH) and a non-magnetized control group (CK). CH seeds received a four-stage dynamic pulsed magnetic field (50–150 mT, 17 min total), and both groups were compared for germination phenotypes, physio-biochemical traits, time-course transcriptomes, 54 targeted phytohormones (47 retained after QC), and field grain yield. Magnetic priming was accompanied by enhanced germination starting from 24 h (17.80% for CH vs. 14.53% for CK, + 22.5% at 24 h and + 12.9% at 48 h), accelerated radicle emergence (+ 43.6% at 24 h), and increased bud length, root length, and seed‑vigor index (+ 15.7%). Physiologically, H2O2 accumulated in CH during early imbibition (+ 24.0% at 12 h, + 18.7% at 24 h), ATP rose by 13.8% at 24 h, and α-amylase activity increased by 30.7% at 48 h. Antioxidant enzyme activities rose by 20.3–46.0%, while MDA decreased by up to 26.0%. Transcriptome analysis identified 7414 DEGs at 12 h, with starch and sucrose metabolism the most enriched pathway (fold = 15.27), and phytohormone profiling showed coordinated changes in auxin-, gibberellin-, cytokinin-, and brassinosteroid-associated hormones and genes, alongside altered ABA-related signaling. Field trials showed that magnetic treatment increased emergence, effective panicles, and grains per spike, raising yield by 6.81% in 2025 (P < 0.01) and 5.35% in 2026 (P < 0.05), for a combined increase of 6.10% across the two seasons, despite a small but significant reduction in 1000‑grain weight. Our multi‑omics dataset documents physiological, transcriptomic and hormonal changes correlated with magnetic‑field priming and improved field‑level yield performance in hulless barley. Note that these observations represent correlative responses; candidate magneto‑perception modules inferred from transcriptome data require further genetic‑functional validation.

articles.title: Microscopic Foundations of an Entanglement Tapestry
articles.abstract: We specify a background-independent microscopic theory for an entanglement tapestry: an infinite pre-geometric graph of unlabeled nodes connected by entanglement threads. Nodes carry no intrinsic properties. The physically meaningful degrees of freedom reside on the threads. Each thread is taken to be a qubit. A three-term many-body Hamiltonian — a valence potential, a local swapping term, and a combinatorial frustration term — generates the dynamics. The valence potential favors a preferred coordination . The integer value of is not derived here; it remains a free parameter. When a concrete continuum expression is required we use the illustrative value v_* = 4.The new content is not a new gravitational action. It is an explicit state space, a dynamical law, and a staged continuum pathway from that Hamiltonian to an effective metric. An Einstein-like equation is obtained by varying a covariant continuum action in which the Einstein–Hilbert term is introduced as an effective gravitational sector, not derived from the graph measure. A tensor-network blocking on a two-dimensional square lattice is used only as a proof of principle that the leading linear coefficient in the beta function is extractable once a blocking rule is fixed. No thermodynamically controlled numerical value of that coefficient is reported. High-density patterns admit an entanglement bound of Ryu–Takayanagi type from thread counting across relational cuts; saturation is not claimed for generic states. The continuum description is of closed-time-path type, which avoids a local wrong-sign kinetic term for a single propagating field. A complete stability analysis of the model’s continuum kernels is left open.This paper does not derive a preferred integer v_*, an Einstein–Hilbert term from the microscopic measure, or a reduced vault–forge master equation. Those problems are stated where they arise and are left open.

articles.title: Narrow-Band Magnetism Allowed by Quantum Geometry: Altermagnetism and Beyond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum geometry plays a central role in shaping correlated phases in narrow bands, yet its influence on the competition between distinct magnetic orders, especially the emergence of altermagnetism, remains largely unexplored. To address this question, we study the quadrupole insulator model with strictly onsite generalized Hubbard-Kanamori interactions, in which both Néel antiferromagnetism and altermagnetism are symmetry-permitted. Depending on the parameters, the isolated narrow lowest band of the model can either be obstructed atomic with strong quantum geometry or trivial atomic with weak quantum geometry, while the dispersion is identical in the two cases. By partially filling the lowest band, our Hartree-Fock calculations show only conventional ferromagnetic phases for the weak quantum geometric case, while we find two collinear altermagnetic phases, as well as nematic phases, for the strong quantum geometric case. Such a dramatic difference can be understood by the distinct characters of the projected interaction: the projected interactions acquire sizable longer-range channels only for the strong quantum geometric case, while they are dominated by the on-site Hubbard channel in the weak quantum geometric case. These results establish the essential role of quantum geometry for altermagnetism to emerge from interacting narrow bands where crystalline symmetries cannot sufficiently constrain the magnetic order.

articles.title: Invertible parafermionic topological phases in one dimension
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Invertible topological phases of matter are described by gapped ground states of local Hamiltonians that are non-degenerate on any closed spatial manifold. Classification of invertible topological phases realized by bosonic or fermionic degrees of freedom is well-understood, particularly in low dimensions. In one-dimensional space, the classification can be understood through the boundary projective representations. We extend this paradigm to one-dimensional invertible topological phases of parafermionic degrees of freedom with symmetries. We define cohomological invariants that characterize distinct boundary projective representations and compute their stacking rules. Among other results, we show (i) how these cohomological invariants can be used to compute protected boundary degeneracy and (ii) how, in contrast to bosons or fermions, invertible phases of parafermions can form a non-Abelian group under stacking. For order-N parafermions with N a prime power, we define representative Hamiltonians realizing invertible topological phases with Z³N symmetry. We show that under stacking they generate a non-Abelian group of order 2N³. When N is an odd prime, this group is Heis(Z_N)rtimes Z,₂, where Heis(Z_N) is the Heisenberg group of order N³.

articles.title: Machine-learning charge density for electronic materials and devices simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a machine-learning (ML) charge density model, DeltaChargeNet, integrated with the full-potential tight-binding muffin-tin orbital (FP-TB-MTO) method for electronic structure and quantum transport simulations of materials and devices. The ML model predicts electron density from atomic structures with low linear-scaling cost, while FP-TB-MTO provides an accurate tight-binding representation of the system Hamiltonian. To achieve high-fidelity ML density for complex devices with interfaces and disorder, we train an equivariant graph convolutional network to predict Δ ρ-the difference between DFT and atomic superposition densities-under a charge neutrality constraint required for inhomogeneous systems. A secondary ML residual charge model compensates for errors in the primary Δ ρ model. The predicted density is then used within the full-relativistic FP-TB-MTO framework combined with the non-equilibrium Green's function method. We validate our method on bulk HgCdTe disordered alloys (including vacancy defects) and Au/HgCdTe/Au disordered devices. The maximum band energy error is below 10 meV for bulk HgCdTe. For devices, the charge neutrality constraint suppresses long-wavelength charge bias that would otherwise distort the electrostatic potential by 0.68-1.88 eV near the device center, while residual compensation corrects the remaining 0.16-0.46 eV potential mismatch, essential for reproducing the correct potential barrier profile. Together, these corrections reproduce the layer-resolved potential, including interface steps and bulk-like plateaus, within 0.1 eV of fully self-consistent DFT. Finally, we demonstrate quantum transport in a 11220-atom infrared detector. By combining first-principles accuracy with linear-scaling inference, DeltaChargeNet enables large-scale device simulations without the full DFT self-consistent field loop.

articles.title: Theoretical exploration of ambient-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate: A strategy of atomic substitution for tuning chemical pressure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The possibility of ambient-pressure superconductivity in La₃Ni₂O₇ is theoretically explored via chemical substitution. Using first-principles and many-body calculations, we propose substituting Ba at the lanthanide site to exert chemical pressure, thereby mitigating the octahedral distortions that suppress superconductivity. Phonon calculations demonstrate the dynamical stability of the high-symmetry tetragonal phase in mathrmLa₃₋ᵢₜₓBaᵢₜₓNi₂O₇ at a small doping ratio of x sim 0.15. By applying the fluctuation exchange approximation to an effective model Hamiltonian derived from this stable structure, we calculate the Eliashberg eigenvalue λ to evaluate the relative superconducting transition temperature T_c to existing unconventional superconductors. We conclude that s_±-wave superconductivity is likely to emerge, as the required Ba concentration (x sim 0.15) is sufficiently small to minimize the detrimental suppression of superconductivity induced by hole doping.

articles.title: Quantum Fluctuations drive Emerging Bosonic Quantum Phases in a Moiré Flatband Superconductor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum fluctuations play a central role in superconductors by mediating the interactions that promote electron pairing and controlling the phase coherence required for macroscopic condensation. Thus far, understanding the interplay between quantum fluctuations and superconductivity remains challenging in unconventional superconductors. Here, we establish quantum phase fluctuations as the organizing principle linking superconductivity and Bose-insulating quantum criticality in a moiré flatband superconductor of alternating twisted trilayer graphene (ATTG). Superconductivity is optimal near half-filling of the moiré flatband and gives way to a density-wave-like resistance peak at high temperatures, in which we observe distinct temperature scales for the pairing (~6 K) and the condensation (~1 K). We observe compelling evidence of a bosonic superconducting quantum phase transition, driven by both out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic fields, with a universal critical resistivity of R_c =~0.62R_Q and finite-temperature scaling of zν_B = 2.3, where R_Q = h/4e² is the quantum resistance for bosons. Strikingly, the observed bosonic insulator shows a nearly quantized resistivity of R_Q that saturates at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, together with a zero-bias peak, a nearly zero Hall resistance, and a logarithmic dependence at higher temperatures. Both the superconductor and the bosonic insulator could be driven into the same critical quantum fluctuation regime dynamically under a large bias. Our results establish moiré flatband as a clean platform for studying unconventional superconductivity and bosonic quantum criticality governed by quantum fluctuations.

articles.title: Influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and periodicity on giant chiral asymmetry of domain wall mobility in epitaxial Cu/Pd/Co/Pd(111) films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity on the chirality-dependent mobility of domain walls (DWs) in epitaxial Si(111)/Cu(2-7 nm)/Pd(3 nm)/Co(0.7 nm)/Pd(3 nm) heterostructures. By varying the Cu buffer layer thickness, we systematically modify the morphology of the magnetic interfaces while maintaining a constant composition and thickness of the Pd/Co/Pd trilayer. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that increasing the Cu thickness leads to the development of a hierarchical interfacial morphology characterized by increasing roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity. We observe a dramatic enhancement of the asymmetry between the velocities of DWs with opposite chirality in the creep regime, reaching a velocity ratio of approximately 50000 in the sample with a 7-nm-thick Cu buffer layer. This value exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the effective saturated asymmetry previously observed in Pd/Co/Pd structures with roughness controlled by the bottom Pd layer thickness. Despite comparable root-mean-square interface roughness in both series, the Cu-buffer-induced morphology exhibits a substantially larger characteristic lateral periodicity. We propose that the enhanced asymmetry originates from the different spatial organization of interfacial disorder, which modifies the pinning energy landscape and amplifies chirality-dependent thermally activated DW propagation. Our results suggest that engineering not only the amplitude but also the lateral spatial correlations of interfacial roughness provides an effective approach for controlling chiral DW dynamics in magnetic heterostructures.

articles.title: Vestiges of magnon fractionalization in the quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet rouaite Cu₂(NO₃)(OH)₃ with alternating ferro- and antiferromagnetic S=frac12 chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ferro- and antiferromagnetic quantum spin chains host qualitatively distinct elementary excitations --- magnons (S=1, bosonic quasiparticles) and spinons (S=frac12, fractionalized quasiparticles), respectively. Weakly coupled networks of both chain types therefore provide an ideal platform for exploring spinon-magnon coupling and the hybridization of sharp magnon modes with spinon continua. Here we investigate the spin-excitation spectrum of the frustrated quantum magnet rouaite, Cu₂(NO₃)(OH)₃ --- a model realization of weakly coupled ferro- and antiferromagnetic Cu²⁺ spin-frac12 chains. The frustrated interchain interactions, while weaker than the dominant intrachain exchange, are sufficient to stabilize a long-range-ordered state that is not reproduced by classical calculations. Neutron spectroscopy reveals a spectrum of well-defined spin waves associated with both types of chains, with clear signatures of hybridization but no observable spinon continuum. Certain magnon branches resulting from this hybridization exhibit substantial broadening near the zone center. We attribute this to vestiges of spinon fractionalization persisting partway through the dimensional crossover from isolated quantum spin chains to a 2D network of frustrated spins.

articles.title: Pressure dependent DFT study of mechanical, thermal, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of EuCd2As2: a magnetic semimetal
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the pressure-dependent physical properties of EuCd2As2, a magnetically and topologically rich compound with potential applications in spintronics and optoelectronics technologies. We have investigated the structural, mechanical, thermophysical, acoustic, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of this material at pressures of 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 GPa. The calculated lattice parameters at zero pressure are in good agreement with experimental values. The mechanical stability of EuCd2As2 is maintained over the investigated pressure range. The elastic constants, bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Young's modulus are found to be tunable with applied pressure. The compound undergoes a brittle to ductile transition at higher pressures. The Debye temperature, melting temperature, and Grüneisen parameter are found to be strongly pressure-dependent. Phonon thermal conductivity has been evaluated. The electronic properties of EuCd2As2 were studied through band structure and density of states (DOS). The effect of pressure up to 8 GPa was investigated for the ferromagnetic (FM) phase. At 0 GPa, the calculated FM band structure exhibits no band gap at the Fermi level, which confirms the semimetallic nature of EuCd2As2. The net magnetic moment of 6.96 μ_B per unit cell was obtained for this compound indicating its potential for spintronics application. The optical properties, including the dielectric function, refractive index, absorption coefficient, optical conductivity, reflectivity, and loss function, are calculated. The calculated optical spectra indicate strong absorption in the visible and ultraviolet regions, suggesting that EuCd2As2 may have potential for optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Making Plasticity Visible: A Case Study for High-Temperature Exposed Aluminum Alloy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18120v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the onset of plastic deformation and the early development of strain localization is essential for characterizing material behavior and identifying failure-prone regions. However, these transitions are not always distinguishable from conventional full-field strain measurements. This study investigates a data- driven framework combining Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to extract temporal and spatial deformation signatures during uniaxial tensile loading. The methodology is evaluated using AA6063-T5 aluminum alloy specimens in the as-received condition and following thermal exposure at 100~^circC, 200~^circC, and 300~^circC. PCA applied to sequential strain fields reveals a characteristic peak in the second principal component projection near the yielding transition, showing agreement with the conventional 0.2% offset criterion across the investigated conditions. Furthermore, principal component maps extracted from high-temporal-resolution strain fields preceding this transition highlight localized deformation features associated with subsequent failure regions. These features are more clearly distinguishable than competing strain concentrations in the corresponding instantaneous strain maps. The results indicate that PCA-derived deformation signatures remain identifiable despite thermally induced variations in mechanical response. This approach demonstrates the potential of unsupervised dimensionality reduction for extracting physically interpretable information on plastic deformation and early strain localization from experimental full-field measurements.

articles.title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group P4₃₃₂ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3,048 within 50~meV/atom. We analyze their structural motifs, stability, and electronic band structures, highlighting recurring prototype families, several of which show intrinsic intermediate-band features. Our results substantially expand the known phase space of cubic chiral semiconductors and may guide future efforts in the discovery and design of chiral materials.

articles.title: Controlled Magnon Chirality and Its Reversal by Anisotropy in Altermagnetic FeF₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In altermagnets, the exchange symmetry of two mutually compensating magnetic sublattices permits spin-polarized electronic bands and chirality-split magnon bands. Because these effects have opposite signs in domains related by time reversal, magnetic-domain control is essential for their observation and utilization. Using half-polarized neutron diffraction, we demonstrate that we can control magnetic domain imbalance in a single crystal of FeF₂ by field cooling, and we relate this response to the established piezomagnetism in this material. Our half-polarized inelastic neutron scattering measurements directly resolve the altermagnetic splitting of chiral magnon bands. Strikingly, we observe a clear reversal of chirality near Q=(0.5,0.5,1), where the altermagnetic exchange splitting vanishes and no chirality is expected in a nonrelativistic exchange model. This reversal of the chirality is well explained by the presence of a transverse component of the single-ion anisotropy tensor, which rotates between Fe sublattices related by the crystal's altermagnetic 4₂ screw symmetry. These results allow us to resolve fine features of the spin Hamiltonian for FeF₂ and show how symmetry-governed relativistic anisotropy can reshape altermagnetic spin dynamics, as well as providing an avenue for control of magnetic domains and the net chiral response.

articles.title: Tunable coupling between valley and magnetic excitons in WS2/CrSBr heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. Here, we examined the magneto-optical properties of 2D semiconductor heterostructures made of antiferromagnetic CrSBr and a monolayer WS2, both of which host intriguing excitonic properties. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. The interlayer charge transfer shows strong spin selectivity and is governed by the relative alignment between the valley-spin polarization of photoexcited carriers in WS2 and the magnetization in CrSBr, giving rise to spin-sensitive circularly polarized photoluminescence (PL) from WS2. Furthermore, the highly anisotropic electronic dispersion in CrSBr enables stacking-dependent control of interlayer interactions, as inferred from a twist-angle dependence of PL quenching. Our work establishes a highly tunable 2D system that integrates valleytronics and magnetic excitons through multiple coupling channels, opening up new opportunities in all-optical manipulation of spin and magnon states and for the development of flexible spin-optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Thermally Hysteretic Room-Temperature Nonlinear Hall Effect in Bulk EuTe4
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) is a novel transport phenomena and shows great potential applications of future electronics. However, the realization of a giant and tunable NLHE in bulk materials at room temperature remains elusive. Here, we report a NLHE in bulk EuTe4 single crystals, which persists up to 400 K and exhibits pronounced thermal hysteresis behaviors. The ratio of nonlinear Hall voltages during warming and cooling processes is about 4.7 at 340 K. Such phenomena could be related to the inversion-symmetry-broken charge density wave state in EuTe4. These findings demonstrate bulk EuTe₄ as a promising platform for tunable nonlinear electronic devices at room temperature.

articles.title: Edge spin generalization for quantum Hall Laughlin droplets with elliptic shapes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that quasiparticles in the bulk of quantum Hall systems possess an emergent spin, which satisfies a spin-statistics relation. Recent results show that this spin can fractionalize: a quasiparticle spin in the bulk induces an opposite edge spin on the boundary. So far, the edge spin has only been studied in the simplest possible geometries, where the boundary is either circular or straight, without considering that a generic confining potential could give the droplet a non-symmetric shape. Yet, the value of the edge spin is not dictated by symmetry, but by topology: it is expected that the specific shape of the edge should not matter. In this work, we therefore generalize the edge spin to elliptically shaped droplets. We consider two different generalizations of the edge spin and test them on a family of elliptic Laughlin states introduced in the present work. The first, most straightforward, generalization is based on the properties of the single-particle orbitals for the elliptic confining potential. We show that this proposal applies to non-interacting states. The second proposal is based on the emergent properties of the quantum fluid. We show that this proposal also applies to interacting states, making it the suitable definition of the edge spin in the elliptic case. Our work demonstrates that it is possible to define an edge spin for Laughlin fluids with a non-trivial shape.

articles.title: Uniaxial strain induces d-wave phonon chirality in ferroelectric BaTiO₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Circularly dichroic resonant inelastic x-ray scattering has revealed electrically switchable g-wave phonon chirality in freestanding BaTiO₃ membranes. Here, we show from first principles that uniaxial strain changes the angular class of this texture. Lowering C₄ᵥ to C₂ᵥ adds a d-wave helicity that is bilinear in the orthorhombic strain η and the polarization, with nodal lines along the stress axis. For the 38~meV branches at η=1%, we find that (i) along the diagonal, where the helicity vanishes by symmetry without strain, it reaches about 60% of the unstrained maximum, and (ii) at the measured wave vectors off the mirror it is reduced by more than half. With PBEsol and PBE+D3 force constants, the d-wave component grows linearly in η and equals the g-wave one at η^*approx1.3--1.4%. Resolved by branch, the response of strain-split E doublets is non-analytic in η, as captured by a two-band model. Strain therefore provides a second knob, besides the electric field, that controls the symmetry and the sign of phonon chirality in ferroelectric membranes.

articles.title: Testing correlated spin--orbit multiplets beyond excitation centroids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Matching an excitation centroid does not establish the resolved structure of a correlated spin--orbit multiplet. Across eight embedded iridium and osmium compounds, ligand-active XMS-CASPT2 places the K₂OsCl₆ centroid within 0.5~meV of a RIXS maximum while splitting its nearly degenerate reference triplet by 2.54~meV, and matched OpenMolcas 26.10 controls retain the bare-anion sensitivities. Independent BAGEL calculations isolate contraction dependence in a three-state spin-free model: on the same reference, replacing SS--SR with MS--MR reduces the symmetry-defined E-block splitting from 0.448~meV to 4.67×10⁻⁵~meV. Native reconstruction, reference symmetry, representation invariance, sensitivity controls and comparison with fitted spectral features or magnetic response provide an ordered validation procedure whose tests constrain different properties of the Hamiltonian.

articles.title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. In TMC, an interaction is written as a function of the transfer matrix, and one set of contraction rules then yields the effective Hamiltonians of DMRG and VUMPS, the tangent-space excitation action, and the energy variance, without an MPO. Long-range interactions thus enter with their prescribed distance dependence. For the half-filled lattice Coulomb chain with a 1/d interaction of strength V, theory predicts CDW order for all V>0, but at weak coupling this order is too weak for earlier numerics to resolve. Using TMC, we obtain infinite-MPS ground states at V=2 directly in the thermodynamic limit, with an energy variance per site of 2×10⁻¹⁰. Our data, extrapolated to zero energy variance, indicate a small nonzero CDW amplitude, m₀=0.002213(14), consistent with this prediction. The complete V=2 optimization workflow across the full series of bond dimensions takes less than a day on a single AMD MI250X GPU die. For an exactly solvable long-range hopping model, TMC reproduces the nonanalytic |k| cusp of the one-particle dispersion that any fixed finite sum of decaying exponentials rounds off. We also use TMC to optimize first-quantized MPS directly in the thermodynamic limit. For half-filled free fermions, our entanglement entropy data show scaling consistent with central charge c=1 over the studied bond dimensions, as for second-quantized MPS.

articles.title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical artifacts. Here, we present a methods validation study that deliberately overfits a physics-aware GNN ensemble to probe the robustness of feature-ranking approaches. Using the CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy system with three stoichiometries, we train GNNs to predict decomposition enthalpies from DFT-calculated structures while explicitly constraining output weights to encode feature importance. By design, our dataset is limited (approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways) to control compositional complexity and enable precise interrogation of local chemistry effects. We validate that feature rankings capture meaningful local-environment information through a series of atomic swap perturbations: perturbing individual atomic sites and re-ranking features reveals spatial decay consistent with the GNN's interaction cutoff, confirming that weights encode neighbor-shell effects rather than global stoichiometric artifacts alone. Results demonstrate that feature attribution methods can remain physically interpretable even under overfitting, provided validation is rigorous. This work establishes a foundation for trustworthy interpretability in materials GNNs and sets the stage for scaling to multiple chemistries and testing generalization across compositional spaces.

articles.title: High Entropy Oxides as Room Temperature Anderson Insulators with Colossal Soft Gaps
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Anderson effect, arising from destructive quantum interference of electron wave packets in disordered potentials, is usually observed at cryogenic temperatures and typically arises from extrinsic defects in conventional materials such as phosphorus dopants in silicon or oxygen vacancies in transition metal oxides. Here we demonstrate that a multication lattice of transition metals in a high-entropy oxide (HEO) natively establishes an interacting Anderson insulator that extends up to 500,K. By controlling the population of transition metal cations in La₀.₇Sr₀.₃Mn₁₋ₓ(Cr,Fe,Co,Ni)ₓ/₄O₃ (LS5B), we tune the system from the prototypical correlated metal La₀.₇Sr₀.₃MnO₃ at x=0.00 to a localized insulator at x=0.80, where the disorder length contracts to near the unit cell (3.85 mathringA) and drives the electron mean free path to the Ioffe-Regel limit. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals the systematic localization of itinerant d-quasiparticle states at the Fermi level, consistent with the emergence of a soft Coulomb gap, while the underlying band structure and symmetry are preserved. Transport reveals Efros-Shklovskii variable-range hopping governed by a colossal soft gap with characteristic temperature TES>50,000,K and screened Coulomb interaction strengths as high as 1.6 eV. Together, multiple lines of evidence indicate that interacting Anderson behavior is a native characteristic that survives to temperatures as high as 500,K in high-entropy materials.

articles.title: Regularized Neural Quantum States for Heisenberg Magnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an approach to solving locally ordered quantum spin systems using neural network quantum states. First, our approach rests on choosing a spin basis constructed from the magnetic texture of a classical or quantum reference state. Second, the method improves convergence and suppresses parameter-space drift through a regularized Riemannian gradient descent adapted to the quantum state geometry of the variational state manifold. Combining these techniques enables stable ground-state calculations for two- and three-dimensional chiral spin systems with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions. The resulting variational ground-state energies are competitive with those of high-fidelity density matrix renormalization group calculations and, for periodic and layered geometries, provide significantly tighter upper bounds on the ground-state energy.

articles.title: Fibonacci Non-Abelian Quantum Hall States with Pair Structure - a classification of chiral 2-cluster many-body wave-functions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fibonacci anyons support universal topological quantum computation. They have been proposed to emerge in fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, such as the filling-fraction ν=tfrac23 state described by an effective SU(3)₂ Chern-Simons theory, and the ν=tfrac25 state with a 3-cluster structure (an n-cluster structure means that n-electron bound states form a Laughlin-type wave function of the form (z⁽ⁿ⁾ᵢ-z⁽ⁿ⁾ⱼ)^m). In this work, we systematically classify FQH wave functions P(z₁,ldots,z_N) in the N→infty limit, through a generalized pattern of zeros (gPOZ) approach, where the wave function is determined by the leading order of zero along with the accompanying leading polynomial that develops as successive number of zᵢ's are brought together. Within this approach, we obtain a (ν,h,c)-classification of wave functions with a 2-cluster (pair) structure. Among these wave functions, those with (h,c) = (tfrac12,tfrac12), (tfrac32,tfrac710), (3,tfrac45) correspond to gapped FQH states with filling fraction ν and edge-state chiral central charge c+1, while others with c<0 may be gapless. We find that even a 2-cluster structure can give rise to Fibonacci statistics, for (ν,h,c) = (tfrac14,tfrac32,tfrac710), corresponding to the (5,4) minimal model, and for (ν,h,c) = (tfrac17,3,tfrac45), corresponding to the (6,5) minimal model. We further construct an ideal 4-body Hamiltonian whose ground state is the (tfrac14,tfrac32,tfrac710) state.

articles.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnetization yields a Chern insulator with a chiral edge state, whereas in-plane magnetization supports a two-dimensional Weyl semimetal with node-connecting edge states. Continuous spin canting further demonstrates how magnetic reorientation can drive the transition and stabilize the Chern phase before full magnetic saturation. Although material-specific transition conditions depend on electronic correlations and structural stability under compression, the underlying strategy identifies interlayer hybridization as a link between magnetic order and band topology. These results provide a design principle for externally tunable topological phases in layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.

articles.title: Probing Spatiotemporal Quantum Correlations with Two-Qubit Relaxometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum impurities and spin qubits are powerful local probes of magnetic fluctuations, but conventional relaxometry reduces their information to a local relaxation rate at a single frequency. Building on advances in two-qubit sensing of spatial correlations, we show how two complementary protocols probe finite-time correlations in interacting quantum matter. Phase-cycled Bell-state relaxometry isolates the signed contribution of correlated relaxation to the joint ground-state population. To second order in the probe-environment coupling, the resulting population contrast measures a finite-time integral of the energy-ordered cross-correlator. In the longitudinal regime, XY8 covariance probes the complementary symmetrized cross-correlator within a tunable frequency window. For a gapless quantum spin chain, the signals reveal interaction-dependent algebraic scaling and ballistic propagation. Luttinger-liquid theory links sign changes as the qubit frequency is swept to the propagation time between the probes. It also predicts distinct spatial power laws for the Bell signal before the correlation front and at late times, when the sensing window resolves the qubit frequency. Matrix-product-state calculations for the spin chain test the pre-front scaling at zero and finite magnetization and extract the propagation velocity from Bell oscillations at zero magnetization. The probe coupling geometry determines which spin and momentum sectors contribute to the measured signals.

articles.title: Local gluing classification and bulk-locked clock rings for Z_N models on a Klein bottle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify local reflection gluings of the Z_N plaquette model on lattice Klein bottles and solve the obstructed literal seam. Within the monomial far-corner ansatz, all commuting gluings form a family labelled by a unit u of Z_N. They exist for every N at even seam length and, at odd length, exactly when -1 is a square modulo N. We determine the anyon transport, including exchange seams with P²=C for charge conjugation C, and the relation phases that distinguish an unfrustrated code from a commuting but frustrated Hamiltonian. For the literal gluing, the 2Lₓ noncommuting plaquettes form self-dual clock rings whose sectors are locked by the bulk. This gives an exact reduction of the spectrum to clock-ring spectra, closed-form ring ground energies for N=2,4, and a closed-form ground-state degeneracy. We further determine twisted-coefficient homology on the stated surface domains and compare it with logical modules on registered lattice grids; composite dimensions need not give squares of cyclic groups. Dressed-isometry gates and monodromy are reported with their finite-grid scope. Finally, the qudit Gottesman--Knill theorem bounds the computational interpretation: Clifford deformations and Weyl measurements with stabilizer inputs and no external magic states cannot supply a non-stabilizer resource. Charge-conjugation measurements that do supply such states lie outside this operation model. The new results concern explicit seam classification, phase-sensitive consistency and bulk-locked spectra, not a new general no-go theorem or a universal computing architecture.

articles.title: Observing Enhanced Entanglement in an Ising Quantum Register Beyond Weak Measurement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Measurements often yield a disentangled quantum state which is the most probable measurement outcome while the measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement could be exponentially less probable or absent. Higher probability in measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement is virtue in experimental observation of enhance entanglement in post-selected or Born-rule measurements with less resources in noisy quantum devices. We develop a periodic measurement sampling(PMS) protocol in the framework of uniform matrix product states. Using PMS, we identify a peak enhancement of entanglement in a uniform post-measurement state whose probabilistic outcome can be maximized by optimizing a measurement super-cell. A measurement super-cell is the smallest repeating building block of qubits defined by the measurement density, external field strength and exchange interactions between quantum register and ancilla qubits. The above prediction based on a classical description of the many-body quantum state is demonstrated in a quantum computing experiment in a loop of quantum register qubits with Ising interactions in the presence of transverse magnetic field. Further, we show the scalability of predictions of the periodic measurement sampling protocol in the thermodynamic limit to finite size systems. Especially, we present a rescaling ansatz which would enable predicting the possibility of observing enhanced entanglement in finite size systems.

articles.title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical phase-field models of brittle fracture capture toughness-controlled crack growth but not the material's strength surface, which governs crack nucleation. The theory of Kumar et al. (2020) incorporates the strength surface through a nucleation driving force, and Chockalingam (2025) derived this driving force for arbitrary strength surfaces described by n material parameters, with which the phase-field strength surface (PFSS) converges to the material strength surface as the regularization length ε → 0 and matches it exactly at n chosen states for any ε. In practice, however, the strength surface must be supplied as an analytic form chosen and calibrated case by case, and for the widely used analytic surfaces (n=2) accurate strength reproduction requires ε commensurate with the Irwin characteristic length lcₕ, imposing prohibitive mesh requirements for large structures. We introduce a neural-network (NN) strength function that is learned directly from strength data, is physics-constrained by construction, and provides far more calibration parameters than analytic surfaces; the calibration is generalized to any number of strength states and to enforce openness in chosen directions. A single architecture captures synthetic data from the Mohr-Coulomb, Drucker-Prager, Mogi-Coulomb and 3D Hoek-Brown surfaces and experimental data for graphite, natural rubber and styrene-butadiene rubber. The resulting PFSS is accurate up to ε = 10,lcₕ, whereas that of the exact analytic surfaces performs comparatively poorly even at ε = 0.5,lcₕ. Finite-element simulations validate the theory across fracture regimes. By decoupling strength fidelity from the regularization length, the approach substantially reduces the mesh resolution required for phase-field fracture simulations of large structures.

articles.title: Intertwined Orders, Quantum Criticality and Skyrmions in Tunable Topological Bands
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.21913v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Skyrmions are emergent many-body excitations that lie at the heart of both multi-component quantum Hall-like systems and deconfined quantum criticality. In a companion article (X. Wang et al., arXiv:2507.22971), we studied a microscopic time-reversal symmetric model of tunable interacting Chern bands using numerically exact determinant quantum Monte Carlo calculations, and presented evidence for the emergence of robust skyrmion excitations. These charged excitations emerge in the vicinity of a many-body insulator at a commensurate filling of the Chern bands, and lead to the onset of superconductivity when doped away from the insulating phase. Here, we present quantum Monte-Carlo results and a complementary field-theoretical analysis for the quantum phase transition(s) that arise between the intertwined phases as a function of two distinct tuning parameters. Our numerical results are consistent with a single continuous quantum phase transition between an insulating Chern antiferromagnet and a fully gapped superconductor, with an emergent SO(5) symmetry at the putative critical point, highly suggestive of deconfined quantum (pseudo-)criticality. We also present a detailed comparison between the momentum-resolved spectral functions associated with the neutral collective modes, single electron and composite spin-polaron excitations obtained using a combination of Monte-Carlo computations and a Bethe-Salpeter analysis built on top of the self-consistent Hartree-Fock calculation. We end with a brief outlook on some of the interesting open problems.

articles.title: SmoQyElPhQMC.jl: An open-source Julia package for efficient and scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.14425v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce version 1.0 of the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package, an open-source Julia code for performing scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled model Hamiltonians. SmoQyElPhQMC.jl is built upon the SmoQyDQMC.jl codebase and implements improved versions of the algorithms presented in [B. Cohen-Stead et al., Phys. Rev. E 105, 065302 (2022)] to enable (near-linear) scalable simulations of a broad class of uncorrelated e-ph models both in system size and inverse temperature. By extending the functionality of the flexible scripting interface introduced in SmoQyDQMC.jl, the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package continues to allow users to adapt it to different workflows and interface with other software packages in the Julia ecosystem. The code for this package can be downloaded from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/SmoQySuite/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl or installed using the Julia package manager. The online documentation, including examples, can be obtained from our documentation page at https://smoqysuite.github.io/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl/stable/.

articles.title: Intrinsic Defect Energetics and Fluorine Doping Effects in Li2CO3 and Li2O2: A First-Principles Study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.25408v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lithium carbonate, Li2CO3, is a thermodynamically stable carbonate phase whose defect energetics are closely related to its stability and decomposition behavior in various lithium-based electrochemical systems. These properties of Li2CO3 are particularly important in lithium-oxygen battery environments. In these systems, Li2CO3 can form as a parasitic discharge product alongside Li2O2, the primary discharge product, leading to performance degradation. However, compared with Li2O2, the intrinsic defect thermodynamics of Li2CO3 and how chemical doping modifies its defect energetics remain insufficiently understood. In this study, first-principles calculations were performed to systematically analyze the intrinsic point-defect energetics of Li2CO3 and to evaluate the effects of fluorine doping on vacancy formation energies in Li2CO3 and Li2O2. Intrinsic defect analysis reveals that defect behavior is predominantly governed by lithium-related defects. Upon fluorine doping, lithium and carbon vacancy formation energies decrease selectively in Li2CO3, partially destabilizing the carbonate framework, while a reduction in lithium vacancy formation energy is also observed in Li2O2. These results suggest that fluorine doping modulates the defect energetics of both discharge products, potentially providing a thermodynamic basis for controlling the stability of Li2CO3 and Li2O2 under thermodynamic conditions representative of lithium-oxygen batteries.

articles.title: Altermagnetism across the BCS-BEC crossover
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.14613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a two-dimensional paired Fermi system in which altermagnetism produces a spin splitting that depends on momentum. The interaction strength is described through the two-body binding energy, so that the chemical potential and pairing gap evolve self-consistently from the weak-coupling Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) regime to the strong-coupling Bose-Einstein-condensate (BEC) regime at fixed density. The stability of the uniform paired state is examined by giving the pairs a small center-of-mass momentum and following the resulting change in free energy. We show that at zero temperature, the phase stiffness follows a universal quadratic suppression, J/J₀ = 1 - (α/α₀)², across the entire fully gapped crossover regime. Deviations from this relation emerge only on the BCS side upon the opening of gapless Bogoliubov pockets, which rapidly reduce the stiffness and can trigger an instability toward finite-momentum pairing. In the BEC regime, this universal quadratic correction corresponds to the altered effective mass of the tightly bound composite bosons. The model therefore provides a simple setting in which to compare altermagnetic pair breaking on the BCS and BEC sides of the crossover.

articles.title: What DINO saw: ALiBi positional encoding reduces positional bias in Vision Transformers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.16840v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) - especially feature foundation models like DINOv2 - learn rich representations useful for many downstream tasks. However, architectural choices (such as positional encoding) can lead to these models displaying positional biases and artefacts independent of semantic content. This makes zero-shot adaption difficult in fields like material science, where images are often cross-sections of homogeneous microstructure (i.e. having no preferred direction). In this work, we investigate the positional bias in ViTs via linear probing, finding it present across a range of objectives and positional encodings, and subsequently reduce it by finetuning models to use ALiBi relative positional encoding. We demonstrate that these models retain desirable general semantics and their unbiased features can be used successfully in trainable segmentation of complex microscopy images.

articles.title: Hidden defects return a qubit's lost energy
articles.abstract: Today, many leading quantum computers are built from superconducting circuits. However, the qubits in these circuits can easily lose energy to their surroundings, scrambling the fragile quantum information they hold.

articles.title: Quantum teleportation method uses weaker entanglement to transfer encoded information
articles.abstract: Over the past several decades, researchers have demonstrated quantum teleportation, the transfer of one quantum system's state to another, in a range of systems. However, many quantum computers encode logical qubits (units of quantum information) across groups of physical qubits, which makes teleporting the encoded state without losing information more challenging.

articles.title: Tangled quantum whirlpools caught unraveling in an ultracold gas
articles.abstract: When a cloud of atoms is cooled close to absolute zero, its atoms can merge into a Bose–Einstein condensate (BEC): an exotic fluid in which atoms across the whole cloud share a single quantum state. Current theories predict that as a disordered quantum gas settles into this ordered state, a tangle of tiny vortices should form and gradually unravel.

articles.title: Rank-One Ultralight Dark Matter Response in a Full-Tensor Gravity Gradiometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer whose four test masses carry two compositions in a 2+2 pattern acquires a composition-dependent channel for dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter. The reconstructed response is the rank-one tensor K=gv_φ(t)otimesqv, with the axis of qv fixed in advance by the material assignment, and obeys the parameter-free null condition K(I-Pq)=0, which no gravity gradient or platform rotation alone can satisfy; it vanishes for a single composition. For copper and lead, the sensitivity reaches dₕₐₜ ₘ-d_gsimeq3.4×10⁻⁸, and 4.9×10⁻¹⁰ with upgraded accelerometers.

articles.title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a 2+2 arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector qv proportional to the charge contrast ΔabaralphaAB between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor KULDM(t)=gv_φ(t)otimesqv, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of m_φ. The axis of qv is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition KULDM(I-Pq)=0 at every instant, for any gv_φ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition qv=0. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches dₕₐₜ ₘ-d_gsimeq3.4×10⁻⁸ for the baseline instrument and 4.9×10⁻¹⁰ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.

articles.title: Energy resolving optical transition-edge sensor approaching fundamental limits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transition-edge sensors (TES) have long held promise for exhibiting single-photon spectral resolution with near-unity detection efficiency, no read noise, and negligible dark counts. A TES detector capable of simultaneously achieving these traits could be revolutionary in fields including quantum computing, quantum sensing, biological imaging, and the detection of life on alien worlds by spectroscopy of exoplanet atmospheres. The applicability of optical TES detectors in these fields has been limited by energy resolution results that differ significantly from the theoretical expectations. We report significant enhancement of the single-photon energy resolution of tungsten (W) TESs by mitigation of athermal phonon loss during the photon-absorption energy down-conversion cascade. Implementing barriers to phonon loss dramatically increased the TES energy resolution (delta E). We achieve delta E of 34 meV - 61 meV, with resolving power (R = E/delta E) of 24 - 43, in a band spanning 1550 nm - 471 nm. All relevant electrical/thermal device parameters are explored in order to model theoretical limits to delta E imposed by noise, and provide an estimate of the athermal phonon trapping factor. Based on a simple model of electrical, thermal, and phonon escape noise sources, we estimate a phonon trapping factor approaching 90% for our best performing TES architecture. These results bring optical TES technology closer to theoretical predictions and to achieving the ambitious goals of photon-starved optical spectroscopy and fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.

articles.title: MR-ToF-assisted In-Source Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy at IGISOL
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-Reflection Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometer (MR-ToF-MS) assisted in-source laser resonance ionization spectroscopy (RIS) has been implemented at the Ion Guide Isotope Separator On-Line (IGISOL) facility, University of Jyväskylä. Exotic nuclei, produced via fusion-evaporation reactions, are stopped and neutralized in a hot-cavity catcher, and selectively laser-ionized through a multi-step resonance ionization scheme before being transported to the MR-ToF-MS device. This combination of techniques is aimed at optically probing the very exotic N=Z nuclei in the immediate vicinity of ¹⁰⁰Sn. The laser system, hot-cavity ion source, isobaric purification and detection stages are described. A representative hyperfine-structure spectrum of the proton-rich silver isotope ¹⁰¹Ag is presented as a case example.

articles.title: Study of neutron flux redistribution and shadowing effect in rod worth measurements with the rod drop experiment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates neutron flux redistribution and the shadowing effect between control rods during rod-worth measurements using the rod-drop experiment. A simulation-based instrumental calibration methodology is proposed to account for spatial effects on neutron detector responses and improve the accuracy of reactivity measurements. The IPEN/MB-01 research reactor was modeled using the MCNP Monte Carlo neutron transport code. Reactivity behavior during the initial transient of the rod-drop experiment (t < 10 s) was evaluated and compared with experimental measurements using the source-jerk method. The methodology quantifies control rod shadowing and detector-dependent neutron flux redistribution, allowing correction factors to be established for the measured reactivity. Control-bank worth values obtained through the stable-period method were adopted as reference measurements. The reported maximum deviations from the reference values were 0.5% and 11.3%, respectively. The results demonstrate the relevance of spatial neutron flux effects, control rod interactions, and detector calibration in rod-drop experiments, providing a computational and experimental basis for improving control rod worth measurements in research reactors.

articles.title: Observation of Non-Equilibrium Phonon Loss Across a Solid-Superfluid Interface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We measure the performance of an athermal phonon calorimeter in vacuum and in thermal contact with superfluid ⁴He. Using a cryogenic photon calibration system, we show that the superfluid suppresses the collection of the phonon signal by over 99%. We conclude that submerged sensors will not benefit TESSERACT's superfluid helium dark matter target, but that superfluid helium may be useful to superconducting qubits as a sink for athermal phonons generated by radiation and other spontaneous sources. Our measurement is the first probe of solid-to-superfluid phonon transmission at energies higher than those stably supportable by the superfluid. We discuss thermal flow inside the calorimeter, as well as systematics from an alternative calibration scheme.

articles.title: A trap-based platform for cooling and laser spectroscopy of fast ions toward radioactive-ion applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on the first experiments with the Stopping and Trapping of Radioactive Isotopes for Precision Experiments (STRIPE) segmented linear Paul trap. The intent for this apparatus is to serve as an efficient capture and laser-cooling trap for radioactive isotopes produced at radioactive ion beam facilities. We demonstrate the deceleration of 10 keV ion beams and their trapping and laser cooling into Coulomb crystals. As an initial spectroscopic benchmark, the dipole-forbidden 5s ²S₁/₂ → 4d ²D₅/₂ transition in ⁸⁸Sr⁺ was driven, partially resolving the Zeeman structure and yielding a Gaussian linewidth of 14.5(8) MHz, with the residual width attributed to the ions' micromotion. The lifetime of the metastable 4d ²D₅/₂ state was measured to be 0.325(5)ₛₜₐₜ(4)ₛyₛ s, uncorrected for collisional quenching. Several measurements to quantify the cooling timescale, the detection rate of the photon collection region and the trap storage lifetime were also performed. The developed technique will allow radioactive ion beams to be decelerated and cooled for precision spectroscopy measurements.

articles.title: Real-time Electron Tagging by Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy in the PTOLEMY experiment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The PTOLEMY project aims at measuring the neutrino mass and, in the future, the Cosmic Neutrino Background from Tritium endpoint measurement. The Radio-Frequency (RF) Tracker is a sub-detector with the goal of measuring in real time the electrons by exploiting the Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy. In this work, an overview of the PTOLEMY project is given together with the design, simulation, construction and commissioning of the RF Tracker prototype: the Electron Trap. The measurements and data analysis of the Electron Trap are presented, establishing the primary path for the development of the RF Tracker.

articles.title: Equilibrium Elongation of Charged Nanoclusters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When internal electrostatic stresses from electron repulsions overcome surface tension, charged nanoclusters elongate. However, the exact shape they reach at equilibrium has been unknown. We present an analytical model for the equilibrium structure of charged ellipsoidal nanoclusters via a free energy analysis. Energy maps are constructed that determine the equilibrium states as a function of cluster size, net charge, surface tension, and local curvature. The model is compared with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters having solvated electrons. Despite the discreteness of the simulated atoms and electrons, both the predictions of the continuum analytical model for elongation and the equilibrium elongated shape show good agreement. The model could therefore predict nanocluster shape evolution in astrophysical and laboratory complex plasmas and atmospheric aerosols.

articles.title: Oversampled Filter Bank Channelizer for Cryogenic Detectors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the field programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of an oversampled gener- alized DFT (GDFT) filter bank, optimized for its usage in the readout of cryogenic detectors, such as the microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID). A polyphase structure is derived underlin- ing the efficiency of complex valued subband processing, raised by a GDFT modulation. For the latter, a fast Fourier algorithm realization may be used, yielding a highly efficient polyphase imple- mentation for arbitrary integer decimation ratios. The filter bank is tested through a 16-channel GDFT channelizer. The implementation is based on the Xilinx Zynq family of FPGAs and aims to show the data reuse and flexibility offered by the GDFT channelizer structure. General design criteria are summarized for the 16-channel polyphase filter bank channelizer. The performance in hardware resource usage is also presented, taking into account one of the main objetives of the current physics experiments, aiming to have extremely large readout format.

articles.title: Influence of transverse oscillatory shear on the viscous fingering instability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oscillatory shear can delay the onset of viscous fingering. In addition, uniaxial translational shear also breaks the symmetry of the resulting pattern so that the interface evolves differently depending on its direction of propagation relative to the shear axis. We observe a delayed fingering onset and reduced subsequent finger growth rate for all directions as shear speed or amplitude increases. However, shear widens fingers growing in the direction perpendicular to shear and elongates those in the parallel directions. After onset, neighboring fingers in the perpendicular directions can reconnect near their base when the shear amplitude exceeds approximately five times the excess linear finger wavelength at the onset. Concentration profiles reveal smoother azimuthal edges and overlapping structures behind the tips. These observations show that shear smears individual fingers and connects neighboring ones. This correlates lateral fingering interactions with radial propagation.

articles.title: An Inverse-Designed Multilayer Selective Emitter for High-Efficiency Thermophotovoltaics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High thermophotovoltaic (TPV) conversion efficiencies have typically relied on photovoltaic cells that reflect sub-bandgap radiation back toward the emitter. Here, we numerically investigate an alternative approach in which spectral selectivity is engineered primarily on the emitter side. We optimize an emitter consisting of 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten, for coupling to a GaSb cell with an antireflection coating and an Au mirror. A detailed-balance framework incorporates polarization- and angle-resolved emissivity, multiple reflections, and Auger nonradiative recombination. At an emitter temperature of 1500 K, the optimized structure suppresses 97.1% of the incident-blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power at the source; a further 1.9% is returned to the emitter by the cell, leaving 1.0% absorbed parasitically in the cell. The resulting modeled radiative-to-electrical conversion efficiency reaches 47.0%, compared with 30.8% for a SiC emitter paired with the same cell, while maintaining a comparable maximum electrical power density.
