These findings indicate that emitter-side spectral engineering could substantially relax cell-side photon-recycling requirements and provide significant improvement in TPV conversion.

articles.title: A passive, battery-free flexible metasurface for implantable millimetre-wave radar glucose sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous glucose monitors (CGM) break the skin barrier and require periodic sensor replacement. We investigated whether a passive, battery-free flexible metasurface, implanted beneath tissue and read by a commercial 60 GHz radar, can track blood glucose levels. The metasurface contained no electronics or reagents. We fitted a conical helix to the in-phase and quadrature radar signals across the frequency sweep and used its mean radius (the spiral radius) as the glucose-dependent feature. We tested glucose concentrations of 25 to 400 mg/dL in saline solution with and without the metasurface, and 196 to 596 mg/dL of total glucose in porcine whole blood beneath ex vivo porcine tissue and in a murine cadaver model with pulsatile blood flow. The metasurface was essential for achieving a monotonic sensor response; in saline, the coefficient of determination (R²) of a logarithmic fit increased from 0.18 without the metasurface to 0.90 with it. In a murine (rat) cadaver model, the signal's spiral radius increased monotonically with glucose concentration despite pulsatile flow (R² = 0.91), and this monotonic behavior persisted through up to 6 mm of tissue. Although sensitivity decreased at higher glucose levels, each discrete concentration step remained clearly detectable. These results demonstrate that a shallow, passive implant paired with a commercial radar can effectively track blood glucose without requiring onboard electronics or batteries.

articles.title: Polarization Lifetime as a Design Axis for Task-Adaptive Photonic Reservoir Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic time-delayed reservoir computing (TDRC) based on conventional Class B lasers is limited by fragile external cavity mode (ECM) locking dynamics. Here, we show that engineering the polarization lifetime (T₂) with the carrier lifetime (T) reshapes the topology and stability of TDRC. Comparing four laser classes (Class A, Class B, Class C_A, and Class C_B), a finite polarization lifetime acts as an intrinsic dynamic filter, dissolving discrete ECM chaos grids into continuous, phase-tolerant operational basins. Information processing capacity (IPC) decomposition further exposes distinct computational profiles: matched Class C_A achieves the highest nonlinear capacity (16.28) and the highest total capacity (19.29), whereas Class A exhibits the highest linear capacity (4.70). A task-dependent reversal governs hardware design: Class A and Class C_A achieve comparable, and the lowest, NRMSE on short-horizon Mackey--Glass prediction (0.0103 and 0.0105, within one standard deviation), while the time-scale-matched Class C_A dominates the higher-dimensional Lorenz (0.0506) and the experimental Santa Fe (0.4251) tasks. Linear-IPC ranking matches Mackey-Glass accuracy; nonlinear-IPC ranking matches the Lorenz exactly and Santa Fe within the mask-to-mask uncertainty. Under realistic quantum noise, resilience is dictated mainly by T, not T₂: Class A retains the lowest NRMSE (0.47) even at spontaneous emission factor β = 10⁻¹, whereas the long-carrier Class B degrades (0.98). A residual T₂-mediated benefit of 20% persists in the slow-carrier Class C_B (0.78 vs. 0.98). Time-scale engineering thus offers a nuanced design paradigm for optical computing, where optimal hardware is set by the task's time-scale hierarchy rather than a universal figure of merit.

articles.title: Sign-switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature of liquid jets by microscopic laser-induced cavitation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Localized forcing of liquid jets can trigger Rayleigh-Plateau breakup at low perturbation amplitudes or explosive fragmentation at high amplitudes, while controlled bending in the intermediate regime has remained unexplored. We show that femtosecond-laser-induced cavitation, seeded at the interface of a 100 micrometre-diameter water jet, produces a selectable curvature in 0.4-1 mm long segments. Cavitation rupturing at the liquid-air interface drives fast outward jetting and induces a slower recoil on the opposite boundary, which evolves on the capillary-inertial timescale and results in curving of the liquid segment. The curvature is governed by three laser parameters. Off-axis laser illumination on the jet shifts the refractive caustics and redistributes energy deposition between the front and rear interfaces. The resulting recoil imbalance determines the curvature sign, with a straight configuration in the balanced case. Laser energy offers additional control over the recoil impulse via plasma defocusing and nonlinear absorption in the liquid jet, where the response is bounded by axisymmetric deformation at low energy and explosive vaporization at high energy. Repetition rate sets the spacing between successive cavitation events and hence the length of the bent segment. Curvature extends across the segment for lengths of 6-10 jet diameters; shorter segments undergo Rayleigh-Plateau breakup, whereas longer ones bend mainly near their retracting ends. Our results offer a platform for optofluidic control of switchable and tunable macroscopic curvature in flowing liquid jets.

articles.title: Spectral dependence of Berry phase and topological bound states in the continuum in Möbius resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Möbius strip and the bulk Möbius resonator are of great interest to specialists in optics, acoustics, and quantum physics. Despite the apparent simplicity of the object and numerous publications, the Möbius resonator, like a magic box, still holds many surprises. Here, we demonstrate experimentally, theoretically and with a simple illustrative example that in a "thin" Möbius resonator with an odd number of twists, the longitudinal wavenumber is determined by the additional phase shift π (traditionally called the geometrical Berry phase) only if the total transverse index of the photonic mode is odd. For an even index, the Berry phase is zero. We also discovered "topological" quasi-bound states in the continuum in Möbius resonators with a square cross-section; they differ from "ordinary" ones by the exchange of azimuthal indices of the interfering modes in the anti-crossing region. Finally, we demonstrate an example of resonant topology by determining the dependence of the Berry phase on the Möbius resonator geometry based on the frequency difference between the eigenmodes of planar ring resonators and those of Möbius resonators. The discovered effects significantly expand our knowledge of the topology of single resonators and promise new practical applications.

articles.title: Symmerty-Engineered Moire Metasurface for Multibeam Control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moiré metasurfaces offer a versatile platform for wavefront engineering through the relative rotation of periodic structures. Despite extensive demonstrations of continuous beam steering, the physical mechanisms governing beam multiplicity remain poorly understood, hindering the systematic design of multibeam radiation states. Here, we establish a predictive framework for engineering beam multiplicity in reflective moiré metasurfaces based on the dominant Fourier coefficients of their constituent patterns. We reveal that the rotational symmetry of these Fourier components in reciprocal space fully determines the symmetry of the resulting moiré unit cell and, consequently, its radiation characteristics. By further incorporating their phase information, both beam multiplicity and steering trajectories can be accurately predicted. We demonstrate this approach using reflective moiré metasurfaces constructed from patterns with p6m, p3m1, and p4m plane-group symmetries, achieving one-, two-, three-, four-, and six-beam radiation states with continuously tunable steering trajectories. Beyond symmetry-based design, we identify two additional degrees of freedom for beam multiplicity control. Selecting different rotation centers reshapes the phase distributions of the dominant Fourier coefficients, enabling further manipulation of beam multiplicity and spatial arrangement, while varying the relative twist angle alters the pairing of Fourier components, inducing transitions between distinct beam multiplicities. These findings establish a systematic framework for versatile and reconfigurable multibeam wavefront engineering.

articles.title: Tunable Hybridization of Whispering Gallery Modes in High-Index Photonic Molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic molecules formed by coupled dielectric microresonators provide a platform for controlling collective optical modes, yet the interplay between molecular topology, resonator detuning, and dielectric environment in determining their spectral response remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we systematically quantify the evolution of Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) hybridization in high-index TiO₂ and perovskite coated TiO₂ microresonators with molecular topology, and establish the corresponding effective inter-cavity coupling using a combined numerical and analytical analysis. We further show that perovskite-shell incorporation provides a diameter and thickness-dependent modification of the effective coupling, producing a non-monotonic response rather than a uniform suppression of coupling. Despite the resulting closely spaced hybridized resonances in the high-index perovskite environment, the supermodes remain spectrally resolvable, with Q-factor of order (10³) for representative modes. The observed spectral splitting is quantitatively related to the effective inter-cavity coupling strengths, revealing a non-monotonic coupling response to perovskite-shell incorporation that depends on resonator size and shell thickness. These results establish molecular topology and dielectric environment as distinct parameters for controlling WGM hybridization, inter-cavity coupling, and spectral response, providing a basis for the design of coupled resonator systems for applications in optical sensing, filtering, switching, and other resonant photonic devices.

articles.title: The effect of particle shape on sunlight exposure in a wind-driven free-surface flow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how nonspherical marine particles, such as microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice, are exposed to sunlight near the water surface in wind-driven surface boundary layer conditions. We measure the depth and orientation of these particles in a laboratory wind-wave tank, then use this data to model how much sunlight the particles would be exposed to in an aquatic environment. In particular, we explore how their orientation affects their sunlight exposure in these conditions, since most studies to date do not account for orientation, turbulent shear flow, and wind-waves at the water surface. We find that in all cases, particles prefer certain orientations, and this causes the average sunlight exposure of the particles to be 5 to 40% higher than would be expected if their orientations were random. Further, we find that the mean irradiance depends on the ratio of the particle mixing length Lₘ to the light decay lengthscale λ, and the nature of this dependence differs between disks and rods. Disks experience disproportionately greater mean irradiance at smaller Lₘ/λ due to the vertical variation in their orientations. These results have important implications for accurately estimating the sunlight exposure of particles in the surface boundary layer.

articles.title: A charge-dependent electron emission yield from electron irradiated dielectrics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The total electron emission yield (TEEY) of dielectric surfaces may vary during electron irradiation owing to charge accumulation within the material. In the present work, the generation, transport, and escape formulation of Dionne is extended by introducing an additional attenuation of secondary electrons that depends on trapped positive charge. The resulting emission law is coupled to a charge-balance equation, allowing the TEEY to be calculated as a function of incident energy and injected charge. The model is examined using measurements on polycrystalline Al2O3, from which effective cross sections describing interactions between trapped charge and secondary electrons are determined. Their mean value is then used to predict the evolution of the TEEY curves without further adjustment. Finally, an analytical approximation of the nonlinear charging law is derived to facilitate the implementation in electron-irradiation simulations.

articles.title: KELP v1.0: an agent-ready Lagrangian particle tracker for unstructured meshes and HEALPix grids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lagrangian particle tracking follows virtual particles in the velocity fields of an ocean model to study transport pathways, connectivity and dispersion. Setting up such a study takes many technical steps, and this work is increasingly done with coding agents, programs in which a language model writes code, runs it and checks the result. We present KELP v1.0, the Kinematic Engine for Lagrangian Particles, a tracker for unstructured ocean-model meshes and HEALPix grids that is built to be operated by such agents. KELP computes two- and three-dimensional trajectories with established methods on triangular, quadrilateral and mixed meshes, with global FESOM2 and coastal FESOM-C meshes as examples, and on HEALPix, the equal-area grid on which kilometre-scale digital twins distribute their output. Documentation and short task instructions, called skills, tell an agent how to prepare releases and configurations, run calculations and process the trajectories. An agent prepared and ran all experiments of this paper with these skills, and most of the preparation was completed within hours. In a controlled evaluation, the skills raised the completeness of study files prepared by five language models from 75-93% to 88-100%. KELP reproduced the particle distributions of two other trackers on the same fields. Trajectories on HEALPix fields converged to those on the model mesh as the pixels were refined. After one year, the median distance between the two was 1.6 km at a pixel spacing of 25.5 km. HEALPix output can therefore be used for Lagrangian studies of ensemble statistics when the original mesh is not available. In a 63-year calculation with 7.92 million particles released in the Beaufort Gyre, transport from the gyre to Fram Strait took years to decades, and the run took 3 h 36 min on one 128-core node. A test tracked 10¹⁰ particles on a HEALPix mesh of 35.5 million wet surface nodes.

articles.title: Deformation Kinetics of Charged Nanoclusters via Surface Diffusion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-temperature charged nanoclusters deform, primarily via surface diffusion, when surface electrostatic stresses and surface tension stresses are not balanced. We derive an analytical model for the kinetics of this process, based on the cluster size, net charge, surface tension, local curvature, temperature, and diffusivity. The model predicts the deformation time when either surface tension or electrostatic stress dominates, leading respectively to the collapse or elongation of the cluster. Comparison with molecular dynamics simulations of ice nanoclusters with solvated electrons shows quantitative agreement with a single fitted parameter. The model can predict the deformation kinetics of charged nanoclusters in atmospheric aerosols and complex plasmas.

articles.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17731v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm²/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm²/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.

articles.title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17906v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach. Furthermore, we investigate device-independent certification and causal inequalities applied to an entangled quantum system, and show that in this regime too, the notions of trajectories and of a strict causal order are perfectly preserved.

articles.title: Spin-adapted sample-based quantum diagonalization with randomized time evolution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum algorithms based on the classical post-processing of measurement samples have emerged as effective and robust methods to approximate low-energy wavefunctions of many-body quantum systems on present-day and early-fault-tolerant quantum devices. This paper introduces a generic framework for enforcing spin symmetry within these approaches. We tailor this framework to SqDRIFT, a sample-based quantum diagonalization variant that uses the qDRIFT randomized compilation protocol to generate the quantum samples. We discuss how three key components of SqDRIFT (the initial-state preparation, the construction of the time-evolution circuits, and the classical post-processing) can be adapted to incorporate spin symmetry. We show that spin-pure circuits alone are not sufficient, since the sampled determinants generally span a subspace that is not closed under hatS², and we restore this closure by completing the sampled electronic configurations. In classical simulations of 4-aminobenzonitrile and of an [Fe(NH₃)₄]²⁺ model complex, and in experiments on an IBM quantum processor for the oxo-Mn(Salen) complex, this spin-adapted post-processing yields roots that are exact spin eigenfunctions at every subspace size. On hardware, it does so with diagonalized subspaces two to three orders of magnitude smaller than those of the conventional constructions for the same circuit depth.

articles.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay tSR and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number N. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode. We find that number fluctuations enhance emission and that the ensemble-averaged emission trace encodes the initial number distribution. We show how to reconstruct second-order correlations from photon counting with finite detection efficiency and temporal resolution, even when the full distribution cannot be resolved. For atom loss at rate r, we derive exact results for the population dynamics and show that the peak intensity scaling is governed by the single scaling variable gᵣ=r tSR. The peak remains quadratic in N for gᵣ<1, follows logarithmically corrected subquadratic power laws for gᵣ>1, and crosses over to linear scaling under strong loss with gᵣgg1.

articles.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector k=0, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands. Our results provide a useful theoretical framework for interpreting existing experiments and serve as a guide for future experimental investigations of this system.

articles.title: Fine-tuned atomistic foundation model for accurate sodium-carbon chemistry in Na-ion batteries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. Hard carbon features diverse local structural motifs, including defective and curved graphitic regions, amorphous regions, and closed/open pores. Motivated by its importance for Na-ion batteries, we systematically evaluate existing pretrained foundation models based on the MACE architecture across different local Na/C motifs. We find that the pretrained models fail to accurately capture Na-Na and Na-C interactions for metallic Na clusters on graphene. To recover a DFT-level energetic description, we employ targeted fine-tuning, showing that it can describe the energetic stability of local motifs and achieve sufficient transferability to unseen Na/C environments. With the developed fine-tuned model, we establish a correlation between closed-pore radius in hard carbon and plateau voltage, showing that the small pores contribute at larger voltages than large ones, suggesting thus how the developed fine-tuned foundation model can link atomistic information with materials design for complex bonding environments.

articles.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions. Encoding each qubit as one fermion in two orbitals, we prove that the representable qubit marginals form an exposed face of the set of N-representable fermionic reduced density matrices, selected by the vanishing of every site-occupation variance. Complete hierarchies of fermionic representability conditions therefore transfer exactly to qubits. Applications to frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings show that the (2,3)-positivity conditions are exact at the Majumdar--Ghosh point and accurate to about 0.5% at criticality. Because the conditions hold for any quantum state, they also provide a framework for mitigating measurement errors on qubit-based quantum devices.

articles.title: Experimenters' Free Will and Quantum Certainty
articles.abstract: arXiv:1211.1917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Physics has long lived with a split personality that desires determinism for measured systems while demanding that experimenters decide what to measure on a whim. Intriguingly, such a free will assumption for experimenters has thwarted many attempts to provide a satisfactory explanation of how quantum probabilities evolve to clear-cut measurements. An overview of this quantum measurement problem is presented without equations, and the lesson is drawn that denial of experimenters' free will may be the only workable solution. A holistic view is offered of a self-consistent superdetermined spacetime block universe of events. The goal of future research is to develop the underlying principle that generates this Escher-like global pattern.

articles.title: A fast and rigorous numerical tool to measure length-scale artifacts in molecular simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.01442v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The two-sided Bogoliubov inequality for classical and quantum many-body systems is a theorem that provides rigorous bounds on the free-energy cost of partitioning a given system into two or more independent subsystems. This theorem motivates the definition of a quality factor which directly quantifies the degree of statistical-mechanical consistency achieved by a given simulation box size. A major technical merit of the theorem is that, for systems with two-body interactions and a known radial distribution function, the quality factor can be computed by evaluating just three six-dimensional integrals. We present a numerical algorithm for computing the quality factor and demonstrate its consistency with respect to results in the literature obtained from simulations performed at different box sizes.

articles.title: DD-03B: Target-level analysis of ligand-protein dissociation pathways reveals ligand-specific exit pathways weakly coupled to binding affinity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.06761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Protein-ligand interactions are conventionally described by a structure and a binding affinity (Kd). Kinetic simulation datasets have grown rapidly, but most analyses remain structure-centred and RMSD-based, and the kinetic information carried by the trajectories is rarely extracted. Here we analyse 766,550 complete dissociation trajectories for 15,540 protein-ligand complexes grouped into 3,687 UniProt accessions. Each trajectory is reduced to a uniform record of 119 descriptors-ligand and structure size, trajectory statistics, the pathway distribution of escape events, and pocket and escape-volume descriptors-so that records from different systems can be compared, joined and searched. This tokenisation shows that the pocket and the ligand act on the same quantity at different levels: the pocket defines the repertoire of exits, and the ligand sets the weights. In open sites the repertoire collapses to one broad mode and affinity tracks ligand size and contact; in confined pockets the exit ensemble splits into several channels whose weights follow ligand size rather than binding affinity. UniProt grouping is a convenient classification above the PDB entry but not the right final unit: two systems illustrate domain separation and degeneracy, and a structural classifier would be preferable. We present the framework as a general analysis paradigm for molecular dynamics trajectory libraries.

articles.title: Improved lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal-loss channel
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.27792v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The bosonic thermal-loss channel is a fundamental model for quantum communication. This Gaussian channel models the transmission of bosonic systems subject to both loss and thermal noise. It describes many practical systems, including optical fibres, waveguides and free-space links, where background thermal noise is significant. Determining the channel's two-way-assisted quantum capacity, the maximum rate at which quantum information can be transmitted reliably through the channel with two-way classical assistance, remains an open problem. Here, we improve upon the best known lower bound for this capacity for a wide range of channel parameters. We achieve this by combining an improved qubit-bosonic distribution technique with a recently introduced technique for discovering entanglement distillation protocols.

articles.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. We make two technical contributions on top of DTS that are particularly relevant for AI-for-science applications. First, we show how to use existing property-conditional generative models (e.g., models fine-tuned for classifier-free guidance) as guided proposals inside DTS, without distorting the target distribution. Second, we extend DTS to multi-objective sampling, so that a single search produces samples spanning an entire Pareto front. We instantiate both adaptations on de novo crystal generation: improving the stability of crystals generated by different models, using pretrained conditional models to generate crystals belonging to rare space groups or with high bulk modulus, and generating crystals along a Pareto front of high dielectric constant and high bandgap materials. Across these tasks, DTS-based inference-time adaptation successfully improves model outputs without modifying the models themselves.

articles.title: SURFACE: Preference Distribution Matching on Pareto Fronts via Scalarization Steering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constructing a finite Pareto representation requires allocating a limited number of solutions across the Pareto front (PF). A desired preference distribution specifies this allocation by assigning more solutions to some PF regions and fewer to others. Scalarization generates Pareto solutions by varying objective weights and solving single-objective problems. However, a distribution of scalarization weights generally does not translate into the same distribution of Pareto solutions along the PF, because the weight-to-solution map is nonlinear and unknown in advance.To account for this distortion, we introduce SURFACE (Scalarization Updates for Redistributing Finite Approximations with Chart Estimation}), which adaptively updates scalarization weights to match a desired PF distribution. SURFACE estimates how each region of the weight grid corresponds to an area of the PF from the current scalarized solutions, then redistributes the weights accordingly. The method supports parallel, warm-started, inexact optimization with standard single-objective solvers. Theoretically, we establish that, under the stated regularity conditions, SURFACE achieves linear convergence of the preference distribution mismatch to a finite-resolution error floor of O(N⁻²/⁽M⁻¹⁾), where N is the number of adaptive weights and M is the number of objectives. Empirically, experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate improved target-mass balance and PF coverage compared with established baselines.

articles.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable use of large language models (LLMs) requires uncertainty estimates that separate ambiguity intrinsic to a prompt from genuine knowledge gaps. Bayesian and deep-ensemble methods deliver this aleatoric/epistemic decomposition in principle, but are computationally prohibitive at LLM scale and require white-box access. Existing black-box methods, in contrast, summarize to a single scalar that cannot make the distinction. We introduce a two-level ensemble that bridges this gap. Stochastic decoding of a fixed prompt forms the inner ensemble; meaning-preserving semantic perturbations of the prompt form the outer ensemble. Variability is measured in a continuous embedding space, and the law of total covariance gives an exact within-/between-perturbation decomposition to estimate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty (AU/EU); it requires only black-box sampling access. On top of this estimator, we contribute three theoretical results that ground the framework: (i) a finite-sample bias identity for nested Monte Carlo with a closed-form bias-corrected epistemic estimator; (ii) a Bayesian bridge bounding the gap between perturbation-population AU/EU and Bayesian targets; and (iii) a separation result identifying a class of failure modes that any consistency-only black-box method provably misses while perturbation-based EU detects. Across five short QA benchmarks and four instruction-tuned LLMs spanning two families and two scales, our estimator is competitive with strong white-box baselines, and at a matched generation budget it matches leading black-box methods on error ranking while decomposing AU and EU; controlled paired interventions show that AU and EU respond selectively to distinct, actionable sources of failure: prompt ambiguity and model knowledge gaps; and a long-form pilot on the NQ long-answer split shows the framework extends to claim-level factuality without retraining.

articles.title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard coding-agent benchmarks primarily evaluate binary task success, treating execution as a black box and obscuring the behaviors that produce those outcomes. We analyze a large corpus of 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 agent configurations spanning 117 unique models. To enable comparisons across heterogeneous agent interfaces, we develop a rule-based parser that maps raw execution traces to high-level actions such as repository search, file editing, and test execution, and audit its predictions against a six-model consensus reference on 500 events. We find that agents with similar solve rates can nevertheless differ substantially in how they explore, modify and verify code. Moreover, without using task outcomes, token counts, or tool names as features, aggregate behavioral profiles retrieve the corresponding agent stack across disjoint repository sets and programming languages, although task composition is not fully controlled in the cross-repository setting. Through analyses of frontier models and agent scaffolds, we further show that scaffold choice and reasoning effort systematically shift agents' search, editing, and testing behavior. We release the deterministic parser together with the full annotation and analysis pipeline alongside an annotated trajectory subset.

articles.title: Tractable Importance Sampling for Monte Carlo Privacy Accounting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating tight Differential Privacy (DP) parameters for DP matrix factorization with privacy amplification by sampling requires analyzing high-dimensional, correlated Gaussian mixtures. Because integrating these mixture distributions to find the exact privacy failure probability (δ) is analytically intractable, these mechanisms are typically analyzed using Monte Carlo accounting. However, standard sampling suffers from prohibitive variance when estimating small δ associated with strict privacy guarantees, which in turn requires a large sample complexity, making Monte Carlo accounting inefficient. We demonstrate that Monte Carlo accounting can be made much more efficient via importance sampling. We give a shifted importance sampling proposal distribution parameterized by a stretch factor α > 1. We prove a closed-form bound B(α) < 1 on the support of the importance-weighted estimator that holds identically for both directions of the hockey-stick divergence, show that B is log-convex so that the optimal α is a one-dimensional root-finding problem, and show that the resulting estimator seamlessly plugs into the KL-Hoeffding verification protocol used by past work, with a sample complexity reduced by exactly a factor of 1/B(α^*).

articles.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but sacrifice reproducibility, since pages and data drift between runs. Moreover, existing benchmarks do not meaningfully evaluate whether agents can understand and use audio and video content embedded within web tasks. To address these gaps, we introduce WebArena-Pro, a benchmark comprising 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications in six domain categories, spanning distinct interface conventions, workflows, and data models. Across the evaluated agents, the best performance is achieved by both Codex with GPT 6.1 Sol and Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 at 62.3%, followed by OpenCode with Kimi 3.1 Pro at 60.7%. The strongest GenericAgent configurations, Gemini 3.1 Pro omni and Gemma4 31B, both achieve 30.3%. Among reproducible, human-curated web agent benchmarks, WebArena-Pro provides the broadest application coverage and the most comprehensive multimodal support to date. The benchmark treats audio and video as core observations alongside text and vision, with dedicated actions for extracting information from each. WebArena-Pro runs each task in isolation and supports reproducible, parallel evaluation. Tasks are authored through a dedicated annotator interface, filtered by LLM-assisted triage, and finally validated by humans before release. Project page: https://webarena-pro.github.io

articles.title: Structure makes quantum circuits trainable
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The scalability of variational quantum algorithms is limited by barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in system size. This worst-case result raises fundamental questions about the trainability of quantum AI models. We present a major advance towards resolving this trainability question by answering whether a given quantum circuit has a barren plateau. We do this using an analytical framework that bounds the gradient variance for arbitrary input states ρ and observables M by decomposing the unitary representation of the associated compact Lie group. When the circuit segments on both sides of a gate form 2-designs, we obtain the variance exactly and prove a sufficient condition for trainability: if ρotⁱmes ² and Motⁱmes ² are sufficiently concentrated on the same irreducible invariant subspace of polynomial dimension, and the differentiated gate moves this subspace by an inverse-polynomial amount, then the gradient variance is at least inverse-polynomial. We further present a sampling algorithm that estimates the gradient variance from runs of the ansatz, without constructing the representation-theoretic projectors. Our algorithm decides whether the variance exceeds a tolerance τ with the number of runs polynomial in 1/τ, including cases in which the bounds are inconclusive. This resolves the question of the trainability of the circuit before expensive training procedures.

articles.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.

articles.title: Certified Improvements to Best-Known Thomson-Problem Configurations with a Search Pipeline Built with Large Language Model Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Thomson problem asks for N unit charges on a sphere with minimum Coulomb energy; for large N the best configurations known are curated in the Cambridge Cluster Database, whose largest-N entries were set in October 2026. We report configurations for N = 912, 1382 and 2502 with energies 0.0036186, 0.0109730 and 0.0614033 below the database values, certified by exact integer arithmetic. All three are numerically strict local minima modulo rotations and keep the defect inventory and scar compositions of the database configurations; the database value for N = 912 had been reached by two different methods. Our search runs unconstrained replica-exchange basin hopping from the database configurations, with a shared pool of minima, recombination of improved regions after relabelling by geometry, and gradient-only polishing; replica-exchange basin hopping alone found the N = 912 and 1382 configurations, the former in one of five runs. We built and ran it with large language model agents (Claude, through a chat interface and the Claude Code agent), and we report every search, including those that failed. Two findings matter for others who search the database. Polishing alone lowers two entries by more than the threshold at which our pipeline reports a candidate, which produced two spurious records until candidates were compared with the polished database energies (the polished baseline). A local-relaxation speed-up passed its exactness test yet found nothing in a controlled comparison in which every arm with full relaxation went below the database value within 15 minutes. We distil three practices for computational discovery with large language model agents: calibrate the search code and verify candidates with code separate from the search, compare candidates with the polished baseline, and test design changes in controlled comparisons with pass criteria fixed in advance.

articles.title: Robustness Evaluation of GPU Cloud Pricing Benchmarks under Incomplete Observations: A Controlled Missingness Study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Daily GPU rental-price benchmarks can fail when marketplace quotes are missing. This article stress-tests a fixed equal-weight median rule under four imposed masking mechanisms and four benchmark-level recovery methods. Across 5,800 Monte Carlo realisations in 27 scenarios on 190 held-out days, whole-source outages reduce publication coverage to 0.77 while preserving zero conditional error on published dates; composition-changing loss retains 0.86 coverage but produces 7.74 log points of error. A separate past-only stratum-level ablation reduces error by 4.15 to 6.70 log points in five composition-changing cases, using a richer information set. An observable-signal withholding rule improves the primary error-coverage criterion in 0 of 10 cases. Results concern observed asking-price measurements, not transaction prices or identified real-world missingness mechanisms.

articles.title: Optimizing Drilling Trajectories in Multi-Material Structures Using Quantum Annealers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we present a quantum-hybrid optimization approach for planning drilling trajectories on multi-material structures, with the objective of minimizing total energy consumption. The proposed formulation models the drilling process as a constrained routing problem in which each hole must be visited while accounting for heterogeneous material properties, material-dependent drilling costs and displacement energy, as well as tool-wear penalties. Our method incorporates realistic industrial constraints, including open-path routing and mandatory grouping of holes belonging to the same material to avoid frequent tool-bit changes. The modeled problem is solved using D-Wave's Leap Constrained Quadratic Model Hybrid Solver. To evaluate performance, we benchmark instances ranging from 10 to 55 holes with varying material distributions and cost matrices. The results highlight the capability of quantum-hybrid optimization to handle complex multi-physics constraints and to generate energy-efficient drilling sequences under realistic manufacturing conditions.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is a multi-objective control problem that requires reducing charging time and sustaining high energy throughput while suppressing accelerated degradation and safety-critical electrochemical reactions. Conventional protocols are easy to implement but have limited ability to adapt to variations in battery chemistry, operating conditions, and aging state. Model-based optimization and conventional data-driven control often require accurate models, costly iterative search, or task-specific policies. We develop a large language model (LLM)-empowered intelligent agent for adaptive battery fast-charging control. In this closed-loop framework, the agent interprets structured battery states, generates executable charging actions, observes the resulting battery response, and continuously adjusts subsequent decisions. We construct a large-scale simulation corpus with PyBaMM across five battery chemistries and 11 parameter sets and convert the resulting state-action-response trajectories into structured process data for agent training. Our two-stage strategy combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). SFT establishes battery-control semantics and feasible decision priors from simulation-derived demonstrations. GRPO aligns the agent with a multi-objective control objective covering energy throughput, degradation mitigation, and operational constraints. Closed-loop simulations show that, under matched energy-throughput requirements, the agent achieves longer cycling life than conventional charging baselines and optimization-based strategies across heterogeneous battery configurations. This study provides a simulation-grounded proof of concept for using LLM agents as sequential decision makers in battery management and takes a step toward language-model-enabled control of physical energy systems.

articles.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. Existing systems fall short on two counts: (1) they process sEMG in fixed windows and carry nothing from one window to the next, discarding context accumulated over a session, and (2) they lack any understanding of the linguistic structure that drives typing, so every keystroke is inferred from the muscle signal alone. We propose a fully causal, zero-lookahead sEMG typing decoder built on a state space model (SSM), in which a single model decodes a whole session without windowed partitions, conditioned on what has already been typed. We achieve this by fusing a traditional typing decoder with an efficient autoregressive language model, instilling both sEMG and linguistic understanding in one model. To train such a model for per-character typing rather than whole-word text, we introduce a retokenization method that rewrites ordinary prose as human-like typing, with keystrokes, typos, backspaces and line breaks included, converting WikiText into a large typing corpus where none existed. Our model, having never seen a single sEMG-to-character transcript in typing, achieves a state-of-the-art character error rate of 25.13% on emg2qwerty's cross-user benchmark, a 5.4% relative improvement over the previous best with 6.7 times fewer parameters, while running strictly causally with no future context.

articles.title: GraphScent: Calibrating Directional Relevance Signals for Bounded-Context Code Localization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Running open-weight language models locally on a single consumer GPU requires replacing expanding multi-turn exploration histories with short, stateless code inspections. Stateless repository localization, however, hinges on a foundational question: when a frozen language model evaluates an unedited code entity from a compact view, which structural relationships make its relevance judgment informative about a nearby repair target? Studying Gemma 4 models across 211 real-world Python issues in 86 repositories, we uncover a systematic directional relevance asymmetry: zero-temperature relevance scores on enclosing scopes and upstream callers consistently separate true structural neighbors from hard lexical distractors, whereas scores on downstream callees, peer methods, historical co-change partners, and dense node embeddings remain near chance. Zero-leakage masked-scope probes and regressions controlling for lexical similarity and snippet length confirm that this asymmetry reflects functional role (callers expose symptom entrypoints delegating to defective routines, while downstream helpers appear benign alone) rather than target leakage or surface overlap. Guided by this finding, we introduce GraphScent, a training-free search controller that propagates out-of-repository, relation-conditioned log-likelihood ratios over runtime Typed-AST multigraphs before resolving ties via a single listwise comparison, alongside AST Ripple, a lightweight post-edit check for missed co-edits. Likelihood calibration prevents overconfident smaller models from chasing false-positive callers while lifting exact localization on lexically hard targets from 12.8 to 23.4 percent at 31B within a single-GPU budget.

articles.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption maps. We decouple long-term static urban morphology from short-term dynamic energy consumption. By conditioning on static urban land use, DySENSE can generate realistic, diverse and new static urban imagery with aligned energy maps. By conditioning on dynamic monthly and climate prompts, DySENSE can jointly generate dynamic, monthly energy consumption maps while keeping the urban morphology static. Experiments across four cities (New York, Washington, Norfolk, Busan) demonstrated that DySENSE can generate annotated high-fidelity synthetic energy data using less than 25% labelled data, boosting downstream prediction performance by 8% mIoU, and achieving strong energy dynamic consistency. Compared to existing methods, DySENSE significantly improved prediction performance (8.7% accuracy) and reduced prediction error (9%-18% CVRMSE, ASHRAE). DySENSE offers an effective foundation for energy-efficient cities, peak-load analysis, building performance simulation and dynamic demand response for city, energy, and building science. The data and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/skl24/MUSE2 and https://github.com/kailaisun/DySENSE

articles.title: An In-Silico Audit of Topographic Organization in a Multimodal Brain-Response Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: TRIBE v2 (d'Ascoli et al., 2026) predicts fMRI responses across the cortical surface from video, audio and text. Its authors validated it with category-selective localizers (faces, places, bodies, words) and language contrasts, but not with the classic topographic organization of sensory cortex: retinotopy, tonotopy, and motion selectivity in area MT+. There is a clear architectural reason to expect retinotopy to fail: TRIBE's video features are averaged over space before the response head, which should discard visual-field position. I present mapping stimuli, a fitting pipeline adapted from standard fMRI mapping analyses, and a stand-in model with known ground truth that serves as a positive and negative control, and apply them to TRIBE v2's predictions, comparing the fitted maps with human atlases using spin tests. TRIBE v2 shows a sharp split. There is no contralateral hemifield response and no polar-angle map, robustly across stimulus controls. There is no tonotopic gradient in primary auditory cortex: best frequencies span an interquartile range of only 0.14 octaves across core and belt, and the null persists with loudness-equalized tones. An eccentricity-like gradient appears only when the ring geometry changes, consistent with global image statistics rather than a positional code. In contrast, motion selectivity is strong and precisely localized: 22% of the 1% most motion-selective vertices fall in MT+, which covers 0.42% of cortex. In-silico experiments that depend on feature identity appear viable with TRIBE v2, while those that depend on visual-field or frequency position are not supported by the current model.

articles.title: Self-Building Labs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23826v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still requires extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together. We validate SBL's end-to-end capabilities through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment. By shifting human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable. Project website: https://self-building-labs.github.io/

articles.title: Evolution of shear instability and multi-source precursor characteristics of soft–hard interbedded rock masses
articles.abstract: To address the difficulty of reliably identifying instability precursors during collapse development in soft–hard interbedded rock masses using a single monitoring parameter, two large-scale shear tests were conducted on soft–hard interbedded composite specimens. Digital image correlation (DIC), acoustic emission (AE), RA–AF analysis, and principal component analysis–hierarchical cluster analysis (PCA–HCA) characterized deformation and fracture evolution. Both specimens exhibited four stages: soft-rock compaction, coordinated deformation, crack propagation, and crack coalescence and instability. DIC revealed that scattered high-strain zones progressively localized near interfaces and flaw tips, ultimately forming a continuous band. RA–AF analysis indicated that tensile or mixed tensile–shear events dominated the first two stages, whereas shear-type events exceeded 50% during crack propagation. PCA–HCA classified AE signals into five types. Type 4 signals increased abruptly during crack development and coalescence and exhibited shear-fracture characteristics. Rapid expansion and incipient connection of high-strain zones, an increased shear-event proportion, and an abrupt rise in the Type 4 proportion constituted a multi-source precursor criterion for the transition from coordinated deformation to crack propagation. These findings provide an experimental basis for stage identification and monitoring-based early warning of collapse in soft–hard interbedded rock masses.

articles.title: Effect of Nb2O5-TiO2 Co-doping on the Properties of ITO Targets
articles.abstract: With the development of high-performance high-end display devices and the iterative upgrading of photovoltaic cells, higher requirements have been imposed on ITO targets. The preparation technology for ITO targets with high carrier mobility has therefore become a research focus in related fields. Conventional ITO targets have relatively low carrier mobility (30–40 cm²·V⁻¹·s⁻¹), making it difficult to meet the performance requirements of transparent conductive oxide targets for the next generation of high-end displays and photovoltaic devices. In this study, 0.1 wt% Nb2O5 and 0.1 wt% TiO2 were co-doped into an indium tin oxide powder (In₂O₃:SnO₂ = 9:1, wt%). After die pressing and cold isostatic pressing, ITO green bodies were prepared and sintered in an oxygen atmosphere at 1450°C for 6 h, yielding an ITO target with a relative density of 99.54%, a resistivity of 1.940×10⁻⁴ Ω·cm, and a carrier mobility of 57.4 cm2·V− 1·s− 1. The results showed that an appropriate amount of Nb2O5-TiO2 co-doping could improve the carrier mobility of ITO targets. In addition, Nb2O5-TiO2 co-doping could reduce the sintering temperature of the ITO target from 1550°C to 1450°C. This study achieved the preparation of an ITO target with high density and high mobility while reducing the sintering temperature, providing a reference for the development of low-temperature sintering processes for high-performance ITO transparent conductive targets and for research on TCO materials for high-end displays and photovoltaic devices.

articles.title: A Preliminary Biosecurity Audit of Phylo’s Biomni Lab
articles.abstract: Biological research agents combine language-model reasoning with retrieval, code execution, and scientific tools, creating a need for evaluations that distinguish response content from demonstrated capability. We conducted an exploratory audit of Phylo’s Biomni Lab using 18 matched biological topics across six task categories. Each topic was expressed in three prompting conditions that jointly varied vocabulary, professional framing, and technical specificity, yielding 54 responses with one generation per prompt. A study-defined composite averaged six universal content dimensions and one category-specific dimension on a 0–5 scale. GPT-4o scored all responses. Mean composite scores were 2.81, 3.52, and 4.09 for lay-framed, professional-underspecified, and technically explicit prompts, respectively. All six category means increased across these conditions, although each category-condition cell contained only three responses. Claude Sonnet, used as a secondary evaluator, scored 29 assessment requests and refused 25 (46.3%). Refusal rates differed across categories, ranging from 8 of 9 assessments in sequence and molecular design to 0 of 9 in end-to-end discovery pipelines. These results document an association between prompt formulation and automated response scores, alongside category-dependent evaluator coverage. The composite includes overlapping measures of detail and does not validate scientific correctness, successful execution, user uplift, or real-world risk. We propose an evidence-to-governance framework that separates these claims and identifies the validation required before automated scores inform deployment decisions.

articles.title: Thermal Modeling and 3D Geometry Prediction of Multi-layer, Multi-Track Directed Energy Deposition
articles.abstract: Laser powder directed energy deposition (LP-DED) is highly sensitive to process-induced thermal variation, which governs deposition accuracy, surface quality, and solidification microstructure. Analytical thermal models predict meltpool behavior quickly, but multi-layer builds require capturing heat accumulation in an increasingly preheated, geometrically evolving part. This study extends the classical Gaussian moving-source model to multi-layer, multi-track LP-DED of SS316L by incorporating surface heat loss, the enthalpy sink of the powder stream, beam attenuation through the powder cloud, and a spatially resolved layer-to-layer thermal carry-over field. The meltpool width from the predicted isotherms feeds a parabolic bead-geometry model based on powder mass conservation to predict the three-dimensional print profile. Four model parameters are calibrated from a single build using infrared-measured meltpool core temperatures, and the predictions are validated against SS316L thin-walls and cubes. For the thin-walls, the predicted meltpool width and length deviated from measurements by 16.1% and 15.6% on average, and by less than 2% at the lowest scan speed and powder feed rate. For the cubes, the predicted length, width, and height deviated by 13.7%, 8.6%, and 23.1% on average. The deviations of the predictions from the experimental results were investigated and are attributed mainly to treating the attenuated laser energy as entirely lost, which leads to under-predicted meltpool dimensions. This under-prediction can be overcome by properly calibrating the model around the nominal processing window. By rapidly predicting thermal behavior and part geometry, the model offers an efficient basis for process planning, parameter selection, and digital twins.

articles.title: Large Sample Size Effects on Maximum Likelihood Estimation in Multinomial Logistic Regression
articles.abstract: Multinomial logistic regression is used for outcomes with more than two categories, but evidence on how large sample sizes affect coefficient-estimation performance remains limited for specific model structures. Previous studies have often focused on prediction, sample-size planning, sparse-data methods, or other estimation settings. This study assessed coefficient performance in a five-category multinomial logistic regression model with ten binary explanatory variables, using category 5 as the reference. Monte Carlo simulation was conducted at sample sizes of 1,000, 3,000, 5,000, and 10,000, with 10,000 datasets generated at each size. The model was fitted to each dataset, and the mean estimates, bias, empirical standard errors, and mean squared errors (MSEs) were calculated for 44 coefficients. All 10,000 model fits succeeded at each sample size. Across the 44 coefficients, mean absolute bias decreased from 0.0453 at (:n:=:1,000) to 0.0038 at (:n:=:10,000). Median coefficient-level MSE decreased from 0.0598 to 0.0055, while mean empirical standard error declined from 0.3216 to 0.0922. MSE decreased for every coefficient at each successive sample size. The study fills a focused evidence gap by comparing coefficient-level estimation measures across several large sample sizes within the same five-category model. Under the specified simulation conditions, larger sample sizes were associated with estimates that were, overall, less biased and more precise.

articles.title: High-Capacity Multi-Copy Quantum Key Distribution via Hypercontractive Complexity Games
articles.abstract: The rate-loss trade-off in repeaterless quantum key distribution (QKD) bounds the secret key capacity of optical links. The Quantum Computational Timelock (QCT) framework overcomes this limit by utilizing the difference between computational security and quantum memory coherence times. We introduce the Information Reconciled Khot-Vishnoi (IR-KV-QCT) protocol, which maps the Khot-Vishnoi communication complexity game onto a high-dimensional prepare-and-measure QKD scheme under the QCT framework. Using a large-alphabet phase encoding, the protocol transmits log₂ n bits per qudit and corrects phase-alignment and channel-induced decoding errors via non-binary Slepian-Wolf Information Reconciliation. To combat channel attenuation, the protocol transmits identical copies of each state. We prove that this multi-copy ensemble is confined to the symmetric subspace, whereby Holevo's theorem strictly bounds the adversary's accessible information from an immediate measurement. Furthermore, we demonstrate that current and near-future quantum error correction thresholds are insufficient to sustain coherent attacks under the QCT framework, thereby limiting the operational threat model to collective attacks. Under this constraint, we bound the adversary's accessible information and prove the security of the protocol using the hypercontractivity of the Khot-Vishnoi game. This exponential suppression of information extraction supports a secure multi-copy transmission threshold of O(n / log₂ n). Consequently, the protocol circumvents the exponential rate-loss decay of single-photon schemes, enabling high-capacity key rates with everlasting security against collective attacks.

articles.title: Effect of Spatial Stiffness Variability in CDM-Improved Ground on Retaining Wall Displacement
articles.abstract: Cement deep mixing (CDM)-improved ground is often modeled using uniform properties, although its stiffness varies spatially. This study examines how this variability affects wall displacement in a soft-ground excavation in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The excavation was supported by a CDM retaining wall and a CDM-improved base. A two-dimensional finite-element model was calibrated against inclinometer measurements. Tests on 578 specimens from 65 field columns yielded a mean secant modulus E50 of 956.61 MPa and a coefficient of variation (COV) of 0.53. Lognormal stiffness fields were generated using spectral representation and assigned to the equivalent material representing the improved base. Wall properties and material strengths were held constant. The baseline analysis included 300 realizations. Six additional cases, each with 50 realizations, examined changes in COV and the horizontal and vertical scales of fluctuation. The baseline displacements formed two clusters around 8.5–8.6 mm and 9.5–9.6 mm. A two-component lognormal mixture was fitted to this distribution. Increasing COV from 0.1 to 0.3 increased the displacement standard deviation from 0.085 to 0.26 mm, with little change in the mean. Changes in the scales of fluctuation also affected dispersion. The probability of exceeding the measured displacement of 8.84 mm was approximately 44% in the baseline case and 42–52% in the parametric cases. These values represent the probability of exceeding a field-measured displacement, not the probability of structural failure. The results show that base-stiffness variability can affect displacement dispersion more than the mean response within the investigated ranges. Their interpretation remains subject to the equivalent-continuum assumptions and finite Monte Carlo sample sizes.

articles.title: Error Correction and Feedforward Timing in a Simulated Dual-Rail Photonic Architecture
articles.abstract: In a linear-optical quantum computer, error correction must finish before the encoded photon leaves the optical delay line. We present a 33-mode dual-rail architecture for single-error detection and evaluate repeated-syndrome distance-3 correction using an extended 55-mode circuit-level simulation model. We co-design the timing budget and an FPGA decoder. On a Basys3 board, the decoder was validated at distances 3, 5, and 7 using 40,000 Stim-generated syndrome vectors per distance (120,000 in total), with no mismatches. Under a reference two-term circuit-level Pauli noise model, finite-size scaling gives a threshold estimate of 0.194 ± 0.001, with statistical uncertainty only; the fitted suppression exponents are consistent with ⌈d/2⌉. Post-place-and-route timing gives a conservative decoder cycle of 8.79 ns (113.8 MHz). With assumed detection and switching latencies of 50 ns and 10 ns, respectively, decoding uses about 9% of the 99.8 ns optical-buffer interval, identifying detector readout as the main target for latency reduction. The stated source-quality model also yields a photon-indistinguishability bound of V > 0.982; this is a model-dependent estimate, not an experimental measurement.

articles.title: Gaussian Surface Reconstruction with Adaptive Depth Supervision for Geographic Information Systems
articles.abstract: Surface reconstruction from overlapping images supplies geometry for three-dimensional geographic information systems (GIS), but stereo depth errors can constrain the recovered surfaces. We present HelixGau, a Gaussian surface reconstruction method that filters and updates stereo depth during optimization. Local correlation with monocular depth selects pixels for supervision, while stereo estimates supply the supervised values. Rendered planes with higher photometric correlation across views provide candidates for stereo plane updates. The updated depth maps are filtered before supervision, and surfaces are extracted after optimization. On 16 BlendedMVS scenes, mean F1 is 88.64 with a standard deviation of 0.09 over four runs, compared with the highest baseline mean of 76.85. Mean F1 is 0.500 on six Tanks and Temples scenes. On the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) benchmark, overall error is 0.505 mm, compared with the lowest baseline error of 0.504 mm. Component ablations measure the separate effects of filtering and updates on the reconstructed geometry.

articles.title: Agricultural TFP Dynamics and Ozone-Depleting Substances Panel Analysis in Latin America
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the long-term relationships between ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out policies, land surface temperature anomalies, and agricultural Total Factor Productivity (TFP) dynamics across a panel of 23 countries over a 35-year period (1990–2024). Employing a two-stage analytical framework combining an input-oriented Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) Malmquist index with second-stage panel fixed-effects econometric regressions, aggregate TFP growth is decomposed into technical efficiency change and technological progress. Empirical findings reveal that regional agricultural TFP dynamics were primarily driven by shifts in the production frontier and cross-country structural variations. Second-stage econometric estimates demonstrate that historical consumption of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs_IHS) and Methyl Bromide (MB_IHS) did not exert statistically significant negative disruptions on agricultural productivity (β = 0.0160,p = 0.2744; β = 0.0218,p = 0.3691, respectively), reflecting successful technological substitution and producer adaptation during the Montreal Protocol phase-out mandates. Furthermore, annual surface temperature anomalies showed no significant aggregate impact (β = 0.0093,p = 0.9388), highlighting the limitations of macro-level climate averages. Marked cross-country heterogeneity underscores the imperative for targeted policies that bridge technical efficiency gaps and enhance agricultural resilience.

articles.title: High-temperature thermal performance of ceramic-array load bearing multi- layer insulation for radioisotope thermophotovoltaic system
articles.abstract: A hollow ZrO2 ceramic array Load Bearing multi-layer insulation (LBMLI) is proposed for the radioactive thermophotovoltaic system (RTPV). Two theoretical models including the finite element model and layer-by-layer model are compared to analyze the thermal insulation performance. The number of layers, spacing, ceramic array quantity, thermal conductivity of spacing material, and reflective screen emissivity on heat loss are analyzed. At the LBMLI of 9 dots’ ceramic array, as the quantity of layers increased from 15 to 20, the heat power loss significantly decreased from 22.5 W to 17 W. By reducing the emissivity from 0.1 to 0.025, the heat loss is almost linearly reduce to 8.5 W. For mechanical stability, a 15-layer-screen ceramic array LBMLI is designed for the present RTPV, with 25 ceramic arrays in each layer. When the input power is 250 W, if not considering insulation frame heat loss of the ceramic array LBMLI, the temperature at heat source center could reach 1106.3 ℃, and the thermal efficiency of ceramic array LBMLI is 69.5%. When it is considered, the temperature of the heat source is 1079.4 ℃, and ŋthermal is 57.0%. Moreover, considering optical cavity size, when reducing the lateral two dimensions of ceramic array LBMLI by 8 cm each, the temperature at heat source center changes to 1159.9 ℃ when considering insulation frame heat loss, with ŋthermal being 60.2%. Results show that hollow ZrO2 ceramic array LBMLI is expected to reduce the heat leakage.

articles.title: Analytical Solution of Pipe-Soil Interaction and Prediction of Construction Stress and Settlement for Large-Diameter Fabricated Circular Pipe Jacking
articles.abstract: Aiming at the problems that the pipe-soil interaction mechanism of ultra-large-diameter fabricated circular pipe jacking under non-uniform earth pressure is unclear, there is a lack of systematic analytical methods for the coupled stress of jacking force and circumferential load during construction, and the prediction of stratum loss and settlement excessively relies on empirical parameters. Based on plane strain elasticity theory and Fourier series decomposition theory, this paper derives a complete analytical solution of stress and displacement for thick-walled cylinders under 0 ~ 3 order harmonic loads, considering the coordination of radial and tangential displacements between pipe and soil, and clarifies the contribution proportion of each order harmonic to the internal force of pipe segments. A strength checking system for pipe segments under the coupling action of axial jacking force and circumferential non-uniform earth pressure is established for two typical working conditions of axial jacking and eccentric jacking during construction, and the distribution law and critical control value of axial tensile stress of pipe segments under eccentric loading are revealed. Combined with the elastoplastic theory of cylindrical cavity expansion, an analytical calculation model of stratum loss rate directly determined by soil physical and mechanical parameters and construction grouting parameters is constructed, and then the prediction method of ground surface settlement is given. Verified by engineering measured data, the stratum loss rate calculated by the analytical method in this paper is in good agreement with the field measured value, and the checking result of pipe segment strength can provide theoretical support for structural safety control during construction. The research results can provide reference for the structural design and environmental impact assessment of large-diameter fabricated pipe jacking.

articles.title: Thermomechanical modelling of concrete with aggregate inclusions using total Lagrangian B-spline material point method
articles.abstract: Abstract Concrete with aggregate inclusions exhibit coupled heat transfer, stress-wave propagation, and damage across mortar, aggregates, and interfacial transition zones. This study develops a total Lagrangian B-spline material point method (TLBSMPM) for coupled mechanical and thermal analysis, with interpolation ﬁxed in the reference conﬁguration. We assess the method using elastic-wave and bending benchmarks, a heat-conduction test, a thermally shocked cantilever, and impact simulations of homogeneous and three-phase concrete disks. For TLBSMPM, errors decrease with grid reﬁnement in the wave and heat-conduction tests, and the cantilever frequency agrees with beam theory within 0.75%. In bending, total Lagrangian methods reduce stress oscillations and computation time relative to updated Lagrangian methods at the same grid size.
