Wave accuracy depends on particle arrangement: linear interpolation performs better for uniform particles, whereas cubic B-splines perform better for the tested nonuniform arrangement. In the three-phase disks, damage concentrates in and around the interfaces. The ranking of mass-weighted global damage changes over time; because undamaged aggregate mass remains in the average, this measure does not compare damage only in mortar and interfaces. These results support phase-resolved thermomechanical analysis under the tested conditions.Keywords: B-spline material point method, total Lagrangian formulation, concrete with aggregate inclusions, thermomechanical modelling, interfacial transition zone

articles.title: Impact of solvent vapor annealing on the electrical properties of electrochemical transistors
articles.abstract: Electrochemical transistors (ECTs) represent a specialized class of thin-film transistors utilizing ion-conducting electrolytes as gate dielectrics. Benefiting from substantial volumetric ion-doping and large interfacial capacitance, these devices achieve remarkable electrical characteristics, such as low operating voltage, elevated drain currents, and superior charge carrier mobilities. Consequently, extensive research has focused on identifying the primary factors governing ECT operation, ranging from ionic dimensions and transport kinetics within the electrolyte to the microstructural arrangement of the semiconducting layer. Although solvent vapor annealing (SVA) is routinely employed to optimize conventional organic field-effect transistors, its application in ECTs remains largely unexplored. Herein, we comprehensively examine how SVA modifies both the specific capacitance and semiconductor morphology in ECTs to clarify their respective roles in device operation. By employing SVA to tune these physical attributes, we reveal that the microstructural organization of the semiconductor; specifically, its degree of crystallinity, serves as the decisive factor determining overall transistor performance. These findings clarify fundamental electrolyte-gating mechanisms and offer a practical design strategic for developing high-performance electrochemical electronics.

articles.title: Condition-Dependent Corrosion Responses of L415 Pipeline Steel under SRB-Inoculated and Sterile Conditions: Effects of pH, Chloride, and Sulfate
articles.abstract: Environmental changes reshape the corrosion contrast between SRB-inoculated steel and its sterile reference. L415 pipeline steel was evaluated across separate pH, nominal chloride, and supplemental-sulfate series using gravimetry, polarization, impedance, and surface observations. Inoculated gravimetric corrosion rates peaked at pH 6.6, but agreement between mass loss and fitted current densities depended on the condition: inoculated loss was lower at pH 4.6 despite near-equal currents, and higher at pH 8.0 despite a lower current. In the chloride series, the inoculated-to-sterile current-density ratio decreased from 15.51 at 3000 mg/L to 0.25 at 12000 mg/L. This variation involved both a declining inoculated response and a rising sterile response; the highest-label gravimetric rate difference remained small. Inoculated mass loss increased across the sulfate labels, while the sterile reference exhibited an intermediate minimum. The principal finding is that environmental dependence emerges from the trajectories of both exposure groups and from their correspondence across indicators. Together, the environmental comparisons identify where cumulative loss, fitted electrochemistry and local surface appearance converge or diverge, extending the earlier temporal characterization of L415 steel.

articles.title: Development and Microstructural Investigation of Ni– Mo–FeCrAl Modified 40H Steel for Furnace Roller Applications
articles.abstract: This study investigates the effect of complex alloying on the microstructure and mechanical behavior of modified 40H structural steel intended for metallurgical furnace rollers. The steel was modified with Ni, Mo, Al, and FeCrAl-based additives and subjected to normalization at 880°C, quenching at 860°C, and tempering at 550°C. Microstructural evolution was analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with EDS characterization, while hardness was evaluated using Rockwell (HRC), Brinell (HBW), and Vickers (HV) methods. The as-cast condition exhibited a heterogeneous cast microstructure characterized by pronounced dendritic segregation and significant hardness scatter (473–561 HB). After heat treatment, the microstructure developed a more uniform and refined appearance, accompanied by a reduction in hardness scatter. Hardness values stabilized in the range of 42–48 HRC, accompanied by a decrease in measurement dispersion. SEM/BSE observations indicated a more uniform morphology after heat treatment, while local SEM/EDS analysis was used only as a supplementary semi-quantitative tool to evaluate elemental distribution in selected regions. The combined alloying and heat-treatment strategy contributed to microstructural refinement and reduced hardness scatter after heat treatment. These findings suggest that the proposed processing route may be beneficial for the development of 40H steel components intended for furnace roller applications.

articles.title: Collapse misclassification dominates the uncertainty in city-scale earthquake fatality estimates: a validated probabilistic seismic risk model for the residential building stock of Peshawar, Pakistan
articles.abstract: Probabilistic seismic risk estimates for rapidly growing cities in data-scarce regions are increasingly used to set mitigation priorities, yet the fatality component of these estimates is rarely tested. This study develops an updated event-based seismic risk model for the residential building stock of District Peshawar, Pakistan (361,357 buildings; 4.31 million people; USD 7.83 billion replacement value), using the seismic source model of the 2021 Building Code of Pakistan, a census-based exposure model mapped to seven Global Earthquake Model (GEM) building classes, and GEM analytical fragility functions. A hazard-consistent closed-form model is then derived by inverting the event-based aggregate loss curve into an equivalent spectral-acceleration hazard curve. The closed-form model reproduces the event-based average annual loss (AAL), and its 475- and 2,475-year intensities agree with the building-code hazard and 13 published hazard studies. The baseline AAL is USD 20.2 to 22.8 million (0.26 to 0.29% of replacement value), and unreinforced brick and adobe masonry account for 97% of it. Fatality estimates, however, depend critically on how the complete-damage state is translated into casualties. Treating every completely damaged building as collapsed, as is common in practice, yields 412 to 881 deaths per year, which, in a back-analysis of the 2015 Mw 7.5 Hindu Kush earthquake, can exceed the death toll of the entire province. Applying HAZUS collapse fractions, or GEM fatality vulnerability functions, reduces the estimate to 51 to 77 deaths per year (1.2 to 1.8 per 100,000) and reconciles the model with the 2015 observations. A nine-factor sensitivity analysis and a 1,500-run Monte Carlo propagation show that the casualty model, the hazard level and the collapse lethality dominate the uncertainty in fatalities (5 to 95% range 18 to 259 per year), whereas the choice of vulnerability model dominates AAL. Retrofitting single-storey adobe houses is five to six times more cost-effective per life saved than retrofitting brick masonry, although no strategy is economically justified on direct losses alone.

articles.title: Radioactive disequilibrium chronometry of uranium and radium loss from weathering gold mine tailings in tropical Ghana
articles.abstract: Radiological surveys of gold tailings can only provide activity concentrations, and not indicate whether uranium and radium are being lost. On a 1–49 year chronosequence of 54 Ghanaian tailings, 226Ra/238U rose from 1.02 to 1.44 and 228Ra/232Th fell from 1.02 to 0.92. Loss rate constants derived from these chronometers are 1.7–2.2 × 10 − 2 y− 1 for uranium and 1.0–1.3 × 10− 2 y− 1 for radium, a little higher than the measured losses, though the numbers are still subject to uncertainty and are treated as upper limits. Leachate 234U/238U, determined using alpha spectrometry, rose from 1.05 (acid-reactive) to 1.29 (oxide-rich) tailings, which falls within the range of 1.27–1.38 reported for local groundwater. Radionuclide mobility is determined by the weathering stage rather than the activity level.

articles.title: Synthesis of Iron-Based ZSM-5 Zeolite via Interzeolite Conversion and Its Application in Phenol Hydroxylation
articles.abstract: A series of Fe-containing ZSM-5 zeolites (Fe x -ZSM-5) was synthesized via an ionothermal interzeolite conversion strategy using Beta zeolite as the precursor, and the effects of iron incorporation method and loading on iron speciation and catalytic performance were systematically investigated. Characterization results reveal that iron in the Fe x -ZSM-5 series predominantly exists as highly dispersed isolated framework Fe 3+ species and extra-framework oligomeric FexOy clusters. At comparable iron loading, Fe0.1-ZSM-5, which exhibits superior iron dispersion, achieves a phenol conversion of 53.51%, markedly surpassing that of Fe/ZSM-5 (25.83%) prepared by incipient wetness impregnation. Notably, the regenerated Fe0.3-ZSM-5 exhibits a markedly higher dihydroxybenzene selectivity (89.35%) than its fresh counterpart (71.29%), owing to the leaching of iron species during the first run, which triggers a less selective homogeneous pathway. However, the influence of acidic properties of iron-containing catalysts on the dihydroxybenzene selectivity remains controversial. These results demonstrate that interzeolite conversion provides an effective route to Fe-ZSM-5 catalysts that host highly dispersed, speciation-tunable iron species, rendering them highly efficient for phenol hydroxylation.

articles.title: Multi-decadal trends in SST, chlorophyll-a, NPP and atmospheric forcing across oligotrophic and upwelling regions of the Northeast Atlantic
articles.abstract: Climate change is reshaping the Northeast Atlantic, yet its impact differs between oligotrophic and upwelling ecosystems. We analysed multi-decadal trends from satellite and reanalysis datasets of sea surface temperature (SST), chlorophyll-a (chl-a), net primary production (NPP), and wind stress across the Northeast Atlantic Subtropical Gyre and adjacent upwelling regions. SST increased across the region, with the strongest warming in the Azores (+ 3.18°C century⁻¹) and the weakest in the Permanent Upwelling (PU) region (+ 1.37°C century⁻¹). Chl-a trends were predominantly negative, with the largest decline in PU (− 1.62 mg m⁻³ century⁻¹), accompanied by a reduction in highly productive area (− 6.25% century⁻¹). NPP also declined, with the strongest trends in the Cape Juby Weak Permanent Upwelling and Seasonal Upwelling region (− 459.56 and − 351.38 mg C m⁻² day⁻¹ century⁻¹, respectively). Upwelling-favourable wind stress intensified in the Northwest African upwelling system, reaching + 15.98 mN m⁻² century⁻¹ in PU and + 12.32 mN m⁻² century⁻¹ in Cape Juby, but without increased chl-a concentrations. Comparison with trends ending in 2019 indicated stronger SST and chl-a trends, suggesting that the 2023–2024 North Atlantic marine heatwave influenced warming estimates.

articles.title: Thermo-Mechanical Material Screening and Constraint-Based Optimization of an Automotive Clutch Using Response Surface Methodology
articles.abstract: This study presents an integrated computational framework combining multiscale material homogenization, transient thermo-mechanical analysis, and constraint-based optimization for automotive clutch design. Using ANSYS Material Designer, polymer matrix composites containing 15 vol.% Al₂O₃ were initially evaluated against a commercial friction material (COM_FM). Preliminary finite element analysis (FEA) indicated that increased thermal conductivity alone was insufficient to limit localized temperature rise. A composite containing 25 vol.% Al₂O₃ (PMC-M1-25) was therefore selected for further investigation. A 30-point design space was constructed using Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) with an optimal space-filling (OSF) configuration, considering clamping pressure (1.0–3.0 MPa), engine torque (150–350 N.m), and friction coefficient (0.25–0.40). Response surface methodology (RSM) was used to model global component deformation and peak interface temperature. The maximum sampled temperature reached 456.83°C, highlighting the importance of evaluating thermally unfavorable operating conditions. Sensitivity analysis and response surface models were used to examine the effects of the operating parameters on the thermo-mechanical responses. Constraint-based optimization was then applied to identify operating conditions satisfying the prescribed thermal limit, followed by direct FEA verification of the selected condition. The proposed framework links composite material homogenization, thermo-mechanical response prediction, and constraint-based optimization to support the numerical assessment of automotive clutch operating conditions.

articles.title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Specimen Geometry Effects on Temperature Homogeneity of Advanced High-Strength Steels by Direct Electrical Heating
articles.abstract: All kinds of matter are built up from elements in different compositions under physical laws. Thermal processes produce complex compositions, such as metal alloys. The quality of these processes heavily affects precise thermal conditions. Therefore, a homogeneity study of the temperature field on the surface of metal sheets under Direct Electrical Heating (DEH) was performed. The study was focused on measurements by infrared cameras and temperature field analyses. The most frequent steel, 22MnB (Svoboda et al. 2019), was used to prove the simulations. Suggestions for actions to optimize and enlarge homogeneous heating areas are raised up. The steel 22MnB5 is often used in the automotive industry for hot-stamping processes that require high strength, toughness, and durability, such as in structural components. The homogeneity of direct heating temperature depends on the type of heating (AC or DC), the shapes, positions, and dimensions of the electrodes. The relationships and balance among these parameters, as well as the optimum homogeneity, depend on cost, complexity, and technical capabilities. Using simulations, we optimized trench parameters in the samples and compared the results with real measurements.

articles.title: A Digitally Trimmable Bandgap Voltage Reference Using a Transmission-Gate Switched Resistor Ladder in 180-nm CMOS
articles.abstract: A bandgap reference is only as good as the silicon it is built on, and silicon never repeats itself exactly. This paper follows one bandgap circuit from its variation-limited state before trim to a digitally corrected one after trim. The core is a folded-cascode-regulated, mirror-based reference in a 180-nm CMOS process with VDD = 1.8 V; the correction is a 3-bit transmission-gate-switched resistor ladder placed in the output branch. Before trim, a 200-point Monte Carlo run swept over all eight codes (− 50°C to 125°C) evaluates successfully at 199 points (99.5%) and has a mean reference of 1.235 V with σ = 80.15 mV (6.5%), a spread of 0.888–1.418 V and a temperature coefficient (TC) of 17.7–2570 ppm/°C, the upper extreme being a single outlier. After trim, a 20-point Monte Carlo run gives a mean of 1.193 V with σ = 51.69 mV (4.3%), a 35% reduction in σ, a spread of 1.112–1.297 V and a TC of 44.9–192.3 ppm/°C. At the nominal corner the reference falls from 1.206 V to 1.183 V over the range, about 105 ppm/°C. The trim step, switch-resistance effects and test-time code selection are analysed.

articles.title: Composition Driven Band Alignment Evolution in Grafted Si/GeSn Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding and controlling band alignment in lattice-mismatched group-IV semiconductor-based heterostructures is fundamental to rational band-structure engineering, as it governs the electronic structure and carrier transport in heterointegrated semiconductor systems. Despite growing interest in Si/GeSn heterostructures, the composition-dependent band alignment has not been experimentally established. Here, we experimentally establish the evolution of band alignment in semiconductor-grafted Si/GeSn heterostructures with contents ranging from 8.8% to 12.4% using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Kraut's core-level method. The valence-band offset increases systematically from ~0.29 to ~0.57 eV with increasing Sn composition, whereas the corresponding effective conduction-band offset decreases from ~0.30 to ~0.12 eV. The observed band-alignment evolution is attributed to an upward shift of the GeSn valence-band maximum arising from enhanced p-p orbital hybridization, reduced bonding-antibonding splitting, and compressive-strain-induced heavy-hole band lifting. These findings establish the experimental relationship between alloy composition and interfacial band alignment in semiconductor-grafted Si/GeSn heterostructures, providing a quantitative framework for rational band-structure engineering in lattice-mismatched group-IV semiconductor heterostructures.

articles.title: High-harmonic generation along a structural phase transition in silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore high-harmonic generation (HHG) in silicon treated by a variable dose from a Ga focused ion beam (Ga⁺ FIB). We identify four qualitatively different dose regimes as the sample transitions from a crystalline to amorphous phase. The phase transition manifests as a giant enhancement in yield of low-order harmonics, which is strongly correlated with surface swelling as measured by atomic force microscopy. Below the critical dose, we observe a mixed phase regime where the HHG spectra display elements of both crystalline and amorphous silicon. We show how the samples can be laser-annealed with intense non-resonant pulses, where energy is deposited preferentially into amorphous regions, allowing us to disentangle the relative importance of chemical and structural modifications to the strong-field dynamics. At very high dose, we observe an increased sensitivity to laser-induced damage, which is correlated with FIB-induced etching. Energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy reveals that laser damage leads to the formation of Ga-rich nanoparticles and porosity at the surface.

articles.title: Data-driven exploration of the strength-ductility synergy in refractory high-entropy alloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) have attracted increasing attention for their exceptional ability to retain strength at high temperatures. However, current research mainly concentrates on compositions close to equimolar alloys, leaving a large part of the composition space unexplored. Here, we develop a multiscale framework based on a data-driven dislocation genome method that constructs energy landscapes for edge dislocation motion across various compositions. The local configurational force derived from the energy landscape is incorporated into dislocation dynamics simulations, revealing a scaling law connecting macroscale strength and atomic-scale local resistance governed by fluctuations in the local configurational force. Based on this scaling law, a new solid-solution strengthening model for edge dislocation in BCC alloys is developed, followed by a data-driven exploration of refractory alloys considering both strength and ductility. The developed method and theory are adaptable, allowing for extension to other BCC alloy systems and guiding high-throughput alloy design.

articles.title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting plastic flow in body-centered cubic metals across temperature and strain-rate regimes requires distinguishing structural resistance from kinetic contributions. Here, we develop a temperature dependent mobility law for screw dislocation, integrating thermal activation theory and relativistic effects. Through discrete dislocation dynamics simulations, uniaxial tension and compression simulations were conducted on configurations with different initial dislocation densities, elucidating the correlation between plastic strain rate and key parameters such as stress, temperature, and dislocation density. Subsequently, a unified constitutive model incorporating temperature and strain rate is derived based on microscopic mechanisms. The model naturally bridges microscopic mechanisms to continuum response, resolving the additivity dilemma by establishing explicit physical criteria for how structural resistances and competing kinetic mechanisms superimpose. Through rigorous bottom-up simulations, we quantitatively capture the crossover point where phonon drag overtakes thermal activation, providing a mechanism-based explanation of anomalous thermal hardening. This work enables physically consistent predictions of strength and creep behavior across broad temperature and strain-rate regimes, advancing beyond phenomenological descriptions toward transparent, mechanism-based alloy design.

articles.title: Pressure-driven evolution of crystal and molecular structures reshapes excited-state competition in coronene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular nanocarbons exhibit unique optoelectronic properties and considered as promising candidates for organic device applications, however, understanding how molecular geometry and crystal packing jointly govern physical properties remains a fundamental challenge in π-conjugated molecular materials. Here, we demonstrate how these structural factors modulate the photoluminescence of coronene under high pressure. Combining high-pressure single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, optical spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations, we establish a relationship between distinct structural changes and the evolution of competing emissive states. Our results reveal that crystal polymorphism modifies the balance between free-exciton (FE) and self-trapped-exciton (STE) emission, while pressure-induced molecular bending is associated with a nonmonotonic evolution of STE emission. As intermolecular distances shorten, enhanced intermolecular electronic interactions give rise to excimer-related emission, introducing an additional emissive pathway. Although pressure-dependent optical properties of coronene have been linked to changes in crystal packing, our findings highlight that the optical response of a molecular solid is not governed by molecular deformation or crystal packing alone, but emerges from their interplay with intermolecular electronic coupling. By directly resolving molecular bending alongside changes in excited-state emission, this work provides insight into how distinct structural degrees of freedom can reshape the photophysical behavior of π-conjugated molecular solids.

articles.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial Z₂timesZ₂ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an S₃ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic Z₂⁽¹⁾ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a PSU(3)₃timesSpin(8)₋₁ Chern-Simons-Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the (8ₐdⱼ,8ᵥ) representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: PSU(3)₃/₂ QCD₃ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's unitary symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. The continuum theories are proposed to recover lattice time reversal at criticality. This connection to adjoint QCD₃ points to a possible continuous S₃-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

articles.title: Dopant-vacancy complexes as single-photon-emitter candidates in monolayer silicon carbide: radiative and nonradiative decay
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solid-state color centers have emerged as promising single-photon sources (SPSs). In particular, color centers in two-dimensional (2D) materials combine high photon brightness with scalable fabrication and ease of integration, offering a versatile platform for quantum information technologies. Realizing high-efficiency SPSs, however, requires strong radiative emission and negligible nonradiative decay. Using first-principles calculations, we assess radiative and nonradiative decay in dopant-vacancy complexes XSiVC (X = N, O, P, and S) in monolayer silicon carbide. All four defects exhibit stable neutral charge states and inter-defect optical transitions. Among them, PSiVC emerges as the leading single-photon-emitter candidate, combining rapid radiative decay with negligible nonradiative decay and a near-unity quantum yield within the modeled channels. By contrast, multiphonon decay limits the quantum yield of NSiVC despite its high Debye-Waller factor. Hyperfine tensors provide characteristic signatures for identifying the spin-active centers. Beyond identifying promising candidates, these results establish a joint radiative-nonradiative screening strategy and provide theoretical guidance for the rational design of color centers as solid-state SPSs.

articles.title: Classical weak antilocalization in electron hydrodynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weak localization is strongly suppressed in electron hydrodynamics, where frequent electron--electron collisions rapidly dephase the Cooperon. Nevertheless, disorder can still produce a logarithmic correction to the bare hydrodynamic resistivity. We show that spatial fluctuations of the momentum-relaxation rate generate a classical memory kernel through the diffusive return of transverse momentum. In two dimensions, this return is logarithmic, as in weak localization, but involves a single shear propagator rather than quantum interference. Conservation laws and positivity of dissipation fix its antilocalizing sign: the return reduces momentum relaxation and hence the bulk resistivity. Unlike quantum weak localization, the logarithm is cut off by momentum relaxation and has a viscosity-dependent amplitude. For temperature-independent impurity friction, the resistivity correction scales as -T²ln(T_ξ/T) in a Fermi liquid and -Tln(T_ξ/T) in a Planckian metal. In channels, the return competes with viscosity renormalization, and a width scan separates the two effects.

articles.title: Correlating orbital order and photovoltaic effect in Layered Ruddlesden-Popper Pr0.5Ca1.5MnO4 and PrCa2Mn2O7
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The understanding of growth and structure-property relations of epitaxial thin films of layered Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite oxides open up new pathways to tune correlated electron properties and to fabricate new types of correlated electron junctions, such as e.g. photovoltaic devices. In particular, the layered Ruddlesden-Popper systems Pr₀.5Ca₁.5MnO₄ and PrCa₂Mn₂O₇ at half doping exhibit much higher transition temperatures for the formation of charge and orbital ordered phases of T_c = 320 K and T_c up to 370 K, respectively, compared to the half doped non-layered system Pr₁₋ₓCaₓMnO₃ (PCMO) with T_c = 240 K. Here, we demonstrate the successful growth of epitaxial PrCa₂Mn₂O₇ thin films by ion beam sputtering and compare electric transport, optical absorbance, electronic bandstructure and photovoltaic response with epitaxial Pr₀.5Ca₁.5MnO₄, both deposited on (Nb:)SrTiO₃ (110) substrates. An enhanced density of Ruddlesden-Popper type of stacking faults is identified as a relaxation channel for misfit strain in PrCa₂Mn₂O₇ and seems to be the origin for the reduced T_c = 320 K and the reduced spatial coherence of charge and orbital order in comparison to Pr₀.5Ca₁.5MnO₄. Since the onset of the hot polaron photovoltaic effect is correlated to the formation of charge and orbital ordering, the comparative study of temperature dependent electric transport and photovoltaic response gives insights into the different role of strain and strain relaxation related defects on photo-electric properties.

articles.title: Epitaxial integration of GaN μ-platelets and thin films on metallic TiN using a hybrid approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the synthesis of epitaxial, self-organized GaN μ-platelets on metallic TiN thin films. To this end, we first nucleate self-assembled GaN nanowires with number densities between 0.01 to 300 μ m⁻² by molecular beam epitaxy. Subsequent overgrowth of these seed nanowires by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy yields GaN μ-platelets with corresponding number densities. The platelets exhibit N-polarity and form an ohmic contact to the metallic TiN substrate. By adjusting the growth conditions during the metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy, particularly the carrier gas and precursor ratio, the morphology of the GaN can be controlled across a broad range. Growth under N₂ carrier gas and with a 1:1 NH₃/trimethylgallium precursor flow ratio results in platelet ensembles with broad diameter and height distributions. In contrast, employing an N₂/H₂ carrier gas mixture promotes the formation of more homogeneous ensembles with narrower size distributions around a diameter of approx2 μ m. Finally, N-rich growth conditions under H₂ carrier gas enhance lateral growth, leading to the formation of coalesced GaN layers. GaN grown under these latter conditions exhibits strong near-band-edge emission, accompanied by only weak deep-level luminescence at room temperature.

articles.title: Charge and spin orders of the generalized Wigner crystal phases at fractional fillings in twisted MoTe₂: unrestricted Hartree-Fock and variational Monte Carlo studies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent experiments have revealed interaction-driven insulating states at various fractional fillings of twisted bilayer MoTe₂. Many of these insulating states are believed to be generalized Wigner crystals (GWC) condensed in the background of triangular moiracutee lattice. In this work, we focus on revealing the charge and spin order of the insulating states at 4/3 and 3/2 hole fillings over a range of twist angles and applied displacement fields using unrestricted Hartree-Fock (HF) and variational Monte Carlo (VMC) methods. We find that, at 4/3 filling for low twist angles the charge ordered ground state is valley-polarized (VP), characterized by weak charge delocalization approaching the classical limit. Application of the displacement field induces layer-polarization and suppresses the charge fluctuations even further. In contrast, at 3/2 filling, the VP phase exhibits signatures of a two-component GWC phase, which is particularly robust at finite displacement field. Additionally, by increasing the twist angle one pushes the system into an intervalley-coherent (IVC) phase, which is found to be fluctuation-dominated. Our VMC-based analysis shows that the correlation energy is negligible in the VP phase, which is consistent with its classical nature. However, the IVC phase shows significant gain in correlation energy, which is dominated by the nonlocal correlations captured by the Jastrow factors, while the local Gutzwiller factors play a minor role.

articles.title: The Rise of Zirconium Metal-Organic Polyhedra
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zirconium metal-organic polyhedra (Zr-MOPs) assembled from cyclopentadienyl (Cp)-capped Zr₃ clusters and carboxylate linkers form a structurally diverse family. Which MOP forms depends on the connectivity of the Zr₃ node, the geometry of the linker, and assembly conditions. This review classifies Zr-MOPs into edge- and face-directed tetrahedra, a cube, and cocoons according to the connectivity and geometry of their building blocks. From reported structures, we map which linkers give which MOPs and examine how the Zr₃ cluster precursor and the reaction conditions decide between the tetrahedron and the cocoon when one linker can give both. We describe how hydrogen bonding and ionic association organize the MOPs into reticular nets and porous salts in the crystal. Together, these comparisons relate cage geometry to node-linker connectivity and crystal packing to the geometry and distribution of external interaction sites, providing a structural basis for designing Zr-MOPs and their supramolecular assemblies.

articles.title: Phase-resolved spin-orbit exciton transfer with dressed quantum encodings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum simulation of a material runs on a register much smaller than the electronic problem behind it, and the map between the two decides what a measured correlation means. We study this map for spin--orbit exciton transfer across an Ir--Ir bond of a LiIrF₆-derived model. Exact references show that a bare product-state encoding has an amplitude floor above a 0.02 state tolerance at sampled times, whereas a polar-dressed encoding lowers the ten-window projected error from 0.320 to 3.54×10⁻⁴. Three-CZ axial and two-CZ transverse circuits, run on IBM Kingston in eight acquisitions with 1.6 million shots, resolve population transfer together with both quadratures of the intersite coherence. Raw half-transfer Bell-projector scores reach 0.935 in two independent acquisitions, and on a second bond a coherent arm with lower bound 0.871 is separated from a matched dephased control. Across 2,520 model points, adaptive spectral encodings meet fixed accuracy targets with explicit dimension costs.

articles.title: Analytic spread complexity in three-level systems and the spacing-ratio distribution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spread complexity characterizes the spreading of a quantum state over the Krylov basis and has been proposed to capture the correlations between energy levels. How such correlations manifest in the dynamics has been studied mainly numerically for large matrices. Here we consider three-level systems, the smallest setting with spacing correlations, and derive exact results for the spread complexity, the Krylov variance, and the Krylov entropy. At infinite temperature, the Krylov basis depends on the spectrum only through the ratio of consecutive level spacings, and the spectral variance enters only as an overall time scale. For Gaussian ensembles, these variables are statistically independent, and the averaged spread complexity and variance reduce to one-dimensional integrals over the spacing-ratio distribution encoding the level statistics. We establish universal late-time values of the complexity and variance, and an algebraic relaxation with exponents set by the Dyson index. We also outline the extension to d levels, with the ensemble-averaged spread complexity expressed as a (d-2)-dimensional integral over the joint distribution of consecutive spacing ratios.

articles.title: Non-ergodic Area Scaling of Andreev Transport in Al/AlOₓ/Al Tunnel Junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: State-of-the-art superconducting qubits rely on Al/AlOₓ/Al Josephson junctions (JJs) as a nonlinear element with an ideal sinusoidal current-phase dependence, with its inductance set by the junction area and oxidation conditions. This idealization holds only if the many conduction channels through the amorphous AlOₓ barrier transmit weakly and almost identically. Here, we measure the second-order subgap Andreev current, which sets the second Josephson harmonic, in Al/AlOₓ/Al JJs. For junction sizes relevant to qubits, we find that this current is dominated by lesssim 300 effective channels whose transparencies exceed the ideal tunneling limit (lesssim 10⁻⁶) by orders of magnitude. For small and high-aspect-ratio junctions, increasing the junction size does not average out the effect of these high transparency channels but instead adds additional channels of even greater transparency. The trend inverts once both the width and length of the junction exceed a critical length scale, above which the effective transparency decreases with area. This non-ergodic scaling of the Andreev current is reproduced by simulations and attributed to non-self-averaging statistics of the transparency distribution, which arise from variations in oxide thickness. The effect is largely invisible to the normal-state conductance used to target the inductance and reveals unexpected geometric and size-related trade-offs for scaling superconducting qubit systems to large numbers of junctions.

articles.title: Reference-Assisted Qutrit Control and Conditional One-Round Distillation in a Charge-4e Superconductor Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.17823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate a charge-4e parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record. For charge-conjugation-invariant inputs, record probabilities are independent of the supported reference state; for arbitrary inputs, discarding the reference gives a population-weighted mixture of conjugate sector maps. We give a finite-depth stability bound for complete labelled instruments, including postselection and initial zero-sector contamination. A self-contained calculation reproduces the known dense single-qutrit closure of the registered Clifford-plus-Flip gate set. We also specify an abstract ternary CSS [[11,1,5]]₃ syndrome/recovery decoder: 243 classical representatives per CSS component correct all 3,609 Pauli errors of support weight at most two, and an exact integer dynamic program yields the full independent-Pauli logical enumerator. Its all-syndrome acceptance is distinct from the known 1/1728 ideal acceptance of one-round strange-state Golay distillation. An accepted-run target-infidelity budget and a synthetic parameter protocol expose the remaining noise assumptions. Native charge-4e syndrome extraction, material feasibility, a device threshold, and unconditional fault tolerance are not established.

articles.title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity q and Fermi momentum k=(6π²ρ/q)¹/³, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy [ Dᵣₘ M(k)=frac34π²log k+O(1),qquad Dᵣₘ CHF(k)=12e⁻¹/²⁻π^²/⁸ k²e⁻π³/²sqrtk(1+o(1)). ] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted L² convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

articles.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group G detects Brunnian links with up to n+1 components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if G is n-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

articles.title: Quantum melting and Pomeranchuk effect of zero-field Wigner solids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.18532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wigner solids and crystals are many-body phases of matter in which repulsive interactions between the charge carriers cause them to freeze into a solid. How Wigner solids compete or cooperate with integer and fractional quantum Hall liquids has been a long-standing open question. Here, we investigate this question for zero-field, electron and hole Wigner solids in cadmium arsenide quantum wells. In the low temperature limit, our results are consistent with a recent theoretical model [A. P. Reddy and L. Fu, Phys. Rev. B 113, L161403 (2026)] that proposes that the quantum Hall liquid can become energetically favored over the solid at low integer filling factors. Going beyond the low-temperature limit, we observe a re-entrant solid that emerges from the quantum Hall liquid. We explain this observation by considering the role of spin entropy, in close analogy with the zero-field Pomeranchuk effect, but appearing here at finite fields. The competition between quantum Hall liquids and Wigner solids is thus governed by both energy and entropy terms, giving rise to rich phase stability diagrams that result from the interplay between topology and correlations.

articles.title: A Practical Route to Demonstrating Core Reactivity in Cs Polyoxides under Pressure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2110.07865v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Activating normally inert core electrons expands the bonding possibilities of elements beyond conventional valence chemistry. Although Cs core reactivity under pressure was predicted in polyfluorides more than a decade ago, experimental confirmation remains elusive, largely because loading highly corrosive F₂ poses serious challenges for diamond anvil cells. Here, global crystal structure searches combined with first-principles calculations identify Cs polyoxides as a practical alternative for investigating core reactivity. Compression activates Cs 5p electrons, leading to oxidation beyond the usual +1 state and a striking reversal of conventional polyoxide behavior: O-O bonds disappear, while strong Cs-O covalent bonds generate molecular units and extended sheets. Most importantly, CsO, a solid peroxide stable at ambient pressure, is predicted to undergo this transformation at 221 GPa, forming linear [CsO₂]⁻ units. This approach replaces a chemical reaction between separate reactants with a phase transition in a single solid, avoiding F₂ loading and simplifying experimental implementation without changing the overall composition. The loss of peroxide O-O pairs provides a vibrational signature of the transformation, while calculated infrared and Cs L₃-edge XANES spectra, together with simulated X-ray diffraction patterns, guide experimental identification. These results establish an experimentally testable route toward core reactivity and show how pressure can extend the chemical possibilities of a familiar alkali metal.

articles.title: Ultralow Lattice Thermal Conductivity in Orthorhombic Rb2Se3 with rigid covalent trimers and a soft ionic framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.21634v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Alkali-metal-containing compounds often exhibit exceptionally low lattice thermal conductivity, yet the structural origins and transport mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate orthorhombic Rb2Se3 using first-principles bonding, lattice-dynamical, and thermal-transport calculations. Bonding analyses reveal strongly covalent, V-shaped Se3 trimers embedded in a soft ionic coordination framework. Representing each trimer as a pseudo-atom reveals a pseudo-one-dimensional chain arrangement along [001] within the three-dimensional crystal.This bonding hierarchy produces a dense low-frequency phonon manifold and four separated high-frequency optical branches dominated by internal trimer stretching. Four-phonon scattering strongly suppresses particle-like heat transport, leaving the coherent contribution dominant. The coherent contribution is largest along the pseudo-atom-chain direction [001] and accounts for most of the thermal conductivity anisotropy. At 300 K, the total lattice thermal conductivities are 0.067, 0.096, and 0.265 W/mK along [100], [010], and [001], respectively. These results connect the coexistence of rigid covalent trimers and a soft ionic framework to ultra-low thermal conductivity, while revealing how their structural arrangement is reflected in directional coherent heat transfer.

articles.title: Facile On-Chip Growth and Spatially Selective Color Tuning of CsPbBr₃@TFA Nanoplatelets via Ion Engineering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.16290v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Metal halide perovskite (MHP) nanoplatelets are attractive for integrated optoelectronics because of their strong light-matter interactions and composition-tunable optical response. However, their high surface-to-volume ratio promotes surface defects and trap-assisted nonradiative recombination. In addition, their ionic nature facilitates rapid halide migration and limits selective composition tuning. Here, we combine in-synthesis (in situ) and post-synthesis ion engineering to suppress nonradiative recombination and enable selective on-chip color conversion. CsPbBr₃ nanoplatelets were grown directly on-chip via a solution process incorporating trifluoroacetate (TFA⁻) pseudohalides. CsPbBr₃@TFA emits at 520 nm with a linewidth of 14.56 % ± 0.5 nm and an average lifetime of 26.38 ns. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that TFA⁻ passivates uncoordinated Pb²⁺ and suppresses metallic lead (Pb⁰) formation. Spatially selective halide exchange was then achieved using a photolithographically patterned PMMA/Al₂O₃ mask to confine HCl vapor exposure. In the unmasked regions, the photoluminescence peak shifts from 520 nm to 413 nm, producing laterally defined green- and violet-emitting regions. The nanoplatelets were further integrated with graphene field-effect transistors, yielding responsivities of 2.5 x 10⁵ A W⁻¹ at 450 nm and 1.9 x 10⁵ A W⁻¹ at 370 nm, respectively. Our method enables scalable growth and selective color tuning of MHP nanoplatelets for on-chip optoelectronic integration.

articles.title: Emergent Electronic Bond-Order Wave in a Quasi-One-Dimensional Chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09383v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Collective order is notoriously difficult to stabilize in one dimension, where strong fluctuations suppress symmetry-breaking states. Here we report the emergence of an electronic bond-order wave (BOW) in the quasi-one-dimensional (1D) material Ba9Rh8O24, in which structural bonds become active electronic degrees of freedom that overcome 1D fluctuations to establish long-range order. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction uncovers a striking inversion of inequivalent Rh-Rh bonds across a transition TA = 180 K, where short and long bonds interchange their identities rather than undergoing conventional Peierls dimerization. This bond inversion coincides with a heat-capacity anomaly and a profound reorganization of the dielectric response with strong suppression of dielectric loss upon cooling. The BOW exhibits strongly nonlinear, frequency-dependent I-V characteristics, clockwise hysteresis, and nonvolatile memristive switching. These findings uncover an unprecedented transformation from a dynamic bond liquid to a rigid yet electrically reconfigurable BOW, establishing bond-centered electronic order as a new organizing principle for 1D quantum matter.

articles.title: Quantitative Impact of Occupation Smearing Methods on Conventional Superconductivity: from Electronic Structure through Lattice Dynamics to Electron-Phonon Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18185v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In first-principles calculations of metallic systems, the discrete electronic mesh in the Brillouin zone necessitates a smearing function and its width (e.g., the widely used 0.02 Ry Methfessel-Paxton scheme) to enforce continuity of energy and occupation at the Fermi surface. However, the quantitative impact of such empirical parameters on phonon-mediated superconductivity has long been overlooked, leading to their habitual selection by mere convention. Here, using hexahydride CsH6 as a benchmark, we systematically investigate the magnitude and propagation mechanism of smearing-induced errors against the parameter-free optimized tetrahedron method. Long-tailed smearing delocalizes the occupation window, causing substantial Fermi-level shifts, flattening of the density of states, and hardening phonon modes, thereby weakening electron-phonon coupling. Conversely, short-tailed smearing suffers from insufficient sampling, producing density-of-states oscillations and enhanced Fermi-surface nesting. These artifacts amplify electronic screening and Peierls instabilities, which soften acoustic modes and generate imaginary frequencies, causing CsH6 to be dynamically unstable and discarded. However, the optimized tetrahedron method reveals that CsH6 is dynamically stable under ambient pressure with a remarkable superconducting transition temperature of 121 K. To prevent subjective empirical parameters from obscuring theoretically promising high-temperature superconductors, we derive a simple scaling relation for the smearing width, applicable to different smearing functions, from the free-electron-gas model, offering an objective, precise, and efficient protocol for parameter selection in high-throughput screening.

articles.title: Modification of optical properties in ultrathin ALD-grown NbN layers using oxygen plasma treatment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32553v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: NbN thin films with a nominal thickness of 10,nm were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on Al₂O₃-buffered Si substrates and treated with oxygen plasma for 0,s (untreated), 20,s, 40,s, and 60,s to investigate oxygen-induced changes in their optical properties. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements were performed before and after oxygen plasma treatment over the ultraviolet--visible--near-infrared (1.24--6.20,eV) and infrared (0.041--0.827,eV) spectral ranges. Film thickness determined by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) was used as a fixed parameter in the optical modeling to extract the dielectric function, optical constants, and effective free-carrier concentration. We observed the emergence of a distinct absorption feature near 4.9,eV following oxygen plasma treatment, consistent with the oxidation of the NbN surface and the resulting change in its optical properties. Increasing the treatment time from 0 to 60,s reduced the effective carrier concentration from 1.20 × 10²² to 1.03 × 10²²,cm⁻³ and the effective carrier mobility from 2.44 to 2.27,cm²,V⁻¹,s⁻¹. The obtained results provide a basis for understanding the effects of oxygen plasma treatment on NbN thin films.
